en.name: *Mosque of the Sultan, Cairo*
short_description:
During the 1850s and 1860s, Francis Frith was one of England's most celebrated photographers. In September 1856, he set sail for Alexandria. This was the first of three trips that Frith would take to the Near East. The model was that of the 'Grand Tour'.  
Any analysis of Frith's work leads to the discourse of the tension between empirical knowledge and spiritual awareness in Victorian England. The photograph operated as a tool that could have moral influence upon those who viewed them with their ability to bring viewers to the locations of holy events.  
But even from a purely secular point of view, Frith's photographs become operators within an ideology specific to the era. Frith's thematic choices are manifest of the Victorians' tendency to regard themselves in relation to the larger history of mankind.
keywords: Albumen process; Grand Tour; Holy Land; Victorian; Egypt; travel; history of photography

en.name: Garden Mosque
short_description: The mosque is surrounded by a “Turkish garden” with winding paths and exotic plants. The architectural feature of the central building provides an original variation on the language of shapes found in baroque churches. Quotations from the western architectural history are combined with oriental motifs and inscriptions from the Qur'an. The minarets are positioned slightly in front of the western façade. The colonnade walkway with its rectangular layout is comprised of latticework open on all sides. The octagonal pavilions are decorated with dictums in Arabic and German. One striking feature is the refined roofscape with different basic slatecovered shapes, adorned by innumerable gilded crescents. The mosque’s interior is comprised of a round central hall, richly and colourfully decorated. Various general maxims are inscribed in Arabic and translated into German. These texts are not religious in nature, but generally invoke virtues, such as wisdom, diligence and discretion.
holder: Baden-Württemberg Castles and Gardens, State Agency for Property Assets and Construction
dates: The mosque complex comprises a cloister-like colonnade in the east (1779–84) and a main building (1782–86) flanked by two minarets (1786–95) in the west
history:
The mosque in the Schwetzingen palace gardens today is the last surviving example of a type of building quite common in European landscape gardens up to the end of the 18th-century.  
The mosque, built 1782–95 by Nicolas de Pigage, was preceded by the Ambulatory, designed inside a Turkish Garden, which was first mentioned in 1774. Work on the actual mosque building started after Elector Carl Theodor had moved to Munich. The Ambulatory itself already represents contemporaneous ideas of what a mosque building looked like; the similarities with the feature of the holy sites of Mecca, published by Fischer von Erlach, are as unmistakable as the similarity of the corner pavilions with the mosque built by Chambers at Kew Gardens. The mosque itself is a fairly autonomous structure with a temple-like portico and Baroque dome.
keywords: Garden Building; Turkish garden; Arabic inscriptions; minarets; Mosque; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens

ar.name: خمس قطع من النسيج.
description:
خمس قطع من نسيج الصوف مستديرة الشكل يزخرف كل منها رسم طائر، ربما يكون بطة أو أوزة، بألوان وأحجام مختلفة منسوجة بطريقة اللحمات غير الممتدة. والقطع مأخوذة من قطع كبيرة ربما كانت تضم تصميمات زخرفية من وحدات مكررة، واستخدمت كمفارش أو ستائر مما اشتهرت به مصر العليا (صعيد مصر) في أسيوط وإخميم وكذلك مدينة الفسطاط في العصر الطولوني (القرن 3 هـ / 9 م).  
  
وقد تميزت المنسوجات في العصر الطولوني بظهور الظل في العناصر الزخرفية حيث يتدرج اللون من فاتح إلى غامق. كما تميزت بقوة التعبير، وتأثرت بالأسلوب الساساني الذي أتى به أحمد بن طولون (حكم في الفترة 254 – 270 هـ / 868 – 884 م) من العراق. وتمثل صناعة النسيج في مصر في العصر الطولوني فترة انتقال بين العصر القبطي والعصر الإسلامي الخالص من حيث العناصر الزخرفية وتطورها.  
  
وكانت معظم الجزية التي يرسلها أحمد بن طولون إلى بلاط الخلافة العباسية في بغداد تتكون من منسوجات دور الطراز (مصانع الأقمشة) من الأقمشة الفاخرة المصنوعة من الصوف والكتان. ومن الجدير بالذكر أن أحمد بن طولون قد اهتم بمصانع النسيج التي كانت منتشرة في شمال الدلتا في كل من تنيس ودبيق ودمياط وغيرها من المدن التي اشتهرت بصناعة المنسوجات الكتانية ذات الكتابات المنسوجة من الحرير متعدد الألوان. وازداد الاهتمام بصناعة الأنسجة في مصر في عصر أبناء ابن طولون خمارويه (حكم في الفترة 270 – 282 هـ / 884 – 896 م) وهارون (حكم في الفترة 283 – 292 هـ / 896 – 905 م) الذين حرصا على تدوين اسميهما على الأشرطة الكتابية على الأقمشة.

تعدَّدت مصانع النسيج في مصر، واستُخدم القطن والكتّان في الإسكندرية ودمياط والفرما والبهنسا وأخميم وأسيوط، وظل أسلوب الزخارف القبطية واضحاً عليها خلال القرون الثلاثة الأولى بعد الهجرة، وتتميز هذه القطعة بوجود الظل للعناصر الزخرفية، حيث يتدرَّج اللون من الفاتح إلى الغامق.
holder: متحف النسيج (أحد فروع  متحف الفن الإسلامي في القاهرة)

en.name: Five textile fragments.
description:
Five circular woollen textile fragments each decorated with a depiction of a bird, perhaps a duck or a goose, in different sizes and colours, and woven in a non-extended weft pattern, a tapestry technique. The fragments were taken from bigger textiles, perhaps used as a counterpane or curtains, and which may have consisted of a decorative design with repetitive motifs. Upper Egypt was famous for sumptuous woven cloth such as this, with Asyut, Akhmim and the City of Fustat prominent places of production during the Tulunid period (AH 3rd / AD 9th century).  
During the Tulunid period, textiles were distinguished by the appearance of a shadow in the decorative components, where the colour was graded from light to dark, as well as for their powerful expression. They were also influenced by the Sassanid style, brought by Ahmad ibn Tulun (r. AH 254–70 / AD 868–84) from Iraq. The production of textiles in the Tulunid period represents a period of transition in Egypt between the Coptic period and the Islamic period with regard to the decorative components and their development.  
Most of the *jizya* (tribute) which Ahmad ibn Tulun sent to the court of the Abbasid caliphs consisted of textiles made in the *Tiraz* workshops, under royal decree, which produced magnificent fabrics of wool and linen. Tulun took a personal interest in the textile factories of Egypt, which were widespread in the north delta regions of Tanis, Dabik, Damietta, and other cities. These regions were famous for the manufacture of linen cloth with inscriptions woven in silk in a multitude of colours. Interest in textile manufacture increased in Egypt with the rule of the sons of Ibn Tulun: Khumarawayh (r. AH 270–82 / AD 884–96) and Harun (r. AH 283–92 / AD 896–905), who were inclined towards recording their names in inscription bands on the textile itself.

Cotton and linen textiles were woven in various factories in Egypt: Alexandria, Damietta, Farma, Bahnasa, Akhmim and Asyut. Coptic-style decorations remained prevalent during the AH 1st–3rd / AD 7th–9th centuries. The pieces here are notable for the shadow effect in the decorations, where colour is graded from light to dark shades.
holder: Textile Museum (One of the branches of the Museum of Islamic Art in Cairo)
keywords: Figurative decoration; wool; tiraz; Coptic; textile; tapestry; figurative representation; animal decoration; bird; royal manufacture; workshop
materials: Wool with the woven decorations woven in a non-extended weft pattern (tapestry technique).
tags: Wool with the woven decorations woven in a non-extended weft pattern (tapestry technique).

es.name: Cinco fragmentos de tejido.
description:
Estos cinco fragmentos circulares de tejido de lana están decorados con la imagen de un ave, quizá un pato o un ganso, de diferentes tamaños y colores; está tejido en punto de tapiz. Los fragmentos pertenecieron, posiblemente a cubrecamas o cortinas que quizá estuvieron decorados con dibujos repetidos.  
El Alto Egipto fue célebre por su producción de suntuosos tejidos como este; Asyut, Ajmim y la ciudad de Fustat fueron lugares famosos por sus telas durante la época tuluní (siglo III / siglo IX). En dicha época, los tejidos destacaron por la gran expresividad de sus elementos decorativos, en los que además se introdujeron las sombras, que se creaban oscureciendo los colores gradualmente. Asimismo, recibieron influencia del estilo sasánida que Ahmad ibn Tulun (r. 254-270 / 868-884) trajo de Irak. La producción de telas en la época tuluní representa un periodo de transición en Egipto entre la época copta y la islámica en cuanto a evolución decorativa.  
La mayor parte de los *yizya* (tributos) que Ahmad bin Tulun envió a la corte de los califas abbasíes fueron telas fabricadas en los *tiraz* bajo decreto real, que producían extraordinarios tejidos de lana y lino. Cabe mencionar que Ahmad ibn Tulun demostró un gran interés personal por los telares de Egipto, que eran abundantes en la región del delta, en ciudades como Tanis, Dabik, Damietta y otras, célebres por la fabricación de tejidos de lino con inscripciones en seda de muchos colores. El interés por la producción de telas en Egipto aumentó con los hijos de Ibn Tulun, Jamarawih (r. 270-282 / 884-96) y Harun (r. 283-292 / 896-905), que acostumbraban a plasmar sus nombres en bandas de inscripción en el propio tejido.

En varios lugares de Egipto –Alejandría, Damietta, Farma, Bahnasa, Ajmim y Asyut– se producían telas de algodón y lino. En los primeros siglos de la Hégira predominaban los adornos de estilo copto. Estas piezas están adornadas con un efecto de sombra que se conseguía con la gradación de colores.
dates: Siglo III de la Hégira / IX d. C.
keywords: decoración figurativa; lana; tiraz; copto; punto de tapiz; textil; tapices.

fr.name: Cinq fragments textiles.
description:
Cinq fragments de tissu de forme circulaire, chacun décoré d'une représentation d'oiseau (canard ou oie) de différente taille et couleur, tissée selon un patron de trame discontinue, une technique de tapisserie. Ces fragments peuvent provenir de rideaux ou de courtepointes et faisaient sans doute partie d'un motif répétitif. Les tissus de Haute-égypte étaient réputés pour leur somptuosité, illustrée par ces fragments. Pendant la période toulounide (IIIe siècle H / IXe siècle J.-C.), Assiout, Akhnim et Fustat furent fameuses pour ce type de tissages.  
Les textiles toulounides se distinguent par la présence d'ombre dans les éléments décoratifs, aux couleurs allant du clair au foncé, et par leur puissance d'expression. Ils étaient également influencés par le style sassanide apporté d'Irak par Ahmad ibn Touloun (r. 254-270 H / 868-884 J.-C.). Pour l'égypte, cette phase de la production textile constitue une transition entre la période copte et la période islamique.  
L'essentiel du *jizya* (tribut) envoyé par Ahmad ibn Touloun à la cour des califes abbassides consistait en textiles fabriqués dans les *tiraz* (ateliers) sous brevet royal, qui produisaient de magnifiques tissus en laine et en lin. Ahmad ibn Touloun s'intéressait personnellement à ces fabriques égyptiennes répandues dans les régions du nord du delta, dont les villes de Tanis, Dabik, Damiette, fameuses pour leurs tissus de lin à inscriptions tissées en soie dans une multitude de couleurs. L'intérêt pour les textiles se développa en égypte sous le règne des fils d'Ibn Touloun, Khamaraweh (r. 270-282 H / 884-896 J.-C.) et Haroun (r. 283-292 H /896-905 J.-C.) qui aimaient retrouver leur nom dans des bandeaux épigraphiques intégrés au tissu lui-même.

Les textiles de coton et de lin étaient tissés dans différentes manufactures en Égypte : Alexandrie, Damiette, Farma, Bahnasa, Akhnim et Assiout. Les décorations de style copte restent très répandues pendant le Ier-IIIe siècle H (VIIe-IXe siècle J.-C.). Les fragments de tissu présentés ici sont remarquables pour l'effet d'ombre dans les éléments décoratifs, où la couleur est déclinée du clair au foncé.
holder: Musée du textile (un département du Musée d’art islamique du Caire)
dates: IIIe siècle de l’Hégire (IXe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Décoration figurative ; laine ; tiraz ; copte ; textiles ; tapisserie

ar.name: طبق.
description: طبق ذو حافة مفصصة تم تنفيذ الزخرفة عليه تحت التزجيج، وقد امتدت حتى حافة الطبق، وهي تمثل باقة من الأزهار تتضمن الخزامى الزرقاء التي تنمو على أغصان فيروزية، وأزهار بنفسجية تميل إلى الرمادي تشبه القرنفل تنمو من أغصان خضراء شائكة. تبدو الأزهار وكأنه قد تم توزيعها بشكل عشوائي إلا أن التشكيل منتظم تماماً، فالخزامى الكبيرة الزرقاء تتناوب حول إطار الطبق مع مجموعات تتألف من زهرة خزامى أصغر تتميز بإطار فيروزي شوكي الشكل محصورة بين زهرتين بنفسجيتين، ولا يختل هذا الإيقاع إلا في مكان وحيد هو الجانب الأيمن الأعلى حيث يحل شريط متموج مكان زهرة الخزامى. تتوازن أغصان الأزهار الطويلة في وسط الطبق بواسطة زهرات متوضعة بشكل مدروس. يمثل هذا النوع من التركيبات مرحلة انتقالية في زخرفة الخزف الإزنيقي عندما تراجعت النزعة نحو التركيبات المرتبة المؤلفة من أوراق مسننة وأزهار كبيرة لصالح تركيبات أكثر طبيعية وحرية.

صحن ذو حافة رفيعة، منحنية إلى الخارج قليلاً، مُزخرف برشَّات من التوليب الأزرق، وأزهار النباتات المثمرة، ذات اللون البنفسجي المائل للرمادي. يدلُّ هذا التصميم على مرحلة انتقالية في تصاميم فخار إزنيق، واستخدام التصاميم والمُكوِّنات التي تعطي شعوراً بالحرية والتفاعل مع الطبيعة.
keywords: زخرفة زهرية.

en.name: Dish.
description: A dish with a slightly foliated rim. The decoration, executed in underglaze painting, extends all the way to the edge of the bowl. It features a floral spray which includes blue tulips growing on turquoise stems and greyish-purple, carnation-like blossoms growing at the ends of spiky green stems. The flowers appear to be distributed at random, but in fact the composition is quite orderly: the large blue tulips alternate around the rim of the dish with groupings in which one smaller tulip (characterised by a fork-like turquoise 'frame') is sandwiched between two purple blossoms. The only place in which this rhythm is interrupted is at the upper right, where a lonely cloud-band takes the place of the expected tulip. The long stems of all these flowers are balanced out in the middle of the bowl by judiciously placed blossoms. This type of composition represents a transitional period in Iznik ceramic decoration, when a taste for elaborate compositions with long serrated leaves and large rosettes was giving way to a more free and naturalistic idiom.

A dish with a slightly foliated rim, decorated with a spray of blue tulips and greyish-purple blossoms. The composition represents a transitional period in Iznik ceramic decoration, when a taste for elaborate compositions was giving way to a more free and naturalistic idiom.

es.name: Plato
description:
Plato con borde. La decoración, pintada bajo vidriado, se extiende prácticamente hasta el borde. Consiste en un ramo de tulipanes azules con tallos color turquesa y morado grisáceo, y flores parecidas a claveles de tallos verdes con espinas. Aparentemente, las flores están repartidas aleatoriamente, pero en realidad la composición es metódica: en el borde, los grandes tulipanes azules se alternan con grupos de tres flores con un tulipán pequeño (su forma recuerda a un tenedor) en medio. Este ritmo compositivo sólo se interrumpe en la parte superior derecha, donde una nube en S ocupa el lugar donde debería ir otro tulipán. Destaca también el buen criterio a la hora de colocar las pequeñas flores que equilibran los largos tallos en la zona central de la composición.  
Este tipo de composición corresponde a un periodo de transición en la decoración de la cerámica de Iznik.

Plato con borde ligeramente y decorado con un ramo de tulipanes azules y capullos de color morado grisáceo. Esta composición representa un periodo de transición en la decoración de la cerámica de Iznik en el que los sofisticados diseños con largas hojas dentadas y grandes rosetas estaban dando  paso a un lenguaje más libre y naturalista.

fr.name: Plat.
description: Plat à bord légèrement chantourné. Le décor peint sous glaçure s'étend jusqu'au bord de l'aile. Il se compose d'un bouquet de tulipes bleues sur des tiges turquoise et de sortes d'œillets gris-violet, s'épanouissant à l'extrémité de tiges épineuses vertes. Les fleurs semblent réparties au hasard, mais la composition est en fait assez ordonnée : les grandes tulipes bleues alternent en bordure de l'aile avec des ensembles formés par une petite tulipe bleue (à calice en fourchette turquoise) prise entre deux fleurs violettes. Ce rythme est interrompu une seule fois en partie supérieure droite, où un petit ruban de nuages prend la place de la tulipe attendue. Les longues tiges s'équilibrent au centre grâce au judicieux emplacement des fleurs. Ce type de composition illustre une période de transition de la céramique d'Iznik, à un moment où le goût des compositions élaborées à longues feuilles dentelées et grandes rosettes laisse place à un langage plus libre et plus naturaliste.

Plat à bord légèrement chantourné orné d'un bouquet de tulipes bleues et de fleurs gris violet. La composition représente une période de transition dans la décoration de la céramique d'Iznik, lorsque le goût pour les compositions élaborées laisse place à un langage plus libre et plus naturaliste.

ar.name: مجموعة من أربع بلاطات من القاشاني.
description: مجموعة من أربع بلاطات من القاشاني المصنوع من عجينة كوارتزية بيضاء، والملون بالأزرق والزمردي والأحمر تحت طبقة من التزجيج مع سعف نخل كبيرة مشطورة وأزهار اللوتس. تكوَّن البلاطات الأربعة معاً تشكيلاً متناظراً من الأوراق والأزهار التي كانت جزءاً من مجموعة أكبر تغطي الجدران الداخلية لأحد المباني. وتشكل السعف المشطورة بنية هندسية محاطة بأزهار ملتفة أكثر نعومة وأوراق خضراء صغيرة، أما الأحمر الناري المتألق فهو مصنوع من مركبات الحديد اللزجة التي تم الحصول عليها من الطين الغني بالحديد في أرمينيا. لقد تم استعمال مركبات الحديد اللزجة في صناعة الخزف في إزنيق حوالي عام 956/ 1550، وقد تم وضعه على شكل طبقات كثيفة لمنعه من السيلان تحت طبقة التزجيج، وقد ظهرت تشكيلات زخرفية جديدة مع استعمال هذا اللون القوي تحت التزجيج جنباً إلى جنب مع الأوراق المعروفة باسم الساز الموجودة على القاشاني والأواني التي ظهرت في العقود السابقة، مثلت نباتات أكثر واقعية مثل الزهرة الياقوتية، والقرنفل، والخزامى، وأزهار اللوتس الكبيرة.

مجموعة فخارية، مكونة من أربعة بلاطات، مُزخرفة بأوراق الشجر، وأزهار البنفسج، والقرنفل، والتيوليب، واللوتس. تتميَّز باللون الأحمر المصقول، الذي أُنتج للصناعات الفخارية في إزنيق، عام 956 هـ/ 1550م، والذي أصبح شائعاً في إنتاج الأوعية والجرار الفخارية.

en.name: Group of four tiles.
description: A group of four stone-paste ceramic tiles painted in blue, emerald-green and red underglaze with large split-palmettes and lotus blossoms. The four tiles together create a symmetrical formation of leaves and flowers that would have been part of a larger group covering the interior of a building. Split-palmettes form a geometric structure surrounded by softer swirling flowers and small green leaves. The brilliant flame-red was created from iron-slip made from the iron-rich bole found in Armenia. Introduced to the ceramics industry in Iznik in about AH 956 / AD 1550, the iron-slip was applied thickly to prevent it from running under the glaze. New forms of decoration appear with this striking red underglaze; alongside the so-called *saz* leaf found in tiles and vessels from the previous decades, are more realistic plant forms such as hyacinths, carnations and tulips, as well as large lotus blossoms.

These tiles feature the distinctive *saz* leaf next to flowers such as hyacinths, carnations, tulips and lotus blossoms. The bright red glaze on these tiles was a colour introduced to the Iznik ceramic industry in about AH 956 / AD 1550 and became popular for both vessels and tiles.
type: Stone paste blue, red and turquoise painting
dates: Second half of hegira 10th / AD 16th century.
keywords: Geometric decoration; floral decoration; hyacinths; tilework
materials: Stone-paste ceramic with blue, emerald-green and red painting under the glaze.

es.name: Composición de cuatro azulejos
description: Grupo de cuatro azulejos en pasta de frita pintados en azul, verde esmeralda y rojo bajo vidriado y decorados con grandes medias palmetas y capullos de loto. Los cuatro azulejos unidos forman una composición simétrica de hojas y flores, y con otros similares revestirían la pared interior de un edificio. Las medias palmetas trazan un diseño geométrico rodeado de dinámicas flores y pequeñas hojas verdes. El color rojo fuego se consiguió con un engobe ferroso hecho a partir de bolo arménico, rico en hierro. Alrededor del año 956 / 1550, la industria cerámica de Iznik comienza a utilizar el engobe rojo, aplicando una gruesa capa para evitar que se corra con el vidriado. Este llamativo color trae nuevas formas de decoración: además de las conocidas hojas de *saz* de azulejos y vasijas de décadas anteriores, aparecen nuevas y más naturalistas formas vegetales, como jacintos, claveles, tulipanes y grandes capullos de loto.

Azulejos decorados con la característica hoja de *saz* en combinación con jacintos, claveles, tulipanes y capullos de loto. Alrededor del año 956 / 1550 comenzó a aplicarse en Iznik este color rojo brillante bajo vidriado, que fue haciéndose frecuente en recipientes y azulejos.
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo X de la Hégira / XVI d. C.

fr.name: Groupe de quatre carreaux.
description: Ensemble de quatre carreaux de céramique frittée peints en sous-glaçure bleu, vert émeraude et rouge à grandes demi-palmettes et fleurs de lotus. Les quatre carreaux créent une composition symétrique de feuilles et de fleurs qui a sans doute fait partie d'un ensemble plus vaste recouvrant l'intérieur d'un bâtiment. Les demi-palmettes constituent une structure géométrique entourée de fleurs et de petites feuilles vertes tourbillonnantes. Le rouge feu brillant était dû à une barbotine ferreuse fabriquée à partir d'une riche terre bolaire trouvée en Arménie. Introduite à Iznik vers 956 H / 1550 J.-C., cette barbotine était appliquée en épaisseur pour éviter qu'elle ne coule sous la glaçure. De nouveaux décors apparurent parallèlement à ce rouge surprenant. À la feuille *sfaz* des carreaux et récipients des décennies précédentes s'ajoutent des plantes naturalistes comme des hyacinthes, des œillets et des tulipes, ainsi que de grandes feuilles de lotus.

Ces carreaux font appel à la caractéristique feuille *saz* à côté de fleurs comme les yacinthes, les œillets, les tulipes et les boutons de lotus. La glaçure rouge et brillante qui couvre ces carreaux est due à une couleur introduite dans l'industrie céramique d'Iznik vers 956 H / 1550 J.-C. et qui s'est popularisée autant pour les récipients que pour le carrelage.
dates: Seconde moitié du Xe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIe siècle J.-C.).

en.name: Italian Company Breda Ernesto. Factory for Torpedoes and Navy Equipment, Milan. View of the Female Section of Lathes Division. Production of 75 mm Shrapnel Shells
names: Women working in a factory that produced military equipment, during World War I
Soc. Italiana Breda Ernesto. Stabilimento per siluri e lavori di marina, Milano. Veduta  del reparto femminile della torneria. Lavorazione degli shrapnels da 75 mm.
short_description:
Women working at lathes to make shrapnel shells in an Italian factory that produced torpedoes and other weapons. The war had an important impact on women’s work.  
As historian Perry Willson pointed out, during WWI “women rarely directly substituted for men, instead tending to move into new work roles produced by wartime expansion.”  
In Italy, the number of women who worked in factories producing weapons and ammunitions rose from 23,000 in 1915 to 198,000 in 1918. The numbers were far less than the women who participated in war production with more traditional “female roles”, such as making uniforms (400,000) or knitting woollen garments for the soldiers (200,000). However, Willson explained, women working in weapons’ factories had a relevance “as symbolic harbinger of change that greatly outweighed their actual numbers.”
partner: MIBACT | Central State Archives of Italy

Μοναδική διακόσμηση είναι η αραβική επιγραφή σε μαύρο χρώμα πάνω στο λευκό βάθος και το κεντρικό σχηματοποιημένο άνθος. Η κουφική ευχετική επιγραφή αναφέρει: «Ευλογία και χαρά στον ιδιοκτήτη». en.name: Bowl with inscription
description: A ceramic bowl covered with a white slip and transparent glaze. The sole decoration on a white background is an Arabic inscription in black and a stylized flower in the centre. The inscription is benedictory in the *kufic* script: “Blessings and joy to the owner”. The bowl belongs to a type of pottery typical of the Samanid workshops in eastern Iran. The characteristic inscriptions usually include proverbs or wishes, and the reader is invited to rotate the object to read them.

ar.name: أسطرلاب.
description:
أسطرلاب على شكل ساعة، يشتمل على سبع صفائح، واحدة منها مثبتة والباقي دوَّارة. تتصل الصفائح الست الدوارة بالصفيحة الثابتة بواسطة لولب مزخرف بوريدة. وقد حُفر على هذه الصفائح خطوط الطول ودوائر متحدة المركز ومصطلحات وأسماء خاصة بعلم الفلك والنجوم. كما وُضع في أعلى سطوح هذه الصفائح مؤشر ذو نهايات معقوفة يمكن استخدامها لتحديد مواقع 29 نجماً. وهذه بدورها يمكن أن تستخدم لقياس الزمن والمسافة.  
  
تشير المصادر التاريخية إلى أن الأسطرلاب قد اخترع على يد العالم الفلكي الإغريقي هيباركوس في القرن الثاني قبل الميلاد. وقد استخدم المسلمون في الأندلس والمغرب أكثر أنواع الأسطرلاب تطوراً.

الإسطرلابات أدوات فلكية، تُستخدم لقياس الزمن والمسافة. أقراصها تحمل دوائر مُتَّحدة المركز، وخطوط سَمْت، وعبارات فلكية، وأرقاماً. كانت الإسطرلابات الأكثر تطوّراً، وهي مبتكرة في القرن الثاني قبل الميلاد، مُستخدمة من قبل المسلمين في الأندلس والمغرب.

en.name: Astrolabe.
description:
The astrolabe is in the form of a clock face. Seven plates belong to it, one of them fixed and the others rotating. The six rotating plates are attached to the fixed one by a central screw decorated with a rosette. On top of the faces of these plates, which have meridians, concentric circles and astronomical and astrological terms and names engraved on them, is placed an indicator with hooked ends which can be used to determine the positions of 29 stars. These in turn can be used to measure time and distance.  
  
Historical sources indicate that the astrolabe was invented by the Greek astronomer Hipparchus in the second century BC. The most advanced types of astrolabe were used by the Muslims of al-Andalus and the Maghreb.

es.name: Astrolabio.
description:
El astrolabio tiene forma de esfera de reloj y está formado por siete placas, una de ellas fija y el resto giratorias. Las seis placas móviles están unidas a la placa fija por medio de un tornillo central decorado con una roseta. Las placas tienen grabados meridianos, círculos concéntricos, y términos y nombres astronómicos y astrológicos, y sobre ellas hay un indicador con puntas en gancho con el que se puede determinar la posición de 29 estrellas. También sirve para medir el tiempo y la distancia.  
Las fuentes históricas indican que el astrolabio fue inventado por el astrónomo griego Hiparco en el siglo II a. C. Los musulmanes de al-Andalus y el Magreb utilizaron los modelos más avanzados de astrolabios.

tr.name: Usturlap.
description:
Usturlap, saat kadranı formundadır. Biri sabit, altısı hareketli yedi plakadan meydana gelmiştir. Hareketli altı plaka, merkezde rozetli bir vida ile en alttaki yedinci plakaya tutturulmuştur. üzerlerinde meridyen, paralel daireleri ile astronomi ve astroloji ile ilgili terim ve isimler bulunan bu plakalar üzerine yerleştirilen, uçları kancalı bir gösterge çubuğu sayesinde 29 yıldızın yerleri tespit edilebilmekte ve bu yıldızlara göre de zaman ve uzaklık ölçülebilmektedir.  
  
Usturlabın eski Yunan Astronomu Hipparkhos (M.ö. 2. yy.) tararından keşfedildiğini yazan kaynaklar bulunmakla beraber, usturlabların en gelişmiş şekillerini Endülüs ve Magrib'de yaşayan Müslümanların kullandığı bilinmektedir.

Usturlap, zaman ve uzaklık ölçümünde kullanılan, üzerinde paralel, meridyen daireleri ile astrolojik terim ve rakamlar içeren astronomi ile ilgili araçlardandır. M.ö. 2. yüzyılda keşfedilen usturlabın en gelişmişlerinin Endülüs ve Mağrip'te yaşayan Müslümanlar tarafından kullanıldığı bilinmektedir.

en.name: Constitution of the Slav-Macedonian Scientific and Literary Society in Saint Petersburg
short_description: The Slav-Macedonian Scientific Literary Society was established in St. Petersburg on 16 December 1903, acting under the patronage of the St. Petersburg Slav Charitable Society. Its founders were Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) and Dimitija Chupovski, who worked actively on the recognition of Macedonian as distinct Slavic language and the opening of native-language schools for children in Macedonia. The Society, also known as the Macedonian Colony in St. Petersburg, gathered many distinguished Macedonian writers, poets and publicists. Its extensive scientific and literary activities have brought about explicit formulation of the Macedonian national program. The Society largely contributed to issuing a periodical publication in Macedonian and Russian language called “Makedonski Golos” (“Macedonian Voice"). It played an important role in the national awakening of Macedonians and bringing forth the issue of the Macedonian autonomy in the international community.

en.name: Vase
description: This vase is one of the most impressive examples of Mamluk glass in known existence. Made of blown cobalt blue glass, this pear-shaped vase — with a cylindrical neck flaring to a rounded thickened rim and resting on a low splayed foot — is entirely painted with polychrome enamel and gilt decoration consisting of horizontal registers of vegetal motifs, calligraphy, and birds. The elegant *naskhi* script encircling the neck translates as, “Glory to our Lord the King, the holy solider, the defender, Sultan of Islam and the Muslims, tamer of unbelievers, possessor of justice in the world”; with the verse around the middle of the body reading, “Glory to our lord the Sultan, the King, the learned, the doer, the holy soldier, the defender, the King, the learned, the just, the holy soldier, the defender, the pious, the victorious, trusting in God, the triumphant, Sultan of Islam, the doer, the just, the holy soldier, the defender, the pious, trusting in God, the triumphant, Sultan of Islam and the Muslims, tamer of unbelievers and polytheists, possessor of justice in the world.” These inscriptions carry the heroic and pious attributes of an unnamed sultan, a form of eulogistic titling commonly found on objects from early seventh century AH / thirteenth century AD Ayyubid Syria, and later continuing into the Mamluk period. Three exotic birds also decorate the vase, which reflect the influence of luxury central Asian textiles (Mongol in particular) arriving into Egypt in the mid-eighth century AH / mid-fourteenth century AD. The birds may also relate to the famous phoenix from the 572 AH / 1177 AD Persian literary work, *Conference of the Birds*, and represent symbols of immortality and hope. The precision and detail of the vase’s decoration suggest that it was made in an accomplished workshop in either Egypt or Syria, both established centres of enamelled glass making during the Mamluk period.

en.name: Hospital Real (Royal Hospital)
description:
The Catholic Monarchs founded the Hospital Real (Royal Hospital), intending to make the state responsible for problems of hygiene and public health. The Hospital was built outside the Islamic city on top what had been a Muslim cemetery. To find the architectonic model followed here we have to look beyond the Iberian Peninsula, namely to the Renaissance hospitals of Milan and Florence. The ground plan is a large square divided by a central cross that forms four interior patios. The cross was probably reserved for the wards and the exterior square for medical consultations, the pharmacy, storerooms, kitchens, and so on.  
In the interior elements from the Gothic tradition are found, such as the *cimborrio*, or rib vaulting of the lower floor of the cross, as well as Renaissance forms in the windows of the main façade, in the *Patio de los Marmoles* (Marble patio) and in the Chapel. Mudéjar craftsmanship can be seen in the wooden ceilings that cover wide spaces, whether as flat *alfarjes* on the ground floor or double pitch *armaduras* on the upper floor. The decoration of the staircases situated in the *Patio de los Marmoles* and the *Patio del Archivo* (Archive patio) is outstanding: it is known that artists of the category of Juan de Plasencia or Melchor de Arroyo took part in the decoration of them. While the formerly used designs were clearly Islamic in origin, the later decorative models were imports from Italy. We find this ambivalent language again in the cross on the upper floor, which is now the Central Library of the University of Granada. Here, carpenter Melchor de Arroyo explored the possibility of using geometric coffers in perspective to design a “half-orange” dome as a solution to the problem of the inside of the great *cimborrio*, making the Hospital Real stand out above the whole of the rest of the city. In 1552, Melchor de Arroyo’s solution for the roof was approved by Diego de Siloé, the architect of the Cathedral in Granada and renowned as an artist in Spain and Italy at the time.

es.name: Hospital Real
description:
El Hospital Real fue fundado por los Reyes Católicos con la intención de que el Estado se hiciera cargo de los problemas de higiene y sanidad públicas. El Hospital fue construido fuera de la ciudad islámica, sobre lo que había sido cementerio musulmán. El modelo arquitectónico que se siguió hay que buscarlo fuera de la Península Ibérica, en los hospitales renacentistas de Milán y Florencia. Su planta es un gran cuadrado dividido por una cruz central que define cuatro patios interiores. El crucero se reservó seguramente para salas de enfermos y el cuadrado exterior para consultas médicas, farmacia, almacenes, cocinas, etc.  
En el interior encontramos elementos de tradición gótica, como el *cimborrio* o la bóveda de nervios del crucero inferior, junto con formas renacentistas en las ventanas de la fachada principal y en los patios de los Mármoles y de la Capilla. Lo mudéjar se manifiesta en las techumbres lignarias que cubren los amplios espacios, ya sea mediante *alfarjes* planos en el piso bajo, ya como *armadura*s a dos aguas en el superior. Destacan por su importancia decorativa las cajas de las escaleras situadas en los patios de los Mármoles y del Archivo. En ellas intervinieron artistas de la categoría de Juan de Plasencia y Melchor de Arroyo. El primero diseñó soluciones de clara raigambre islámica y el segundo modelos decorativos venidos de Italia. Esta ambivalencia de lenguaje volvemos a encontrarla en el crucero del piso superior, actual biblioteca central de la Universidad de Granada, donde el carpintero Melchor de Arroyo exploró la posibilidad de situar artesones geométricos en perspectiva para ir dibujando una media naranja que resuelve interiormente el gran *cimborrio* que hace destacar el Hospital Real sobre el conjunto urbano.  
En 1552, la solución que Melchor de Arroyo dio a la techumbre fue aprobada por Diego de Siloé, arquitecto de la catedral de Granada y artista reconocido en la España y la Italia de entonces.

en.name: *The bas-reliefs of Trajan's Column, reproduced in electroplating and exhibited in a room of the new Louvre*
names: Taken from the collection *Topographie de Paris*, "1er arrondissement, 1er quartier, Le Louvre"
short_description: Trajan's Column, erected in Rome, is famous for its exceptional bas-reliefs commemorating the victory of the Emperor over the Dacians. In 1861, with the aim of making it known to the French public, Napoléon III had the column moulded and a replica installed in Paris. This was achieved thanks to the new electroplating technique, and the copy was placed in the Musée du Louvre. However, in 1870 the column was judged too large, and was sent to the Château de Saint-Germain, where it was quickly installed in the moat. In this image shows visitors at the Louvre, examining the story reproduced by Trajan's Column.
keywords: Roman antiquities; Musée du Louvre

fr.name: *Les bas-reliefs de la colonne Trajane, reproduits par la galvanoplastie, exposés dans une des salles du nouveau Louvre*
names: Extrait du Recueil. Topographie de Paris. Ier arrondissement. 1er quartier. Le Louvre
short_description: La colonne de Trajan, érigée à Rome, est exceptionnelle pour son bas-relief qui commémore la victoire de l’empereur sur les Daces. Désireux de la faire connaître aux Français, l’empereur Napoléon III la fait mouler en 1861 pour en installer une réplique dans Paris. La reproduction, grâce à la nouvelle technique de la galvanoplastie, prend place au musée du Louvre. Jugée trop encombrante, elle est envoyée en 1870 au château de Saint-Germain où on l’installe bientôt dans les fossés. L’image montre les visiteurs du Louvre pouvant contempler les uns après les autres les tronçons reproduits de la colonne Trajane.
keywords: Antiquités romaines; musée du Louvre

en.name: 'A Giant Fish Rescues Abu Ubayda and his Men from Dying of Starvation'
description:
The style of the miniatures from this manuscript is slightly old-fashioned compared with the otherwise refined Timurid painting, and it has in fact been called Shah Rukh’s historical style. Its inspiration was undoubtedly the illustrations made about a century earlier for Rashid al-Din’s famous ‘History of the World.’  
  
The rescue of the close companion of the Prophet, Abu Ubayda, from starvation is one of Islam’s early miracles. His desperate men have eaten the leaves from the trees and although they do not look quite as emaciated as the two dromedaries lying on the ground, the yellow desert underlines the gravity of the situation. When a giant fish appears, the Muslims are saved from dying of starvation.
keywords: Water; folio; miniature; manuscript; Herat; Timurids

en.name: Convent and Church of Santa Clara
description:
"Construction of the 15th-century Convent of Santa Clara in Funchal, founded by João Gonçalves da Câmara, was started in 1492, and it was only five years later that the first nuns arrived from Setúbal to take up residence. The complex was built round an earlier, smaller chapel, with a Gothic portal that is still used as an entrance today.  
The exceptional but simple Gothic cloister, with pointed arches remains and, inside, the significantly modified church contains the Flamboyant Gothic tomb of Martim Mendes de Vasconcelos, the son-in-law of João Goncalves Zarco.  
A series of *azulejos* almost completely covers the floors of the upper and lower choirs, a total of almost 4,000 *cuenca tiles* covering some 90 sq. m., with eight different geometrical patterns and two with phytomorphic elements. The body of the tiles is covered with lead glaze to produce different shades of green. A panel like a square carpet, or medallion made up of 100 tiles in the same colours, was placed in the centre of the upper choir. *Mudejar* taste was also a feature of the tracery decoration of the ceiling, which is clearly suggested by some of the oldest vestiges.  
The lower choir was considerably remodelled in later periods, mainly in the mid-18th century, but the *Mudejar* flooring was maintained and has recently been uncovered and restored. This unique ensemble is an expression of refined taste, economic capacity and knowledge of how to adapt the best materials to everyday use."

en.name: Cup with Handle
description: With its squat globular body on a disk-like base and a high, flaring neck nearly as tall as its body, this object shares key features with a small group of vessels. Such vessels have been called drinking cups or pouring jars because their shape differs from typical Islamic ewers or pitchers with globular bodies and cylindrical necks. Some related examples are plain or have moulded decoration, while others—like this piece—have wheel-cut designs in a linear style. All seem to have been produced in the Iranian region. Apart from the typical grayish colourless glass and the decoration, a strong argument for an Iranian origin is the fact that two vessels of this shape have been excavated from a tomb in Inner Mongolia with finds dated to 1018.

en.name: *Flight of the French army and retreat of the Duke of Alençon across the Ticino*
description:
The famous series of seven Flemish tapestries depicting the Battle of Pavia, which are displayed in a large room in the Museum of Capodimonte, entered the public collections as part of the 1862 bequest of Alfonso d’Avalos, who donated his family’s collection to the National Museum of Naples.  
Produced to be given to Emperor Charles V by the Estates-General of Brussels, on the occasion of the latter’s meeting in Brussels in 1531, the decorative series of tapestries was designed to celebrate the victory of the imperial troops over those of the French, under the command of Francis I. This victory, which occurred on 24 February 1525, was fought in the environs of the Visconti Park, at the gates of Pavia.  
Woven in Brussels, the tapestries were produced using designs by Bernard van Orley (now in the Louvre in Paris) in the workshop of William Dermoyen (or Van der Moyen), identified thanks to the presence of a weaver’s mark on the right-hand border of the tapestry; the mark can also be found on another example in the series. The presence of the weaver’s mark has also allowed the years in which the series was produced to be established: after 1528, the year in which a decree required tapestry workers to “sign” their products, and by the start of 1531, given that the tapestries would be presented to the Emperor in the March of that year.  
Recently, an interpretation of the entire cycle has been proposed that aims to recreate sequentially the landscape depicted in the seven tapestries as a single, panoramic, overview (Paredes 2014). According to this perspective, the tapestry examined here, placed in the sequence suggested by Paredes, constitutes the last in the series and should be read in close continuity with the subject represented in the tapestry that precedes it, *Flight of the besieged and retreat of the Swiss who drown in great numbers in the Ticino*. In particular, from the juxtaposition of the two tapestries, the landscape south of Pavia can be recreated, distinguished by the presence of the small island of Gravellone, separated from the city by the waters of the Ticino. The tapestry represents one of the final moments of the battle, with a portrait of the Duke of Alençon – identified by the writing on the caparison of his horse – who, after having crossed the bridge of boats on the Ticino, orders its destruction to prevent the enemy from following. In the foreground, a few infantrymen are depicted, busy destroying the bridge, while a horseman and other soldiers are the last to cross it. The action of the Duke of Alençon, brother-in-law of the King of France, condemns all those who do not manage to cross the bridge to the wrath of the enemy or to the swirling waters of the river. In the distance, one can glimpse a herd of cows grazing serenely, indifferent to the war, in the rural landscape.
artist: William Dermoyen atelier on a cartoon designed by Bernard van Orley
keywords: Flemish tapestries; Battle of Pavia; National Archaeological Museum; Alfonso d’Avalos; Francesco Fernando d’Avalos; Fernando Francesco d’Avalos; Francis I; Visconti Park; Bernard van Orley; Willem Dermoyen; Carlo V; atelier; frames; preparatory cartoons; drawings

it.name: Fuga dell'esercito francese e ritirata del duca d'Alençon oltre il Ticino
description:
La celebre serie dei sette arazzi fiamminghi della Battaglia di Pavia, esposti in una grande sala del museo di Capodimonte, entra nelle raccolte museali con il legato testamentario del 1862 di Alfonso d’Avalos che dona al Museo Nazionale di Napoli la collezione di famiglia.  
Attraverso il ciclo decorativo si intendeva celebrare la vittoria delle truppe imperiali su quelle francesi, comandate da Francesco I, avvenuta il 24 febbraio del 1525, e combattuta nella zona del Parco Visconteo, alle porte di Pavia.  
Realizzata per essere donata dagli stati Generali di Bruxelles all’imperatore Carlo V, in occasione della riunione degli stessi a Bruxelles nel 1531, la serie decorativa intendeva celebrare la vittoria delle truppe imperiali su quelle francesi, comandate da Francesco I, avvenuta il 24 febbraio del 1525, e combattuta nella zona del Parco Visconteo, alle porte di Pavia.  
Tessuti a Bruxelles, gli arazzi sono stati realizzati su disegni di Bernard van Orley (oggi a Parigi, Musée du Louvre), nell'atelier di William Dermoyen (o Van der Moyen), identificato grazie alla presenza del marchio del tessitore presente sulla bordure destra del panno, riscontrata anche in un altro esemplare della serie. La presenza del marchio del tessitore ha permesso anche di stabilire gli anni di realizzazione della serie: dopo il 1528, anno in cui un editto imponeva agli arazzieri di firmare i loro prodotti, e l'inizio del 1531, dato che verrà donata nel mese di marzo all'imperatore.  
Recentemente è stata proposta una lettura d’insieme del ciclo, tesa a ricostruire il paesaggio rappresentato nei sette arazzi in un’unica, e panoramica, visione d’insieme (Paredes 2014). Secondo questa prospettiva, l'arazzo in esame, disposto nella sequenza suggerita dalla studiosa, costituisce l'ultimo della serie e va letto in strettissima continuità con quanto raffigurato nel panno che lo precede, *Sortita degli assediati e rotta degli svizzeri che annegano in gran numero nel Ticino*. In particolare, dall'accostamento dei due arazzi, si ricompone il paesaggio a sud di Pavia, caratterizzato dalla presenza dell'isolotto del Gravellone, separato dalla città dalle acque del Ticino. Nel panno è raffigurato uno degli ultimi momenti della battaglia con la ritirata del duca di Alençon - identificato dalla scritta sulla gualdrappa del cavallo -, che dopo aver attraversato il ponte di barche sul Ticino, ordina di distruggerlo per impedire l’inseguimento dei nemici. In primo piano, sono raffigurati alcuni fanti impegnati nella distruzione del ponte, mentre un cavaliere e altri soldati lo attraversano per ultimi. Il gesto del duca d'Alençon, cognato del re di Francia, condanna tutti coloro che non riescono ad oltrepassare il ponte alla furia del nemico o alle acque vorticose del fiume. In lontananza si intravede una mandria che pascola tranquillamente, indifferente alla guerra, nel paesaggio campestre.
holder: Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte
artist: Atelier di William Dermoyen su disegni di Bernard van Orley
materials: Lana, seta, cotone colorato con fili d'oro e d'argento
tags: Lana, seta, cotone colorato con fili d'oro e d'argento

en.name: Çırağan Palace
short_description: Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. In 1857 he opened his first photography studio in Istanbul. Çırağan Palace, built by Sultan Abdülâziz, was designed by the palace architect Nigoğayos Balyan and constructed by his sons Sarkis and Hagop Balyan between 1863 and 1867. This was a period in which all Ottoman sultans used to build their own palaces rather than using those of their ancestors. Çırağan Palace is the last example of this period. The inner walls and the roof were made of wood, the outer walls of colourful marble. The palace is connected with a beautiful marble bridge to the Yıldız Palace on the hill behind. A very high garden wall protects the palace from the outer world.
keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Pascal Sebah

en.name: Omar Pasha (1806–1871)
short_description: Portrait of Omar Pasha. He was born in Croatia in 1806 near the Turkish-Hungarian border. In 1828 he deserted from the Austrian army and joined the Ottoman administration in Bosnia. After a long career in the Ottoman army, he became the military governor of Bucharest and commanded the Ottoman forces at the siege of Sevastopol in Crimea. In 1862 he suppressed an uprising in Herzogovina and led a victorious campaign against Montenegro. In 1868 he became War Minister and died in 1871 in Istanbul.
keywords: Omar Pasha; Croatia; Bosnia; Ottoman empire; Herzegovina

en.name: Wooden Qur’an Stand
short_description: Items like this Qur’an stand were popular props in Orientalist painting. On the inside, this hard wood Qur’an stand, which is inlaid with ebony, bone and mother-of-pearl, is decorated with two large square geometric panels, surrounded by a wide zig-zag border. The two squares are in turn subdivided into four small squares, filled with abstract star motifs. On the underside, the stand has two large geometric roundels. Two narrow, rectangular mashrabiyyah panels occupy the upper part of the feet. The remaining surfaces surrounding them are filled with chequerboard designs.
type: Hardwood Qur'an Stand with bone and mother-of-pearl inlay
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century

en.name: *The Aqueduct in the Forest of Belgrade, Istanbul*
short_description: This painting by an anonymous Ottoman artist shows the aqueduct of Belgrade Forest outside Istanbul. Istanbul’s water was stored in the reservoirs of Belgrade Forest and conveyed to the city across a number of aqueducts like this one. Established in early Ottoman times, the Istanbul water supply system was expanded and improved throughout the Ottoman period, incorporating complex systems of reservoirs, aqueducts and supply pipes endling in fountains and waterspouts.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department

en.name: Bottle
description:
The absence of decoration on this bottle suggests that it belongs to the large group of utilitarian vessels which were made for everyday use in glass workshops throughout the Islamic world. Fragments of such vessels found during archaeological excavations tell us that they were blown in great quantities and in very different shapes and sizes. However, because very few vessels like this one actually survived, little is known about this group. Several features point to its origins in Egypt: its colourless glass with a greenish tinge; its short, rounded mouth; its rim that folds inwards; and the fact that this bottle has obviously been buried in a dry climate which has hardly destroyed its surface. It is thus very likely that it was blown in Egypt during the period of the Fatimid caliphs (909–1171), a time when many varieties of glass vessels were produced.  
A bottle with a related thick rounded mouth is said to be in the Museum of Islamic Art in Cairo. For a utilitarian bottle from 17th-century Iran with a rim that folds inward.
materials: Glass, colourless, greenish tinge; free-blown, tooled, worked on the pontil

en.name: Cadillac Series 75
description:
Known for its luxurious and powerful vehicles, Cadillac produced several cars equipped with large V8 engines between the 1930s and the 1980s. Of those models, the Series 75 is the best known. Differing in size and bodywork as well as the level of trim, the Series 75 models were most popular among Cadillac’s affluent clientele. In the post-war period, they were the most prestigious automobiles in the United States of America, and it is not surprising that in 1947, the firm produced 59,436 units.  
  
That same year, the Portuguese government sanctioned the purchase of two identical Cadillac Series 75s, one for the President of the Republic – Óscar Carmona – and the other for the President of the Council of Ministers – Prof. António de Oliveira Salazar. Before that, all official vehicles were standardised on make and models. All ministers had Packard Clipper cars, with eight cylinders and seven seats, while the secretaries and under secretaries of states drove cars were of the same brand, but with five seats.  
  
Salazar always used his allocated Cadillac until his death in 1970, even refusing a Mercedes-Benz 600 acquired by the Ministry of Finance in 1968—a car now under the Presidency of the Republic. He claimed that the Cadillac was still in good condition and served him very well in his official capacity.  
  
In April 1971, less than a year after Salazar’s death, the Cadillac Series 75 was sold at auction and was then acquired by João de Lacerda to be exhibited at the Museu do Caramulo. Interestingly, the interior of the model remains in perfect condition, having been protected with seat covers by order of Salazar himself.

en.name: Book of the Sea
description: The multimedia artist Anne Petters, has a growing reputation for creating technically innovative and creatively complex works in glass that reflect her interest in controlling and displaying moments of our fleeting, vulnerable existence. Her work ‘Book of the Sea’ is influenced by the history of Caithness in the far North of Scotland, and its coastal communities which grew and fell with the Herring trade.  The text glimpsed on the pages is composed in a variety of languages, written in reverse—a product of Petters’ process—often illegible, the words or phrases are symbols, for her perspective of the stories we create about a place. Anne utilises a specific kiln casting and pate de verre glass technique that she developed herself, pushing the boundaries of traditional craft processes to create sculptures that have a unique physicality and aesthetic, giving life to the pages as if they have been caught by a breeze.
keywords: Contemporary Glass; Studio Glass; Art Glass

ar.name: حصن ماتزالاكار.
description:
هذا البناء عبارة عن أطلال؛ يبدو أنه كان يحتوي على سور شبه مربع وفي زواياه أبراج أسطوانية الشكل مسقوفة بقبب نصف كروية غير مرئية بشكل واضح من الخارج. ما يزال جزء من هذا البناء، من سور الحصن، محافظاً على شكله الأصلي الذي كان مستطيل الشكل قبل أن تغمره المياه وتزيل معالمه، وكان قد شيِّد فوق هضبة.  
الأخبار التي تتحدث عن استعمال هذا البناء غير دقيقة؛ فقد قيل إنه حصن يحمي مدينة سامبوكا، ويؤكد هذا القول كتابات المؤرخ الإدريسي، ورجح بعض الباحثين استعماله خانات للقوافل بسبب سعة قاعاته وضعف أسواره، وآخرون قالوا إنه مركز متقدم لمراقبة الطريق بين باليرمو وشاكا.

المعلومات التي تخص وظيفة هذه البناية غامضة، وتم التعرف عليها كقلعة خاصة بضواحي سامبوكا التي يشير إليها الإدريسي. وبالنظر إلى ضيق الفضاءات المتبقية والمتانة الضعيفة للجدران، فإن بعض الباحثين يظنون أن الأمر يتعلق بمركز متقدم بسيط؛ بينما يرى فيه آخرون خاناً نظرا لموضعه بالقرب من الطريق التي تربط باليرمو وسياكا.
keywords: عمارة عسكرية.
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

en.name: Fortress of Mazzallaccar.
description:
The building, now in ruins, is an approximately square enclosure with cylindrical corner towers, each with a domed ceiling invisible from the outside. The only building within the fortress walls is a rectangular structure in a state of partial ruin. Before the valley was flooded artificially, the fortress was entirely visible and appeared higher up.  
The purpose of the building, identified as the fortress near Sambuco referred to by al-Idrisi, is uncertain. The limited space in the surviving rooms and the relative weakness of the walls have led some academics to suggest that it was used simply as an outpost, and others that is was a caravanserai, given its proximity to the Palermo–Sciacca road.

The intended use of this building, identified as the fortress outside Sambuca referred to by al-Idrisi, is unclear. es.name: Fortaleza de Mazzallaccar.
description:
La fortaleza, actualmente en estado de ruina, presenta una planta casi cuadrada provista de torres cilíndricas en sus esquinas, cubiertas por cúpulas hemisféricas no visibles desde fuera. El único volumen parcialmente conservado es un cuerpo rectangular del interior de la fortaleza. La construcción era totalmente visible y aparecía en posición más elevada antes de que se anegara artificialmente el valle.  
Son inciertas las noticias sobre el uso de este edificio, al que se refiere al-Idrisi como una fortaleza de las cercanías de Sambuca. El tamaño tan reducido de las habitaciones que aún se conservan, junto con la escasa solidez de los muros, ha llevado a algunos investigadores a proponer que su función fuese la de simple puesto avanzado, mientras que otros, dada su proximidad a la carretera que unía Palermo con Sciacca, se decantan por que fuera un caravasar.

No existe acuerdo sobre cuál sería el uso de este edificio, identificado como la fortaleza en las cercanías de Sambuca a la que se refiere al-Idrisi. Algunos investigadores, considerando lo exiguo de los lugares de vivienda conservados y la dudosa robustez de los muros, le atribuyen una función de simple puesto avanzado, mientras que otros lo consideran un caravasar, dado su estratégico emplazamiento en la vía comercial que unía Palermo con Sciacca.
keywords: arquitectura militar
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

fr.name: Forteresse de Mazzallaccar.
description:
L'édifice, à l'état de ruine, présente une enceinte à peu près carrée, munie de tours angulaires cylindriques coiffées de coupoles hémisphériques, non visibles de l'extérieur. Le seul volume architectural partiellement conservé à l'intérieur de l'enceinte de la forteresse est un corps de bâtiment rectangulaire. Avant que la vallée ne soit inondée artificiellement, la construction était entièrement visible et apparaissait en position plus élevée.  
  
On ignore la destination de cet édifice, identifié comme étant la forteresse des environs de Sambuca, dont parle al-Idrisi. Certains chercheurs, compte tenu de l'exiguïté des salles subsistantes et de la fragilité de la maçonnerie, supposent qu'il devait s'agir d'un simple avant-poste ; d'autres, du fait de sa position sur la route reliant Palerme à Sciacca, y voient un caravansérail.

Les informations concernant la fonction de cet édifice sont incertaines. Il a été identifié comme étant la forteresse des environs de Sambuca à laquelle al-Idrisi fait référence. Certains chercheurs, compte tenu de l'exiguïté des espaces subsistants et du peu de robustesse des murs, pensent qu'il s'agissait d'un simple avant-poste, d'autres d'un caravansérail, vu sa position, près de la route reliant Palerme et Sciacca.
keywords: architecture militaire
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

it.name: Fortezza di Mazzallaccar.
description: L'edificio, in stato di rovina, presenta una recinzione pressoché quadrata, munita di torri angolari cilindriche coperte da cupole emisferiche, non visibili esternamente. Unico volume edilizio, in parte conservatosi all'interno del recinto della fortezza, è un corpo di fabbrica rettangolare. Prima che fosse allagata artificialmente la valle la costruzione era interamente visibile ed appariva in posizione più elevata. Incerte sono le notizie sull'uso di questo edificio, identificato come la fortezza nei pressi di Sambuca della quale riferisce Al-Idrîsî. Alcuni studiosi, per l'esiguità dello spazio degli ambienti superstiti e per la scarsa robustezza della muratura, ne ipotizzano un uso di semplice avamposto, altri di caravanserraglio, dal momento che sorgeva presso la strada che congiungeva Palermo a Sciacca.

names: Etienne 8mm (solid frame, 9-chamber cylinder, ejector, grip silver plates, checking, barrel)
description: The Lebel Revolver was the standard issue sidearm in the French military during the First World War, produced in Saint Etienne and used by the French army between 1892 and before 1924. The 1892 Model is a double/single action, six round cylinder revolver that fires 8-millimetre rounds. It was issued to officers in the French Army, Navy, and National Gendarmerie, amongst others. It is commonly called the Lebel Revolver after the gun designer Colonel Nicolas Lebel. For loading and releasing the empty cases, the chambers are accessed through swinging the cylinder to the right. Originally chambered for an 8mm gunpowder cartridge round, later models issued during World War I and thereafter fired the same 8mm cartridge loaded with smokeless powder. Serial number 21093.
holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities

de.name: Holzlöffel
description: In der Ambraser Kunstkammer befanden sich mehrere osmanische Holzlöffel. Da es einen derartigen Löffel bereits 1596 auch in der Münchner Kunstkammer gab, dürften die Ambraser Exemplare, trotz ihrer späteren inventarischen Nennung, gleichfalls in das 16. Jahrhundert zu datieren sein.  Die Löffel zeigen  florale Motive, wie Tulpen Nelken und Hyazinthen in Goldmalerei. Die Rückseiten und teilweise auch der Stiel sind mit Wellenbändern oder schlangenartig gebogenen Wolkenbändern geschmückt.

en.name: Ottoman wooden spoons
description: The Kunstkammer at Ambras contains a number of wooden Ottoman spoons. One such spoon is recorded in the Kunstkammer at Munich as early as AD 1596, suggesting that the ones at Ambras also date from the 16th century, despite only being listed on a later inventory. The spoons feature floral motifs such as tulips, carnations and hyacinths in gold paint. Their backs and part of the handles are decorated with wave-band motifs.
dates: Hegira second half of the 10th century / AD 2nd half of the 16th century
keywords: Domestic vessels; kitchenware; floral motifs; floral decoration; stripes; hyacinths; Ottoman empire; spoons

en.name: Roman Catholic Parish Church and Monastery of St. Ignatius of Loyola
names: Jesuit Church and Monastery of Győr
description:
According to certain experts, the layout and architectural character of the Jesuit Church in Győr – besides the Italian patterns of Jesuit church architecture and the first church of the Order in Hungary in Nagyszombat (Trnava) – was influenced by the Jesuit Church in Vienna. Its layout (a nave with three adjoining closed chapels on both sides) later became an emblematic element in Hungarian Jesuit church architecture. On the side walls of the nave topped by a barrel vault, there is a tabernacle. The sanctuary has a rectangular end, and is the same width as the nave.  
Besides traditional Jesuit iconography, specific features of Hungarian iconography from the period can also be seen relating to the Ottoman wars and the closely related theme of the *Regnum Marianum/Patrona Hungariae* (St. Stephen offering the country to the Virgin Mary). All the saints, kings and bishops lined up on the decorative programme were founders and supporters of the Catholic Hungarian Kingdom, and defenders against the infidels or non-believers (images of Turks and Protestants appear on the altars).  
The Tyrolean painter, Paul Troger, painted the main altarpiece (*Apotheosis of St. Ignatius*) and also the ceiling mural in the sanctuary (*Ascension of St. Ignatius*) in 1744; the ceiling of the nave (*Annunciation*) in 1747 and the murals of the vault pendentives of four Prophets and four Evangelists (dated with Troger's signature beneath *St. Luke the Evangelist*) in 1744. The *trompe-l'œil* architectural wall painting and the ceiling of the sanctuary are by Gaetano Fanti.    
The main façade, completed by Martin (Athanasius) Wittwer a Carmelite architect around 1726, is articulated by statues in niches (St. John of Nepomuk, St. John the Evangelist, St. Andrew, St. Francis Borgia, the Virgin Mary and St. Ignatius of Loyola), by windows and volutes, two towers and the main stone gate (1641).  
Between 1743 and 1744, János Götzelmayer from Győr created the main altarpiece adorned by two columns and sculptures representing St. Peter, St. Joseph, St. John of Nepomuk and St. Paul (made by Josef Rössler \[Ressler\]) and the coat of arms of the patron, Prebendary Ádám Acsády.   
Acsády's coat of arms also appears on the triumphal arch. János Burghar(d)t from Győrsziget made the organ (1755–1757) and Mihály János Crines from Győr made the altar cross (c. 1710). The embossed pulpit was donated by Bishop Márton Padányi Bíró and made by Lajos Gode, a disciple of G. R. Donner, in 1748–1749.  József Ullydeszki made the *ciborium* in the mid-1780s. The furniture is by local craftsmen. Both the monastery refectory and the former Jesuit apothecary are decorated with stuccoes.

The Jesuit Order settled in Győr in 1627 and played an important role in the Catholic spiritual renaissance (rooted in the Counter-Reformation movement) and the spread of Baroque art in Hungary. Building of the Jesuit Church dedicated to St. Ignatius of Loyola began in 1634/1635. The church was consecrated in 1641, but the interior decoration was not complete until the mid-18th century.
artist: György Szelepcsényi, Archbishop of Esztergom (1595–1685); Ádám Acsády (1680–1744), Prebendary in Győr between 1713–1736 and Roman Catholic Bishop as of 1726; Márton Padányi Bíró (1696–1762) Bishop of Veszprém

Architectural plan: Baccio del Bianco (1604–1656?); construction: Bartolomeo Torre; organ: Gáspár János Burghar(d)t; altar cross: Mihály János Crines; pulpit: Lajos Gode (active 1741–1759); main altar: János Götzelmayer; painters: Paul Troger (1698–1762), Gaetano Fanti; *ciborium*: József Ullydeszki; sculptors: Martin (Athanasius) Wittwer (1667–1732), Josef Rössler (Ressler) (1700–1772)
history:
The Episcopate of Győr, founded by King Stephen I, flourished until the Turkish occupation of Hungary diminished its prosperity. Győr, where the bishop resided, was only under Turkish rule for a short period, but the army of Suleiman the Magnificent ravaged the Episcopate on its way to and from Vienna (1529; 1532). Following liberation from Turkish rule, the city, an important link in the chain of Hungarian strongholds, was unable to return to normalcy as its infrastructure was in a state of decay. During this period, the bishop resided in Győr for short periods only.  
Apart from nurturing and supporting the spiritual life of Catholics, the renaissance of Catholicism in the 17th century also fostered the reconstruction of the city's infrastructure. The Jesuit order settled in Győr in 1627 establishing the church (dedicated to the founder, St. Ignatius of Loyola), monastery and school. The Jesuits played a central role in the infrastructural restoration of Győr, as well as the spiritual, cultural and scientific life of the city, until the order was dissolved in 1733.  
The financial difficulties that beset the Jesuits meant that the construction and interior decoration of the church was largely financed by patrons, among which, Archbishop György Szelepcsényi, Prebendary Ádám Acsády, Bishop of Győr, other members of the chapter and the families of children that attended the Jesuit school.  
Scholars tend to attribute the plans of the church to an Italian master, Baccio del Bianco. The construction was supervised by the Italian Bartolomeo Torre (from 1634/1635 to 1641). After the church was consecrated in 1641, local benefactors helped to install the first altars in 1642. The second era of construction extended into the 18th century: the main altar, ceiling murals of the bay, the sanctuary, general interior decoration and decoration of the towers of the main façade. The nave took on its current form after reconstruction of the church in 1738.  
After the Jesuit order was dissolved in 1733, the Benedictines obtained the building complex in 1802. Today the church is a Roman Catholic parish church. In place of the former Jesuit school stands a Benedictine high school built in 1888. The former Jesuit pharmacy houses an Apothecary Museum.

en.name: Portrait of Abraham Salamon De Camondo
short_description: The Camondo Family is a family of Spanish-Portuguese Jewish origin. Abraham Salomon Camondo, who was born in İstanbul in 1781, acted as the Ottoman government's banker before the establishment of the Ottoman Bank. He founded a bank called "*Isaac et Compagnie Camondo*" with his brother Isaac in 1815. The bank grew in a short time period into a reputable international financial institution. Camondo prospered greatly and became the prime banker to the Ottoman Empire until the founding of the Imperial Ottoman Bank in 1863. The bank had a close relationship with the business community and banks of London, Paris and the Vienna Stock Exchange. The bank had also funded defence needs of Ottoman Empire during the Crimean War.
holder: The Quincentennial Foundation Museum, Zulfaris Synagogue Museum
partner: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (General Directorate for Cultural Heritage and Museums)

en.name: Cup and a stand
short_description: Dimitrija Chupovski (1878-1940) was a distinguished Macedonian intellectual who lived and worked in Russia. Being the President of the Slav-Macedonian Scientific Literary Society in St. Petersburg, he contributed to the publishing of historical memorandums and other official acts that presented the national ideology and objectives for unity and liberation of Macedonia. He also published numerous articles drawing attention to the partitioning of Macedonia after the Balkan Wars. In his struggle for preserving the integrity of Macedonia he wrote various memoranda to governments of western countries on many occasions.
keywords: Political and diplomatic engagement; cup; stand; metalwork; domestic vessels

ar.name: مصباح مسجد.
description:
مصباح مسجد مُعد للتعليق، له جسم منفوخ وعنق طويلة تتسع باتجاه الأعلى. يشتمل على ست حلقات لتعليقه بواسطة سلاسل. تمت صباغته من الداخل بالأخضر، أما سطحه الخارجي فمزخرف بتشكيلات من الألوان الأزرق الداكن والأبيض والأحمر والتذهيب تشكِّل أشرطة كتابية منقوشة ورسوم زهرية وهندسية. وبما أن الزخارف مطلية بالمينا، فإن مظهرها البارز يضفي على جسم المصباح إحساساً بالعمق.  
  
تنتشر على جسم المصباح زخرفة زهرية لرصائع مع دلايات باللونين الأحمر والأبيض، في حين يحيط بالعنق حواشٍ من الأرابسك وآيات قرآنية من سورة النور (رقم 24). كما يوجد في وسط الأشرطة الكتابية رصائع دائرية الشكل يظهر داخلها عصوا بولو ملونان بالأبيض فوق أرضية زرقاء داكنة، وهذا تشكيل مميز في العهد المملوكي.
كانت المصابيح الزجاجية المُعلَّقة تُنتج لإضاءة الأمكنة المقدَّسة، كما كانت رموزاً سماوية للنور. ومصابيح الفترة المملوكية الزجاجية، مُزينة بشعارات الحكّام التي تجسِّد قوة الدولة، وسطوتها.
keywords: زجاج؛ مصباح مسجد.

en.name: Mosque lamp.
description:
A hanging mosque lamp, with a fat body and a long neck, that widens towards the top. Six loops are attached for hanging up the lamp from chains. The entire surface of the lamp's body, which is painted green on the inside, is decorated with compositions in dark-blue, white, red, and gilding which form inscription bands and geometric and floral designs. Since the decoration is enamelled, its raised appearance gives the lamp's body a sense of depth.  
  
The body features floral decoration in red and white medallions with pendants, while the neck has a border of arabesques and bears verses from the 'Light' chapter of the Qur'an (*sura* 24). Amid the inscription bands are round medallions showing polo sticks depicted in white on a dark-blue ground, a characteristic motif of the Mamluk period.

Hanging glass lamps were produced for lighting the holy areas and they were a divine symbol of the light. The glass lamps of the Mamluk period are decorated with the blazons of the rulers, which symbolise the power of the state.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
dates: first half of hegira 8th century / AD 14th century.
keywords: Glass; mosque lamp; Mosque interior decoration

es.name: Lámpara de mezquita.
description:
Lámpara colgante de mezquita con cuerpo voluminoso y cuello largo que va ensanchándose hacia la boca. Tiene seis agarraderas para colgarla de cadenas. La superficie externa del cuerpo, que por dentro está pintado de verde, está decorada con composiciones en azul oscuro, blanco, rojo y dorado que forman bandas epigráficas y diseños florales y geométricos. La decoración está esmaltada y, por tanto, tiene un ligero relieve, lo cual produce un efecto de profundidad en la superficie.  
El cuerpo de la lámpara muestra una decoración floral con medallones rojos y blancos, mientras que el cuello tiene una cenefa con arabescos y presenta versículos de la sura 24, “La luz”. Entre las bandas epigráficas se ven medallones redondos con palos de polo blancos sobre fondo azul oscuro, motivo típico del periodo mameluco.

Las lámparas colgantes de mezquita se fabricaban para iluminar las zonas sagradas y eran un símbolo divino de la luz. Las lámparas de cristal mamelucas estaban decoradas con los blasones de los gobernantes, que simbolizaban el poder del Estado.
holder: Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico.
dates: Siglo VIII de la Hégira / XIV d. C.

materials: Vidrio pintado y esmaltado en azul oscuro, blanco, rojo y dorado.

fr.name: Lampe de mosquée.
description:
Lampe de mosquée à panse volumineuse et long col évasé en son extrémité. Des attaches en forme de boucle permettent de suspendre la lampe à des chaînes. La surface tout entière est décorée de compositions de bandeaux épigraphiés et de motifs géométriques et floraux peints en bleu foncé, blanc, rouge, et de dorures. Le décor émaillé, donc en relief, confère à cette lampe une profondeur particulière.  
Le corps est orné de médaillons à décor floral rouge et blanc et lambrequins, tandis que le col reçoit une bordure d'arabesques et porte les versets de la “Lumière” (sourate XXIV du Coran). Au milieu des inscriptions, des médaillons ronds contiennent des cannes de polo en blanc sur fond bleu foncé, motif caractéristique de la période mamelouke.

Les lampes en verre suspendues qui étaient fabriquées pour éclairer les lieux sacrés étaient un symbole divin de la lumière. Celles de la période mamelouke sont décorées avec les blasons des souverains, ce qui symbolise le pouvoir de l’État.

tr.name: Cam Kandil.
description:
Şişkin gövdeli ve yukarıya doğru genişleyen uzun boyunlu bir askı kandildir. Gövdesinde zincir asmak için altı kulp vardır. İçten yeşile boyalı cam kandilin tüm yüzeyi, koyu mavi, beyaz, kırmızı renkler ve altın yaldızla boyanan; yazı bordürleri, geometrik ve bitkisel kompozisyonlarla bezelidir. Mineleme tekniği ile yapıldığı için bezemelerin bir bölümünün kabarık olması kandilin yüzeyine derinlik kazandırmaktadır.  
  
Gövdesinde kırmızı ve beyazla yapılmış dilimli madalyonlar içine bitkisel bezemeler, boyunda ise bordürler halinde rumi kompozisyonlar ve Nur suresinden alınmış ayetler yer almaktadır. Yazı bordürleri arasında ise yuvarlak madalyonlar içinde, koyu mavi zemin üzerine beyazla yapılmış, Memluk döneminin karakteristik özelliklerinden polo sopaları yer almaktadır.

Kutsal mekânları aydınlatmak için üretilen asma cam kandiller, ışığın ilahi bir sembolü olarak kullanılmışlardır. özellikle Memluk döneminde üretilen cam kandillerde, hükümdarlık alameti olarak kullanılan armalarla devletin gücü ifade edilmiştir.
keywords: Kandil; Cam.
materials: Cam kandilin tüm yüzeyi, koyu mavi, beyaz, kırmızı, altın yaldızla boyama ve mineleme tekniğiyle bezenmiştir.
