en.name: Mosque lamp of Sultan Al-Nasir Muhammad
description: This mosque lamp consists of two parts with original production dates that are separated by a hundred years.  The top – later – part bears the following inscription: "Glory to our Lord, the Sultan, the victorious king, Nasir al-dunya wa-l-din, the father of virtues, Muhammad bin as-Sultan al-Malik al-Mansur, may his victory be mighty." Al-Nasir Muhammad ruled with interruptions from AD 1293 to 1341. The lower part with enthroned princes and musicians is from the first half of the thirteenth century.
keywords: Mosque lamp; Brass; Sultan Al-Nasir Muhammad; Mosque interior decoration
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: Sidi Abdarrahman Complex
description:
Sidi Abdarrahman is the patron saint of Algiers. He was born in 784 / 1383 in Algiers (or its surroundings) and came from the Thaaliba tribe. At sixteen he left the city to undertake a long voyage that took him to Béjaia, Tunis and Mecca, the last stage of his journey of study and devotion. Returning to Algiers after a twenty-year absence, he divided his time between writing at least thirty books, teaching religious sciences and worshipping.  
He is universally appreciated among his contemporaries and subsequent generations for his inexhaustible knowledge, his exemplary life and the blessing, *baraka*, that his presence brought to the city of al-Djazaïr, which made him its holy protector. He is the archetype of this line of mystics, who were energised by a passionate faith, and who – with great culture and deep virtue – inspire the veneration of all. Thus was born the cult of the saints widespread in the Maghreb, which responds to the deep longings of the popular masses for intercession with God.  
At his death in 875 / 1471, at the age of 90, his remains were laid above the gate of Bab al-Oued, halfway up the hill of Algiers. In 1019 / 1611, 140 years after his death, his fame continued to grow, and a mausoleum was built to house his sepulchre.  
To access this mausoleum you cross, via a long stairway shaded with centuries-old trees, a necropolis that was built around the mausoleum. It contains the tombs of famous figures. Immediately to the left of the entrance is the tomb of Ouali Daddah, a saint who died in 961 / 1554, whose legend says that he raised the sea by striking it with his staff, thus creating the storm that ruined the fleet of Charles V.  
At the bottom of the stairs, just before reaching the heart of the mausoleum, you find the tomb of Sidi Mansour, a saint renowned for his miracles, whose sarcophagus can be seen through the opening in the wall, and who died in 1074 / 1664. Opposite this tomb, against the back wall, another necropolis houses the tomb of Hadj Ahmed, the last bey of Constantine, interred in 1848. Then you reach the *koubba* (dome) of the tomb of Lalla Aïcha, daughter of Sidi Abdarrahman.  
The entrance to the mausoleum itself is marked by a door with a semicircular arch surmounted by an inscription in praise of the *oukil* Abdelkader, who built the monument in 1036 / 1627. The first line reads, “This is the tomb of Sidi Abdarrahman”.  
Past the vestibule one reaches the funerary chamber and the tomb, covered with rich fabrics. This funerary chamber, later turned into a mosque, is an octagonal room surmounted by a dome, each panel of which is pierced by three delicately carved openings in geometric or floral motifs.  
In the corners formed by the panels of the octagon are eight groups of three marble half-columns embedded in the walls that support the dome. The column capitals are Muslim adaptations of Corinthian capitals with carved acanthus leaves.  
Framed by two marble columns, the *mihrab*, added around 1107 / 1696, is richly decorated with unusual Persian faïence (glazed ceramic) tiles with a large floral design.  
Lodging and kitchens were set up at the end of the entry vestibule of the funeral chamber when the mausoleum became a pilgrimage site. These rooms were restored in 2007.  
The entire building is crowned by the square minaret added during its final transformation into a mosque in 1142 / 1730. It is decorated with columns and arcades surmounted by bands of glazed tiles on three floors. It serves as a gathering place for the people of Algiers – the mausoleum being extremely popular even today, especially during religious holidays.

fr.name: Mausolée Sidi Abderrahmane
description:
Sidi Abderrahmane est le saint patron d’Alger. Il est né en 784/1383 à Alger ou dans ses environs et est issu de la tribu des Thaaliba. À l’âge de seize ans, il quitte la ville pour entreprendre un long voyage d’études qui le mènera à Béjaia, Tunis et La Mecque, dernière étape de son périple d’études et de piété. De retour à Alger après vingt années d’absence, il partage sa vie entre l’écriture de pas moins de trente ouvrages, l’enseignement des sciences religieuses et la dévotion. Il fait l’unanimité, auprès de ses contemporains comme auprès des générations suivantes, par son savoir inépuisable, sa vie exemplaire et la bénédiction, la *baraka*, que sa présence apporte à la ville d’al-Djazaïr qui en fait son saint protecteur. Il est l’archétype de cette lignée de mystiques qui, animés d’une foi passionnée, d’une grande culture et d’une profonde vertu, suscitent la vénération de tous. Ainsi naît le culte des saints qui se généralise au Maghreb, répondant aux aspirations profondes, de la part des masses populaires, d’intercession auprès de Dieu.  
  
À sa mort, en 875/1471, à l’âge de quatrevingt-dix ans, sa dépouille est déposée au-dessus de la porte de Bab al-Oued, à mi-hauteur de la colline d’Alger.  
En 1019/1611, soit cent quarante années après sa mort, sa gloire ne cessant de grandir, on construisit un mausolée pour abriter sa sépulture.  
  
Pour accéder à ce mausolée, on traverse, par un long escalier ombragé d’arbres centenaires, la nécropole qui s’est constituée autour du mausolée et qui renferme les tombeaux de personnages illustres. On y trouve, immédiatement à gauche de l’entrée, le tombeau de Ouali Daddah, autre saint, mort en 961/1554, dont la légende dit qu’il souleva la mer en la frappant avec son bâton, provoquant la tempête qui ruina la flotte de Charles-Quint.  
En bas de l’escalier, juste avant d’accéder au coeur du mausolée, on trouvera le tombeau de Sidi Mansour, mort en 1074/1664, saint réputé pour ses miracles et dont on peut voir le cénotaphe à travers l’ouverture dans le mur. Face à ce tombeau, une autre nécropole abrite, contre le mur du fond, la tombe de Hadj Ahmed, dernier bey de Constantine, inhumé en 1848, et enfin la *koubba* de Lalla Aïcha, fille de Sidi Abderrahmane.  
L’entrée du mausolée lui-même est marquée par une porte à arc en plein cintre surmontée par une inscription à la gloire de l’*oukil* Abdelkader qui, en 1036/1627, édifia le monument. La première ligne dit : “Ceci est le tombeau de Sidi Abderrahmane.”  
Après le vestibule, on accède à la chambre funéraire où se trouve le tombeau recouvert de riches étoffes. La chambre funéraire, devenue mosquée, est une salle octogonale surmontée d’une coupole dont chaque pan est percé de trois ouvertures finement ajourées de motifs géométriques ou floraux.  
Dans les angles formés par les pans de l’octogone, on observe les huit groupes de trois demi-colonnes en marbre, engagées dans les murs supportant la coupole. Les chapiteaux des colonnes sont des adaptations musulmanes des chapiteaux corinthiens à feuilles d'acanthe.  
Encadré de deux colonnettes de marbre, le *mihrab*, ajouté vers 1107/1696, est richement orné de placages de faïences persanes rares à grand motif floral.  
À la coupole sont suspendus des lustres de cristal et des étendards.  
Le sanctuaire fait aussi office de nécropole. On y trouve les tombeaux de plusieurs pachas : Hassan Pacha, Mustapha Pacha et son fils Omar. Près du *mihrab* reposent la fille de Hassan Pacha et, au pied du tombeau, la dépouille du maître Boudjemaa, un érudit qui fut le professeur de Sidi Abderrahmane. Au-dessus de ces tombes, les murs présentent des inscriptions dans une élégante calligraphie blanche sur fond bleu. Une étroite galerie bordée par une balustrade de bois ouvragé d’arcs et de doubles colonnettes surmonte toute la salle.  
Le mausolée devenant un lieu de pèlerinage, des lieux d’hébergement et des cuisines furent aménagés au fond du vestibule d’accès à la chambre funéraire. Ces pièces sont actuellement (2007) en cours de restauration.  
L’ensemble de l’édifice est couronné par le minaret de plan carré ajouté lors de la transformation finale en mosquée en 1142/1730 et décoré de colonnettes et d’arcatures surmontées de bandeaux de faïences sur trois étages. Il constitue un lieu de ralliement pour la population d’Alger, le mausolée étant, aujourd’hui encore, un lieu extrêmement fréquenté, particulièrement lors des fêtes religieuses.

ar.name: كتيفة (حاملة إفريز).
description:
تشكل القطعة كتيفة حاملة، تزين وجوهَها المصبوغة زخرفة نباتية مبسطة، تتكون من غصينات زرقاء وصفراء، وتنتهي بسعفتي نخيل نقوشها ثلاثية أوثنائية الفصوص، وأرضيتها مطلية بلون أحمر لامع. أما محيطها الذي يأخذ شكل حاملة الإفريز، فقد أشير إليه بنقاط صفراء محاطة بدوائر زرقاء. تندرج هذه العناصر الزخرفية النباتية تماماً ضمن الرصيد الزخرفي الإفريقي (التونسي) خلال القرن 3 وحتى القرن 5 الهجري/ القرن 9 – القرن 11 الميلادي.  
من جهة ثانية، جرى نحت زخرفة الواجهة والتي تتخذ شكل جرادة، بطريقة الأخاديد المنحنية. ويقدم فن العمارة الإفريقية (التونسية) نماذج مشابهة لها منحوتة على الحجر، على شاكلة جامع الأبواب الثلاثة، منذ على الأقل القرن 3 الهجري/ القرن 9 الميلادي، فيما لم يورث المشرق حاملات إفريز تمكن من إجراء بعض المقارنات. إن هذه الكتيفة التي كانت تشكل جزءًا من السقف الخشبي لقاعة الصلاة في الجامع الكبير في القيروان، حيث كانت تستخدم كحاملة للعوارض الخشبية للسقفيات، تشكل، على الأرجح، اشتقاقا بعيدا من النماذج القديمة. غير أن المرء تأخذه الدهشة من عبقرية نجار الأبنوس الذي كان عليه، لتزيين عنصر شديد البروز، القيام بنجر الخشب ببساطة وكذلك ترصيع سطوحه بعناصر زخرفية تسطيرية.

كانت هذه الكتيفة تشكل جزءا لايتجزأ من السقف الخشبي لقاعة الصلاة بالجامع الكبير للقيروان؛ وكانت تستخدم كساذجة (جائزة) لإحدى رافدات السقوف؛ وتنضوي الأشكال الزهرية ضمن السجل الزخرفي الإفريقي (التونسي) من القرن 3 إلى القرن 5 للهجرة (9 – 11 للميلاد).
dates: نهاية القرن 3 - بداية القرن 5 الهجري/ نهاية القرن 9 - بداية القرن 11 الميلادي.
keywords: أثاث؛ منقولات؛ زخرفة زهرية ؛ زخرفة تسطيرية/هندسية؛ نحت؛ زخرفة تصويرية.

en.name: Corbel.
description: The sides of this corbel are painted with a simplified floral decoration of blue and yellow foliate scrolls ending in tri-lobed or four-lobed palm-leaf motifs on a bright red background. The edges of the corbel are decorated with yellow dots within blue circles. These floral motifs are perfectly typical of the Ifriqiyan decorative repertoire of the AH 3rd and 4th century (AD 9th and 10th century). The front projection of the corbel is carved in the shape of a grasshopper's head with curved grooves. Although the Orient has not left to us any other comparable wooden corbels, Ifriqiyan architecture does feature similar stone models as early as the AH 3rd century (AD 9th century), for example at the Mosque of the Three Doors. This corbel was part of the wooden roof of the prayer hall of the Great Mosque of Kairouan and served to support one of the ceiling beams. It is probably derived from an ancient design. However, one is struck by the consummate skill of the woodcarver's simple, rough-hewn, linear treatment of the surfaces, so appropriate for the decoration of a protruding architectural element.

This corbel was part of the wooden ceiling of the prayer room of the Great Mosque of Kairouan, acting as a joist for the ceiling beams. Its floral motifs belonged to the Ifriqiyan decorative repertoire from the AH 3rd–5th / AD 9th–11th centuries.
dates: Hegira, end of 3rd–beginning of 5th century / AH 9th–11th century.
keywords: Furnishing; floral decoration; sculpture; figurative decoration

es.name: Ménsula
description:
Los laterales pintados de este tipo de modillón están adornados con un diseño floral simplificado, compuesto por follajes azules y amarillos terminados en palmetas bilobuladas o trilobuladas. La superficie de sostén está pintada en rojo intenso. Los contornos están dibujados con puntos amarillos rodeados por círculos azules. Estos motivos florales pertenecen al repertorio decorativo ifriqí de los siglos III-V / IX-XI. La decoración de la parte frontal, en forma de cabeza de saltamontes, está labrada con estrías curvadas.  
La arquitectura ifriqí presenta, a partir del siglo III / IX, modelos semejantes tallados en piedra, como en la mezquita de las Tres Puertas, mientras que no se ha encontrado ninguna ménsula procedente de Oriente que permita realizar un análisis comparativo.  
Perteneciente a la techumbre de madera del oratorio de la Mezquita Mayor de Kairuán, esta ménsula servía de vigueta para reforzar una de las vigas de los techos. Se trata sin duda de una evolución a partir de modelos antiguos; no obstante, es sorprendente el arte con que el ebanista talló y decoró con elementos lineales una superficie de tan prominente relieve.

Esta ménsula integraba el artesonado de madera del oratorio de la Mezquita Mayor de Kairuán. Reforzaba una de las vigas de los techos. Los motivos florales pertenecen al repertorio decorativo de Ifriqiya de los siglos III-V / IX-XI.
dates: Finales del siglo III-principios del V de la Hégira / IX-XI d. C.
keywords: Mobiliario; decoración floral; escultura; decoración figurativa
materials: Madera de cedro labrada y decorada.
tags: Madera de cedro labrada y decorada.

fr.name: Console.
description: Sorte de corbeau dont les côtés peints sont meublés par un décor floral simplifié, formé par des rinceaux bleu et jaune qui se terminent par des palmettes trilobées ou bilobées. Leur plate-forme est de couleur rouge vif. Les pourtours qui suivent la forme de la console sont indiqués par des points jaunes entourés de cercles bleus. Ces motifs floraux s'inscrivent parfaitement dans le répertoire décoratif ifriqiyen du IIIe au Ve siècle H (IXe-XIe siècle J.-C.). Le décor de façade, qui est en forme de tête de sauterelle, est sculpté de rainures courbes. L'architecture ifriqiyenne offre des modèles semblables en pierre, au moins dès le IIIe siècle H (IXe siècle J.-C), à l'exemple de la mosquée des Trois Portes, alors que l'Orient ne nous a pas légué de consoles permettant de faire une comparaison quelconque. Cette console, qui faisait partie de la toiture en bois de la salle de prière de la Grande Mosquée de Kairouan, servait de solive pour une des poutres des plafonds. Il s'agit, sans doute, d'une dérivation lointaine de modèles antiques ; néanmoins, on est frappé par le génie de l'ébéniste qui, devant orner un organe de forte saillie, l'épannelle simplement et en meuble les surfaces avec des éléments linéaires.

Cette console faisait partie intégrante de la toiture en bois de la salle de prière de la Grande Mosquée de Kairouan. Elle servait de solive pour une des poutres des plafonds. Les motifs floraux s'inscrivent dans le répertoire décoratif ifriqiyen du IIIe au Ve siècle H (IXe-XIe siècle J.-C.).
dates: fin IIIe-début Ve siècle de l’Hégire (fin IXe-début XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Mobilier; décoration florale; sculpture; décoration figurative
materials: Bois de cèdre sculpté et décoré.
tags: Bois de cèdre sculpté et décoré.
partner: Musée des arts islamiques de Kairouan

en.name: Bowl (*Sakızlık*)
short_description: From historical sources, we learn that vessels made of gold and silver were widely used in the Ottoman palace. Starting from the end of the 18th century, Baroque and Rococo forms of Western style replaced classical Ottoman designs. We find roses in relief, the Ottoman coat-of-arms, architectural compositions, casted flowers, birds and animals on a multitude of the vessels of the era. This cylindrical cup with pedestal foot and cupola-like hinged lid was made of vermeil silver. On the body of the cup we see a floral pattern and hanging lambs placed alternatingly. Flowers, buds and leaves are made from rubies and diamonds nailed into gold and silver contours. On the lid – instead of lamb motif on the body – a chalice was used. The foot of the chalice is in the form of a cherub from which a bundle of rays projects.
holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
keywords: minor arts, applied arts, silver objects
partner: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

en.name: *Constantinople et le Bosphore de Thrace*
short_description: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.
keywords: travel books; travelling; orientalism; Istanbul

de.name:
Stift Rein  
Reiner Stiftskirche und Kloster
names: Zisterzienser Abtei und Kirche in Rein
description:
Was alle Gebäude – die des Klosters und die Kirche – gemein haben, ist die Tatsache, dass sie romanische und gotische Bauteile enthalten. Die meiste Architektur um den Kreuzgang im Süden, die Wirtschaftsgebäude im Westen, die Flügel im Osten und im Norden sind alter Gebäudebestand. Einiges ist sichtbar, anderes nicht, weil die meisten Teile eine barocke Hülle übergestülpt bekamen. Zuletzt wurde die Kirche – in den 1730er-Jahren – barockisiert. Der Grundriss des Klosterkomplexes ist unregelmäßig, ein anderes Überbleibsel aus dem Mittelalter.  
Wenn man sich der Abtei vom Osten nähert, von wo die Landstraße direkt darauf zuführt, denkt man, dass das die Hauptfassade ist. Betrachtet man aber die unregelmäßig angeordneten Gebäudeteile, vier davon vorspringend, erkennt man, dass diese Seite stark mittelalterlich beeinflusst ist. Die Haupteinfahrt befindet sich um die Ecke, an der Nordseite des Stifts und erweckt vollständig den Eindruck eines barocken Klostergebäudes. Der leicht vorspringende, dreigeschoßige und siebenachsige Teil mit dem Haupteingang in der Mitte empfängt ankommende Gäste seit drei Jahrhunderten auf typisch barocke Art.

Ab der Gründung im Jahr 1129 bis zum Bau des neuen Konventgebäudes, der Renovierungen und Barockisierungen zu Beginn des 17. Jahrhunderts bis in die späten 1770er-Jahre wurde an der Architektur der Gebäude nur wenig verändert. Nur nach dem Einfall der Türken wurden Schäden an den Gebäuden repariert und die wehrhafte Ummauerung vergrößert. Ab Anfang des 17. Jahrhunderts begannen die Zisterzienser, die mittelalterlichen Gebäude umzubauen. Die Mitglieder des Konvents erhielten neue Zellen, und der östliche Teil der Klosteranlage wurde renoviert. An der Stelle der mittelalterlichen Kirche entstand ein neues Gotteshaus, wobei man die Wände, das Presbyterium und den Eingang zum ehemaligen Konventgebäude beließ. Nach dem Entfernen der romanischen Pfeiler erhielt der neue barocke Raum – mit Seitenkapellen und einer Empore – größere Weite und mehr Licht.

Sakristei, Winterkirche): Stuckdekoration: Alexander Serenio (keine Daten) zugeschrieben Klostergebäude, neues Konventgebäude: Bartolomeo di Bosio (keine Daten); Barockisierung Nordflügel und östlicher Teil des Gebäudekomplexes: wahrscheinlich Johann Georg Stengg (1689 – 1753) Huldigungssaal und Bibliothek Fresken: Joseph Amonte (1703 – 1753)
history:
Nachdem sich die Benediktiner wegen unterschiedlicher Auslegung der Ordensregeln gespalten hatten, gründeten drei Mönche in Cîteaux den neuen Zisterzienser-Orden. Als sich ihnen der charismatische (spätere heiliggesprochene) Bernhard von Clairvaux mit Freunden und Verwandten anschloss, führte das zu einem großen Aufschwung des Ordens. Von ursprünglich vier Primarabteien verbreitete sich der Orden rasch über Europa. In Deutschland gab es zwei Zisterzienser Abteien, eine war Ebrach in Oberfranken, von wo sich eines Tages einige Mönche im Auftrag Markgraf Leopolds des Starken nach Rein begaben. Am 25. März 1129 kamen sie an und gründeten dort ein neues Kloster. Der Landesherr schenkte ihnen dafür Land. Gerlach, einer der Brüder, wurde zum ersten Abt gewählt.  
Die Mönche von Ebrach hatten bald ein Oratorium und ein Klostergebäude aus Holz errichtet. Ein paar Jahre später bauten sie, diesmal aus Stein, eine Kirche, ein Klostergebäude und eine Schutzmauer, die den gesamten Komplex umgab. Ab der barocken Epoche wurden die meisten Bauten erneuert oder stilistisch angepasst und blieben bis in unsere Tage beinahe unberührt.

en.name:
Rein Abbey  
Rein Abbey Church and Monastery
names: Cistercians' Abbey and Church in Rein
description:
What all buildings – monastery and church – have in common is the fact that they contain Romanesque and Gothic remains. Most of the architecture around the cloister in the South, the agricultural buildings in the West, the wings in the East and in the North are originally old building stock. Some are visible, others are not because most of them got a baroque coat overlaid. The church was the latest – in the 1730s – to be baroquized. The building floor plan of the monastery complex is irregular, another relict of the medieval epoch.  
Approaching the abbey from the East, from where the course of the street leads directly to it, one would consider this aisle as the main façade. Noticing the irregularly arranged components of the building, four of them protruding, one understands that this side has many medieval parts. The main entrance is round the corner, on the abbey´s North side and utterly evokes the impression of a baroque monastery. The slightly protruding part of the building with entrance amid three floors and seven axes has been welcoming arriving guests for three centuries in the typically baroque way.

From the abbey´s foundation in the year 1129 until the erection of the new convent building, the renovations and baroquization from the beginning of the 17th century until the late 1770s, there was almost no change in the abbey´s architecture. Only after the Turkish invasion the damages to the buildings were being repaired and the fortifications expanded. From the beginning of the 17th century, the Cistercians started with structural changes of the Medieval buildings. The members of the convent got new apartments, and the Eastern part of the monastery complex was renovated. The new church was built on the site of the Medieval one, reusing the walls, the presbytery and the entrance to the former convent building. After removing the Romanesque pillars the new Baroque room – with side chapels and galleries above - became spacious and light.

Monastery complex, new convent building: Bartolomeo di Bosio (n.d.); baroquization North wing and Eastern part of the monastery´s building complex: probably Johann Georg Stengg (1689–1753) Homage Hall and library fresco paintings: Joseph Amonte (1703–53)
history: After a split had occurred among the Benedictines – because of different interpretation of the order´s rules – three friars founded the new Cistercian order in Cîteaux. When the charismatic, (later saint) Bernhard joined them with friends and relatives, the religious community underwent a major upswing. Soon there were Cistercian abbeys all over Europe. Two were in Germany, one was Ebrach in Upper Franconia from where monks set off to Rein on Margrave Leopold´s the Strong order. On 25th March 1129 they arrived there and founded a new monastery on the very place. The sovereign donated the land. Gerlach, one of the friars, was elected the first abbot. The monks from Ebrach erected a first oratory and a monastery building from wood. A few years later they built a church (this time made of stone), a new monastery building and a protective wall enclosing the complex. From the Baroque epoch on, most of the buildings were renewed or stylistically adapted. They stayed almost untouched until our present day.

en.name: House of the Prior
description:
Construction of this house was in two different stages: the main work was carried out at the end of the 15th century, when García Ramírez was the prior, since the house was in a bad state of repair and inappropriate to its function. Dating from this time is the façade that is somewhat set back from the street; it has a doorway with a flat arch, over which is the arms of the Priory of San Marcos de León.  
Entering through this door, a passageway communicates with the main part of the palace, organised around a patio that initially had only one gallery of arches on its eastern side. This gallery is a Mudéjar construction that has two storeys of arcades, in a combination that the extension carried out in the mid-16th century also adopted.  
At the beginning of the 16th century, the prior’s house became the primary headquarters of the Inquisition in Llerena and remained so until the middle of the century, at which time it reverted to the Prior’s residence. It was at that time that a series of works gave the building its definitive shape.  
The most noteworthy of these works was the completion of the principal patio, adding galleries on two of its sides, with the final configuration being that of a square with two floors of arches on three of its sides. The arches on the lower level are stilted and semicircular, while those on the upper floor are basket-handled. In both cases, the *alfiz*\-framed arches rest on octagonal pillars with a base and a capital. The patio was whitewashed, and the galleries covered by a wooden roof. Around the patio are 30 rooms, while behind it is a vegetable garden with a waterwheel.

es.name: Casa Prioral
description:
Esta edificación se hizo en dos etapas constructivas. La primera gran intervención se realizó a finales del siglo XV, en el priorato de García Ramírez, pues las casas priorales estaban en mal estado y eran poco apropiadas para su función. De estos años es la fachada, algo retranqueada respecto de la calle, con una puerta de arco adintelado sobre la que va el escudo del priorato de San Marcos de León.  
Por esta puerta se accede a un callejón que comunica con la zona principal del palacio, centralizada por un patio que, en el momento inicial, solo contó con una galería de arcos en el frente oriental. Esta galería es una construcción mudéjar formada por dos pisos de arquerías con una combinación que luego se repitió en la ampliación realizada a mediados del siglo XVI.  
A principios del siglo XVI, la casa prioral se convirtió en la primera sede del Santo Oficio de Llerena, que la utilizó hasta mediados de siglo, en que de nuevo pasó a ser la residencia del prior. Fue entonces cuando se realizó una serie de obras que dieron a la construcción su forma definitiva.  
Lo más destacado de estas obras es la conclusión del patio principal, al que se añadieron dos lados de galerías, quedando finalmente configurado como una planta cuadrada con dos cuerpos de arquería en tres de sus frentes. Los arcos del piso inferior son de medio punto peraltado mientras que en el alto son carpaneles, y en todos los casos están enmarcados en *alfiz* y apoyan en pilares octogonales con basa y capitel. El patio iba encalado y las galerías se cubrían con techo de madera. Alrededor del patio hay unas treinta estancias, y en las traseras había una huerta con noria.

ar.name: زوج من الشمعدانات.
description: زوج من الشمعدانات الخزفية الزرقاء والبيضاء تحت طبقة من التزجيج متطابقة الشكل. لم تجر العادة على تصنيع هذا الشكل من الشمعدانات من مادة الخزف، فهو مشتق من القطع المعدنية التي كانت تنتج للسوق الإيطالية. لقد تم تزيين الجوانب المائلة لأحد الشمعدانات برصائع بيضوية الشكل موشاة بزخارف زهرية في حين تم تزيين جوانب جسم الشمعدان الثاني بوريقات لولبية متماوجة، أما قاعدتا الشمعدانين، فقد تم تزيينهما بزخارف زهرية، في حين تميز الحاملان بخطوط زرقاء وبيضاء مع صف من الأزهار حول قمته. وتعتبر الورقة الواوية الشكل من العناصر المميزة للفخار الأزرق والأبيض العائد لهذه الفترة، فأصل الفخار الإزنيقي، الذي بدأ بالأزرق والأبيض، يعود إلى الخزف الصيني. لقد تم إنتاج هذين الشمعدانين خلال حكم السلطان سليمان (926-73/ 1520-66) عندما ازدهرت صناعة الخزف في إزنيق.
شمعدانان مصنوعان على طريقة الفخار الإزنيقي، ومُستوحيان من البورسلان الصيني، الأزرق والأبيض. صُنعت هذه القطع في بداية حكم سليمان الأكبر, في الفترة ذاتها التي انتشرت فيها صناعة فخار إزنيق بشكل واسع.
materials: خزف أزرق وأبيض تحت طبقة من التزجيج.
tags: خزف أزرق وأبيض تحت طبقة من التزجيج.

en.name: Pair of candlesticks.
description: A pair of ceramic candlesticks of identical shape, with blue-and-white underglaze. Candlesticks of this shape were not usually produced in ceramic; the form derives from metalwork, of a type produced for the Italian market. The sloping sides of one of the candlesticks are painted with oval-shaped medallions interspersed with floral motifs, while the second candlestick has an undulating leafy scroll around the sides of the body. Both have floral scrolls around the base, a blue-and-white striped candle-holder, with a further row of flowers around the top. The distinctive 'tadpole' leaf featured here is a common feature of blue-and-white ceramics of this period. The origins of early Iznik blue-and-white ceramics can be traced to Chinese porcelain. These candlesticks were produced during the reign of Sultan Suleyman (AH 926–73 / AD 1520–66) when there was a considerable expansion of the ceramics industry in Iznik.

The design of these Iznik ceramic candlesticks is influenced by Chinese blue-and-white porcelain. This pair was produced in the early years of Süleyman the Magnificent’s reign, when the Iznik ceramic industry expanded considerably.
type: Stone paste blue and turquoise painting
keywords: Commerce; floral decoration; Chinese influence

es.name: Par de candeleros
description: Par de candeleros de idéntica forma, en cerámica azul y blanca bajo vidriado. La forma de estos candeleros es inusual, deriva de un modelo en metal que se producía para el mercado italiano. La curvatura de uno de los candeleros presenta medallones ovale entre motivos florales. En el otro otro hay están decorados con tallos de hojas onduladas. Ambos presentan en la base un motivo de roleos florales y, en el cilindro para la vela, líneas verticales azules y blancas y más motivos florales en la parte superior. Las “hojas-renacuajo” que se aprecian en estos candeleros son un motivo decorativo habitual en la cerámica azul y blanca de este periodo y su origien hay que buscarlo en la influencia de la porcelana china. Estos candeleros fueron producidos en la época de Suleimán el Magnífico (r. 926-973 / 1520-1566), momento álgido de la industria cerámica de Iznik.

El diseño de estos candeleros de cerámica de estilo Iznik es de influencia china, concretamente de la porcelana azul y blanca. Este par debió de fabricarse en los primeros años del sultanato de Suleimán el Magnífico, momento de expansión de la industria cerámica de Iznik.
dates: Alrededor del año 936  de la Hégira / 1530 d. C.
materials: Cerámica azul y blanca bajo vidriado.
tags: Cerámica azul y blanca bajo vidriado.

fr.name: Paire de chandeliers.
description: Paire de chandeliers en céramique de forme identique à sous-glaçure bleu et blanc. Les chandeliers de ce type n'étaient généralement pas fabriqués en céramique et leur forme vient en fait de versions en métal d'un type prévu pour le marché italien. Les pentes du premier modèle sont peintes de médaillons ovales entremêlés de motifs floraux, tandis que celles du second présentent sur toute leur surface un enroulement folié ondulé. Tous deux sont ornés de rinceaux floraux autour de la base et se terminent par un binet rayé bleu et blanc surmonté d'un bandeau de fleurs. La feuille “de têtard” originale représentée ici est courante dans les céramiques “bleu et blanc” de la période. L'origine de ce type de céramique peut être retracée jusqu'à la porcelaine chinoise. Ces chandeliers étaient produits sous le règne du sultan Soliman (926-973/1520-1566), alors que l'industrie de la céramique d'Iznik connaissait une expansion considérable.

Le motif de ces chandeliers en céramique d'Iznik s'inspire de la porcelaine chinoise bleu-et-blanc. Cette paire a été produite dans les premières années du règne de Soliman le Magnifique, à une époque où la production céramique d'Iznik connut une expansion considérable.
materials: Céramique, décor bleu et blanc sous glaçure.
tags: Céramique, décor bleu et blanc sous glaçure.

ar.name: مبخرة
description: هذه المبخرة هي بشكل بغباء بطراز خاص أو صقر ينتمي لمجموعة صغيرة من التماثيل / المنحوتات البرونزية المتميزة بدرجة عالية تماما من احتمال كونها من العصر الأموي في إسبانيا. ويقف الطائر على مخالب قوية جاثما على كرة التي يمكن أن تكون قد وضعت على قاعدة طويلة. والجسم محفور عليه ريش وسعيفات نخل ونقش بالخط الكوفي.
dates: أواخر القرن الرابع وبداية القرن الخامس الهجري / أواخر القرن  العاشر وبداية  القرن الحادي عشر الميلادي
dynasty: العصر الأموي في الأندلس / عصر الخلافة

en.name: Incense burner
description:
This incense burner in the form of a stylized parrot or falcon belongs to a small group of bronze sculptures, ascribed with a fairly great degree of probability to Umayyad Spain.  
The bird is holding on with strong claws to a perch across a sphere that might have been placed on a tall pedestal. The body is engraved with feathers, palmettes, and a *Kufi* inscription.
dates: Hegira late 4th–beginning of the 5th century / AD late 10th–beginning of the 11th century
keywords: Burner; Metalwork

en.name: The Coffee Shop of Cairo
short_description: This colourful print depicts a typical 19th century coffeeshop in Cairo. An exclusively male domain, its design was characterised by an open front and wide benches for seating, to allow for easy congregation and the gathering of friends and acquainances. Not only in Cairo, which had over a thousands coffeehouses in Roberts's time, but all over the Middle East, coffeehouses were important social hubs for the exchange of news, entertainment, smoking (customers brought their own pipes and waterpipes) and - not rarely - political dissent. Musicians and storytellers often enhanced the experience further. In this image, the proprietor or an employee of the cafe can be seen serving a beverage in the centre. Interestingly, both the ewer and the large copper cup he uses are of a type usually associated with water, not coffee. Perhaps Roberts introduced these items for artistic effect.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department

en.name: Waistband
description: Woman's waistband of cotton threaded with glass beads of red, pink, blue, white and black in geometric patterns with cotton ties at each end: Africa, Eastern Africa, Malawi, probably Yao people, late 19th century. The Yao people were long-distance traders and traded glass beads as well as using them for ornaments.
keywords: beads; glass; Malawi

en.name: *Calligrapher Rıfat Efendi*
short_description: Feyhaman Duran was particularly interested in portrait painting and went to Paris in 1910 through the patronage of the Egyptian Prince Abbas Halim Pasha to further his studies in this genre. He greatly profited from the teaching of Paul Richet, professor of anatomy in the School of Fine Arts in Paris. He also attended the Julian Academy where he learned a great deal from Jean-Paul and Albert Laurens. In 1913-14 he worked in the Cormon studio in the School of Fine Arts. Although devoting most of his time to portrait painting, Feyhaman Duran also did paintings of flowers and nudes, but he was definitely most interested in the portrayal of people, and he had very little time for non-figurative painting.
keywords: Painting; Feyhaman Duran; orientalist painters

en.name: Triumphal Arch – detail
description: Basic shapes of the monument refer to Early Baroque architecture with elements of late Renaissance Classicism.

en.name: *Âftâbe* ewer
description: The profile of this ewer for water or wine suggests glass pieces, which are more expensive to produce and more fragile. Coppersmiths translate the models into bronze or brass because Islam disapproves of gold and silver dishes.
holder: Museum of the Arab World Institute
dates: Hegira last quarter of 3rd-4th century / AD 10th-11th century
materials: Cast bronze and engraved decoration, with an ornamental band
tags: Cast bronze and engraved decoration, with an ornamental band

fr.name: Aiguière *âftâbe*
description: Le profil de cette aiguière pour l'eau ou le vin, évoque des pièces en verre, plus coûteuses à produire et aussi plus fragiles. Les dinandiers transposent les modèles dans le bronze ou le laiton, car l'islam réprouve la vaisselle en or et en argent.
holder: Musée de l'Institut du monde arabe
dates: IVe-Ve siècle de l'Hégire / Xe-XIe siècle J.-C.
materials: Bronze coulé et décor gravé, guilloché
tags: Bronze coulé et décor gravé, guilloché

ar.name: علبة أقلام مطلية باللكر موقعة من قبل حاجي محمد
description: السطح الخارجي للغطاء مرسوم عليه ثلاثة أزواج من الفرس معروضين بمراحل مختلفة من المداعبة الغزلية وموضوعين مقابل خلفية ذات أشجار وأبنية من الطراز الأوربي. ويوجد امرأتان موسيقيتان في الطرف الأيمن. ويوجد طائر ناصع وزهرة مرسومة مقابل خلفية من أوراق ذهبية وتقع داخل الغطاء. وأطراف / جوانب العلبة مرسوم عليها أربعة مناظر طبيعية مستوحاة أوربيا ومفصولة ببورتريهات نصفية في رصائع بيضوية. والقاعدة الحمراء مرسوم عليها لفات من نبات الكرمة بالذهب . وسطح الغطاء يحمل توقيع وتاريخ ولكن يبدو أنها قد طمست عمدا. وبالرغم من أن اسم محمد وكلمة سنا هي ما بقي حتى الآن فإنه في 1970s تم قراءة التوقيع كاملا من قبل شهريار عدلي (راقمه حجي محمد ) أي رسم من قبل حاجي محمد والتاريخ اعتبر بأنه عام 1124.وفي دراسته عن علبة الأقلام هذه فإن شهريار عدلي بيّن أن الأزواج الثلاثة يمثلون انتصار الحب العذري على الشهوة.
type: علبة أقلام ، ورق ماشيه ، طلاء باللكر
holder: عهدة عائلة الخليلي – مجموعة ناصر د. الخليلي للفن الإسلامي
keywords: إيران ، صفوي ، عمل لكر ، موسيقيين ، ورق ماشيه ، تأثير أوربي
tags: إيران ، صفوي ، عمل لكر ، موسيقيين ، ورق ماشيه ، تأثير أوربي
partner: عهدة عائلة خليلي - مجموعة ناصر د. خليلي للفن الإسلامي

en.name: Lacquer-painted pen box signed by Hajji Muhammad
description:
The exterior of the lid is painted with three Persian couples, shown in various stages of amorous dalliance, and set against a background with trees and European-style buildings. Two female musicians are at the right-hand end. A brilliant bird-and-flower study, painted against a gold-leaf background, is on the inside of the lid. The sides of the box are painted with four landscapes of European inspiration, separated by bust-portraits in oval medallions. The red base is painted with vine scrolls in gold.  
The top of the lid bears a signature and a date, but these appear to have been deliberately defaced. Although the name Muhammad and the word *sana* are what remains now, in the 1970s the signature was read in full by Chahryar Adle as *raqimuhu hajji Muhammad* (‘painted by Hajji Muhammad’) and the date as 1124.  
In his study of this pen box, Chahryar Adle has suggested that the three couples represent the triumph of mystic love over mere carnality.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art
keywords: Iran; Safavid; lacquerwork; musicians; papier mâché; European influence
materials: Papier-mâché body and lift-off lid, with a lift-out inner compartment, all lined with leather
tags: Papier-mâché body and lift-off lid, with a lift-out inner compartment, all lined with leather
partner: Khalili Family Trust – Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art

en.name: Essabanin Quarter
description:
**Mill**  
The mill is located on the left bank of the river, linked to the right bank via a bridge. Its architecture comprises a very simple structure. A main room, rectangular in shape, is divided into two floors: a ground floor, on which the mill is located, and a basement which houses the machinery. The lateral walls of both floors are punctured with bays which allow for the channels to pass through. The mill is activated by a helical axis which turns under the effect of the water’s driving force.  
It is difficult to put an exact date on this building, and the same goes for the other three mills which still function, and which were also built above the Ras al-Ma’ source. The only thing that can be claimed as certain is that we owe the placement of an ingenious hydraulic system to the Andalusian refugees; installed at the time of the town’s foundation, it enabled fountains and mills to be endowed with a carefully monitored resource of water. Legend attributes the installation to a certain Sidi Bubker al-Hadad, an engineer in his profession which dealt with the organisation of these resources.  
  
**Bridge**  
This charming little creation, covered in greenery, is Chefchaouen’s only bridge. Situated at the exit of the Lamkadem Gate, it links the right bank of the Essabanin Quarter to the left bank, facilitating the journey to the mills. Solid, imposing walls serve to support the extended arch which reaches across the river. The base of the walls is reinforced by buttresses with cut-off corners to counteract the effects of erosion, in line with bridge construction techniques of the Andalusian period.  
The date of when the bridge was created is unknown; but if one judges it against the chronology of the *medina*’s urbanisation, and takes into account the mode of construction, then one can approximately place it, at the very latest, in the beginning of the 13th/19th century, at the point when the *medina* was at its expansive climax.  
  
**Bakery**  
Situated on the square of the Essabanin Quarter, it is one of 15 active bakeries currently working in Chefchaouen. Like the others, it is located at the neighbourhood’s crossroads in order to better serve the households which continue to knead their own bread at home, and which thus need the bakery’s equipment in order to bake it.  
Its design is simple. A rectangular room of small dimensions with a low ceiling, it is covered by a dual-sloping red-tiled roof from which rises a chimney which, as is the law of this town, contains the hearth and a platform on which the clients’ baking trays are placed. A space is kept for the storage of firewood.  
The walls are made of clay with brick planes, which are also used in the levelling of the door. Skylights pierce them open, to assure that there is ventilation, and a door acts as a means of access and of light.

es.name: Barrio Esabanin: molino, puente, horno
description:
**El molino**  
Está situado en la orilla izquierda del barrio y unido a la otra orilla por el puente. Su arquitectura es muy simple; consiste en una habitación rectangular, dividida en dos niveles: una planta baja, donde se encuentra la muela, y un sótano que contiene la maquinaria y cuyos dos muros laterales están perforados por vanos para permitir el paso del agua. La muela se mueve por medio de un eje con hélices, que gira impulsado por la fuerza motriz del agua.  
Es difícil dar la fecha exacta de la edificación de este caserón, como tampoco la de los otros tres molinos, todavía activos, que fueron construidos aguas arriba del manantial Ras al-Ma’. Sea como fuere, lo cierto es que, desde la fundación de la ciudad, los andalusíes organizaron un ingenioso sistema hidráulico para dotar a las fuentes y molinos de una red de distribución de agua cuidadosamente estudiada. La leyenda atribuye a un tal Sidi Bubker al-Hadad, ingeniero especialista, el origen de estas redes.  
  
**El puente**  
Este encantador puente, pequeño y cubierto de verdor, es el único existente en Xauen. Está situado a la salida de la puerta de Lamkadem y une la orilla izquierda del barrio Esabanin con la orilla derecha, facilitando el acceso a los molinos. Unos sólidos e imponentes muros sirven de apoyo a un arco de medio punto que salva el río. Están reforzados en su base por contrafuertes achaflanados para contrarrestar los efectos de la erosión, siguiendo la técnica constructiva de los puentes de la época andalusí.  
Se ignora la fecha de construcción, pero, a juzgar por la cronología del urbanismo de la *medina* y por la forma del propio puente, se considera que puede ser de comienzos del siglo XIII/XIX, momento de máxima extensión de la *medina*.  
  
**El horno**  
Situado en la plaza del barrio Esabanin, es uno de los 15 hornos todavía activos en Xauen. Como los demás, se encuentra en una encrucijada para servir mejor a las familias que continúan amasando el pan en sus casas, y que necesitan el horno para cocerlo.  
Es de concepción sencilla: se trata de una sala rectangular de pequeñas dimensiones y no muy alta, cubierta por un tejado a dos aguas de tejas rojas del que emerge una chimenea, como es habitual en esta ciudad. En la sala está el hogar, situado en un rincón; una plataforma, sobre la que se colocan las planchas con el pan de los clientes, y un espacio para almacenar la leña.  
Las paredes son de adobe, con el enrasado de ladrillo, material que se utiliza también en los pies derechos de la puerta. Las paredes tienen tragaluces para la ventilación, y hay una puerta para el acceso y la iluminación.

fr.name: Quartier Essabanine: moulin, pont, four
description:
**Moulin**  
  
Le moulin se situe sur la rive gauche du quartier relié à l’autre rive par le pont. Son architecture utilise un volume très simple. Une chambre principale de forme rectangulaire est divisée en deux niveaux: un rez-de-chaussée, où se trouve la meule, et un sous-sol qui contient la machinerie, et dont les deux murs latéraux sont percés de baies pour permettre le passage de la rigole. La meule est en effet actionnée par un axe à hélices qui tourne sous l’effet de la force motrice de l’eau.  
Il est difficile de dater de façon exacte cette bâtisse, tout comme les trois autres moulins, encore en fonction, qui ont également été construits en amont de la source Ras al-Ma’.  
Seule certitude, on doit aux réfugiés andalous la mise en place, dès la fondation de la ville, d’un ingénieux système hydraulique permettant de doter les fontaines et les moulins d’un réseau d’eau soigneusement étudié. La légende attribue à un certain Sidi Boubker al-Hadad, ingénieur de son métier, l’organisation de ces réseaux.  
  
  
**Pont**  
  
Ce charmant petit ouvrage, couvert de verdure, est le seul pont de Chefchaouen. Situé à la sortie de la porte de Lamkadem, il relie la rive droite du quartier Essabanine à la rive gauche, et facilite le passage vers les moulins. Des murs solides et imposants servent de support à l’arche en plein cintre qui enjambe la rivière. Ils sont renforcés à leur base de contreforts à pans coupés pour contrecarrer les effets de l’érosion, selon la technique de construction des ponts de l’époque andalouse.  
On ignore la date d’édification de cet ouvrage, mais si l’on en juge par la chronologie de l’urbanisme de la médina et le mode de construction, on peut approximativement le dater, au plus tard, au début du XIIIe/XIXe siècle, au moment de l’extension maximale de la médina.  
  
  
**Four**  
  
Situé sur la place du quartier Essabanine, il est l’un des quinze fours encore en activité à Chefchaouen. Comme tous les autres, il se trouve au croisement des voies du quartier, pour mieux desservir les ménages qui continuent à pétrir leur pain dans leur demeure, et qui ont besoin de cet équipement de service pour le faire cuire.  
Son plan est simple. Une salle rectangulaire de petite dimension, de faible hauteur, couverte d’un toit à tuiles rouges à double pente d’où émerge une cheminée, comme cela est la règle dans cette ville, renferme le foyer, et une plate-forme sur laquelle sont posées les planches à pain des clients. Un espace est réservé au stockage du bois.  
Les murs sont en pisé avec les arases de briques utilisées également dans les pieds droits de la porte. Ils sont percés de lucarnes, pour assurer la ventilation, et d’une porte pour l’accès et l’éclairage.

de.name: Ehem. Damenstift (heute Herz-Jesu-Kloster) mit Stiftskirche (heute Herz-Jesu-Kirche)
description: Der unregelmäßige Grundriss des Stiftes ist geprägt von den Fundamenten bzw. den einbezogenen Bauteilen der vormaligen landesfürstlichen Burg Sparberegg. Im Zentrum steht ein zweigeschossiger Renaissance-Kreuzgang über fast quadratischem Grundriss, an den im Westen die Klosterkirche, ein Längsbau, und im Osten die unregelmäßigen, von der Burg übernommenen Bauteile der Stiftseinrichtungen anschließen. Der dreigeschossige Komplex begrenzt den Stiftsplatz, gegen den sich auch die Kirchenfassade ausrichtet, nach Südosten.

Das Damenstift in Hall, ein bedeutender vierflügeliger Baukomplex der Spätrenaissance über den Fundamenten einer mittelalterlichen Burg, geht auf die Gründung Erzherzog Ferdinands II. (1529-1595) zurück. Auch die Stiftskirche, ein Saalbau mit eingezogenem Chor, stammt aus dieser ersten Phase (1567-70), doch wurde ihre ursprüngliche Stuckausstattung später in reichen frühbarocken Formen ersetzt.
artist: Erzherzogin Magdalena von Österreich (1532-1590, Gründerin und erste Fürstäbtissin) / Damenstift Hall

Stiftskirche:  
Architektur: Giovanni Lucchese (?-1581)  
Stuck: Onofrius Weigl  
Stiftsgebäude:  
Giovanni und Alberto Lucchese  
Sommerhaus:  
Architektur: Simon Gremblich  
Fresken: Kaspar Waldmann (1657–1720)
history: Für den 1566 gegründeten Damenstiftsorden ließ Erzherzogin Magdalena, eine Schwester Erzherzog Ferdinands II., 1567-1569 Stiftsgebäude und Kirche von Hall an Stelle einer landesfürstlichen Burg und Münzprägestätte errichten. Die Weihe erfolgte 1560. Die Stiftskirche, 1567-1570 von Giovanni Luchese erbaut, wurde 1629-36 durch Onofrius Weigl aus München neu stukkiert und nach dem Erdbeben von 1670 erneuert. Der Turmabschluss datiert von 1681, der Fassadenstuck wurde 1691/92 hinzugefügt. 1783 erfolgte die Aufhebung, 1912 wurden die Gebäude dem Kloster der Schwestern vom Herzen Jesu überlassen.
keywords: Damenstift; Spätrenaissance; Frühbarock; Felderstuck;

en.name: Former endowment for ladies of rank (today Sacred Heart Convent) with collegiate church (today Sacred Heart Church)
description: The irregular ground plan of the convent is shaped by the foundations, i.e. the architectural elements incorporated from the former princely castle of Sparberegg. At the centre is a two-storey Renaissance cloister on a virtually quadratic ground plan, with the convent church adjoining to the west, a longitudinal building, and to the east the irregular architectural elements of the endowment building adopted from the castle. The three-storey complex forms the perimeter of the convent square, also bordered by the church façade facing southeast.

The endowment for ladies of rank, an important four-winged complex of the late Renaissance built on the foundations of a medieval castle, was founded by Archduke Ferdinand II (1529–95). The collegiate church, a hall building with retracted choir, originates from this first period (1567–70), however its original stuccowork was later replaced by rich Early Baroque forms.
type: Secular architecture (endowment, convent building) and ecclesiastical architecture (former collegiate church)
artist: Archduchess Magdalena of Austria (1532–1590, founder and first Princess Abbess) / Noble Convent of Hall

Collegiate church, architecture: Giovanni Lucchese (?–1581); stuccowork: Onofrius Weigl \[n.d.\]. Endowment building: Giovanni Lucchese, Alberto Lucchese \[n.d.\]; portal, attributed: Alexander Colin \[n.d.\].  
Summerhouse, architecture: Simon Gremblich \[n.d.\]; frescos: Kaspar Waldmann (1657–1720)
history: For the endowment for ladies of rank Archduchess Magdalena, a sister of Archduke Ferdinand II, erected the endowment building and church of Hall on the site of a princely castle and mint between 1567 and 1569. The consecration took place in 1560. The collegiate church, built between 1567 and 1570 by Giovanni Lucchese, acquired new stuccowork, executed by Onofrius Weigl of the Munich school, between 1629 and 1636, which was subsequently renewed following the earthquake of 1670. The spire dates from 1681. The façade stucco was added in 1691/92. In 1783 followed the annulment and in 1912 the building was bequeathed to the Convent of the Sisters of the Sacred Heart.
keywords: Endowment for ladies of rank; Late Renaissance; Early Baroque, panelled stucco

en.name: Construction Site at Shellal

short_description: In 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont, an Italian diplomat, visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several pictures of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were going to be submerged by the water. He published some of them on the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

en.name: The museum of 'rare possessions'
names: Fatma Ismail’s Palace Museum at the Agricultural museum; The Antiquity Collection Museum
short_description: This building was once the villa of Fatma Ismail, daughter of Khedive Ismail, and now it is a museum that houses over 500 rare pieces of art dating to the late 19th and early 20th centuries. When the palace was built and then restored, Egyptian architecture was being influenced by the European trends of the time (Italian and French). Italian and French architects were designing and building edifices for the Egyptian elite.
history: Princess Fatma Ismail (1853–1920) was one of Khedive Ismail's daughters. She married Prince Tusun ibn Muhammad Sa`id Pasha, alderman of Egypt, in 1871. She is distinguished from her sisters by her philanthropic contributions to culture and science. Princess Fatma took the initiative of dismissing the university from its financial crisis by providing it with an endowment. She also donated jewellery to provide the university with much-needed cash and land for the campus to be built on. She participated in laying the foundation stone of the university. She passed away before seeing the university built.

en.name: Islamic Alenquer
description:
In the Islamic period, the small town of Alenquer, built close to a navigable stretch of the River Tagus, was an integral part of the network of urban centres linked to Lisbon by an intense river traffic. With Arruda, Xira, Azambuja and Benavente, it shared the bread-producing region of Ballata, whose products were sold in the capital, benefiting and controlling all the trade routes from Coruche, Tomar or Santarém.  
Because of a lack of archaeological information, it is not possible to infer that there was any structure here prior to the buildings evidently erected in the Low Middle Ages, particularly those dating from the period of the Renaissance, which left the region with a number of impressive monuments. On the walls of the *medina* – an enclosed and heavily populated area of roughly five hectares – a monumental fortified tower can be seen, the base of which would almost certainly have been part of the Muslim defensive system.  
Unlike the castle, whose foundations may perhaps be revealed only by future excavations, it is possible today for people to visit the city walls and the fortified tower associated with them. There is a small archaeological museum with a collection of ceramic artefacts, mainly from the 14th century, although there are also some from the Islamic period.

es.name: Alenquer islámica
description:
En tiempos del Islam, la pequeña ciudad de Alenquer, ubicada junto a un canal navegable del Tajo, formaba parte de la red de centros urbanos unidos a Lisboa por un intenso tráfico fluvial. Con Arruda, Xira, Azambuja y Benavente, se repartía las tierras de cereales de Ballata que traían a la capital sus productos, y aprovechaba y controlaba asimismo las rutas comerciales que nacían en Coruche, Tomar o Santarém.  
Por falta de información arqueológica, no puede adivinarse ninguna estructura anterior a las notables intervenciones de la Baja Edad Media y, sobre todo, del Renacimiento, que imprimieron al lugar cierta monumentalidad. En el amurallamiento de la *medina* —un área intramuros densamente poblada que ronda las 5 ha— se observa una monumental torre coraza, cuyos cimientos pudieron pertenecer al sistema defensivo de época musulmana.  
Al contrario que en el castillo, donde solo una futura excavación arqueológica podrá mostrar los cimientos, hoy se pueden visitar las cortinas de la muralla y la torre coraza unida a ellas. Un pequeño museo arqueológico guarda objetos de cerámica, principalmente del siglo XIV y algunos de época islámica.

en.name: Bottle
description: Typical Iranian glass bottles from the fourth and fifth centuries AH / eleventh and twelfth centuries AD usually have a specific decoration on the entire surface except for the neck. These motifs include various designs such as the honeycomb, the rosette, or the curly vegetal pattern. This free-blown pale green glass bottle has a bulbous body, a long tubular neck with a flared opening, and a splayed trumpet foot. Its body is decorated with a moulded band of scrolled motifs, raised dots and a plain band with applied manganese trails around the shoulder.

en.name: The Arrival of the Mahmal
description: The painting is after is after Konstantin Makovsky’s 1876 work, ‘The Arrival of the Holy Carpet in Cairo’ (during this period the mahmal was often referred to as ‘the holy carpet’, or ‘le tapis sacré’ in French). It is not clear whether de Mango had seen Makovsky’s work or if he had access to the original photograph from which the painting was made. However, we do know that de Mango spent time in Cairo and was greatly inspired by life in the Middle East. An engraving of Makovsky’s work by R. Brendamour also appeared in a German periodical of 1893, and de Mango may have been aware of that version as well.

en.name: Cathedral
description: Building work began on the Cathedral during the reign of D. Afonso V, on the site of a previous 12th-century church. As it was still incomplete when D. Manuel I visited Silves in 1499, he ordered it to be rebuilt on a larger scale, as he considered the one being built to be far too small. The dividing arches of the aisles were erected at that time, as well as the side walls of the main vessel, the façade, and the wooden roof before the transept. The architecture, although sober and simple in line, is well designed, quite different from the more popular, exuberant decorative styles of the parish churches in the region. It has three aisles, divided by pillars supporting the wooden roof, and linking the main vessel of the church by a large transept to the triple apse in a traditional 15th-century Gothic style, on the lines of Batalha.

ar.name: لوح خزفي مزجَّج عليه صورة الكعبة.
description:
تم استخدام أصبغة زرقاء وخضراء وحمراء على خلفية بيضاء. يؤطر القطعة الخزفية المكونة من بلاطة واحدة حاشية ملونة بالأسود على شكل سلسلة من الرسوم فوق خلفية زرقاء. وثمة حاشية أخرى مزينة بسعيفات زرقاء اللون تنتهي عند قمة اللوح الخزفي متخذة شكل محراب. أما زاويتا المحراب فمزخرفتان بسعيفات مشطورة ومتشابكة فوق خلفية زرقاء. وفي مركز المحراب، وعلى خلفية زرقاء أيضاً، ثمة رسم لقوصرة متماثلة التصميم مزينة بالأرابسك، وتحتها نقش من ثلاثة أسطر كتبت بالخط النسخي الأسود. يتألف النقش من الآية 96 وجزء من الآية 97 من سورة آل عمران (رقم 3): "إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبَارَكاً وَهُدًى لِّلْعَالَمِينَ {96} فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّـنَاتٌ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِناً." تحت هذا النص يوجد رسم للمسجد الحرام ضمن مستطيل ملون بالأزرق والأخضر. وفي وسط المسجد الحرام تُرى الكعبة مميزة بفناء ذي أروقة. المباني المختلفة والبوابات والمقامات وسبل الماء داخل الأروقة، جميعها محدَّدة ومعرَّفة بأسمائها.  
  
قدِّمت الأماكن والمدن المقدسة (مكة والمدينة) في الكتب منذ العهود الأولى للإسلام، ودُعِّمت بالرسوم. ويوجد رسوم تفصيلية لهذه الأماكن في شهادات الحج التي صدرت خصوصاً في العهد الأيوبي، وتحتل مكانة هامة في مجموعة المتحف. تبدأ هذه الوثائق بشعار الخليفة الذي صدرت في عهده، وتعرض لوحات مرسومة لجبل عرفات والمزدلفة والحرم الشريف والمدينة والقدس أيضاً. في الفن العثماني، هناك صور مشابهة لأماكن مقدسة رسمت لشهادات الحج. منذ مطلع القرن 10 / 16، وُجدت صور للمسجد الحرام في مكة مرسومة على بلاطات خزفية في بعض المساجد.

يُفترض أن يكون هذا اللوح الخزفي منتجاً في ازنيق، لمسجد نسليشاه سلطان، في أدرنه قابي باستنبول. تَمثَّل غَرَضُ الألواح الخزفية، المُزيَّنة بصورة الكعبة، بإحداث الإحساس بحضور الكعبة، التي هي البقعة الأقدس عند المسلمين، أثناء أداء الصلوات في المسجد.
keywords: إزنك؛ خزف؛ كعبة.

en.name: Ceramic tile with a picture of the Ka‘ba.
description:
Blue, green and red pigments have been used on a white background. A border with a chain-motif, drawn in black on a blue background, frames the single-piece tile. This is enriched by a second border made up of blue palmettes which ends at the top of the tile in a *mihrab* shape. The *mihrab*'s two corners are decorated with interlacing *rumi* (split-palmette) motifs on a dark-blue background. In the middle of the *mihrab*, also on a dark-blue ground, is a symmetrical pediment motif decorated with arabesques, at the bottom of which is an inscription in three rows of black *naskhi* script. The inscription contains *sura* 3, verses 96–7 of the Qur'an: 'Lo! the first Sanctuary appointed for mankind was that at Becca \[Mecca\] a blessed place, a guidance to the peoples; Wherein are plain memorials (of Allah's guidance); the place where Abraham stood up to pray; and whosoever entereth it is safe.' Below this text, the Masjid al-Haram is depicted within a rectangle drawn in green and blue. The Ka'ba is shown in the middle of the Masjid al-Haram, recognisable by its porticoed courtyard. The various buildings, gates, sacred spots (*maqams*), and water-wells located within the porticoes are represented and identified with their names.  
  
Introducing the holy cities of Islam (Mecca and Medina) and the sacred sites therein with books, and reinforcing this introduction with pictures, is seen from the early period of Islam. Detailed pictures of these holy places were put in pilgrimage certificates, which were made especially in the Ayyubid period, and which have an important place in the Museum's collection. These documents begin with the banner of the caliph of the time and show painted images of Mount Arafat, Muzdalifa, the Sacred Enclosure (al-Haram al-Sharif), Medina, and even Jerusalem. Similar pictures of the holy places were made for pilgrimage certificates in Ottoman art. Beginning at the end of the 10th / 16th century images of the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca are also found depicted on tiles in certain mosques.

This tile panel is assumed to have been produced at Iznik for the Mosque of Neslişah Sultan in Edirnekapı, Istanbul. The purpose of tile panels depicting the Ka'ba was to feel its presence, the most sacred shrine of Islam, during prayer at the mosque.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
dates: Hegira last quarter of the 10th century / AD 16th century.
keywords: Ka‘ba; Iznik; Tile
materials: Iznik tile of white clay, with a painting of the Ka‘ba in underglaze.
tags: Iznik tile of white clay, with a painting of the Ka‘ba in underglaze.
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

es.name: Azulejo con la Kaaba pintada.
description:
Azulejo con fondo blanco y pintado con pigmentos azules, verdes y rojos. Posee un borde formado por motivos encadenados dibujados en negro sobre fondo azul. Este borde está adornado con un segundo borde de palmetas azules que culminan en la parte superior del azulejo en forma de *mihrab*. Las dos esquinas de este *mihrab* están decoradas con motivos *rumi* (semipalmetas) entrelazados sobre un fondo azul oscuro. En medio del *mihrab*, también sobre un fondo azul oscuro, hay un frontispicio simétrico decorado con arabescos, con una inscripción de tres líneas en letra *nasji* de color negro en la parte inferior. La inscripción contiene los versículos 96-97 de la sura 3 del Corán: "He aquí el primer santuario designado para la humanidad, el de Becca \[la Meca\], lugar sagrado, guía de los pueblos. Aquí se encuentran las evidentes señales \[de la guía de Allah\]; éste fue el lugar donde Abraham se detuvo a rezar; y quienquiera que entre en él estará seguro". Debajo de este texto aparece pintada la mezquita del Haram dentro de un rectángulo verde y azul. La Kaaba está en el centro de la mezquita y se reconoce por su patio con arcos. Los diversos edificios, puertas, lugares sagrados *(maqam)* y los pozos de agua situados dentro de los pórticos están representados e identificados con sus nombres.  
Desde los inicios del Islam, es común encontrar descripciones de las ciudades santas (La Meca y Medina) y de sus lugares sagrados tanto en los libros como en sus ilustraciones. Se redactaban descripciones detalladas en los certificados de peregrinaje, sobre todo durante el periodo ayyubí. Estos documentos constituyen una parte importante de los fondos del museo. Comienzan con la insignia del califa de la época y muestran imágenes pintadas del monte Arafat, Muzdalifa, al-Haram al-Sharif, Medina e, incluso, Jerusalén. En los certificados de peregrinaje otomanos se encuentran imágenes similares de los lugares sagrados. A finales del siglo X / XVI empiezan a encontrarse representaciones de la Masyid al-Haram de La Meca en los azulejos de algunas mezquitas.

Azulejos producido en Iznik para la mezquita de Neslişah en Edirnekapı (Estambul). El objetivo de los azulejos que representan la Kaaba era hacer sentir la presencia del santuario más sagrado del Islam durante las oraciones en la mezquita.
holder: Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico.
dates: Último cuarto del siglo X de la Hégira / XVI d. C.
keywords: Kaaba; Iznik; azulejo.
materials: Azulejo de Iznik de arcilla blanca, con ilustración de la Kaaba bajo vidriado.
tags: Azulejo de Iznik de arcilla blanca, con ilustración de la Kaaba bajo vidriado.

fr.name: Carreau de céramique à représentation de la Kaaba.
description: Carreau de céramique vernissée peint aux pigments noirs, rouges et verts sur fond blanc. Une bordure ornée d'un motif de chaîne en noir sur fond bleu forme un cadre, enrichi d'une seconde bordure de palmettes bleues qui se termine en *mihrab* dans la partie supérieure. Les deux angles entre la bordure et le *mihrab* sont décorés de demi-palmettes entrelacées sur fond bleu foncé. Au milieu, toujours sur fond bleu foncé, figure un fronton décoré d'arabesques à la base duquel une inscription en trois lignes reproduit les versets 96-97 de la sourate III du Coran : “La première Maison qui ait été placée pour les gens est celle de Bakka, lieu béni et chemin de droiture pour les mondes. En ce lieu sont les Signes évidents : l'endroit précis où se tenait Abraham. Celui qui y pénètre se trouve en sécurité (trad. R. Khawam).” Sous ce texte est représenté le Masjid al-Haram dans un cartouche rectangulaire vert et bleu. La Kaaba figure au centre du Masjid al-Haram, reconnaissable à sa cour entourée d'une colonnade. Les divers bâtiments, portes, lieux sacrés (*maqam*) et puits d'eau sous la colonnade sont illustrés et identifiés par leur nom.

Ce carreau de céramique est supposé avoir été fabriqué à Iznik pour la mosquée du sultan Nesli Chah à Edirnekapi, Istanbul. Le but des panneaux de céramiques représentant la Kaaba, lieu de pèlerinage le plus sacré de l’islam, était de faire sentir sa présence durant la prière à la mosquée.
holder: Musée des arts turcs et islamiques.
dates: Dernier quart du Xe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: carreaux, Kaaba, Iznik.
materials: Carreau d’Iznik en argile blanche à illustration peinte de la Kaaba.

tr.name: Kabe Tasvirli Çini Pano.
description:
Beyaz zemin üzerine mavi, yeşil ve kırmızı renkler kullanılmıştır. Lacivert üzerine siyahla tahrirli zencirek motifli bir bordür ile çevrelenmiştir. Bu çerçeveyi mavi renkli palmetlerden oluşan, panonun üst kısmında mihrap şeklinde tamamlanan ikinci bir bordür zenginleştirmektedir. Mihrabın iki köşesi lacivert zemin üzerine yapılan geçme Rumilerle bezenmiştir. Mihrabın ortasında yine lacivert zemin üzerine dilimli Rûmilerle bezeli simetrik bir alınlık ve bu alınlığın altında siyah renk ve nesih hat ile yazılmış üç satırlık bir metin kısmı yer almaktadır. Metinde, Kur'an'dan III: 96-97 ayetleri yazılıdır. Bu ayetler; “Şüphesiz ki, insanlar yararına yeryüzünde ilk konulan ibadet evi alemler için mübarek olan ve doğru yolu gösteren Mekke'deki mabeddir. Onda açık ayetler, İbrahim makamı vardır. Kim oraya girerse her türlü saldırıdan güvencededir,” mealindedir. Bu metnin altında, mavi ve yeşil renklerle yapılmış bir dikdörtgenin içinde Mescid-ül Haram'ın resmi yapılmıştır. Revaklı bir avlu içine çizilerek tanıtılan Mescid-ül Haram'ın ortasında Kâbe yer almakta, revakların içinde bulunan tüm bina ve kapılar, makamlar, zemzem kuyularının resimleri çizilerek ve isimleri yazılarak tanıtılmaktadır.  
  
İslam dininin kutsal yerleri olan Mekke, Medine şehirleri ve bu şehirlerdeki kutsal makamları, camileri, kitaplarda tanıtmak, bu tanıtımı yaparken de resimlerle bir kez daha vurgulamak erken İslam devirlerinden itibaren görülmektedir. özellikle Eyyubi döneminde hazırlanmış olan ve müze koleksiyonunda da önemli bir yeri bulunan hac vekaletnamelerinde, bu kutsal mekanların resimleri detaylı olarak yapılmıştır. Dönem halifesinin sancağı ile başlayan bu belgelerde, Arafat dağı, Muzdalifa, Mescid-ül Haram, Medine ve hatta Kudüs'ün de resimlendirildiği bilinmektedir. Osmanlı sanatında da benzerleri yapılan hac vekaletnamelerinde de kutsal yerler resimle tanıtılmıştır. Mekke'deki Mescid-ül Haram'ın çini üzerine yapılan resimleri 10. / 16. yüzyılın sonlarından itibaren bazı camilerde de görülmektedir.

Neslişah Sultan'ın Edirnekapı'daki camisi için İznik'te üretildiği kabul edilmektedir. Kâbe tasvirli çini panoların yapılmasındaki amaç, İslam dininin en kutsal makamı olan Kâbe'yi cami içinde ibadet ederken de hissedebilmekti.
keywords: Çini; Kabe; İznik
materials: Beyaz hamurlu, sıraltı tekniğinde yapılmış Kâbe tasvirli, tek parça İznik çinisidir.
tags: Beyaz hamurlu, sıraltı tekniğinde yapılmış Kâbe tasvirli, tek parça İznik çinisidir.

ar.name: ديوان بليغ
description: يتألف هذا الديوان من أشعار محمد أمين بليغ وهو شارع تركي غير معروف نسبيا الذي ينتمي لطبقة العلماء ويعمل كقاضي في بلدات متعددة في البلقان. وبالرغم من الاعتقاد أنه قد حاز على قليل من الاهتمام في عصره فإن هذه النسخة من ديوانه قد أنتجت فقط بعد خمسين عاما من وفاته في عام 1174 هجري - 1760 ميلادي). وافتتاحية المخطوطة لها عنوان مذهب في طراز متأثر بالطراز الأوربي الشائع في ذلك الزمن.

en.name: Divan of Belig
description: This *divan* consists of the poems of Mehmed Emin Belig, a relatively unknown Turkish poet who belonged to the *‘ulama* and served as a *qadi* in various Balkan towns. Although he is thought to have been little appreciated in his time, this fine copy of his *divan* was produced just fifty years after his death in AH 1174 / AD 1760. The manuscript opens with a heading illuminated in the European-influenced style popular at the time.
