en.name: '1196 - Arrivée du train a Jaffa'
description: This is a loose albumen print made from an original negative  by Bonfils. It shows a train at the Jaffa railway station with passengers ready to embark. Jaffa can be seen in the distance."Bonfils" and "1196 - Arrivée du train a Jaffa" on the print. From the Finn collection.  The track is the original metre-guage track and so the photograph is dated to before AH 1332 / AD 1914,  and as everything looks new, probably quite close to the date of construction in AH 1310 / AD 1892.   The train seems to consist of one of the Baldwin 2-6-0's locomotives, a couple of vans and two of the bogie carriages - a quite typical train combination.  The people in the picture may well have been station employees, posing for the photographer.
keywords: Jaffa, Jaffa to Jerusalem railway,  railway station,  locomotive, steam.
tags: Jaffa, Jaffa to Jerusalem railway, railway station, locomotive, steam.

ar.name: مزهرية ذات مقبضين.
description: مزهرية ذات مقبضين، قاعدتها على شكل قرص، رقبتها طويلة، زخرفتها ملونة وملمعة باللون الأحمر الغامق، على أرضية مينا بلون أبيض عاجي. زينت برسوم نباتية ذات بريق معدني كما هو معروف عن القطع التي أنتجت بعد الفترة الأسبانية العربية. نجد في قعر جسم المزهرية رسماً على شكل طائرين معروفين باسم "باردالوت" في مدينة فلينسيا، وقد رسما بطريقة مبسطة بواسطة حزمة من الخطوط،  كتعبير مميز لأسلوب وذوق ومستوى صنع هذه القطعة. كما يدل على ذلك أيضاً شكل المزهرية حيث أن عدة خطوط عريضة ذات بريق معدني تحدد الأقسام المختلفة للمزهرية.
تنتمي هذه المزهرية إلى صنف ضخم من الأواني المنتجة في جهة فالانسيا (إسبانيا)، والمزخرفة بأشكال ذات أسلوب مميز جدا.
holder: متحف الحضارات  | متحف الفن الشرقي جوزيبي توتشي
dynasty: مصدر إنتاجه يعود إلى فن المدجنين
keywords: بريق معدني؛ مزهرية؛ فن المدجنين.
partner: متحف الحضارات  | متحف الفن الشرقي جوزيبي توتشي

en.name: Two-handled pot.
description: Two-handled long-neck pot with a foot-ring. The decoration, painted in intense red lustre on a cream-white tin glaze, consists of solid-lustre plant motifs, which was common in later Hispano-Moorish products. The dotted base of the body of the pot depicts two typical birds, known as Valencian 'pardalots', painted in a characteristic style consisting of groups of lines. 'Pardalots' and 'grotesque lions' are unusual in the decorative repertoire of this type of piece, as is the shape of the pot, the different parts of which are outlined with thick bands of solid lustre.

This pot belongs to a large group of objects produced in Valencia that were decorated with typical motifs and styles, although the birds (known as ‘pardalots’) and grotesque lions are unusual in this type of piece, as is the shape of the pot.
holder: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art “Giuseppe Tucci”
keywords: Pot; lustre; Mudéjar art; figurative decoration
partner: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art

es.name: Jarra.
description:
Jarra de cuello alto con doble asa y pie circular. La decoración, pintada en reflejo metálico rojo intenso sobre vidriado estannífero blanco crema, presenta un fondo de decoración vegetal de lustre compacto, como es característico en los productos hispano-moriscos más tardíos. Sobre el fondo punteado del cuerpo de la jarra hay pintados dos típicos pájaros, los llamados *pardalots* valencianos, dibujados con la característica estilización en trazos agrupados.  
*Pardalots* y “leones grotescos” son rasgos distintivos del repertorio ornamental de la serie a la que pertenece esta pieza, como también lo es la forma misma de la jarra, cuyas diferentes partes se marcan mediante franjas gruesas de reflejo compacto.
Esta jarra pertenece a una amplia serie de objetos producidos en talleres valencianos y decorados con motivos y estilos bastante usuales.
holder: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”
partner: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental

fr.name: Vase à deux anses.
description: Vase à deux anses, sur pied en forme de disque et à haut col. Le décor, peint au lustre rouge foncé sur glaçure stannifère crème, présente des motifs végétaux entièrement lustrés, comme c'est généralement le cas pour les pièces les plus tardives de la production hispano-mauresque. Sur la panse du vase, dont le fond est orné de pointillés, sont peints deux oiseaux typiques, appelés “pardalots” de Valence ; leur dessin, stylisé, utilise un motif caractéristique constitué de faisceaux de lignes. “Pardalots ” et “lions grotesques” constituent une note particulière dans le répertoire décoratif de la classe à laquelle appartient cette pièce ; il en est de même pour la forme du vase, dont les différentes parties sont soulignées par de larges bandes d'un lustre compact.
Ce vase appartient à une vaste classe d'objets produits dans la région de Valence (Espagne), décorés de motifs d'un style très caractéristique.
holder: Musée des civilisations | Musée d'art oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”
dates: XIe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIIe siècle J.-C.).
place: Espagne, atelier de la région de Valence.
keywords: vase ; lustre ; art mudéjar
partner: Musée des civilisations | Musée d'art oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”

it.name: Vaso a due anse.
description: Vaso a due anse su piede a disco ed alto collo. La decorazione, dipinta a lustro rosso intenso su smalto stannifero bianco-crema, presenta decorazioni vegetali interamente campite a lustro, come è consuetudine per i prodotti più tardi della produzione ispano-moresca. Sul fondo puntinato del corpo del vaso sono dipinti due tipici uccelli, i così detti “pardalot” valenzani, disegnati secondo una caratteristica stilizzazione a fasci di linee. “Pardalot” e “leoni grotteschi” costituiscono comunque una nota distintiva nel repertorio decorativo della classe di cui fa parte questo esemplare come pure la forma del vaso, nel quale grosse fasce a lustro compatto sottolineano le diverse parti.
Il vaso appartiene ad una vasta classe di oggetti prodotti in ambito valenzano, decorati mediante motivi e stili assai tipici.
holder: Museo delle Civiltà | Museo d’arte orientale “Giuseppe Tucci”
keywords: Vaso; lustro; arte mudéjar; arte figurativa
partner: Museo delle Civiltà | Museo d’arte orientale “Giuseppe Tucci”

en.name: *Maada*
description: The *maada* is a traditional water distribution device used in Moroccan irrigation systems to allocate water shares fairly among rights-holders. Constructed of stone or wood, the system channels water into precisely measured outlets that correspond to established rights, often determined by ancient legal texts or community agreements. The museum’s model reproduces this system at a smaller scale so visitors can understand how communities combined hydraulic engineering with social contracts to regulate a scarce resource. The *maada* reflects the sophistication of traditional Moroccan water law (*qanun al-maʾ*), which was deeply rooted in equity, transparency, and sustainability. By ensuring exact water allocation, it minimized conflicts and symbolised the sacred responsibility of water stewardship. The display preserves not only the technical ingenuity of past engineers but also the social and ethical dimensions of water management in Morocco’s arid regions.
holder: Mohammed VI Museum of Water Civilisation
keywords: maada; water distributor; irrigation; Marrakech; hydraulic heritage; water law
materials: Wood, clay, and stone elements (replica of traditional systems)
tags: Wood, clay, and stone elements (replica of traditional systems)
partner: Mohammed VI Museum for the Civilisation of Water in Morocco

en.name: Belt of *monistra* – tiny beads
short_description: Unlike the metal jewellery worn in towns, which was produced by goldsmiths, jewellery and other articles of adornment from rural areas were made by women themselves, mostly of canvas, *monistra* (tiny beads in varied colours) and by use of the fruits of the nature, flowers, etc.
keywords: Monistra – tiny beads in different colours; costume; accessories

de.name: Die vier letzten Dinge
description: Wegen Johann Nepomuks Rolle als Beichtheiligem ist die Bedeutung des Bußsakraments vor allem im Eingangsbereich durch die Häufung von vier Beichtstühlen hervorgehoben. Deren dramatisch gestenreiches Skulpturenprogramm behandelt die Vier Letzten Dinge: Tod, Gericht, Hölle und Himmel, repräsentiert durch die hl. Bruno, Hieronymus, Petrus sowie einen Seligen.
place: Trennwand von Vestibül und Laienraum, beidseitig über den Beichtstühlen

en.name: The Four Last Things
description: Due to John of Nepomuk’s role as the patron saint of the sacrament of confession, the significance of penance is emphasized most notably by a grouping of four confessionals in the vestibule. Their dramatic array of sculptural depictions, being rich in gesture, pertain to the “Four Last Things”: death, judgement, Heaven and Hell. These are represented by the saints Bruno, Hieronymus and Peter, as well as by a beatified believer.
place: The partition wall between the vestibule and the nave, both sides above the confessionals.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Black Cauldron
description:
The Black Cauldron, which is considered sacred by Bektashi devotees and the Janissary Corps, is situated on the large hearth at the axis of the entrance door. The Black Cauldron was constructed by fusing six substantial pieces of forged copper. Four distinct handles, two large and two small, are positioned on the exterior of the vessel. To grieve the martyrdom of Hz. Hussein – son of Hz. Ali, grandson of Hz. Muhammad – and his relatives in Karbala on Friday, 10 Muharram of the 61st year of the Hijra, Alevi-Bektashis observed a period of mourning. This was followed by a fast of mourning on the days of 1–12 Muharram, during which time the pain of those who were martyred was shared and the descendants of Ehlibeyt were commemorated. This practice continues today.  
In observance of the 10 Muharram, the Alevi-Bektashis engage in a water fast, which concludes at noon on the 10th day. The 10th day of Muharram is commemorated as Ashura, a period of solemn reflection and mourning. Ashura is observed as an important value that ensures social solidarity and unity. It is served to guests, neighbours and the needy.  
During the period when the Külliye was operating as a lodge, the Ashura (dessert)in question was cooked and distributed in the Black Cauldron Currently, people oberve this ritual in their homes and concludes with a visit to the Külliye.

en.name: Qal‘at Shayzar
description:
Based on the layout of the mountainous escarpment on which it stands, this Arab citadel is located 25 km north-west of Hama. Approximately 50 m wide and 450 m long, the citadel dominates the narrow passageway between the River Orontes and the Ghab Plains, on the road between Damascus and Antakiyya, through Middle Syria. The area witnessed long and violent struggles as well as two devastating earthquakes during the medieval period.  
The first mention of a fortress at Shayzar dates to the Hellenistic period when the site was known as Larissa. During the Byzantine reoccupation of northern Syria and the costal mountains, at the end of the 4th/10th century, the fort was developed.  
It was the princely family of the Banu Munqidh, a local Arab tribe, who took control over the citadel and the surrounding area in the 474/1081. Usama ibn Munqidh, the medieval warrior whose memoirs have survived as a precious record of these turbulent times grew up in this citadel, where he probably penned his diary. The citadel suffered massive damage in an earthquake of 552/1157 and many of the Munqidh family perished, at which point Nur al-Din supervised its restoration, which he renewed after another earthquake in 565/1170. After Nur al-Din’s death in 560/1174, integration of Shayzar Citadel into the Ayyubid leadership saw that the surviving members of the Banu Munqidh continued to play a chivalrous role in the fight against the Crusaders and the defence of the Ayyubid Dynasty. It remained a strong defensive fort and, following the devastation of the Mongol attacks, the Mamluk Sultan al-Zahir Baybars reinforced it along with many other fortresses in Syria.  
The most important remnant of the citadel is its impressive entrance supported by a well-constructed stone glacis on its north side and a deep ditch to the south. Large, strong towers once stood along its 1 km surrounding wall. Evidence of storage areas and a two-storey residential building at the far south of the citadel are in evidence. This, the south tower, is the main construction dating to Nur al-Din’s era and exemplifies the massive fortified-building type of the period with its two still-standing storeys and decorated façade built with wellhewn, large limestone. A monumental inscription made on the original stone was added under the reign of the Ayyubid ruler of Aleppo, and patron of the great Citadel of Aleppo, al-Zahir Ghazi, dated 631 (1233).  
Perfectly formed and decorated arrow slits and machicolations defend this tower along with the other towers in the citadel, revealing the architectural mastery of the Arabs in military construction. Thus, **Qal’at Shayzar** is a fine example of medieval Islamic fortifications, especially in that it was a site never conquered by the Crusaders.

en.name: Unicellular House: 'Kukh'
description: This kind of habitation provides only the most basic functions of a house: shelter and warmth. It has no outdoor spaces, and the windows and doors are generally very small. Even today, domestic or social activities (such as cooking, washing, eating, relaxing, working or receiving guests) in these houses generally take place outdoors, either outside the front door or to the side of the house under a canopy or in the shade of a tree. The interior was not divided in any particular way, and divisions between rooms were traditionally created my movable objects, such as cabinets, curtains or wooden partitions. In the *kukh*s of today, solid walls have taken their place.
history: The *kukh* is a modest house. It was the basic model for a traditional house in the agricultural suburbs of Beirut. *Kukh*s were popular until the mid-19th century and were generally inhabited by farmers and their families. They also functioned as temporary shelter for livestock or domestic animals.
keywords: Kukh; Unicellular; House; Architecture; Typology

en.name: Ewer and basin
description: A ewer with a round base and pear-shaped body, ornamented with circular bands, beginning with vegetal motifs in the form of inverted crenellations, followed by a band inscribed with Persian script interspersed with round medallions containing human figures, followed by a wider band decorated with human figures, mythical creatures and birds, alternating with lobed medallions bearing Persian inscriptions and round medallions with human figures. The upper body ends with arched panels filled with depictions of humans, birds and mythical creatures. These bands are interspersed with small frames ornamented with meandering vegetal scrolls sprouting trifoliate leaves. The neck begins with a ridge and widens towards the round mouth, decorated with lobed, pointed-arch motifs enclosing human and animal figures, along with floral rosettes of many petals. The curved handle extends from the lower body to the mouth. The spout is missing.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum FBQ Museum
keywords: Water; ewer; bassin; copper
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

en.name: *Bayt Niyadu, Damascus*
names: Inhabitants in the courtyard demonstrating the new style of decoration and clothing
short_description: Like the Lisbuna House, Bayt Niyadu saw two major construction phases, namely, in the 18th and late 19th century. It was refurbished as so many houses between 1865 and 1872 and features marble ornamentation similar to the one in Bayt Lisbuna´s courtyard. These houses are from the layout typical "traditional" courtyard houses of the region. However, the Niyadu House became known (also on postcards) for its richness and abundance of up to date Ottoman decor. The owners expressed their Damascene modernity proudly to the outside – also in this picture: the gentlemen sports a European-style dinner jacket and the lady a mid-length skirt, teamed with a withe blouse in the latest fashion. This transformation of private forms of urban live – notice also the brand new and modern electrical lightening in the "traditional" courtyard – can be seen throughout the city and is an important example of a local expression of global modernity.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

en.name: Polish carpet
description:
Carpets in Poland were made in manufactories founded by Polish aristocrats on their own estates. This carpet belongs to the group of five stylistically homogenous objects preserved in Polish collections, which were woven probably in Niemirów or Tulczyn, in a manufactory located on the Potocki family estate.  
In the middle of the ivory-coloured central field, there is the coat of arms of the Potocki (Pilawa) and Mniszech (Mniszech) family underneath a nobleman’s crown, displayed above trophies of combat. Looking closer at the trophies, elements characteristic of the Republic of Poland and Lithuania are recognisable: two *karabelas* ‒ sabres with an open hilt and pommel, recalling an eagle’s head ‒ and two maces with spherical heads called *bulawas*, which were the attributes of *hetman*s, the highest-ranking commanders in the Polish and Lithuanian army. There are also banners and cannons. Beneath the coat of arms are bullets, gunpowder barrels and kettledrums. Thanks to the coat of arms of the Pilawa and Mniszech, it is possible to presume that the carpet was made to mark the marriage of Stanisław Szczęsny Potocki and Józefina Mniszchówna in 1774, and to decorate their manor house in Tulczyn.  
The ornamental decoration of the rug is also very interesting. The central field is decorated with isolated palmettes and roses. The wide border is tightly filled with palmettes and flowers, among which we can find irises, typical of Islamic ornamentation. Strong geometrisation of floral motifs brings to mind Caucasian carpets. It is very probable that the Potocki manufactury employed Armenians and this easily explains the Caucasian inspiration.  
The colour green is predominant in this carpet, with the addition of red, yellow, blue and emerald-green, although the colours are somewhat faded now. The wool used to knot Polish carpets was coarser and thicker than the wool used for rugs in warmer, sunnier areas of the world.
keywords: Poland; Ukraine; Niemirów; Tulczyn; Korczak; Pilawa; Potocki; Mniszech
materials: Wool (warp, weft, pile); symmetrically knotted pile (Turkish knot)

en.name: Welcoming figure
description: Glazed cobalt-blue on white *azulejos* of a welcoming figure. The character wears typical early 18th-century livery, is unarmed, and adopts a reverential attitude, his hat in hand. It is likely that the figure represents a doorkeeper in the service of the Brotherhood.
place: Entrance patio at the top of the staircase
artist: Architect unknown. Tile-Painting Master P.M.P., probably Padre Manuel Pereira [n.d.]
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Figura de Convite
description: Figura de Convite pintada a azul-cobalto sobre azulejo branco. A personagem usa um traje típico do início do século XVIII, não tem armas e adopta uma postura de convite, com o chapéu na mão. Provavelmente, a personagem representa um porteiro ao serviço da confraria.
place: Entrada do pátio, no início da escadaria
artist: Arquitecto desconhecido. Pintura de azulejos pelo Mestre P.M.P., provavelmente Padre Manuel Pereira (n.d.)

ar.name: مدرسة الصالح نجم الدين أيوب.
description:
شيدت المدرسة على جزء من القصر الشرقي الفاطمي، وجعلت لتعليم المذاهب الفقهية السنية الأربعة، وتعتبر أول مدرسة أنشئت في مصر لذلك الغرض. وقامت شجرة الدر زوجة السلطان الصالح نجم الدين بإضافة ضريح دفن فيه عام 648 هـ / 1250 م. وتكوّن بذلك مجمّعاً معمارياً أيوبياً في قلب القاهرة الفاطمية، وهو نهج جديد وأسلوب معماري متكامل اتبعه السلاطين المماليك بعد ذلك في إنشاء مجمّعاتهم المطلة على شارع المعز الذي شكل القصبة الرئيسية لمدينة القاهرة، مثل مجمع قلاوون. إلا أن المدرسة الصالحية كانت تشتمل على مدرسة وضريح فقط قبل تطوّر نظام المجمّعات في العصرالمملوكي.  
  
أسهمت الدولة الإسلامية منذ أوائل القرن 5 هـ / 11 م بشكل فعال في إنشاء المدارس باعتبارها مؤسسات تعليمية ذات مستوى عال هدفها التفقيه في الدين حسب المذاهب السنية والتبحر في العلم ونشر الإسلام. وذكرت المراجع التاريخية، مثل خطط المقريزي، أن عدد المدارس في القاهرة في العصر الأيوبي كان 24 مدرسة. غير أن هذه المدارس اندثرت جميعها، ولم يتبق منها غير بقايا مدرستين: المدرسة الكاملية (بنيت عام 622 هـ / 1225 م)، والمدرسة الصالحية التي اندثرت أغلب أبنيتها ولم يبقَ إلا جزء من إيوانها الغربي المجاور لضريح المنشئ، وواجهتها ومدخلها ومئذنتها.  
  
بنيت الواجهة الرئيسية للمدرسة من حجارة مصقولة رصت بعناية فائقة، وهي تنقسم إلى ثلاثة أجزاء رئيسية: الجزء الأوسط ويشمل المدخل وجوانبه ويبلغ طوله 18 م؛ والجزء الأيمن وطوله 31 م؛ والجزء الأيسر وطوله 26 م. ويبلغ ارتفاع الجزء الأوسط 12 م، أما الجزءين الأيمن والأيسر فارتفاعهما حوالي 11.50 م. ويشتمل الجزء الأوسط (المدخل) على شريط كتابي أفقي منقوش بخط النسخ يحمل اسم المنشئ ودعاءً له، ويتوسط هذا الجزء فتحة الباب الذي يعلوه عتب يتكون من صنج معشقة. ويتوج المدخل حنية معقودة زخرفت بخمسة صفوف من المقرنصات.  
  
للمدرسة مئذنة ترتفع فوق كتلة المدخل الذي يمثل اليوم المدخل المؤدي إلى حارة الصالحية التي كانت أصلاً الممر الرئيسي الفاصل بين جناحي المدرسة المتطابقين. وتعتبر هذه المئذنة الوحيدة التي بقيت سليمة من مآذن العصر الأيوبي، وقد رممت عام 1995 م. والمئذنة مبنية من الطوب المغطى بالبياض، وتتكون من ثلاثة أجزاء. يتكون الجزء الأسفل من بدن رئيسي مقطعه مربع طول ضلعه 5 م، وارتفاعه 10.40 م زخرف بثلاث كوّات معقودة. ويعلوه مثمن يصل ارتفاعه إلى 5 م ويشتمل على ثمانية أبواب مزخرفة بعقود مفصصة تفتح على شرفة خشبية مثمنة الشكل يؤذن منها. ويتوج المئذنة أعلى المثمن صفان من المقرنصات يعلوهما قبة مفصصة. وعرف هذا النوع من المآذن بالمبخرة، وذلك بسبب شكل الجزء المثمن المميز والقبة التي تعلوه الذي يشبه المباخر المعدنية الأيوبية. وقد استمر هذا النمط من المآذن في بداية العصر المملوكي، كما يظهر في مئذنة خانقاه بيبرس الجاشنكير التي ترجع إلى عام 709 هـ / 1310 م. وتطور هذا النمط من المآذن في الفترات اللاحقة من العصر المملوكي، فزاد الطابق المثمن في الارتفاع وأصبح عنصراً رئيسياً للمئذنة.  
  
وكان تخطيط المدرسة يتكون من مدرستين متماثلتين لهما مدخل واحد وواجهة مشتركة. وكان المدخل يؤدي إلى ممر فتح على جانبيه بابان متقابلان يؤدي الشرقي إلى إيواني المذهبين المالكي والشافعي، والغربي إلى إيواني المذهبين الحنبلي والحنفي. وهكذا اشتمل كل جانب على مدرسة مستقلة تتكون من إيوانين متقابلين بينهما فناء مكشوف. ويمكن اعتبار هذا التصميم مرحلة انتقال إلى تصميم المدرسة ذات الإيوانات الأربعة المحورية التي ظهرت بعد ذلك في العصر المملوكي.

هي أول مدرسة تنشأ في مصر لتعليم المذاهب السنية الأربعة. وكانت المدرسة ومعها الضريح الذي أقامته الملكة "شجرة الدر" للإمام لشافعي، طرازاً جديداً في القاهرة، يُسمَّى بالمجموعة المعمارية، واحتذته الدولة المملوكية في العمائر التي أقامتها على طول شارع المعز لدين الله، في قلب المدينة. ومئذنة المدرسة هي النموذج الكامل الوحيد الباقي من العصر الأيوبي في القاهرة، وقمتها على طراز المبخرة.
artist: السلطان الصالح نجم الدين أيوب (حكم في الفترة 637 - 647 هـ/ 1240 – 1249 م)، وهو آخر السلاطين الأيوبيين.
keywords: ضريح؛ عمارة دينية؛ مدرسة.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

en.name: Madrasa of al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyub.
names: Madrasa of al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyub
description:
The Madrasa of al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyub was erected on the site where the Fatimid Eastern Palace once stood. It was built to teach the four *sunni* schools of *fiqh* (jurisprudence), and is considered to be the first school built in Egypt for that purpose. Shajarat al-Durr, the wife of the sultan, al-Salih Najm al-Din, added a mausoleum in which the sultan was buried in AH 648 / AD 1250. Thus an Ayyubid architectural complex was built in the heart of Fatimid Cairo that offered the city a new architectural style. Much admired by the Mamluks, the new manner was imitated in the Mamluk complexes that gradually extended along al-Muizz Street, forming the main artery, or *kasba*, of the City of Cairo.  
From the beginning of the AH 5th / AD 11th century the Islamic state participated actively in the building of schools that were high-level educational foundations aimed at religious instruction according to the four Sunni Schools of Law (*Maliki*, *Shafi'i*, *Hanbalii* and *Hanafii*). These schools encouraged students to delve deep into the knowledge and the propagation of Islamic beliefs. Historical sources, such as the *Khitat* of al-Maqrizi, mention that during the Ayyubid period Sunni Schools in Cairo numbered 24. However, today, all the buildings that housed these schools have been obliterated, and nothing remains of them except the ruins of two: the Madrasa Kamiliyya (built AH 622 / AD 1225), and this one, the Madrasa Salihiyya, where a part of the western *iwan*, laying in close proximity to the mausoleum belonging to the builder, its façade and entrance, and the minaret still stand.  
The principle façade of the *madrasa* was built from dressed stone aligned with meticulous attention and composed of a tripartite structure: the middle section, which includes the entrance and its sides, measures 18 m; the right-hand section measures 31 m; and the left-hand section measures 26 m. The middle section reaches a height of 12 m, while the left- and right-hand sections are approximately 11.50 m high. In the middle section (the entrance) there is a horizontal band of inscription carved in the *naskhi* script which bears the name of the builder and which offers supplications for him. In the middle of this section, which is surmounted by a lintel composed of interlocking voussoirs, is an arched niche ornamented by five rows of *muqarnas* which crowns the entrance.  
The *madrasa* has a minaret, which rises above the entrance block indicating the entrance that today leads to the Salihiyya Alley, and which was originally the principle passage dividing the two identical wings of the school. The minaret, built of brick covered with white plaster, is the only remaining intact minaret of the Ayyubid dynasty. Restored in 1995, it is composed of three parts: The lowest section of the main body is a square shaft whose length measures 5 m and height, 10.40 m. It is decorated with three arched recesses. Above it is an octagonal form whose height reaches 5 m, and which includes eight doors decorated with lobed arches opening out on to a wooden octagonal balcony, from which the call to prayers is made. The minaret is crowned above the octagonal form with two rows of *muqarnas*, topped by a lobed dome. This type of minaret is called *al-mabkhara* (the incense burner) due to the distinctive octagonal section and the dome, which crowns it closely, resembling Ayyubid metal incense burners. This style of minaret continued to be popular up to the beginning of the Mamluk period, as seen in the minaret of the Khanqah of Baybars al-Gashanqir dating to AH 709 / AD 1310. The minaret then developed subsequently during the Mamluk period to the point where the octagonal storey increased in height and became a principle component of the minaret.  
The plan of the *madrasa* is composed of two identical buildings (the schools) which have a single, shared, entranceway and a shared façade. The entrance leads to a passageway with two opposing doors. The eastern door leads to the two *iwan*s of the *Maliki* and *Shafi'i* Schools, and the western door leads to the two *iwan*s of the *Hanbali* and *Hanafi* Schools. Thus, each side consists of two independent schools composed of two confronting *iwan*s, in the middle of which is an open courtyard. This design layout may be considered as a transitional stage to the conventional *madrasa* layout of four axial *iwan*s (cruciform), which appeared later in the Mamluk period.

This *madrasa* is the first school founded in Egypt to instruct in the four Sunni schools of jurisprudence. It heralded, together with the mausoleum of its sponsor, a new architectural style in Cairo. It became a model for later constructions that rose along Al-Muizz street in the heart of the city throughout the Mamluk period. Its minaret is the only one extant from the Ayyubid period. Its octagonal section with the dome that crowns it resembles an incense burner.
artist: Sultan al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyub (r. AH 637–47 / AD 1240–9) the last of the Ayyubid sultans.
keywords: Mausoleum; religious architecture; madrasa
partner: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Supreme Council of Antiquities

es.name: Madrasa de al-Salih Naym al-Din Ayyub.
description:
La madrasa de al-Salih Naym al-Din Ayyub se construyó en el lugar en el que, en tiempos, estaba ubicado el Palacio de Oriente fatimí. Se creó para enseñar las cuatro escuelas de jurisprudencia *(fiqh)* sunníes y se considera la primera madrasa construida en Egipto con tal propósito. Shayarat al-Durr, mujer de al-Salih Naym al-Din, le añadió un mausoleo en el que se enterró al sultán en 648 / 1250. Se creó así un conjunto arquitectónico ayyubí en pleno centro de El Cairo fatimí que imprimió a la ciudad un nuevo estilo arquitectónico, estilo admirado después por los mamelucos, que imitaron en los complejos que construyeron a lo largo de la calle al-Muizz y que acabaron formando la arteria principal de la ciudad.  
Desde principios del siglo V / XI, el Estado participó activamente en la construcción de escuelas de alto nivel educativo en las que se impartían enseñanzas religiosas según las cuatro escuelas jurídicas sunníes (malikí, shafí, hanbalí y hanafí). En estas escuelas se alentaba a los alumnos a profundizar en los conocimientos y la divulgación de las creencias islámicas. Fuentes históricas, como *Al-Jitat* de al-Maqrizi, mencionan que en el periodo ayyubí llegó a haber 24 escuelas sunníes en El Cairo. Sin embargo, de todos estos edificios no se conserva hoy en día nada excepto las ruinas de dos de ellos: la madrasa Kamiliyya (622 / 1225) y esta madrasa, de la que sólo quedan el *iwan* occidental, junto al mausoleo del constructor, la fachada con la entrada y el alminar.  
La fachada principal de la madrasa se construyó con piedras cortadas meticulosamente alineadas y dispuestas en una estructura tripartita: la sección central, que comprende la entrada y sus laterales, mide 18 m de ancho; la parte derecha mide 31 m; y la parte izquierda mide 26 m. La parte central mide 12 m de altura, mientras que las partes derecha e izquierda tienen una altura aproximada de 11,5 m. En la parte central hay una banda horizontal con una inscripción tallada en caligrafía *nasji* con el nombre del patrocinador y súplicas a él. Sobre el dintel y el arco de descarga de la entrada hay un nicho enmarcado por cinco filas de mocárabes. La entrada lleva hoy al callejón de Salihiyya, que en su origen fue el pasaje que separaba las dos alas idénticas de la escuela.  
El alminar, que se alza sobre esta entrada, está construido en ladrillo recubierto de yeso y es el único de época ayyubí que se conserva intacto (se restauró en 1995). Consta de tres partes: la inferior es de planta cuadrada, mide 5 m de lado y 10,4 m de alto, y está decorada con tres arcos rehundidos; la parte central es octogonal, tiene una altura de 5 m y en ella se abren ocho vanos de arcos lobulados que forman el balcón para la llamada a la oración; la parte superior consta de dos filas de mocárabes y una cubierta cónica lobulada. Este tipo de alminar se denomina *al-mabjara* ('incensario') porque su peculiar forma octogonal y su cubierta recuerdan a los incensarios de metal ayyubíes, y siguió construyéndose hasta principios de la época mameluca, como lo demuestra el de la *janqa* de Baybars al-Gashanqir (709 / 1310); posteriormente, la parte octogonal fue aumentando de altura y se convirtió en un componente principal.  
La planta de la madrasa consta de dos edificios idénticos (las escuelas) que comparten la entrada y la fachada. La entrada lleva a un pasillo con dos puertas frente a frente. La oriental da a los dos *iwan* de las escuelas malikí y shafí, y la occidental a los dos de las escuelas hanbalí y hanafí. Esta disposición puede considerarse una etapa de transición hacia la estructura convencional de la madrasa de cuatro *iwan* axiales o cruciforme que apareció posteriormente en el periodo mameluco.

Es la primera escuela que se fundó en Egipto para impartir enseñanzas de las cuatro escuelas sunníes de jurisprudencia. Inició, junto con el mausoleo de su patrocinador, un nuevo estilo arquitectónico en El Cairo. Fue un modelo para los edificios que se levantaron en el periodo mameluco a lo largo de la calle al-Muizz, en pleno centro de la ciudad. Su alminar es el único ejemplo que se conserva del periodo ayyubí con cúspide en forma de incensario.
artist: Sultán al-Salih Naym al-Din Ayyub (r. 637-647 / 1240-49), el último sultán ayyubí.
keywords: mausoleo; arquitectura religiosa; madrasa.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

fr.name: Madrasa d’al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyoub.
description:
La *madrasa* d'al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyoub fut édifiée sur le site de l'ancien palais oriental fatimide pour assurer l'enseignement des quatre écoles sunnites de *fiqh* (jurisprudence). Il s'agit probablement de la première école fondée en égypte pour ces matières. Chajarat al-Durr, épouse du sultan al-Salih Najm al-Din, lui ajouta un mausolée dans lequel le sultan fut inhumé en 648 H / 1250 J.-C. Ainsi un complexe architectural ayyoubide qui inaugurait un nouveau style était-il édifié au cœur du Caire fatimide. Très admiré par les Mamelouks, ce style fut repris pour les complexes qu'ils construisirent le long de la rue al-Mouiz devenue l'artère principale, ou *kasba*, du Caire.  
Dès le début du VIe siècle H (XIe siècle J.-C.), l'état islamique participa activement à la construction de fondations éducatives de haut niveau délivrant une instruction religieuse selon les quatre écoles du droit sunnite (malékite, shafiite, hanbalite et hanafite). On y encourageait les étudiants à approfondir leurs connaissances et à participer à la propagation de la foi islamique. Des sources historiques, comme le *Khitat* d'al-Maqrizi, mentionnent l'existence de 24 écoles sunnites au Caire sous les Ayyoubides. Il n'en reste rien aujourd'hui si ce n'est les ruines de deux d'entre elles : la *madrasa* Kamiliyya (622 H / 1225 J.-C.) et celle-ci, la *madrasa* Salihiyya, dont ne subsistent que l'*iwan* occidental, proche du mausolée, sa façade, son entrée et un minaret.  
La façade principale de la *madrasa* en pierres de taille soigneusement alignées se compose de trois parties : la section centrale, qui comprend l'entrée et ses murs latéraux, mesure 18 m de long et 12 m de haut, la partie de droite, 31 m, et la partie de gauche 26 m pour 11,50 m de haut. Au-dessus de l'entrée, marquée par un linteau composé de voussoirs et d'une niche en arc ornée de cinq rangs de *mouqarnas*, figure un bandeau épigraphique horizontal sculpté en style *naskhi* qui porte le nom du commanditaire et diverses supplications.  
La *madrasa* possède un minaret, qui s'élève au-dessus de l'entrée conduisant aujourd'hui à l'allée Salihiyya, qui constituait à l'origine le principal passage entre les deux ailes identiques de l'école. Le minaret en briques plâtrées de blanc est le seul de la période ayyoubide qui ait été conservé intact. Restauré en 1995, il se compose de trois sections : la partie inférieure du fût de section carrée de 5 m de côté et 10,4 m de hauteur, décoré de trois renfoncements en arc ; une partie octogonale de 5 m de haut à huit ouvertures décorées d'arcs brisés donnant sur un balcon octogonal en bois d'où sont dites les prières ; enfin une coupole lobée soutenue par deux rangées de *mouqarnas*. Ce type de minaret est appelé *al-mabkhar* (encensoir), sa section octogonale et sa coupole pouvant évoquer cet objet. Ce style est resté populaire bien après les débuts de la période mamelouke, comme le montre l'exemple du minaret de la *khanqa* de Baybars al-Gachanqir datant de 709 H / 1310 J.-C. Peu à peu, la partie octogonale gagna en hauteur jusqu'à constituer la totalité du fût.  
Le plan de la *madrasa* se compose de deux constructions identiques – les écoles – qui partagent la même façade et la même entrée. L'entrée donne sur un passage à deux portes se faisant face. La porte orientale ouvre sur les deux *iwan* des écoles malékite et shafiite, la porte occidentale sur les deux *iwan* des écoles hanbalite et hanafite. Ainsi, chaque côté est constitué de deux *iwan* au milieu desquels s'étend une cour. Cette disposition peut être considérée comme représentative d'une phase de transition qui précède l'arrivée du plan traditionnel de la *madrasa* à quatre *iwan* (cruciforme) qui apparaîtra plus tard dans la période mamelouke.

Cette *madrasa* est la première école fondée en Égypte pour assurer l'enseignement des quatre écoles sunnites de jurisprudence. Elle annonce, tout comme le mausolée de son mécène, un nouveau style architectural au Caire. Elle devint un modèle pour les constructions ultérieures qui s'érigèrent le long de la rue al-Mouiz, au cœur de la cité, tout au long de la période mamelouk. Son minaret est le seul de la période ayyoubide à être encore debout. Sa section octogonale, avec le dôme qui la couronne, évoque un brûleur d'encens.
artist: Sultan al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyoub (r. 637-647 H / 1240-1249 J.-C.), dernier des sultans ayyoubides.
keywords: mausolées ; architecture religieuse ; madrasa
partner: Ministry of Culture,Supreme Council of Antiquities

en.name: *Six Episodes from the Life of Luigi Ferdinando Marsili*
description:
The peace of Carlowitz between the Habsburg Empire, Venice, Poland and Russia on one side and Turkey on the other was negotiated in 1698–99. Bolognese Count Luigi Ferdinando Marsili, a representative of Emperor Leopold I of Austria, was among the diplomats involved. After his return to Bologna he founded the Istituto delle Scienze (Institute of Sciences) (1711). This series is composed of six paintings: five depicting military camps, travelling armies and trains and one representing the discussion about the borders of the Habsburg empire. The paintings describe the negotiations and the following operations in order to define the borders of Venice, the Empire and Turkey in Bosnia and Dalmatia. All paintings are described in the *Instrumentum Donationis*, housed in the Istituto delle Scienze (first half XVIII century). Each painting originally bore a wooden caption explaining the scene depicted in it, today only one survives. This sort of documentary painting was new for Bolognese culture, and has been connected with the astronomical scenes commissioned from Donato Creti in 1711 by Marsili himself (now in the Pinacoteca Vaticana).  
In scene n. 291, painted with a rich brushstroke showing the influence of Giuseppe Maria Crespi, is depicted an episode of the negotiations for the peace: under a camp tent three diplomats sit next to their respective generals. In the foreground we are able to identify, thanks to the sealed letters they are holding in their hands, from the left the representative of Austria (Leopold Slink von Wischkirken or maybe Marsili himself, even if he was not the head of the diplomatic expedition), the representatives of Turkey (Reys Mohamed Effendi) and Venice (Carlo Ruzzini). We cannot say which exact moment of the negotiations is depicted here because the caption has been lost. The persons depicted are each identified with a letter which was further explained in a caption beneath the painting. However, the caption is now lost. It is a sort of birds-eye view of the military camp where the meeting took place, with a tent housing the diplomats and their respective armies. The paintings, dating to Marsili's most significant period of cultural and scientific zeal, employ a precise topographical description. They are a thorough representation of people, rather than focused on the epic and rhetorical meaning of the episodes.

The persons depicted are identified with a letter which was explained in a caption beneath the painting. However, the caption is now lost. Note the birds-eye view of the military camp where the meeting took place, with the tents housing the diplomats and their respective armies.

it.name: *Serie di sei dipinti raffiguranti episodi della pace di Carlowitz (1698–1701) e l'attività in essa svolta da Luigi Ferdinado Marsili*
description:
La pace di Carlowitz tra l'Impero, Venezia, la Polonia e la Russia da un lato, la Turchia dall'altro, fu negoziata nel 1698–99, ed ebbe tra i suoi protagonisti, in qualità di plenipotenziario dell'Imperatore Leopoldo I d'Asburgo, il bolognese Conte Luigi Ferdinando Marsili, che dopo il suo ritorno a Bologna avrebbe fondato l'Istituto delle Scienze (1711). La serie di opere è composta da cinque tele con figure di accampamenti ed eserciti e cortei in viaggio, e da una raffigurante la discussione dei confini territoriali  dell'Impero d'Asburgo; descrivono i negoziati e le conseguenti operazioni per la delimitazione dei confini tra Venezia, l'impero e la Sublime Porta in Bosnia e Dalmazia. I dipinti sono descritti  nell'*Instrumentum Donationis*, all'Istituto delle Scienze, (prima metà sec. XVIII). Un tempo ogni tela disponeva di un cartiglio ligneo esplicativo, di cui uno soltanto oggi è superstite. Questo tipo di rappresentazione “documentaria” inedita per la cultura bolognese, è stata posta in relazione con con le *Scene Astronomiche* commissionate a Donato Creti nel 1711 dallo stesso Marsili (ora alla Pinacoteca Vaticana).  
Nella n. 291, di stile più corposo, che sembra rivelare gli influssi di Giuseppe Maria Crespi, è raffigurato un momento delle trattative di pace: sotto una tenda tre plenipotenziari siedono affiancati dai rispettivi generali. In primo piano lettere con sigilli che consentono di identificare  da sinistra il ministro austriaco (Leopold Slink von Wischkirken o forse lo stesso Marsili, benché non a capo della missione diplomatica), quello turco (Reys Maometto Effendi) e quello veneziano (Carlo Ruzzini). La perdita del cartellino non consente l'identificazione precisa di quello che doveva essere un momento preciso delle trattative, come pure nel n. xxxx descritto con minuzia e con lettere di rimando alla didascalia perduta per l'identificazione dei vari personaggi: si tratta di  una veduta, quasi a volo d'uccello, del campo del congresso, con un padiglione che accoglie i diplomatici e i rispettivi reparti militari. Le tele, che risalgono al momento di massimo impegno culturale e scientifico di Marsili, all'epica e alla retorica degli episodi privilegiano l'esatta topografia del luogo e dei personaggi.

Nel n. xxxx, descritto con minuzia e con lettere di rimando alla didascalia perduta per l’identificazione dei vari personaggi, compare una veduta, quasi a volo d’uccello, del campo del congresso, con un padiglione che accoglie i diplomatici e i rispettivi reparti militari.

ar.name: مصحف في ثلاثين جزءا
description: من المعتاد أن يتم تجليد المصحف في الصين في ثلاثين جزءا وكل جزء من هذا المصحف الخاص مجلد بجلد مطلي بالورنيش (طلاء لماع) الداكن ومزين بالذهب بزهور اللوتس المتفتحة وورق ملتف كثيف وتؤطر الرسوم التزيينية الصينية الحلقة المشكلة بالتخطيط ومكتوب عليها آية من القرآن : "" لا يمسه إلا المطهرون"" (56 :79) وهي مكتوبة بالخط الصيني بالحبر الأسود مع علامات للآيات متعددة الألوان وبالذهب. وكل ورقة تظهر خمسة أسطر من الكتابة. ويتميز تزيين الإطار بالطرق الإسلامية والصينية . والنص العربي متضمن في التصميم بشكل أهلة وأعلام، مستوحاة من الثقافة والتراث الصيني.وتمتد تزيينات الحدود إلى الهوامش من إطار الزخرفة بشكل مشابه للمصاحف الصينية المنتجة خلال عصر حكم كينج. والجودة العالية لهذه المجموعة تعني أنه ربما كانت مملوكة لشخص نبيل أو ثري.

en.name: Qur’an in 30 volumes
description: It is a tradition for Qur’an *mushaf*s in China to be bound in 30 separate *juz’* (volumes). Each volume of this particular Qur’an is bound in dark varnished leather decorated in gold with lotus blossoms and cloud scroll foliage. The traditional Chinese decorative motifs frame a calligraphic roundel, inscribed with a verse from the Qur'an: "None shall touch but those who are clean" (56:79) It is written in *Sini* script in black ink with polychrome and gold verse markers. Each folio displays five lines of text. The border decoration identifies with both Islamic and Chinese concepts. Arabic script was incorporated within designs such as half moons and flags, inspired by the Chinese culture and heritage. The border decorations extend into the margins from the ornamental frame, in a manner popular to Chinese Qur’ans produced during the Qing dynasty. The high quality of this set suggests that it was probably owned by a nobleman or a wealthy individual.
materials: Paper bound in dark varnished leather in 30-separated *juz’*

ar.name: لوحة تزيينية.
description:
لوحة تزيينية من الحجر الكلسي الأبيض، سطحها متآكل بشكل كبير. وعلى عكس منحوتات أخرى ترجع إلى بدايات العصور الوسطى في لشبونة، يبدو النحت البارز على سطح هذه اللوحة أكثر وضوحاً، وبالتالي يسمح بإبراز تناوب الظل والنور وحيوية الرسم بواسطة تهذيبات تكميلية أنجزت بمشرط دقيق.  
زخرفت اللوحة بثلاثة أقواس إكليلية الشكل تستند على أعمدة صغيرة مجدولة. تهدم العمود الصغير الرابع بسبب انتزاع الحجر من جانبه الأيسر؛ وتمثل الأكاليل الزخرفية سعيفات نخيلية تتناوب فيها ثلاثة إلى خمسة أطراف مدببة؛ وتبدو على الأطراف الداخلية للأقواس زخارف شوكية، في حين يأخذ الطرف الخارجي شكل جديلة؛ ويملأ شكلٌ نباتيٌ ناعمٌ الزاويةَ العليا اليمينية، ليعبر عن "الخوف من الفراغ" الذي تتسم به زخرفة اللوحة بأكملها. لم تعد زخرفة الزاوية اليسرى مرئية بسبب الحالة السيئة التي تتواجد عليها القطعة. والسبب نفسه، يمنعنا من أن نر الحبل الدقيق الذي يربط أفقياً قاعدة الأقواس التي تستند عليها الأصداف الثلاث التي تملأ أوجهها الداخلية. يمكن أن نر، فوق كل فرجة بين الأعمدة وتحت الأصداف، أشكال حيوانات متجابهة، من بينها طائرين يقعان في المركز ودابة من ذوات الأربع على كل طرف. وعلى ظهر كل واحدة من هذه الحيوانات، نجد باقة صغيرة نباتية من تلك التي تميّز بعض التكوينات الإسلامية أو صور الحيوانات المستمدة من تلك التقاليد.  
تأخذ هذه المجموعة، من حيث تصويرها للأشكال، معنى مسيحياً يقترب، على سبيل المثال، من ذلك الذي توحي به بعض النجوم القبطية المنحوتة بنفس الطريقة والتي تمثل الجنة، والدليل على ذلك النصب التذكاري المخصص لمارتا الذي وُجد في إصنح والمعروض في متحف القاهرة، والنجمة المسماة "نجمة الجنة" في متحف بروكلين.

لوحةٌ تزيينيةٌ من الحجر الكلسي الأبيض، مزخرفةٌ بثلاث عقود تستند على أعمدة صغيرة. من الناحية التصويرية، تُقدم المجموعةُ تشابهات مع شواهد قبطية مما يوحي بأن هذا النقش البارز قد قدم في الأصل من بناية مسيحية مشيدة خلال الحكم الإسلامي.

en.name: Ornamental panel.
description: Decorative plate made from white limestone, the surface of which is currently in an advanced state of decay. Unlike other early medieval sculptures in Lisbon, this panel presents a deeper surface carving, enhancing the chiaroscuro effect and the liveliness of the design with small complementary touches made with a fine scalpel.The panel is decorated with three loops with garlands, standing on small twisted columns. The fourth column has disappeared owing to the chiselling the stone suffered on its left-hand side. The ornamental garlands are decorated with palmettes, with three and five points, arranged alternately. The internal border of the loops exhibits a decoration of spines, while the outer border takes the form of a corded pattern. A subtle plant motif fills the upper right-hand corner, in a manifestation of the *horror vacui* or fear of emptiness, which indeed characterises the whole design of the panel. The ornamentation on the left corner has now been largely lost because of the poor state of conservation of the piece. This also accounts for the difficulty in making out the fine cord that links the base of the loops horizontally and on which stand the three scallop shells that fill their interior. In each space between the columns and under the three scallop shells are figures of animals face to face, with two birds in the centre and a quadruped at either end. On the reverse of the piece a small plant cluster is sculpted, typical of certain Islamic compositions or of a certain bestiary inspired by the same tradition.From an iconographic point of view, this group represents a clear Christian meaning, similar, for example, to the meaning of some Coptic steles, with identical motifs, as a representation of Paradise. Examples of this are the stone dedicated to the memory of Marta, from Esna in the Cairo Museum (Egypt) and the so-called 'Paradise stele' of Brooklyn Museum (New York, USA).

Decorative white limestone panel decorated with three festooned arches on small columns. From an iconographic point of view, the whole presents similarities with Coptic steles, suggesting that this bas-relief originally belonged to a Christian building erected during Islamic rule.

es.name: Elemento arquitectónico decorado.
description:
Placa decorativa en piedra caliza blanca, cuya superficie se encuentra actualmente en avanzado estado de corrosión. A diferencia de otras piezas esculpidas altomedievales de Lisboa, este bloque presenta una talla más profunda de la superficie; pequeños retoques complementarios practicados con un fino cincel acentúan los claroscuros y la animación del dibujo.  
El bloque está decorado con tres arcos festoneados sobre pequeñas columnas entorchadas. La cuarta columna desapareció debido al corte que la piedra sufrió en el lado izquierdo. Los festones ornamentales están decorados con palmetas de tres y cinco puntas alternas. La orla interior de los arcos exhibe una decoración en espina, mientras que el borde exterior adopta forma de encordado. Un sutil motivo vegetal llena el ángulo superior derecho en una muestra de *horror vacui* que, por otra parte, caracteriza todo el diseño del panel. La decoración del ángulo izquierdo desapareció hace tiempo debido a la mala conservación de la pieza. Esta misma circunstancia hace que hoy apenas se perciba una fina cuerda que une, horizontalmente, las impostas de los arcos y sobre la cual se asientan las tres vieiras que ocupan el interior de los mismos. Finalmente, en cada intercolumnio, bajo las vieras, hay figuras de animales afrontados: dos aves en el central y cuadrúpedos en los laterales. Sobre sus dorsos hay esculpido un pequeño haz, típico de algunas composiciones islámicas o de ciertos bestiarios inspirados en la misma tradición.  
Desde el punto de vista iconográfico, este conjunto tiene un nítido significado cristiano, asemejándose, por ejemplo, al sentido de algunas estelas coptas, labradas con idénticos motivos como representación del paraíso. Sirvan de ejemplo la lápida dedicada a la memoria de Marta, proveniente de Esneh (Museo del Cairo), y la llamada "estela del paraíso" del Museo de Brooklyn.

Bloque decorativo en caliza blanca, decorado por tres arcos festoneados asentados en pequeñas columnas. Desde el punto de vista iconográfico, el conjunto se aproxima a algunas estelas coptas, lo que sugiere que este bajorrelieve perteneció originalmente a un edificio cristiano construido en época islámica.

fr.name: Panneau d’ornement.
description:
Plaque décorative en pierre calcaire blanche dont la surface se trouve en état de corrosion avancée. Contrairement à d'autres sculptures du haut Moyen Âge lisboète, ce panneau présente un relief plus accentué à sa surface, mettant en valeur les alternances de clair-obscur et l'animation du dessin par des retouches complémentaires réalisées avec un fin bistouri.  
Le panneau est décoré de trois arcs à festons, appuyés sur des petites colonnes torsadées. La quatrième colonnette a été détruite par la découpe de la pierre sur son côté gauche. Les festons décoratifs présentent des palmettes, de trois à cinq pointes en alternance. Le bord intérieur des arcs laisse voir un décor en épine tandis que le bord extérieur présente la forme d'une torsade. Un subtil motif végétaliste remplit l'angle supérieur droit, manifestant “l'horreur du vide” qui caractérise tout le dessin du panneau. Le décor de l'angle gauche n'est plus visible en raison du piètre état de conservation de la pièce. Cette même raison nous empêche de voir la fine corde qui relie horizontalement la base des arcs sur laquelle s'appuient les trois coquilles qui remplissent leurs faces intérieures. Sur chaque entrecolonnement et sous les coquilles, on peut voir des figures d'animaux affrontés, dont deux oiseaux au centre et un quadrupède à chaque extrémité. Sur le dos de chacun, une petite touffe végétale, typique de certaines compositions islamiques ou du bestiaire inspiré par cette tradition.  
Du point de vue iconographique, l'ensemble présente une nette signification chrétienne, proche, par exemple de celle de certaines étoiles coptes, sculptées de la même manière, représentant le Paradis. Pour preuve, la stèle dédiée à la mémoire de Marthe, provenant de Esneh (musée du Caire), et l'étoile nommée “étoile du Paradis” du Musée de Brooklyn.

Plaque décorative en pierre calcaire blanche ornée de trois arcs appuyés sur de petites colonnes. D'un point de vue iconographique, l'ensemble présente des similitudes avec les stèles coptes, suggérant que ce bas-relief provenait à l'origine d'un édifice chrétien érigé pendant le règne islamique.
holder: Chapitre métropolitain du patriarcat de Lisbonne.

pt.name: Painel ornamental.
description:
Placa decorativa em calcário branco, cuja superfície se encontra actualmente em avançado estado de corrosão. Ao contrário de outras esculturas alto-medievais de Lisboa, este painel apresenta uma escavação mais profunda da superfície, valorizando as alternâncias de claro-escuro e a animação do desenho por pequenos retoques complementares, realizados com um fino bisturi.  
  
O painel é decorado por três arcos com festões, assentes em pequenas colunas torsas. O quarto colunelo desapareceu, devido ao entalhe que a pedra sofreu no lado esquerdo. Os festões ornamentais estão decorados com palmetas, de três e cinco pontas, dispostas alternadamente. A orla interna dos arcos exibe uma decoração em espinha, enquanto o bordo exterior assume a forma de um encordoado. Um subtil motivo vegetalista preenche o canto superior direito, numa manifestação de “horror ao vazio”, que, aliás, caracteriza todo o desenho do painel. O ornamento do canto esquerdo já há muito desaparecera, devido ao mau estado de conservação da peça. Esta mesma circunstância faz com que também mal se consiga hoje perceber a fina corda que liga, na horizontal, a base dos arcos e sobre a qual assentam as três vieiras que preenchem o interior dos mesmos. Finalmente, em cada intercolúnio e sob as ditas vieiras encontram-se figuras de animais afrontados, sendo duas aves ao centro e um quadrúpede em cada extremo. É de referir que, sobre o respectivo dorso, se encontra esculpido um pequeno tufo vegetal, típico de algumas composições islâmicas ou de certo bestiário inspirado nesta mesma tradição.  
  
Do ponto de vista iconográfico, este conjunto apresenta um nítido significado cristão, assemelhando-se, por exemplo, ao sentido de algumas estelas coptas, lavradas com idênticos motivos, como representação do Paraíso. São exemplo a lápide dedicada à memória de Marta, proveniente de Esnéh (Museu do Cairo), e a chamada “estela do Paraíso” do Museu de Brooklyn.

Placa decorativa em calcário branco, decorado por três arcos com festões, assentes em pequenas colunas. Do ponto de vista iconográfico o conjunto aproxima-se de algumas estelas coptas, o que leva a crer que este baixo-relevo pertenceu originalmente a um edifício cristão construído em época islâmica.

en.name: Flask
description: Small glass bottles with animal figurines were popular vessels in the pre-Islamic and early Islamic world and have been discovered in Iran, Iraq, Syria and Egypt. These bottles were likely produced in Syria or Egypt sometime from the 1st-2nd century AH / 6th-8th century AD. This free-blown animal flask in the shape of a fish is made of colourless glass with mouth, eyes and fins decorated with applied blue glass. Such an object would have been used as a container for perfume, balsam or kohl or as a decorative element attached to the outside of a glass bowl to give it the appearance of swimming when the vessel was filled with liquid.

The gifting of the rosary to the Dominican saints, St. Dominic and St. Catherine of Siena, was intended for the local Rosary Brotherhood; St. Ulrich embodies the patron saint of the diocese, waking the dead from their sleep.

ar.name: لوحة كتابية.
description: لوحة رخامية مستطيلة على سطحها كتابة تأسيسية منقوشة، وبما أن هذه اللوحات عادة ما يتم وضعها عند تأسيس مبنى، فإنها تحتوي على اسم الراعي وتاريخ البناء. تحمل هذه اللوحة أسماء وألقاب الخليفة الفاطمي المستنصر، وتاريخ (477/ 4-1085)، وهي مكتوبة بالخط الكوفي الهندسي الذي كان مفضلاً للكتابة على الأبنية الفاطمية. لا يعرف البناء الذي أتى منه هذا الحجر، لكن لا بد أن يكون الخليفة نفسه أو قائد جيشه بدر الجمالي (توفي 483/1091) هو الذي أمر بإنشاء المبنى. وقد اشتهر الفاطميون برعايتهم لإشادة العديد من الأبنية في فترة تميزت بالرخاء الاقتصادي. ومن بين الأبنية الفاطمية الأكثر روعة كانت أسوار المدينة القوية والبوابات المحصنة التي أمر ببنائها بدر الجمالي.

نقش على الرخام، يحمل أسماء ومعلومات عن الخليفة الفاطمي المستنصر، (عام 477هـ / 1084- 1085م). تمَّ النقش بالخطّ الكوفي، والذي استُخدم في تزيين العمارة والأبنية في العصر الفاطمي. ما يزال مصدر هذا النقش غير معروف.

en.name: Inscription panel.
description: A rectangular marble panel with a foundation inscription incised on the surface. Laid when a building was constructed, foundation inscriptions usually provide the name of the patron and the date of construction. This panel bears the names and titles of the Fatimid Caliph al-Mustansir and the date AH 477 (AD 1084–5). The angular *kufic* script used on this panel was particularly popular for epigraphy on Fatimid buildings. It is not known which building this stone came from but the building must have been commissioned by the caliph himself or his Commander-in-Chief Badr al-Jamali (d. AH 483 / AD 1091). The Fatimids were renowned for their prolific architectural patronage made possible by a period of economic prosperity. Among the most spectacular Fatimid constructions were the robust city walls and fortified gates ordered by Badr al-Jamali.

This marble panel bears the names and titles of the Fatimid Caliph al-Mustansir and the date AH 477 (AD 1084–5). The inscription has been carved in the angular *kufic* script often used for epigraphy on buildings in the Fatimid period. It is not known which building the stone originated from.
keywords: Calligraphy; Kufic script; Fatimid epigraphy; patronage

es.name: Lápida con inscripción.
description:
Lápida rectangular de mármol con inscripción fundacional. Estas lápidas se colocaban cuando se construía un edificio e incluían, normalmente, el nombre del mecenas de la obra y la fecha de construcción. En este caso aparecen los nombres y títulos del califa fatimí al-Mustansir y la fecha, 477 \[1084-85 d. C.\].  
La angular escritura cúfica, como la de esta lápida, fue muy utilizada en la epigrafía de los edificios fatimías. En este caso, el propio califa, o su comandante en jefe Badr al-Yamali, debió de mandar levantar el edificio del que procede esta piedra, aunque no se sabe cuál fue. Los fatimíes fueron famosos por su mecenazgo arquitectónico, que fue posible gracias a un periodo de prosperidad económica. Una de sus edificaciones más espectaculares fue la robusta muralla de su capital, con puertas fortificadas, que mandó construir por Badr al-Yamali.

Esta lápida de mármol tiene inscritos los nombres y títulos del califa fatimí al-Mustansir y la fecha de 477 [1084-85 d. C.]. Se trata de una inscripción en escritura cúfica angular, una letra muy utilizada en la epigrafía de los edificios fatimíes. Se desconoce a que edificio perteneció esta lápida.
dates: Año 477 de la Hégira / 1084-85 d. C.
keywords: caligrafía

fr.name: Plaque de fondation.
description: Panneau de marbre rectangulaire, inscription fondatrice gravée à sa surface. Posées au début de la construction d'un bâtiment, les inscriptions fondatrices fournissent généralement le nom du mécène et la date de la construction. Cette plaque mentionne les noms et titres du calife fatimide al-Moustansir et la date de 477 (1085 J.-C.). L'écriture coufique anguleuse utilisée était particulièrement appréciée en épigraphie dans les constructions fatimides. On ne sait pas d'où provient cette inscription. Il s'agit certainement d'un bâtiment édifié par le calife lui-même, ou par son commandant en chef Badr al-Jamali (m. 483 H / 1091 J.-C.). Les Fatimides sont connus pour leurs prolifique commande architecturale, favorisée par la prospérité économique de l'époque. Parmi leurs réalisations les plus spectaculaires figurent les robustes murailles et les portes du Caire, dont l'édification fut ordonnée par Badr al-Jamali.

Ce panneau de marbre porte les noms et titres du calife fatimide al-Moustansir et la date de 477 (1085 J.-C.). L'inscription a été sculptée en coufique angulaire, une écriture souvent utilisée pour l'épigraphie sur les bâtiments de la période fatimide. On ne sait pas à quel édifice appartenait cette pierre à l'origine
keywords: Calligraphie

Belt with buckles
names: Articles of adornment worn at the waist – *pafti*
short_description: Buckles were the most prominent articles of adornment worn by Macedonian women. They were also the most frequently worn pieces of jewellery, having been an inevitable element of folk costumes in all parts of Macedonia. Combining functionality and aesthetics, buckles were also considered to play a protective role. The diverse shapes – round, rectangular, leaf-shaped, etc., as well as the exquisite style of their decorating, show the remarkable skill and talent of goldsmiths producing them. These buckles consist of two slightly concave round plates joined with a little round piece used for fastening. They are adorned with decorative stones and decorated with geometric patterns applied by hammering. The belt is made of cotton fabric decorated with geometric and floral patterns by application of silver and gold-wrapped thread and braids.
keywords: Buckles; srma; costume; accessories; fashion
materials: Cotton fabric, *srma* – silver and gold-wrapped thread, braids. Buckles: silver, hammering, decorative stones

en.name: The drawings of Janissary clothes from The Album of Mecmua-i Tesavir-i Osmaniye (The collection of Ottoman Pictures)
short_description: Arif Mehmed Pasha is considered one of the leaders of the western style of painting in Turkey. He developed a talent for drawing and produced a series of pictures detailing the clothes Ottoman state officials wore. He prepared these pictures under the name *Mecmua-i Tesavir-i Osmaniyye*. Although his work was supposed to come out in 12 volumes, only one volume was actually published in French in Paris in 1863 and in Turkish the same year. The other 11 volumes have been lost. The published volume is considered to be the first illustrated book in Turkey. What is amazing is the praise heaped onto Arif Mehmed Pasha for his portraits, the harmony of their colours and tones, the maturity of attitude and delicate detail, the artist’s control over his pen and watercolours. The clothing reflects the time when the Janissaries were still on the scene (before 1826 when the corps was disbanded).

keywords: Ottoman Clothes; Janissary Clothes

description: بعد نصف قرن من وفاته ، حظي الدرويش نور علي شاه (حوالي 1161-1212 هجري/ حوالي 1748-1798 ميلادي) بشعبية كبيرة في بلاد فارس. ويشهد على ذلك عدد لا يحصى من السجاد من كرمان بالإضافة إلى العديد من المنمنمات والصور الزيتية. ويبدو أن هذه الشعبية كانت مرتبطة بشكل وثيق بإحياء التقاليد الصوفية في القرن التاسع عشر. جميع البورتريهات المعروفة حتى الآن يمكن إرجاعها إلى  إثنين من البورتيهات رسمهما إسماعيل جلاير (توفي 1289-1284 هجري/ 1868-1873 ميلادي) حوالي عام 1865.  تنتمي الورقة في الأصل إلى ألبوم تم إعداده للدكتور جوزيف ديزيريه ثولوزون (1235 -1315 هجري/ 1897-1820 ميلادي ) الذي كان الطبيب الخاص لناصر الدين شاه (حكم في الفترة 1313-1264هجري/ 1896-1848ميلادي) . ربما حصل على الألبوم من الشاه عندما تقاعد عام 1889. تحمل هذه الورقة الرقم 50 وحتماً هي الورقة الأخيرة من ألبومه ، الذي تم تفكيكه وربما بيعه في أوائل القرن العشرين. الأوراق الفردية كانت مملوكة سابقًا لمجموعة جان بوزي وهي الآن في مجموعة متحف الفن و التاريخ في جنيف (سويسرا).

en.name: Portrait of the young dervish Nur 'Ali Shah (ca. 1748-1798)
description:
Half a century after his death, the dervish Nur ʿAli Shah (Hegira ca. 1161-1212 / AD ca. 1748-1798) enjoyed great popularity in Persia. Countless carpets from Kerman as well as various miniatures and oil portraits bear witness to this. It seems that this popularity was closely connected with the revival of Sufi traditions in the 19th century. All the portraits known so far can be traced back to two portraits painted by Ismaʿil Jalayer (d. Hegira 1284-1289 / AD 1868-1873) around 1865.  
  
The leaf originally belonged to an album made for Dr. Joseph Désiré Tholozon (Hegira 1235-1315 / AD 1820-1897) who was Nasir al-Din Shahʼs (r. Hegira 1264-1313 / AD 1848-1896) personal physician. He might have received the album from the shah in 1889 when he retired. This folio bears the number 50 and must have been the last leaf of his album, which itself was taken apart and probably sold in the early 20th century. Individual leaves formerly belonged to the collection of Jean Pozzi and are now in the Musée dʼArt et dʼHistoire in Geneva (Switzerland).

de.name: Deckenfresken und gemalter Stuck
description: Wiewohl zum Teil übermalt und erneuert, bilden die Deckenbilder zusammen mit dem gemalten Stuck (“stucco finto”) ein einheitliches Dekorationssystem. Große geschweifte Rocaillekartuschen rahmen Bildfelder mit einem Zyklus zum Leben Mariens (Langhaus: Vermählung, Verkündigung und Himmelfahrt Mariae). Die geschweiften Rocaillerahmen verbinden mehr als dass sie abgrenzen und schaffen somit fließende Überleitungen zwischen Architektur und den Bildfeldern untereinander.

en.name: Ceiling frescos and painted stucco
description: Albeit partly painted over and renewed, the ceiling paintings together with the “stucco finto” or painted stucco, form a uniform decorative system. Large rocaille cartouches frame picture panels forming a cycle depicting the Life of Mary (nave: Marriage, Annunciation and Assumption). The sweeping frames connect more than they divide, thus generating flowing transitions between architecture and picture panels.

en.name: North-Western Khalwa of Ahmad Pasha
description:
A *khalwa* (or cell) usually covers a small, secluded area in a *zawiya*, where a *sufi* finds the ideal atmosphere for meditation, concentration and worship. However, in the Haram it is an independent twostorey structure comprising more than one unit. This style of building was developed here during the Ottoman period and almost 20 cells survive, the most beautiful of which is Ahmad Pasha’s.  
It is known as the “Mamluk Khalwa” as it carries many of the features of Mamluk architecture in Jerusalem. It is currently being used as the Aqsa Mosque manager’s office.  
When Ahmad Pasha founded it in 1009/1600–1601, he dedicated it to the *sufi*s and the study of Islamic jurisdiction. He appointed the *shaykh* al-Ghazi Abu al-Su‘ud, one of the most eminent *sufi* scholars in Jerusalem, as its Inspector. Ahmad Pasha bestowed upon him a lifetime’s annual salary of 600 silver dirhams, which was paid from the revenue of the building’s *waqf*. He also stipulated detailed conditions to ensure the good management of the place, its regular maintenance and the continuance of its scholastic activities. Ahmad Pasha, the ruler of Gaza at the time, was the descendent of a distinguished family that held important posts within the Ottoman Empire and in Jerusalem in particular. His grandfather, Mustafa Pasha, led missions as far as Yemen during the reign of Sultan Sulayman the Magnificent. His father was Radwan Pasha, whose relatives were the Radwan family who had ruled the Gaza province during the 10th/16th and 11th/17th centuries. The family’s Golden Age was during the reign of Ahmad Pasha. He was considered to be the most famous patron of architecture in Jerusalem at the end of the 10th/16th century and the city had a special place in his heart. He visited Jerusalem many times and the renowned architect, ‘Abd al-Muhsen Ibn Namr worked on many of his projects there.  
The building consists of two-storeys, the ground floor of which has two parts: the eastern section is a square chamber, whilst the western part has two chambers, which currently house the Haram’s emergency electricity generators. The upper storey has a large central chamber, and two further smaller chambers, one of which has a *mihrab* in its southern wall. Rich in architectural detail and ornamentation, the building faces each of the cardinal directions. Their symmetry of components has been co-ordinated in such a way as to reflect the spirit of Jerusalem’s architecture and yet remain unique. This singularity is best reflected in the door and window lintels and in the ornamental elements above them.

es.name: Jalwa noroeste de Ahmad Pacha
description:
Con la palabra *jalwa* (celda) se denomina habitualmente a una pequeña estancia retirada en una *zawiya*, donde el sufí encuentra la atmósfera ideal para la meditación, la concentración y la devoción. Pero en el caso de al-Haram se trata de un edificio independiente, con dos niveles en los que hay más de una unidad. En la época otomana se construyeron muchos edificios de este tipo y cerca de veinte celdas han llegado hasta nosotros, de las cuales la más hermosa es la de Ahmad Pacha. Está *jalwa* es conocida con el nombre de “*jalwa* mameluca”, pues en ella se encuentran numerosas características de la arquitectura de aquella época; actualmente sirve de despacho para el director de la mezquita al-Aqsa.  
El establecimiento fundado por Ahmad Pacha en 1009/1600-1601 estaba destinado a los sufíes y al estudio de la jurisdicción islámica. Ahmad Pacha nombró al frente de la *jalwa* a uno de los *ulemas* más eminentes de Jerusalén, el *chayj* al-Gazi Abu al-Su‘ud, y le asignó un salario anual de 600 dirhams de plata deducidos de los beneficios del *waqf* del edificio. También estableció con detalle las modalidades de su administración, para asegurar su funcionamiento, el mantenimiento regular y la misión pedagógica y religiosa de la *jalwa*. Ahmad Pacha, gobernador de Gaza, era descendiente de una familia de notables, cuyos miembros ocuparon cargos prestigiosos bajo el Imperio otomano en Jerusalén en particular. Su abuelo, Mustafa Pacha, ostentó durante mucho tiempo un puesto de mando en el Yemen, en tiempos del sultán Solimán el Magnífico. Su padre era Radwan Pacha, de la familia Radwan que gobernó Gaza durante los siglos X/XVI y XI/XVII. La edad de oro de esta familia corresponde a la época de Ahmad Pacha, considerado uno de los más famosos mecenas de la arquitectura en Jerusalén a finales del siglo X/XVI, ciudad que tenía un sitio preferente en su corazón. La visitó en reiteradas ocasiones y contó con el famoso arquitecto ‘Abd al-Muhsen Ibn Namr para muchos de sus proyectos.  
El edificio está construido en dos niveles. La planta baja está formada por una estancia oeste cuadrada y dos habitaciones, donde se encuentran actualmente los generadores eléctricos para los casos de emergencia que puedan producirse en al-Haram. La planta superior está formada por una gran habitación central y otras dos, más pequeñas; el muro sur de una de ellas está dotado de un *mihrab*. La construcción se distingue por su riqueza arquitectónica y decorativa: sus cuatro fachadas, orientadas a los cuatro puntos cardinales, atestiguan un refinamiento plasmado por el arquitecto en la simetría de sus componentes que fue concebida como una quintaesencia de la arquitectura de Jerusalén: sigue siendo un ejemplo único hasta hoy en día. Es en los dinteles de las puertas y ventanas y en las decoraciones donde esta singularidad resulta más resplandeciente.

fr.name: Khalwa nord-ouest de Ahmad Pacha
description:
Une *khalwa* (ou cellule) désigne généralement un petit espace retiré dans une *zawiya*, où le soufi trouve l’atmosphère idéale pour la méditation, la concentration et le travail. Mais dans le Haram, il s’agit d’un bâtiment indépendant à deux niveaux et comprenant plus d’une unité. Ce type de construction s’est répandu ici pendant la période ottomane et près de vingt cellules ont survécu, la plus belle étant celle de Ahmad Pacha.  
Comme elle présente de nombreuses caractéristiques de l’architecture mamelouke de Jérusalem, elle est également connue sous le nom de “*khalwa* mamelouke”. Elle sert actuellement de bureau au directeur de la mosquée al-Aqsa.  
L’établissement fondé par Ahmad Pacha en 1009/1600-1601 était destiné aux soufis et à l’étude de la juridiction islamique. Ahmad Pacha nomma à sa tête l’un des plus grands soufis de Jérusalem, le *cheikh* al-Ghazi Abou al-Su‘ud, et lui attribua à vie un salaire annuel de 600 dirhams d’argent prélevé sur les revenus du *waqf* du bâtiment.Par ailleurs, il précisa de façon extrêmement détaillée les modalités de gestion susceptibles d’assurer au mieux le fonctionnement, l’entretien régulier et la mission pédagogique et religieuse de la *khalwa*.  
Ahmad Pacha, qui était alors gouverneur de Gaza, descendait d’une vieille famille de notables dont les membres occupèrent des postes prestigieux dans l’Empire ottoman, à Jérusalem en particulier. Mustapha Pacha, son grand-père, fut envoyé en mission jusqu’au Yémen sous le règne du sultan Soliman le Magnifique. Son père était Radwan Pacha, de la famille al-Radwan qui avait gouverné Gaza aux Xe/XVIe et XIe/XVIIe siècles. Cette famille connut son âge d’or sous Ahmad Pacha, qui fut considéré comme l’un des plus grands mécènes de l’architecture à Jérusalem de la fin du Xe/XVIe siècle – la cité tenait d’ailleurs une place de choix dans son coeur. Il visita plusieurs fois la ville, où le fameux architecte ‘Abd al-Mouhsen Ibn Namr collabora à nombre de ses projets.  
Le bâtiment comprend deux niveaux. Le rez-de-chaussée est formé d’une pièce orientale carrée et de deux chambres, qui abritent actuellement les générateurs d’électricité destinés à dépanner le Haram en cas d’urgence. Le niveau supérieur comporte une grande pièce centrale et deux autres, plus petites – le mur méridional de l’une d’entre elles étant doté d’un *mihrab*. La construction se distingue par sa richesse architecturale et décorative, qui témoigne d’une recherche évidente dans l’agencement des façades, orientées vers les quatre points cardinaux, dont la symétrie des composantes a été conçue comme une quintessence de l’architecture de Jérusalem: l’exemple reste d’ailleurs unique à ce jour. C’est dans les linteaux des portes et des fenêtres, et dans les décorations qui les surmontent, que cette singularité est la plus éclatante.

The text, which extols the workmanship, seems to have been written in the voice of the artist and alludes to how the decoration was achieved—through drawings.

de.name: Mantel (*Anterija*)
description: Das heutige Albanien gehörte ab dem Ende des 15. Jahrhunderts für mehr als vier Jahrhunderte zum osmanischen Reich. Die dortige traditionelle Kleidung ist folglich stark osmanisch geprägt, was an diesem bodenlangen Mantel zu erkennen ist. Der Halsausschnitt ist rund geschnitten und die überlangen Ärmel sind im unteren Teil seitlich geschlitzt. Das Kleid wird mittig durch 41 Metallposamentenknöpfe, die bis zur Taille reichen, geschlossen. Reiche, ornamentale Stickereien in Anlegetechnik bedecken den Mantel. Das Futter besteht aus einem vertikal gestreiften *Ikat*.

en.name: Coat (*Anterija*)
description: Starting in the late fifteenth century, modern day Albania belonged to the Ottoman Empire for more than four hundred years. The traditional clothing there is thus very strongly influenced by the Ottomans, as is seen in this floor-length coat. The neck is cut round and the overlong sleeves are slit at the bottom. The garment is fastened in the middle by 41 ornamentally trimmed metal buttons reaching to the waist. Richly ornamental embroidery in appliqué technique cover the coat. The lining consists of a vertically striped *ikat*.
