de.name: Benediktinerabtei- und Pfarrkirche St. Josef
description: Die Stiftskirche ist einer der frühesten Bauten Tirols im Stil des beginnenden Rokoko. Die Architektur gibt sich als Abkömmling von St. Jakob in Innsbruck zu erkennen. An die überkuppelte Chorvierung als Zentrum des Baus schließen sich drei Konchen an. Das dreiachsige, weiträumige Langhaus mit flachen Wandpfeilern und Lünettenfenstern oberhalb des Hauptgesimes zeichnet sich durch klare, systematische Formensprache aus. Zwischen Chor und Langhaus ist ein rudimentäres Querhaus eingeschoben. Der Raumeindruck wird insgesamt stark von den großformatigen Deckenbildern und dem filigranen Rocaillenstuck mitbestimmt.

Neben Stams und Wilten zählt die Abtei St. Georgenberg zu den drei großen Stiften Tirols. Der Neubau der Kirche des 1705 niedergebrannten Klosters erfolgte unter dem aus Wessobrunn stammenden Abt Lambert Höllerer, der für die vorzügliche frühe Rokoko-Ausstattung bedeutende süddeutsche Künstler herangezogen hat. Die klar strukturierte Architektur in der entfernten Nachfolge des Innsbrucker Doms ist indessen ein Werk des Jakob Singer aus der im mittleren 18. Jahrhundert wohl berühmtesten Tiroler Baumeisterfamilie.
dates: 1741-43 (erste Bauphase), 1749/50 (zweite Bauphase nach Gewölbeeinsturz), 1778-81 (Errichtung des Turms), 1743 – ca. 1775 (Ausstattung).
artist: Abtei St. Georgenberg, Abt Lambert Höllerer (Amtszeit 1732-1772)

Architektur: Jakob Singer (1685-1760)  
Stuck: Franz Xaver (1698-1763) und Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696-1772) sowie Johann Georg Üblhör (1700-1763)  
Fresken: Matthäus Günther (1705-1788)
history: Das Stift führt seine Ursprünge im 10. Jahrhundert auf den seligen Rathold zurück. 1138 wurde St. Georgenberg zur Benediktinerabtei erhoben. Nach einem Brand 1705 erfolgte die Übersiedlung des Klosters vom Georgenberg, der weiterhin Wallfahrtsort blieb, ins Inntal. Der schlichten vierflügeligen Klosteranlage folgte ab 1741 die Abteikirche, die 1750 geweiht werden konnte. Die Stuckarbeiten wurden 1743-51 ausgeführt, die Fresken malte Matthäus Günther 1744-1755. Die Ausstattung dauerte insgesamt bis um 1775, der Kirchturm wurde erst 1781 fertig gestellt. Mehrere umfassende Restaurierungen seit 1948 stellten den im 19. Jahrhundert erheblich veränderten ursprünglichen Raumeindruck weitgehend wieder her.
keywords: Abteikirche; Deckenfresken; Rocaillenstuck; Wessobrunner Schule

en.name: Benedictine Abbey and Parish Church of St. Joseph
description: The monastery church is one of the earliest buildings in the Tyrol exhibiting the style of the early Rococo. The architecture is derived from that of St. Jacob’s in Innsbruck. The domed choir crossing, as the centre of the building, is adjoined by three apses and the tri-axial nave with shallow pilasters and lunette windows. A rudimentary transept has been inserted between the choir and the nave. The overall spatial impression is strongly influenced by the large-format ceiling pictures and the filigree rocaille stucco.

Together with Stams and Wilten, St. Georgenberg is one of Tyrol’s three large monasteries. Construction of the new church for the monastery, which was destroyed by fire in 1705, was conducted under Abbot Lambert Höllerer from Wessobrunn who attracted important southern German artists responsible for the exquisite Rococo interior work. The clearly structured architecture, with its distant echoes of Innsbruck Cathedral, is the work of Jakob Singer, a member of the most famous family of Tyrolian master builders of the mid-18th century.
dates: 1741–1743: first building phase; 1749/50: second building phase following collapse of the vault; 1778–1781: construction of the tower; 1743- c. 1775: interior
artist: St. Georgenberg Abbey, Abbot Lambert Höllerer (in office: 1732–1772)

Architecture: Jakob Singer (1685–1760); stuccowork: Franz Xaver Feichtmayr (1698–1763), Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); frames and stucco sculptures: Johann Georg Üblhör (1700–1763); figures and tabernacle: Johann Michael Fischer (1692–1766); frescos: Matthäus Günther (1705–1788); pews: Franz Xaver Nißl (1731–1804)
history: The origins of the monastery can be traced back to Blessed Rathold in the 10th century. St. Georgenberg was elevated to the status of a Benedictine Abbey in 1138. Following a fire in 1705 the monastery was transferred from Georgenberg, which remained a site of pilgrimage, to Inntal. The simple, four-winged monastery complex was followed by the construction of the abbey church beginning in 1741 and which was consecrated in 1750. The stuccowork was carried out between 1743 and 1751; the frescos were painted by Matthäus Günther between 1744 and 1755. Work on the interior continued until 1775, the church tower was completed in 1781. Comprehensive restoration work carried out in stages since 1948 has restored the original spatial impression which was significantly altered in the 19th century.
keywords: Abbey church; ceiling frescos; rocaille stuccowork; Wessobrunn school

en.name: *St. Francis Xavier Preaching in Goa*
description:
The set of 20 paintings portraying the life of St. Francis Xavier (1506–1552) form the back-piece to a large chest-of-drawers in the sacristy of the 16th-century Church of St. Roque, and are the work of the Portuguese proto-Baroque painter André Reinoso and collaborators. Installed in 1619, three years before the official canonisation of St. Francis Xavier on the 12th March 1622, the set of paintings form part of a religious “propaganda” exercise to highlight the life and work of the great Jesuit missionary, which it was hoped, would speed up the process of his canonisation by the Catholic Church. The paintings were inspired by the first Portuguese biography of the saint written by Father João de Lucena (*Histórica da Vida do Padre Francisco Xavier, e do que fizerão na Índia os mais religiosos da Companhia de Jesus*) published in Lisbon in 1600.  
The scene featured here shows the saint ardently preaching in the cosmopolitan city of Goa shortly after his arrival there in 1542. The picture has particular interest from an ethnographic viewpoint in that it shows the variety of oriental customs as well as recording different social classes. In the picture a crowd of new converts: men, women and children, as well as Portuguese noblemen watching on horseback, surround the saint. The background scene features a landscape fashioned in the Italian style.

This oil on canvas painting, part of a set of 20, is attributed to the Portuguese proto-Baroque painter André Reinoso (c. 1590-1641). Commissioned by the Society of Jesus for the sacristy of the Jesuit Church of St. Roque, this and other paintings of the set form the back-piece to a large chest-of-drawers installed in 1619, three years before the canonisation of the great missionary of the Far-East, St. Francis Xavier.
holder: Lisbon's Holy House of mercy / Museum of São Roque
Santa Casa da Misericórdia de Lisboa / Museum of São Roque
artist: André Reinoso (c.1590, Province of Beira, Portugal–after 1641) and his collaborators
keywords: Society of Jesus; Church of São Roque; Goa; India; Sacristy; Orient; painting cycle; pilgrimage; miscegenation; exoticism; travel; naturalism.

pt.name: *Pregação de S. Francisco Xavier em Goa*
description: Este óleo sobre tela pertence à série de vinte pinturas representando episódios da vida de S. Francisco Xavier (1506-1552), da autoria do pintor proto-barroco português André Reinoso (c. 1590-1641) e da sua oficina, situados no espaldar dos arcazes de madeira da sacristia seiscentista da Igreja de S. Roque. Foram colocados no lugar que ocupam actualmente em 1619, três anos antes da canonização do santo jesuíta, em 12 de Março de 1622, integrando-se numa vasta campanha de “propaganda” da vida e da obra do santo missionário, com vista à sua rápida canonização. A cena representa, com palpitante realismo, uma das pregações feitas por S. Francisco Xavier em Goa, cidade onde chegara em 1542. O quadro reveste-se de particular interesse do ponto de vista etnográfico, reproduzindo a diversidade de vestes e usos das populações indianas, bem como a variedade de castas sociais existentes naquela cidade, verdadeira cosmopolis do Oriente. O santo encontra-se de pé, em inflamada pregação, a que assistem nobres portugueses a cavalo, por detrás de um grupo de gentios convertidos – homens, mulheres e crianças. No plano de fundo da pintura, depara-se o cenário citadino de feição italiana.

Três anos antes da canonização oficial de São Francisco Xavier, em 1622, os jesuítas encomendaram a André Reinoso uma série de vinte pinturas sobre a vida do santo. A pintura mostra-o rodeado de convertidos: homens, mulheres, crianças e nobres portugueses a cavalo. Como pano de fundo, uma paisagem influenciada pelo maneirismo italiano.
holder: Santa Casa de Misericórdia / Museu de S. Roque
Santa Casa da Misericórdia de Lisboa / Museu de S. Roque.
keywords: Companhia de Jesus; Igreja de São Roque; Sacristia; Índia; Goa; Oriente; ciclo pictórico; peregrinação; miscigenação; exotismo; viagem; naturalismo.

ar.name: علبة
description: هذه العلبة المصبوبة المدورة لها غطاء مسطح في المركز الذي هو تراجع دائري عميق. ويتألف التزيين المثلم الكثيف من نجوم ثمانية الرؤوس وعناصر تزيين مزهرة وإفريز ذو أوراق مشطورة متراكبة. وعناصر التزيين التخطيطية الأربعة على الإطار تحتوي أبيات شعر من قبل الشاعر الفارسي في القرن الرابع عشر ، حافظ والتي تمجد لظى الحب الخالد وتقارنه بلهب الشمعة. والشيء المعهود في المشغولات المعدنية الصفوية هو التشكيل المنمنم للتزيين والذي يذكّر برسوم المخطوطات.
dates: أواخر القرن السادس عشر – النصف الأول من القرن السابع عشر

el.name: Κυκλικό κουτί
description: Το χυτό κυκλικό κουτί έχει επίπεδο κάλυμμα με βαθειά εσοχή στο κέντρο. Η πυκνή σκαλιστή διακόσμηση αποτελείται από οκτακόρυφα άστρα, άνθινα μετάλλια και ζώνη με  αλληλοεπικαλυπτόμενα φύλλα. Τέσσερα επιγραφικά μετάλλια στο χείλος περιέχουν στίχους του Πέρση ποιητή Χάφιζ που εξυμνεί την άσβεστη φλόγα της αγάπης συγκρίνοντάς την με τη φλόγα του κεριού. Τυπικό στοιχείο της σαφαβιδικής εποχής η μικρογραφική απόδοση του διακόσμου.

en.name: Box
description: This round cast box has a flat lid in the centre of which is a deep circular recess. The dense chased decoration consists of eight-pointed stars, floral cartouches and a frieze of overlapping split-leaves. The four epigraphic cartouches on the rim contain verses by the 14th-century Persian poet Hafiz, extolling the undying flame of love and comparing it to the flame of a candle. Typical of Safavid metalwork is the miniature rendering of the decoration, reminiscent of manuscript illustration.
dates: Hegira 10th-11th century / AD late 16th–first half of the 17th century
keywords: Bow; Safawid; Metalwork; floral decoration; geometric decoration; inscription; calligraphy; poetry

ar.name: قماط للرأس.
description: سمَّى فلسطينيو حبرون والقرى المحيطة هذا النوع من غطاء الرأس **العرقية**.وهي على شكل دائري له مركز محدد، وموشَّى بمنمنمات كثيفة ذات زخارف هندسية متصالبة الدرزات باللونين الأحمر والأسود؛ أما جزؤها الخلفي فقد علِّقت فيه قطع فضية عثمانية. إن قماطي الشعر (اللفائف) بالألوان المتعددة، إضافة إلى الشرائط السوداء الرفيعة المثبَّتة على جانبي غطاء الرأس، هي ملحقات حديثة. إن هذا النوع من غطاء الرأس ما يزال يرتدى في منطقة حبرون منذ أواخر القرن الثالث عشر / التاسع عشر حتى وقتنا الحاضر. وخلال الانتداب البريطاني في فلسطين كانت قُمُط الشعر (التي كانت تستخدم لربط الشعر على شكل كعكة مدورة تستقر على مؤخرة العنق) أطول بكثير ومصنوعة من خيوط صوفية مجدولة. لقد صنع غطاء الرأس للاستخدام اليومي.

يُعرف هذا النمط من أغطية الرأس، لدى النساء الفلسطينيات في الخليل، والقرى المحيطة بها، باسم **العرّاقية**. وهن يستخدمن أربطة الشعر مُتعدِّدة الألوان، المعروفة باسم **اللفّايات**، لعقد خصلات الشعر في كعكات مُدوَّرة تستقر خلف الأعناق. أما القطع النقدية العثمانية، فما هي إلا للزينة، ورمز للوفرة والسعة.
holder: متحف وصالة فنون كيلفينغروف، متاحف غلاسكو.
dates: أواخر الثالث عشر / أواخر التاسع عشر( قبل 1940).
keywords: توشية؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ زي تقليدي؛ عملة كالجواهر؛ عملة

en.name: Headdress.
description: The Palestinians of Hebron and the surrounding villages call this type of cap an *araqiyeh*. It is circular with a pointed centre and elaborately embroidered with red and black cross-stitched geometric decoration. Attached to the back of the cap are silver Ottoman coins. The two multicoloured hair-bands (*laffayef*), together with the thin black ribbons fixed to either side of the cap, are modern replacements. This type of headdress has been worn in the Hebron area from the late AH 13th century / AD late 19th century to the present day. During the British mandate in Palestine, the hair-bands (which were used for tying up the hair into a round bun that rested on the back of the neck) were much longer and were made of plaited woollen thread. This headdress was made for everyday use.

The Palestinian women of Hebron and the surrounding villages call this type of headdress an *araqiyeh*. They use the multicoloured hair-bands (*laffayef*) to tie up the hair into a round bun that rests on the back of the neck. The Ottoman coins are for decoration and a symbol of affluence.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
dates: Hegira late 13th century / AD late 19th century (before 1940).
dynasty: Ottoman, or under the British Mandate

es.name: Tocado.
description:
Los palestinos de Hebrón y los pueblos de alrededor llamaban a este tipo de gorro *araqiyeh*. El casquete, circular y un tanto puntiagudo, está finamente bordado con decoración geométrica roja y negra en punto de cruz; en la parte posterior lleva sujetas monedas de plata otomanas. Las dos bandas de múltiples colores, *(laffayef)*, y las finas cintas negras laterales son copias modernas.  
Este tipo de tocado se viene utilizando en la zona de Hebrón desde finales del siglo XIII / XIX hasta nuestros días. Durante el mandato británico de Palestina, las bandas para el pelo (utilizadas para enrollar el pelo en un rodete detrás del cuello) eran mucho más largas y estaban hechas de hilos de lana trenzados. Este tocado era de uso cotidiano.

Las mujeres palestinas de Hebrón y los pueblos de alrededor llaman a este tipo de tocado *araqiyeh*. El cabello se recoge en un rodete detrás del cuello por medio de coloridas bandas, *laffayef*. Las monedas otomanas, además de decorativas, son símbolo de prosperidad.

fr.name: Coiffure.
description: Les Palestiniens d'Hébron et des villages environnants appellent ce type de coiffure un “araqiyeh”. La coiffe de forme ronde à partie centrale en pointe est richement brodée d'un décor géométrique au point de croix rouge et noir. À l'arrière sont attachées des pièces d'argent ottomanes. Les deux bandeaux multicolores (“laffayef”) ainsi que les deux minces rubans fixés de chaque côté de la coiffure sont modernes. Ce type de coiffure a été porté dans la région d'Hébron de la fin du XIIIe siècle H (XIXe siècle J.-C.) jusqu'à nos jours. Pendant le mandat britannique sur la Palestine, les bandeaux (utilisés pour retenir un chignon qui reposait à la base du crâne) étaient beaucoup plus longs et souvent fabriqués en fil de laine tressé. Cette coiffure était portée tous les jours.

Les femmes palestiniennes d’Hébron et des villages alentour appellent ce type de coiffure *araqiyeh*. Elles utilisent les bandeaux multicolores (*laffayef*) pour retenir les cheveux en chignon, lequel repose à l’arrière du cou. Les pièces de monnaie ottomanes sont là pour la décoration et en signe de richesses.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
dates: Fin XIIIe siècle de l’Hégire (fin XIXe siècle J.-C. ; avant 1940).

en.name: *Assumption of the Virgin*
description: One of the first illusionist ceiling paintings in north Croatia, this is the work of the local painter, Blasius Grueber, whose naïve characters are typical of  the artist’s work. The charm and emotional impact of Grueber’s paintings is similar to that of local painters in Tyrol.

en.name: Nossa Senhora da Graça (Parish Church)
names: Nossa Senhora da Graça (Ega Parish Church)
description: The Parish Church, which is not far from the Paço dos Commendadores, was entirely altered at the beginning of the 16th century; the work being completed by Diogo de Castilho, on the death of Marcus Pires, in 1521. Pires was a disciple and collaborator of Boytac and completed his work at the Mosteiro de Santa Cruz and the Royal Palace in Coimbra. The Manueline portal is particularly fine with its plaited columns, the chancel has a naturalist *triumphal arch* also adorned by plaited columns and *archivolts*, and elegant *quadripartite vaulting*. The altar triptych which dates to c.1543, painted by a Court artist, and includes a portrait of the Commander, D. Afonso de Lencastre.

ar.name: مسامير
description:
تمثل هذه الأدوات مسامير البركة أو البركاتي المصنوعة من الحديد والمزينة بنقوش دقيقة. نشأت في عمان ، ونسبت الصفات التعويذة إلى المسامير لحماية الممتلكات أو المركبات.  
  
عند بناء منزل أو أثاث أو مركبات مثل المراكب الشراعية ، يتم دق هذه المسامير المباركة في الخشب للحصول على مزيد من الدعم والحماية. الصلاة الإسلامية بخط النسخ تغرس النعم الخفية على النفس أو نيابة عن شخص آخر لحسن الحظ.  
  
يتم تحويل الأشياء الصغيرة العادية مثل الأظافر إلى تعويذات لتبديد الشياطين (الجن) والشر والحوادث في الرحلات الطويلة. بما أن الحديد مادة ثمينة في الإسلام ، فإن الأظافر تكتسب المزيد من الخصائص الوقائية.

partner: متحف الشيخ فيصل بن قاسم ال ثاني

en.name: Nails
description:
These tools represent *baraka* (blessings) or *barkati* nails made of iron and adorned with fine inscriptions. Originating in Oman, talismanic qualities were attributed to the nails to protect property or vehicles.  
  
When constructing a home, furniture or vehicles such as dhows (boats), these blessed nails are hammered into the wood for additional support and protection. Islamic prayers in *naskh* calligraphy instil hidden blessings for oneself or on behalf of someone else for good fortune.  
  
Small ordinary objects like nails are transformed into talismans to dispel demons (*jinn*), evil and accidents on long journeys. As iron is a precious material in Islam, the nails gain further protective properties.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: Oman; Dhows; Talismans; India
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

en.name: Port of Alexandria
short_description: The Port of Alexandria during the departure of King Fu`ad on a trip to Europe. The Eastern Port of Alexandria is one of the oldest ports in the world. It was established in 2000 BCE, at the ancient village of Rakotis, to serve the coastal areas of the Pharos island (now the area of Ra's al-Tin in Alexandria). To its west lies the Bay of Anfushi.
keywords: Alexandria Port; King Fouad I; Trips to Europe

en.name: *Ensi*
description: The basic design of the Turkmen rug called *ensi* (or *engsi*) features two long narrow rectangles intersecting at a right angle, which accounts for the term formerly used to designate them: *khachli* or *khachlu* (from the Armenian *khach* = cross). The arch at the upper end, which sometimes also appears on the vertical band of the cross, seems to suggest *ensi*s may have been used as prayer rugs. More recently, though, the idea has been largely abandoned, the *ensi* being currently defined only as a door cover for felt tents. Sometimes, *ensi*s have been compared to the *chahār-bāgh*\-style Persian garden, whose layout resembles the quartered format of the *ensi*’s central field. The present example dates most probably from the last decade of the 19th century; its decorative repertoire is characteristic of the Tekke rugs, with Y-shape motifs and “ram’s horns” along the secondary outer border. This remarkably well preserved rug was part of the Romanian treasure sent to Moscow in 1916.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
keywords: *ensi*; Tekke
partner: The National Museum of Art of Romania

ar.name: عقد
description: لقد تركت العلاقات التجارية القديمة علامتها في مجوهرات شمال أفريقيا حيث بدأت طرق التجارة الممتدة من الهند ، الشرق الأوسط  في نقل الخرز إلى المنطقة في القرن السادس عشر. وإن ملايين الخرزات المنتجة صناعيا من أوربا بيعت لشمال أفريقيا في بداية القرن العشرين وقد كانت صغيرة وملونة وسهلة التصنيع وأتت بقياسات معيارية والتي ثبت إعجاب الناس بها وسريعا حلت محل العديد من المواد المحلية.

en.name: Necklace
description: Ancient trade relations left their mark on North African jewellery. Extensive trade routes from India, the Middle East, and Europe began transporting beads to the region in the 16th century. Millions of industrially produced beads from Europe were sold to North Africa in the early 20th century. They were small, colourful, easy to process, and came in standard sizes, which proved to strike a chord with the population and soon replaced many local materials.
materials: Glass and plastic beads, silver, cotton thread
tags: Glass and plastic beads, silver, cotton thread

en.name: Ewer with epigraphic decoration
description: In Iran, during the Seljuq period, a large number of moulds were produced, typically with epigraphic expressions, though figures or foliage are also found. The potters shaped ewers that often borrowed forms developed by coppersmiths. The turquoise glaze replaces with colour the detailed decoration of carving and silver inlay found in metal pieces.
holder: Museum of the Arab World Institute
materials: Siliceous clay; moulded and under glaze
partner: Museum of the Arab World Institute

fr.name: Aiguière à décor épigraphique
description: En Iran, à la période seljoukide, un grand nombre de pièces moulées ont été produites, essentiellement avec des formules épigraphiées, même si l'on trouve parfois des personnages ou des rinceaux. Les potiers façonnent en terre des aiguières qui souvent empruntent les formes élaborées par les dinandiers. La glaçure, ici turquoise, remplace par la couleur le décor soigné de ciselure et d'incrustation d'argent des pièces en métal.

en.name: Photograph of a steam locomotive (Krauss 74, No. 1769)
description: The first railway in Morocco was in the north of the country. Built in 1859, it connected Tétouan to the River Martil or Rio Martin as the Spanish – who built the railway – named it. In 1887, the Belgian government ordered a small locomotive factory, based in Munich, to build some rolling stock: Krauss 74, No. 1769.

en.name: *Zafraan* (Saffron)
description:
*Zafraan* (Saffron) used to flavour coffee.  
Coffee is always served at the beginning of a visit and is repeatedly offered until guests politely signal that they have had enough by rocking their cup from side to side. In order to keep coffee hot and fresh for unexpected guests it goes through many stages. After roasting and grinding the coffee beans the grains are added to boiling water inside a large *dallah* (coffee pot) called a *khamra*. Next, the liquid is poured into a medium-sized coffee pot called a *taljeemah*. At this stage cardamom seeds, saffron and rose water may be added for flavour. From this jug, the coffee is poured into a serving *dallah* referred to as a *mezallah*, where the coffee is refined and filtered. The server must hold the mezallah with their left hand and distribute the *fanayeel* (coffee cups) using the right hand. The coffee should fill less than half of the cup.
dates: Hegira mid 14th century / AD mid 20th century
keywords: saffron; coffee

en.name: Victor Hugo at Casteret
short_description: A number of important political and literary figures moved abroad during Napoléon III's authoritarian rule. This was the case with Victor Hugo, who left France between 1852 and 1870 as he refused to live under the reign of, "Napoléon le Petit", as he liked to call him.
keywords: Empire; exile

fr.name: Victor Hugo à Casteret
short_description: Sous l'Empire autoritaire de Napoléon III, nombre de personnalités littéraires et politiques partent à l'étranger. C'est le cas de Victor Hugo qui ne voulant vivre en France sous le règne de celui qu'il appelle "Napoléon le Petit", vit en exil de 1852 à 1870.
keywords: Empire; exil

en.name: Spanish Steps
description: The stairway is dynamically structured, fragmented into a series of curvilinear segments, and paused by a large central square. The fluidity of the lines, totally devoid of angles, aim at recalling a waterfall: indeed, it almost simulates the fall of the water along the slopes of the Pincio, ideally ending in the Fontana della Barcaccia by Pietro Bernini, at the centre of the square. Intended as a pleasant place to stop and have a break, as De Sanctis himself stated, the stairway has low walls to allow one to sit on them, stone benches placed every twelve steps and landings large enough to induce a pause during the effort of the ascent. Through the curvilinear movement of the ramps, De Sanctis was also able to correct the visual irregularity of the site, characterized by pre-existing buildings placed on the sides of the stairway which were not aligned along parallel axes; by doing so, he managed to suggest the idea of a pre-existing visual axis between the facade of the church and the city below. In this complex architectural organism, two main sections can be distinguished: one at the top and characterized by a protruding circular volume flanked by two lateral stairs and an underlying ramp in axis with it, and a lower one (separated from the other by a large central widening) which repeats the same compositional scheme, but with a livelier articulation of the ramp that one encounters when going up from Piazza di Spagna.

The Spanish Steps were built to link piazza di Spagna with Via Felice, the first great street planned by Sixtus V (1585). Several projects were made between 1717 and 1720, also by Alessandro Specchi. “A protruding volume is flanked by convex stairs and a straight flight in front. The upper unit presents the theme in its basic form; the lower constitutes an articulate and lively variation” (C. Norberg-Schulz. Late Baroque and Rococo Architecture.).
history:
Until the beginning of the 18th century, the Santissima Trinità dei Monti, the church of the French nation located on the top of the Pincio hill, was connected through steep paths to the lively district below that had flourished around Piazza di Spagna. In the 1660s the French Crown had allocated 10,000 scudi, later raised to 20,000 at the beginning of the following century, for the construction of a stairway between the church and Piazza di Spagna. In 1660, at the time of Cardinal Mazarin, Gian Lorenzo Bernini proposed a project that introduced for the first time the idea of a stairway articulated in a series of curvilinear ramps interrupted by resting areas in place of a rectilinear and rectangular stairway (such as those of the Basilica of St. Mary of the Altar of Heaven known as Aracoeli or at the Capitoline Hill cordonata). However, the project was set aside by Pope Alexander VII, who did not like the idea of the French occupying such a large portion of land. It was only at the beginning of the 18th century, under Clement XI, that a competition was launched. The competitors were Alessandro Specchi (who held the title of Architect of the Roman People and was known for having designed the now the lost Port of Ripetta, which deployed a similar articulation in curvilinear ramps), Francesco De Sanctis (architect of the Minims of the Trinità dei Monti) and Alessandro Gaulli.  
On the death of Clement XI, the new Pope Innocent XIII and the friars of Trinità dei Monti chose De Sanctis’s project, which was carried out between 1723 and 1726 and was partly inspired, though with some variations, to the Berninian design. One of the main reasons why De Sanctis’s stairway was chosen was its being perfectly visible in all its parts (allowing therefore to be properly controlled) both from below and from above, thus guaranteeing respect for public order.

it.name: Scalinata di Trinità dei Monti
description:
La scala si presenta come una struttura dinamica, frammentata in una serie di segmenti curvilinei, pausata da una larga piazza centrale. Elemento distintivo è quello della cascata e della fluidità delle linee, totalmente prive di angoli, quasi si simulasse la caduta delle acque lungo le pendici del Pincio, terminante idealmente nella Fontana della Barcaccia di Pietro Bernini, al centro della piazza.  
Inteso come luogo dove sostare piacevolmente, come lo stesso De Sanctis affermava, la scalinata presenta dei muri bassi per potersi sedere, delle panche di pietra poste ogni dodici gradini e dei pianerottoli sufficientemente ampi da indurre a una pausa per alleviare lo sforzo della salita. Attraverso il movimento curvilineo delle rampe De Sanctis riuscì inoltre a correggere visivamente l’irregolarità del sito, caratterizzato da preesistenti blocchi di edifici posti ai lati della scalinata non allineati secondo assi paralleli; come pure suggerì l’idea che un asse visivo tra la facciata della chiesa e la città sottostante esistesse ancor prima della costruzione della scalinata.  
In questo articolato organismo si possono distinguere due sezioni principali: una posta in alto e caratterizzata da un volume circolare aggettante fiancheggiato da due scale laterali con una sottostante rampa posta in asse con esso, e una più in basso (separata dall’altra dall’ampio slargo centrale) che ne ripete lo schema compositivo, ma con una più vivace articolazione della rampa che si incontra salendo da piazza di Spagna.

La creazione della scalinata costituì un importantissimo conseguimento nella politica urbanistica pontificia: essa metteva in comunicazione l’area intorno alla chiesa della Trinità dei Monti con il sottostante quartiere di piazza di Spagna. Con il suo sistema di rampe e pianerottoli, dalle fluide forme concave e convesse, abolisce per la prima volta la rigidità delle tradizionali scale monumentali come quelle dell’Aracoeli o del Campidoglio.
history: Fino agli inizi del Settecento la Ss. Trinità dei Monti, chiesa della nazione francese situata sulla sommità del colle Pincio, era collegata al sottostante vivace quartiere gravitante attorno a piazza di Spagna attraverso dei ripidi sentieri. La corona francese aveva stanziato, negli anni ’60 del Seicento, 10.000 scudi, aumentati poi a 20.000 agli inizi del secolo successivo, per la costruzione di una scalinata che collegasse la chiesa con piazza di Spagna. Gian Lorenzo Bernini elaborò nel 1660, all’epoca del cardinale Mazzarino, un progetto che introduceva per la prima volta l’idea di una scalinata articolata in una serie di rampe curvilinee intervallate da pause in luogo di una scala rettilinea di forma rettangolare (come quelle dell’Aracoeli o del Campidoglio). Il progetto venne però accantonato da papa Alessandro VII che non gradiva l’occupazione di quella vasta porzione di suolo da parte francese. Fu solo agli inizi del Settecento, sotto Clemente XI, che si bandì un concorso cui parteciparono Alessandro Specchi (architetto del Popolo Romano, già autore dello scomparso Porto di Ripetta in cui era presente un’analoga articolazione in rampe curvilinee), Francesco De Sanctis (architetto dei Frati Minimi della Trinità dei Monti) e Alessandro Gaulli. Alla morte di Clemente XI, il nuovo papa Innocenzo XIII e i frati di Trinità dei Monti scelsero il progetto di De Sanctis, realizzato tra il 1723 e il 1726, che riprendeva con qualche variante il disegno berniniano. Uno dei principali motivi per cui venne scelta la scala di De Sanctis fu il suo essere perfettamente visibile in ogni sua parte (e quindi ben controllabile) sia dal basso che dall’alto, garantendo in questo modo il rispetto dell’ordine pubblico.
keywords: Urbanistica; scalinata

en.name: Weighing stone
description: This weighing stone, which is fitted with an iron suspension ring, has a *kufic* inscription incised around its bulbous body. It reads "Al-Hasan Ibn Hatim…" with the rest of the inscription remaining undeciphered. The original context in which such a stone weight might have been used, remains unknown.
keywords: Measuring instrument; Kufic

en.name: *The Sultan’s Horses* (Drawing 19 for the *XX Dessins* album)
description: This drawing by Amadeo de Souza-Cardoso forms part of an album, *XX Dessins*, which was published in 1912 and represents a key point of breakthrough for the artist. The context of the work can be explained by his interest in the Western primitivists, the influence of African art, the experiences that he exchanged with Brancusi and Modigliani, and his study of Henri Rousseau’s work. The artist aims to present a demarcated image of his own identity: in an elegantly sophisticated picture replete with medieval imagery, he produces an original work that explores volumes, dynamic forms, and the sense of speed. It was this clearly defined image that Amadeo presented at the Armory Show in 1913, where his work achieved great success in both critical and market terms.
holder: Modern Art Centre, Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
keywords: Amadeo Sousa Cardoso; breaks; avant-garde; medieval; primitivists; african art
partner: Modern Art Centre, Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation

en.name: *Thronus Pietatis*
description:
The crucified Christ is at the centre of the painting; the Holy Father hovers in the clouds holding up the cross, supported in the lower part by two *putti*. Above His head the Holy Ghost – a dove radiating light – is surrounded by cherubs.  
*Thronus Pietatis* is by the Bavarian painter, Johann Michael Rottmayr, who later moved to Austria and made his name working for the Austrian Monarchy. His first works in Vienna were frescoes in Lichtenstein Palace. He then worked in Melk Abbey and in the Viennese Church of St Charles, Borromeo.  
One of the best-known painters of late Austrian Baroque, his work is characterised by voluptuous figures, strong colours and Baroque gesture. His later works stand apart with calmer movement and paler colours.  
The painting was a commission for the chapel at Valpovo Castle owned by the Hilleprand-Prandau family, by origin from Tyrol. The Prandaus were one of the four most important foreign aristocratic families in Slavonia. The Habsburg Crown granted estates to foreign nobles in Slavonia after the retreat of the Ottoman Turks.

en.name: Church of San Miguel
description:
In the calle Real de Santo Domingo, the Church of San Miguel occupies the former building of the Convent and Church of Santo Domingo, which moved to the outskirts of the town to an area with an Islamic population that needed to be indoctrinated. The establishment of the Parish of San Miguel at its present site took place in 1958, after the reconstruction carried out by the Dirección General de Regiones Devastadas in 1955. Founded by the Catholic Monarchs at the end of the 15th century, the original church is earlier than other churches in the town, such as Santiago, or Santa Ana. In 1560, a new church was built, which was still unfinished in 1589 when the master Juan Huete was working on it.  
Entry to the church is through a semicircular arch with Doric pilasters and an entablature with the symbols of the Predicant Order of the Dominicans, dogs and angels, set within a simple façade. It has three aisles with pointed arches on pillars, a choir at the foot and a sanctuary with a pointed chancel arch. The separate side aisles are in three individual spaces, which each has a roof of semicircular vaulting perpendicular to the axis of the church itself.  
Outstanding among the whole are the eight-part Mudéjar ceilings in the nave, the sanctuary and the old chapel of the Virgin del Rosario, on the Gospel side near the main altar, as is usual in the other Mudéjar churches in Guadix. The first of these is a magnificent example of an eight-part rectangular *armadura de limas moamares* decorated in polychrome, and with the *almizate* decorated with strapwork. Displayed at both ends are the arms of the Order of Santo Domingo and four pairs of interlocking anchor ties on corbels.  
The natural-wood *armadura* in the sanctuary is also eight-sided and of *limas moamares* on a square base, completely *apeinazada* and with a pinecone of *muqarnas* in the *almizate*.  
The *armadura* of the Old Chapel of the Virgin del Rosario, again eightsided but cupula-shaped, is *apeinazada* with ten-strand knots, and a pinecone- shaped *muqarnas* in the centre.  
The Baroque Chapel of the Virgin del Rosario completes the interior of the church, added and funded by the Bishop Fray Clemente in 1690. The polygonal plan, inspired by the Chapel of San Torcuato in the Cathedral of Guadix, appears to be two-levels high, simulated by means of Ionic entablatures.  
This very simply decorated church has undergone various restorations in more recent times. These, above all, have affected the interior walls and highlighted the magnificent examples of the ceilings preserved in the interior.

es.name: Iglesia de San Miguel
description:
En la calle Real de Santo Domingo, ocupando el edificio del convento y templo de Santo Domingo, que se emplazó a las afueras de la ciudad, en una zona de población islámica a la que había que adoctrinar, la parroquia de San Miguel se instaló en su actual sede en 1958, tras la reconstrucción que hizo la Dirección General de Regiones Devastadas en 1955.  
Fundación de los Reyes Católicos de finales del siglo XV, su obra primitiva es anterior a otras de la ciudad, como las iglesias de Santiago o Santa Ana. En 1560 se edificó el nuevo templo, que todavía en 1589 seguía en construcción, cuando el maestro Juan Huete trabajaba en él.  
El templo, al que se accede por una sencilla fachada con arco de medio punto con pilastras dóricas y sobre cuyo entablamento se ven símbolos de la Orden de Predicadores, perros y ángeles, se organiza en tres naves, con arcos apuntados sobre pilares, coro a los pies y capilla mayor con arco de triunfo apuntado. Las naves laterales se articulan en tres espacios individualizados y cubiertos con bóvedas de medio punto perpendiculares al eje de la iglesia.  
En el conjunto destacan las cubiertas mudéjares ochavadas de la nave principal, el presbiterio y la antigua capilla de la Virgen del Rosario, situada en el lado del Evangelio, junto a la capilla mayor, siguiendo la tónica de las iglesias mudéjares de la ciudad de Guadix. La primera de ellas es un ejemplo magnífico de *armadura* rectangular ochavada de *limas moamares* policromada, *almizate* apeinazado, en cuyos extremos lucen los escudos de la orden de Santo Domingo, y cuatro pares de tirantes apeinazados sobre canes.  
La *armadura* del presbiterio, que conserva el color natural de la madera, es también ochavada de *limas* moamares sobre planta cuadrada, totalmente *apeinazada* y con piña de *mocárabe* en el *almizate*.  
La *armadura* de la antigua capilla de la Virgen del Rosario, de nuevo ochavada y tendente a la forma cupular, se apeinaza con lazo de diez y presenta una piña de *mocárabe* en el centro.  
El conjunto interior se cierra con la capilla barroca de la Virgen del Rosario, agregada y costeada por el obispo Fray Clemente Álvarez en 1690. La planta poligonal se inspira en la capilla de San Torcuato de la catedral de Guadix, y tiene dos cuerpos en altura simulados por medio de entablamentos jónicos.  
La iglesia, decorada muy sencillamente, ha conocido recientes procesos de restauración que han afectado sobre todo a los paramentos interiores y que han resaltado los magníficos ejemplos de cubiertas que encierra en su interior.

en.name: Inkstand (*divit*)
description: The edges of the inkwell, as well as the sides and terminals of the pen case are decorated with chiselled vegetal motifs. Engraved motifs cover the base of the inkwell and partially its back. The hinged cover of the inkwell is set with an amethyst. The base of the inkwell and the back of the pen case are both marked with the *tughra* of Sultan Ahmed III (1703 - 1730). Traces of textile (*liqa*) have been found inside the inkwell. On the upper side, the maker’s stamp: *‘amal Muhammad*.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
keywords: Inkstand (divit)
materials: Cast silver, chiselled, engraved, gilded; amethyst
partner: National Museum of Art of Romania

en.name: Altar of the Holy Cross (Church of the Holy Cross)
description:
This is the final work of the sculptor, Francesco Robba, the most proficient marble sculptor of the Baroque period in northern Croatia. Robba trained in the workshop of the Venetian sculptor, Pietro Baratta, and in 1720 arrived in Ljubljana (Slovenia), where in 1727, he took over the workshop of his father-in-law, the Ljubljana altar builder Luka Mislej. Apart from the Slovene works, there are also known works by Robba in Klagenfurt, and several altars and statues made for clients from Croatia, primarily for the Jesuit Church of St Catherine and Zagreb Cathedral. His works represent High Baroque marble sculpture and altar making at their peak in Croatia.  
By reducing the architectural elements, the decorative parts benefit through sublimation into simple and yet powerful curved motifs. Robba achieves in the Altar of the Holy Cross a monumental altar, a composition both emphatic and dynamic. The diagonal axes of the sculptural groups *Moses with the Bronze Serpent* and *Abraham Sacrificing Isaac* on the side-ends of the altar, direct the viewer's attention to the central figure of the Crucified Christ, which, made prominent with a frame of yellowish marble, stands out against a background of drapery carved in black marble. With the repetition of oval motifs and segments of ovals in the ground plan and elevation of the altar (the framework of the central sculpture), and on its surfaces (the frame of the relief of the stipes and the ornaments on the sculptures' pedestals), a suggestive pulsating rhythm is achieved that corresponds to the marked dynamism of the altar sculpture. The Altar of the Holy Cross recognisably developed from the principles of the Italian High Baroque, with clearly marked features of the mature phase of Robba's individual style. There are clear compositional similarities between the figural groups and some Italian sculptures from the last quarter of the 17th century. For example, G. Le Court's, high altar in Sant'Andrea della Zirada of 1678 and A. Pozzo's Altar of St Ignatius in the Roman Church Il Gesù, as well as that seen 20 years later in the Dorfmeister approach to the altar in the Church of Maria Taferl in Vienna.

The Altar of the Holy Cross is the final and most mature achievement of the sculptor, Franceso Robba, who by his artistic achievements is a notable figure in European Baroque sculpture and altar making. The great suggestiveness and dynamism of his work is achieved by a successful synthesis of the sculptural, architectural and decorative elements of the altar, along with a well-considered application of various coloured marbles.
history: The altar, which was originally in the nave of Zagreb Cathedral, was moved to Križevci as the result of the Neo-Gothic renovation that took place after the great earthquake of 1880. At the beginning of 1748, Robba signed a contract with the Zagreb chapter to make the altar for the sum of 1600 florins, provided from the estate of Canon Georg Rees. However, the altar was only completed and consecrated in 1756.
keywords: Križevci, Zagreb Cathedral, Francesco Robba, sculpture
tags: Križevci, Zagreb Cathedral, Francesco Robba, sculpture

ar.name: كتلة صخرية عليها نقش بارز لزخرفة نباتية من رمان وأغصان منمنمة.
description:
كتلة صخرية متوازية المستطيلات على وجهها الأمامي زخرفة منحوتة بشكل بارز. وتتكون هذه الزخرفة من جذع يتفرع منه غصنان يتقاطعان ويمتدان بشكل متموج، ثم يتفرعان في التفافات مزدوجة لينتهيا بأوراق أو حبات رمان منمنمة.  
ترجع هذه الكتلة المنحوتة إلى مجموعة معمارية كبرى، لأنها كانت مصممة لتكون قطعة من الزخرفة المعمارية في بوابة قصر خربة المنية. ولأن بناء القصر لم يكتمل بقيت هذه المجموعة غير معروفة التركيب. وقد أمر الخليفة الأموي الوليد الأول بين 705 و715 ببناء قصر صغير في خربة المِنية على الشاطئ الشمالي الغربي لبحيرة طبريا، وكان من المقرر أن يشتمل هذا القصر، الذي لم يكتمل بناؤه، على جناح دخول كامل ومزخرف. ويحتوي القصر على مجموعة من غرف الاستقبال الرائعة ذات الأرضية الفسيفسائية إلى جانب مسجد فيه محراب على شكل نصف دائرة. وينتمي طراز زخرفة هذا البناء الحجري في خربة المِنية إلى تقاليد البناء في أواخر العصور القديمة، ولكنه من ناحية أخرى يحتوي على تغييرات كبيرة تتجلى في منمنمات واضحة تعود للعصور الإسلامية الأولى. ويكثر استخدام رسوم الرمان في زخارف البناء المنمنمة على الحجر والجص بالإضافة إلى وجودها على الفسيفساء.  
شاركت المتاحف الألمانية في السنوات 1936 إلى 1939 في عمليات التنقيب الأثري في خربة المِنية وقد تمكن المتحف من الحصول على جزء هام من اللُقى. أما النصف الآخر من المكتشفات فهو موجود في القدس.

هذه الكتلة من الحجر الجيري، تمَّ استخراجه من قصر خربة المنية، غير المنجزة، القريبة من طبريا، على البحيرة التي أعطت اسمها للمدينة، وهو قصر بُني للخليفة الأموي الوليد الأول. وقد كان هذا التصميم مُعَّداً لتزيين جزء من المدخل المُفضي إلى القصر.
place: قصر خربة المِنية على بحيرة طبريا، إسرائيل.
keywords: جزء من مجموعة معمارية؛ حجر منحوت؛ كتلة صخرية منحوتة؛ الفنون الزخرفية
partner: متحف الفن الإسلامي في متحف بيرغامون ، المتاحف الحكومية

de.name: Steinblock mit floralem Relief aus stilisierten Ranken und Granatäpfeln.
description: Hochrechteckiger Steinblock mit Reliefdekor auf der Vorderseite. Der Dekor besteht aus einem Stamm, aus dem zwei Rankenstiele hervorwachsen. Die Ranken überkreuzen sich und verlaufen in Schwüngen wie eine Wellenranke und verzweigen sich in paarige Einrollungen und laufen in Blättern oder stilisierten Granatäpfeln aus. Der Reliefblock stammt aus einem größeren architektonischen Zusammenhang, da er für den Architekturdekor des Eingangsbereiches des Palastes in Khirbat al-Minya vorgesehen war. Da der Palast nie fertig wurde, ist der Gesamtzusammenhang nicht bekannt. Der omaijadische Kalif al-Walid I. ließ zwischen 705 und 715 einen kleinen Palast in Khirbat al-Minya bei Tiberias am Nordwestufer des Sees Genezareth bauen. Der Palast, der nie fertiggestellt wurde, sollte einen umfangreich dekorierten Eingangstrakt haben und zeichnet sich außerdem durch eine prächtige Audienzraumgruppe mit Mosaikfußböden und eine Moschee mit halbkreisförmiger Gebetsnische aus. Der steinerne Baudekor in Khirbat al-Minya steht ganz in der Tradition der Spätantike, läßt aber andererseits deutlich Veränderungen durch stärkere Stilisierungen erkennen, wie sie für die frühislamische Epoche charakteristisch waren. Die Verwendung stilisierter Granatäpfel findet sich häufig im omaijadischen Baudekor aus Stein und Stuck und zudem auf Mosaiken. Die Berliner Museen beteiligten sich in den Jahren 1936-1939 an den Ausgrabungen in Khirbat al-Minya, so daß dem Museum ein wichtiger Teil der Funde überlassen wurde. Die andere Hälfte der Funde befindet sich in Jerusalem.

Dieser Kalksteinquader wurde in dem unbeendeten Palast von Khirbat al-Minya ausgegraben, der in der Nähe von Tiberias am See Genezareth für den Umayyaden-Kalifen al-Walid I. gebaut worden war. Das Relief zeigt wellenförmige Ranken, die in Weinblättern und Granatäpfeln enden. Der Quader diente zur Verzierung des Eingangs zum Palast.
dates: Periode von al-Walid I., um 86-96 H. / 705-715
place: Palast von Khirbat al-Minya am See Genezareth, Israel.
keywords: Relief; dekorative Kunst; Bauglied aus einem architektonischen Zusammenhang
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Decorative stone with stylised scrollwork and pomegranates.
description:
This rectangular block of stone displays decorative relief work on its front side. The decoration comprises two tendril stems growing out of a single stalk. The tendrils interweave with each other, sweeping across like waves, and branch out into pairs of scrolls, before turning into leaves or stylised pomegranates.  
The relief stone block came from a larger architectural complex, and was intended as a piece of ornamental decoration for the entrance area of the palace in Khirbat al-Minya. As the palace was never completed, it is not known what the entire complex would have been. The Umayyad Caliph al-Walid I ordered the building of a small palace in Khirbat al-Minya next to Tiberias on the northwestern banks of the Sea of Galilee between AH 86 and 96 (AD 705–15). The palace, which was never finished, was designed to have an extensively decorated entrance hall, but it was nevertheless exceptional for its splendid audience hall, complete with mosaic floors, as well as a mosque with a semi-circular prayer niche. The stone decoration in Khirbat al-Minya is completely at one with the traditions of Late Antiquity, although it also incorporates clear differences demonstrated by heavier stylisation that was characteristic of the Early Islamic period. The use of stylised pomegranates can principally be found in the architectural ornamentation of the Umayyad period in stone and stuccowork as well as on mosaics.  
The Berlin Museums participated in 1936–9 in the excavation in Khirbat al-Minya, which is why the Museum was allowed to have an important part of the discoveries. The other half of what was found remains in Jerusalem.

This limestone block was excavated from the unfinished palace of Khirbat al-Minya near Tiberias on the Sea of Galilee, built for the Umayyad Caliph al-Walid I. The relief shows undulating stems ending in vine leaves and pomegranates. This design was to decorate part of the entrance into the palace.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
place: Palace of Khirbat al-Minya on the Sea of Galilee, Israel.
dynasty: Umayyad, period of Caliph al-Walid I (r. *c*. AH 86–96 / AD 705–15)
keywords: Relief decoration; decorative arts; vegetal decoration
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

es.name: Piedra decorativa con tallos y granadas estilizados.
description:
Bloque de piedra rectangular con la parte frontal decorada en relieve. La decoración consiste en un tallo del que nacen otros dos, entrelazados y ondulantes. De ellos brotan pares ramitas curvas terminadas en hojas o estilizadas granadas.  
Este relieve iba a formar parte de la ornamentación de la entrada del complejo arquitectónico de Jirbat al-Minya. Durante los años de su gobierno (86-96 / 705-715), el califa omeya al-Walid I mandó construir un pequeño palacio en Jirbat al-Minya, cerca de Tiberíades, en la costa noroeste del mar de Galilea. Del palacio, que nunca llegó a terminarse, se sabe que iba a tener una sala de entrada profusamente decorada y una excepcional sala de audiencias con suelos de mosaico, así como una mezquita con *mihrab* de planta semicircular. La decoración en piedra seguía fielmente la tradición de la Antigüedad tardía, aunque con la fuerte estilización propia del primer estilo islámico. Las granadas estilizadas aparecen principalmente en la ornamentación arquitectónica en piedra, estuco y mosaico del periodo omeya.  
Los museos de Berlín participaron en las excavaciones llevadas a cabo en Jirbat al-Minya entre 1936 y 1939, de ahí que conserven buena parte de los hallazgos, la mitad de los cuales permanece en Jerusalén.

Bloque de piedra caliza hallado en las excavaciones del inacabado palacio de Jirbat al-Minya, cerca de Tiberíades, a orillas de del mar de Galilea, mandado construir por el califa omeya al-Walid I. Este relieve de tallos ondulantes con hojas de parra y granadas iba a formar parte de la decoración de la entrada del palacio.
holder: Museo de Arte Islámico del Museo Pergamon
dates: Alrededor de los años 86–96 de la Hégira / 705–715 d. C.
place: Palacio de Jirbat al-Minya, a orillas del mar de Galilea (Israel).
dynasty: Omeyas, periodo del califa al-Walid I (r. 86–96 / 705–715)
keywords: relieve; arte decorativo; parte de un edificio de un complejo arquitectónico
tags: parte de un edificio de un complejo arquitectónico
partner: Museo de Arte Islámico en el Museo de Pérgamo, Museos Estatales

fr.name: Pierre décorative à relief de rinceaux stylisés et de grenades.
description:
Cette pierre rectangulaire présente sur sa face antérieure un décor en relief composé d'un tronc d'où partent des tiges tournées en rinceaux. Ces rinceaux se recoupent et courent tels des vagues en se ramifiant par paire enroulée et se terminant par des feuilles et des grenades stylisées.  
Ce relief provient d'un ensemble plus important puisqu'il était prévu pour l'ornementation de l'entrée du palais de Khirbat al-Minya. Le palais n'ayant jamais été achevé, on ne peut se faire une idée de l'ensemble. Le calife omeyyade al-Walid Ier fit bâtir entre 705 et 715 J.-C. un palais de petites dimensions à Khirbat al-Minya près de Tibériade, sur la rive nord-ouest du lac Génézareth. La bâtisse devait avoir une entrée imposante et se distingue par l'importance des salles d'audience ornées de mosaïques au sol et par une mosquée à la niche de prière en demi-cercle. Le décor de pierre sculptée de Khirbat al-Minya est tout à fait dans la tradition de l'Antiquité tardive, bien que l'on remarque déjà des changements dus à la forte stylisation, caractéristique des débuts de l'époque islamique. La grenade stylisée est un motif récurrent à l'époque omeyyade, on la trouve dans les décors de pierre, de stuc et surtout de mosaïque.  
Les musées de Berlin prirent part à la campagne de fouilles de 1936-1939 à Khirbat al-Minya et bon nombre des objets découverts leur fut remis, le reste se trouvant à Jérusalem.

Ce bloc de calcaire provient des fouilles du palais inachevé de Khirbat al-Minya près de Tibériade sur la mer de Galilée, construit pour le calife omeyyade al-Walid Ier. Ce relief montre des tiges ondulantes qui se terminent par des feuilles de vigne et des grenades. Ce décor était destiné à orner une partie de l'entrée du palais.
dates: règne d’al-Walid Ier, v. 86-96 H / 705-715 J.-C.
place: Palais de Khirbat al-Minya sur le lac Génézareth, Israël.
keywords: relief ; arts décoratives ; élément d’un ensemble architectural
partner: Musée d’art islamique du Pergamon Museum (Museum für Islamische Kunst)

en.name: *Chancel of the Church of St Helena*
short_description: The slightly confusing title of this print by David Roberts actually refers to the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, first commissioned in 327 AD by the Emperor Constantine and his mother Helena. at the spot where it is believed Jesus was born. The view captures the area before the iconostasis shielding the main altar in the eastern apse of the church, as well as - below on the right - the south-eastern entrance to the Grotto of the Nativity.The Church of the Nativity is one of the foremost pilgrimage sites for Christians and would have been a highlight on the itinerary of European travellers to the Holy Land. As is typical for his works, Roberts exaggerates the proportions of the architecture in relation to the human figures, which appear dwarfed by the majesty and monumentality of the structures that surround them.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority

en.name: *Allegory of Fortune, of Love and of the Four Seasons*
description: Charged by Marc’Antonio Ranuzzi, Marc’Antonio Franceschini and the quadratura painter Enrico Haffner realized the allegorical figures in the ceiling of this room on the first floor of the palace, presumably between 1680 and 1681. Very interesting and original is the allegory in the centre of the vault showing Fortune and her wheel which, moved by the wind, holds Cupid in chains.
place: Ceiling decoration of a room of the first floor of the palace, Palazzo Ranuzzi
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: *Allegoria della Fortuna, dell'Amore e delle Quattro Stagioni*
description: Il pittore Marc’Antonio Franceschini e il quadraturista  Enrico Haffner realizzarono per incarico di  Marc’Antonio Ranuzzi le figure allegoriche del soffitto di questa stanza al primo piano del palazzo, tra il 1680 e il 1681. Molto interessante è l'allegoria della Fortuna e della sua ruota che mossa dal vento tiene incatenato Cupido al centro della volta.
place: Decorazione di stanza al primo piano, Palazzo Ranuzzi

ar.name: بلاطة جدارية.
description: بلاطة مربَّعة الشكل، تحتوي في وسطها على رسم كبير لضميمة متماثلة من زهر اللوتس، مؤلفة من عدة أطوار من البتلات والأوراق، ومحاطة بغصينين على شكل سنابل القمح. وقد نفِّذ التصميم كله بلون واحد هو الأزرق (دون تظليل أو تأطير أسود) على خلفية بيضاء. يبين تصميم هذه البلاطة إلى أي مدى بلغ تأثير صناعة الخزف الأبيض والأزرق الصينية في تطور معالجة المواد الأولية في الشرق الأوسط. إن النوع الذي يندرج ضمنه هذا البلاط يشتمل على ما يعرَف أكثر باسم البلاط السداسي الأبيض والأزرق الذي اكتشف مزخرفاً أحياناً بالفيروزي والأسود.

تصميم شعار الزنبق لبلاط هذا الجدار المكسوّ بالخزف الدمشقي، يشي بمدى تأثر الفن الإسلامي بنظيره الصيني. ثمّة عدد من أمثلة هذا النمط من البلاط الأزرق والأبيض، يمكن أن يُرى على جدران مزار وجامع التيروزي، المبني في دمشق في ثلاثينيات القرن التاسع الهجري/ثلاثينيات القرن الخامس عشر الميلادي.
keywords: زخرفة نباتية؛ عمارة؛  تأثير صناعة الخزف الصينية؛ الأبيض والأزرق
materials: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية، ملونة بالأزرق تحت طبقة مزججة شفافة.
tags: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية، ملونة بالأزرق تحت طبقة مزججة شفافة.

en.name: Wall tile.
description: A square tile decorated with a large, central, symmetrical lotus-rosette design that is made up of several layers of petals and leaves, and which is surrounded by two wheat-stem-shaped branches. The entire design is executed in one colour blue (without shading or black outline) on a white background. The design of this tile shows the extent to which Middle Eastern material culture was influenced by Chinese blue-and-white porcelain ceramics. The genre to which this tile belongs includes the more commonly known blue-and-white hexagonal tiles that are sometimes also found decorated in turquoise and black.

The lotus-rosette design on this Damascus-ware wall tile reveals the extent to which its Chinese counterpart has influenced Islamic Art. A number of examples of this type of blue-and-white tile can still be seen on the walls of Al-Tawrizi Shrine and Mosque, built in Damascus in the AH 830s / AD 1430s.
keywords: Floral decoration; architecture, Chinese influence; blue-and-white
materials: Stone-paste (fritware), painted blue under a transparent glaze.
tags: Stone-paste (fritware), painted blue under a transparent glaze.

es.name: Azulejo.
description:
Azulejo cuadrado decorado con un gran diseño central simétrico en forma de roseta de lotos con varios niveles de pétalos y hojas, rodeada de dos ramas en forma de espigas. Todo el diseño está pintado en color azul (sin sombreados ni contorno negro).  
Este azulejo demuestra hasta qué punto llegó la influencia de las porcelanas blanquiazules chinas en la cultura material de Oriente Próximo. Pertenece a un tipo que incluye los conocidos azulejos hexagonales en azul y blanco, a veces decorados también en turquesa y negro.

El diseño en forma de roseta de lotos de este azulejo procedente de Damasco revela el alcance de la influencia de la cerámica china en el arte islámico. En las paredes del santuario y mezquita de Al-Tawrizi, construida en Damasco en la década de 830 / 1427-1437, aún se pueden contemplar azulejos blanquiazules como este.
dates: Siglo IX de la Hégira / XV d. C.
keywords: decoración floral; arquitectura; influencia china; blanquiazul
materials: Pasta cerámica (frita) pintada en azul bajo vidriado transparente.
tags: Pasta cerámica (frita) pintada en azul bajo vidriado transparente.

fr.name: Carreau mural.
description: Carreau de format carré décoré d'une importante fleur de lotus centrale composée symétriquement d'étagements de pétales et de feuilles, entourée de deux épis de blé sur tige. Le dessin tout entier est traité en une seule couleur, le bleu (sans ombre ni contour) sur fond blanc. Ce carreau montre à quel point la culture matérielle moyen-orientale était influencée par les porcelaines chinoises “bleu et blanc”. Le genre auquel appartient cet élément comprend les carreaux hexagonaux “bleu et blanc” plus courants que l'on trouve parfois traités en noir et turquoise.

La fleur de lotus dessinée sur ce carreau de faïence d’un revêtement mural de Damas révèle à quel point son équivalent chinois a influencé l’art islamique. Un grand nombre d’exemples de ce type de carreaux bleu-et-blanc peuvent encore être observés sur les murs du mausolée et de la mosquée al-Tawrizi, construits à Damas en 830 H (1430 J.-C.).
dates: IXe siècle de l’Hégire (XVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: décoration florale ; architecture; influence chinoise; bleau et blanc
materials: Céramique frittée, peinte en bleu sous glaçure transparente.
tags: Céramique frittée, peinte en bleu sous glaçure transparente.

en.name: *Constantinople*
short_description: With the political developments of 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. Travelling in the 19th century became easier and more reliable due to the advent of steamships and trains. Westerners travelled to the East not only for touristic purposes, but also for scientific research, history, archaeology or for religious reasons. Western travellers told of their experiences and what they saw in eastern countries in their travel books and they even offer advice about the journey. Istanbul, where East and West meet, has been the subject of many a traveller's book.
keywords: travel books; travelling; orientalism; Istanbul

de.name: Kanzel
description: Die reizvolle Rokoko-Kanzel in geschwungenen Formen, eine Theaterkulisse im Kleinen, weist im Bildprogramm auf den universalen Anspruch der katholischen Kirche hin. Den durchbrochenen Aufbau des Schalldeckels bekrönt Paulus, der Völkerapostel, mit vier Putten, die die Erdteile symbolisieren, am Kanzelkorb die Personifikationen der Tugenden Glaube, Liebe und Hoffnung, als dem Kern der christlichen Heilsbotschaft.

en.name: Pulpit
description: The delightful Rococo pulpit in flowing forms, a miniature theatre backdrop, announces the universal claims of the Catholic Church. The open-work construction of the baldachin is crowned by Paul, Apostle to the Gentiles, with four putti symbolising the continents, on the pulpit itself are the personifications of the virtues Faith, Love and Hope as the heart of the Christian message of salvation.

short_description: This tile panel depicting the treshing of wheat using animals originally covered the wall of a bakery in Lisbon. en.name: Archaeological excavations
short_description: This photograph shows a group of German scholars preparing reports of their excavation in the archaeological area of Saqqara. The picture dates to 1901. The original photograph was kept in the German Archive (an archive that the German archaeological mission left in Cairo).

cs.name: Hlavní oltář
description: Sochařsky ztvárněný, výrazně vertikální oltář v symbolickém tvaru jazyka je umístěn do vysoké arkády sahající až ke galerii druhého patra. Narozdíl od jiných staveb interiéru nedominuje, ale pouze jej symbolicky dotváří. Chybí také jakákoliv ornamentální výzdoba a malba. Hlavním nositelem významu je stavba sama, vytvářená jednak hmotou, jednak působením světla v prostoru. I to je zde symbolicky rozděleno. Ve spodní části osvětlují prostor svíčky, tedy oheň, světlo pozemské, zatímco v prvním patře je do prostoru přijímáno pomocí zrcadel světlo Božské. Provázanost a kmitání světelných paprsků symbolického významu vyjadřuje žebrování stěn prvního patra. Druhé patro a vrchol klenby, kde namísto běžného symbolu Ducha svatého je symbol světce – jež je současně znamením Božího zázraku – je osvětleno čistým světlem, procházejícím okny. Je zřejmé, že i toto horizontální, trojčlenné řešení má svůj symbolický význam (aluze na Nejsv. Trojici).

en.name: High altar
description: The sculpted, distinctly vertical altar, symbolically shaped like a tongue, is placed within a tall arcade that reaches to the gallery on the second floor. Unlike many other constructions of its kind it does not dominate the church interior but symbolically enhances it. There is no ornamental decoration or painting. The building itself, created by matter and the work of light in space, is the sole bearer of meaning. Light is also symbolically divided in the space. In the bottom section the area is illuminated by candles, i.e. fire an earthly light, while on the first floor Divine Light enters the space through mirrors. The symbolic linking and oscillation of rays of light is portrayed in the ribbed walls of the first floor. The second floor and the top of the vaulting, where a symbol of the saint (epitomising a holy miracle) is found instead of the usual symbol of the Holy Spirit, are illuminated by pure light coming through the windows. Without a doubt this horizontal three-part approach also symbolises the Holy Trinity.

en.name: Carpet
description:
As a curtain that covers a Torah Ark containing the Torah scrolls in a synagogue, this carpet contains above the arch a Hebrew inscription from Psalms CXVIII:20 that reads “This is the Gate of the Lord: Through it the Righteous Enter.” Material, technique, design elements, and coloring supply sufficient proof that the carpet was woven in a Ottoman court-controlled atelier in Cairo, Egypt, although it is unknown in the ark of which synagogue it was hung. When the Ottoman Turks conquered Egypt in 1517, there was already an established carpet-weaving industry there. This carpet, and others of its time woven in Cairo, reflect Ottoman taste in elements of the design, but they were produced for a wide raging clientele from European aristocracy to Sephardic Jewish comminities who lived in Ottoman lands.  
  
Probably, woven for a Sephardic Jewish community that settled in the Ottoman lands after their expulsion in the late fifteenth century from Iberian Peninsula, this Torah curtain shows many of the same stylistic characteristics as the two seccade hanging behind it. The artistic forms shared between the Muslim *seccade* and the Jewish *parochet* are no coincidence, for they indicate a vocabulary of symbolism: the shared meaning of door- like forms as gateway to heaven given to the Muslim *mihrab* and the Jewish Torah ark and hanging lamps and light as a metaphor for God.  
  
The contrast between styles shows especially well on the carpets produced in Egypt during the Mamluk Sultanate and afterwards during the Ottoman Empire. Curvilinear and naturalistic rendering of the floral motifs on the Ottoman carpets, such as in this example, produces a more sensuous effect than the geometric and angular patterning of the Mamluk style in which the limited colour scheme – red, blue and green – imparts a restrained and intellectual quality.

en.name: Madrasat Nur al-Din
description: This grand *madrasa* and its annexed mausoleum belongs to Nur al-Din and, like the *bimaristan*, features a red-brick *muqarnas* dome. The writer, Ibn al-Jubayr visited this *madrasa* in 580/1184 and describes it as “one of the finest colleges in the world”. The entrance to the *madrasa* is on the east side through a recessed *muqarnas* portal and a structurally impressive cross-vaulted vestibule. Historians have recorded the burial of Nur al-Din in this *madrasa* upon his death in 569/1174, and the rectangular cenotaph located to the left of the entrance is inscribed with a large and simple cursive calligraphic relief (*thuluth*) typical of Nur al-Din’s constructs. A large frieze executed in a similar script circumscribes the four walls of the room under the dome and typically contains “*Ayat al-Kursi*”, the most auspicious verse of the Qur’an (2:255). Typically, the tomb chamber includes windows overlooking the street, thereby receiving the blessings of passers-by, and a *mihrab* featuring two antique colonnettes in the south (*qibla*) wall to indicate the direction of Mecca. Back in the vestibule, a staircase leads up to the residential chambers used by students and professors. Straight ahead, the *madrasa*’s courtyard pool appears, similar in design to the pool in Nur al- Din’s Bimarisan, but with the addition of an above-ground water channel flowing from a fountain in the back wall of the western *iwan*, and thereby offering the glistening effect of water falling over the stone. This type of fountain is known as a *salsabil*, and Ibn Jubayr does not fail to note its beauty. To the left of the courtyard is the wide prayer-hall, including an original *mihrab* and a recently added *minbar*. Thus the visitor to this *madrasa* is greeted by the auspicious abundance of water as well as accommodation for study and prayer. A domed-chamber to the north of the entrance with a near-identical red *muqarnas* dome does not form part of the Nur al-Din complex but is actually a Mamluk-period construct. Nevertheless, it gives visual testimony to the continuation of the architectural heritage that Nur al-Din brought with him from the East and also political testimony to the continued admiration of Nur al-Din’s leadership.

ar.name: شمعدان الناصر محمد بن قلاوون.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن شمعدان يتكون من قاعدة وبدن أسطوانيين ورقبة أسطوانية قطرها صغير مقارنة بقطر القاعدة والبدن. تلتف حول قاعدة الشمعدان ثلاث جدائل زخرفية فوق بعضها البعض تفصل كل واحدة عن التي تليها خطوط تلتف أيضاً حول القاعدة. أما بدن الشمعدان فقد غطي بأكمله بالزخارف، ويشتمل على نقش كتابي كبير بخط النسخ المملوكي، وتمتد الكتابة من أسفل البدن حتى أعلاه ونصها "المقر العالي المالكي العالمي العادلي الناصري." وملئت خلفية الكتابة بزخارف نباتية كثيفة شغلت كل البدن. ويوجد على بدن الشمعدان صرتان (ميداليونان) يتكون كل منهما من ثلاث دوائر: الداخلية صغيرة جداً وفيها زخرفة مروحية الشكل، والوسطى تحتوي على زخارف نباتية داخل خطوط ملتوية قد تكون زهرة لوتس، والخارجية كبيرة وتحتوي أيضاً على زخارف نباتية مكونة من زهرات ووريقات متشابكة. ويلتف حول ظهر (صينية) الشمعدان شريطان زخرفيان. وهناك نص كتابي ملتف على ظهر الشمعدان كتب بخط النسخ المملوكي نصه "المقر العالي المولوي المالكي الغازي المجاهدي العالمي الغياثي الناصري." ويقطع هذا النص صرتان تحتوي كل منهما على رسم طير على الأرجح أنه حمامة أو حجلة؛ والطائران متقابلان. وملئت خلفية النص بمجموعة من الوريقات والزهرات. أما رقبة الشمعدان فمن الواضح أنها ليست أصلية، بل رقبة بديلة حلت محل الأصلية التي ربما تكون تلفت بفعل الاستعمال. وتدل هذه الرقبة البديلة على ضعف واضح في الحِرَفية.  
  
ومن الجدير بالذكر أن الرحالة الذين زاروا المسجد الأقصى وقبة الصخرة في القدس والحرم الإبراهيمي في الخليل ذكروا في وصفهم لهذه الأماكن أنها احتوت على عدد كبير من السرج والشمعدانات. ولم يصلنا من تلك القطع إلا القليل، وهي معروضة في المتحف الإسلامي في القدس.
place: على الأرجح أن تكون القطعة قد صنعت في القاهرة، مصر.

en.name: Candlestick of al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun.
description:
A candlestick consisting of a cylindrical base and body, as well as a cylindrical neck whose diameter is small when compared to the base and body. Three decorative braid-like bands wrap around the base of the candlestick, one on top of the other. They are separated from the one adjacent to it by strokes, which also wind around the base. The body of the candlestick is completely covered with decoration, including a large inscription in Mamluk *naskhi* script that extends from the lowest section of the body to the top. It reads: “The possession of the sublime, the sovereign, the all-knowing, the just, the victorious.” The background of the inscription is filled in with dense vegetal decoration that is worked throughout the body. Two medallions appear on the body of the candlestick, each of which consists of three circles: the interior one is extremely small and in it is a fan-shaped decorative form. The middle circle contains vegetal decoration within twisted lines, which might be lotus blossom. The outer circle is large and also contains vegetal decoration of flowers and intertwining leaves. Two decorative bands are wrapped around the surface (plate) of the candlestick. There is an encircling inscription on the surface written in Mamluk *naskhi* script that reads: “The Possession of the Sublime, The lord, The sovereign, the warrior, the Mujahid, the knower, the helper, the victorious.” Two medallions intercept the inscription, each of which contains a depiction of a bird most likely a pigeon or a partridge. The two birds face each other. The background of the inscription is filled in with a collection of leaves and flowers. The neck of the candlestick is clearly not original and the replacement certainly indicates the decline in craftsmanship during the late Mamluk period.  
It is noteworthy that travellers who visited al-Aqsa Mosque and the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, as well as al-Haram al-Ibrahimi, (the Ibrahimi Mosque) in Hebron (al-Khalil), mentioned in their descriptions of these places that they contained a large number of lamps and candlesticks, only a few of which have survived to the present. Some of them are displayed in the Islamic Museum in Jerusalem.

A cylindrical candlestick with two epigraphic inscriptions. There are no spaces as thick vegetal decoration has been worked over the entire body. From its decoration, script and titles it appears to be associated with al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun. It is typical of Mamluk candlesticks made in Cairo and Damascus. It was formerly at al-Haram al-Ibrahimi in Hebron.
holder: Islamic Museum, al-Aqsa Mosque / al-Haram al-Sharif.
keywords: Naskhi script; naskhi; epigraphic decoration; vegetal decoration; candlestick; Mamluk; engraving; copper
materials: Copper with decorative carving inlaid with silver.
tags: Copper with decorative carving inlaid with silver.

es.name: Candelero de al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun.
description:
Candelero de base y cuerpo cilíndricos, así como el cuello, de diámetro bastante menor. La base está decorada con tres cenefas de trenzados, una encima de otra, separadas entre sí por trazos que también rodean la base. El cuerpo del candelero está totalmente decorado y en él destaca, a todo lo ancho, una gran inscripción en letra *nasji* mameluca que reza: “Posesión del sublime, el soberano, el omnisciente, el justo, el victorioso”. El fondo se ha rellenado con densa decoración vegetal repartida por todo el cuerpo, en el que también se ven dos medallones formados por tres círculos cada uno: el interior es muy pequeño, con formas en abanico; el central tiene adornos vegetales dentro de líneas enroscadas, quizá flores de loto; el círculo exterior es grande y también presenta motivos vegetales de flores y hojas entrelazadas. La superficie horizontal del candelero está decorada con dos bandas y una inscripción circular en letra *nasji mameluca: “Posesión del sublime, el señor, el soberano, el guerrero, el muyahid, el conocedor, el que ayuda, el victorioso”. Dos medallones interrumpen el texto, ambos con la imagen de un ave –que puede ser una paloma o una perdiz– afrontada a la del otro medallón. El fondo de la inscripción es un conjunto de hojas y flores. Resulta evidente que el cuello no es el original; su escasa calidad demuestra el declive de la artesanía a finales del periodo mameluco.  
Viajeros que visitaron la mezquita al-Aqsa y la Cúpula de la Roca (Jerusalén), así como al-Haram al-Ibrahimi (la mezquita de Ibrahim) de Hebrón (al-Jalil), mencionaron en sus crónicas que estos lugares poseían abundantes lámparas y candeleros, de los que actualmente se conservan sólo unos pocos. Algunas piezas se exponen en el Museo Islámico de Jerusalén.*

Candelero cilíndrico con dos inscripciones epigráficas. La densa decoración vegetal no deja espacios libres en el cuerpo de la pieza. Por esta decoración, por el tipo de letra y por los títulos mencionados se ha asociado a al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun.  
Este tipo de candeleros fueron característicos de El Cairo y Damasco. Antes de exponerse en el museo, estuvo en al-Haram al-Ibrahimi (Hebrón).
keywords: Escritura nasji; nasji; decoración epigráfica; decoración vegetal; candelero; al-Haram al-Ibrahimi; candelero mameluco; grabado; cobre
partner: Museo islámico en la mezquita de Al-Aqsa

fr.name: Chandelier d’al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun.
description:
Chandelier composé d'une base, d'un corps et d'une tige cylindrique de diamètres décroissants. Séparés l'un de l'autre par des filets, trois bandeaux décoratifs tressés superposés encerclent la base. Le corps entièrement décoré présente une importante inscription en style *naskhi* mamelouk qui occupe pratiquement toute sa surface. Se détachant d'un dense fond de décor végétal, elle se lit : “Possession du sublime, du souverain, de l'omniscient, du juste, du victorieux.” Le corps comporte également deux médaillons, chacun composé de trois cercles concentriques, dont le plus petit est traité en forme d'éventail. Celui du milieu est meublé d'un décor végétal qui pourrait représenter des fleurs de lotus entre des lignes torsadées. Le cercle extérieur contient également un décor à motifs de fleurs et de feuillages entrelacés. Deux bandeaux décoratifs occupent le plateau. Une inscription circulaire en style *naskhi* mamelouk rappelle : “Possession du Sublime, le Seigneur, le Souverain, le Guerrier ; le Moudjahid, le Savant, celui qui aide, le Victorieux.” Deux médaillons interrompent l'inscription, chacun contenant un oiseau (pigeon ou pintade) affronté à l'autre. Le fond est recouvert d'un décor de feuilles et de fleurs. à l'évidence, la tige n'est pas d'origine, et celle qui la remplace témoigne d'un déclin de l'artisanat au cours de la période mamelouke.  
Les voyageurs qui visitaient la mosquée al-Aqsa et le Dôme du Rocher à Jérusalem ainsi que la mosquée Ibrahimi (al-Haram al-Ibrahimi) à Hébron (al-Khalil) mentionnaient dans leurs récits la présence d'un grand nombre de lampes et de chandeliers dont seuls quelques-uns nous sont parvenus. Certains sont exposés au musée.

Chandelier cylindrique à deux inscriptions épigraphiques. Aucun espace n’est laissé vide, car il est entièrement travaillé de fines décorations végétales. Sa décoration, sa calligraphie et ses titres semblent l’associer à al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun. Ce chandelier est typique des exemplaires mamelouks fabriqués au Caire et à Damas. Il se trouvait jadis au Haram al-Ibrahimi à Hébron.
holder: Musée islamique, mosquée al-Aqsa / Haram al-Charif.
keywords: Écriture naskhi ; naskhi ; décoration épigraphique ; décoration végétale ; chandeliers ; mamelouk ; gravure ; cuivre
