en.name: Turkish and Islamic Art Museum, and Archaeological Museum
names: Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum, and Archaeological Museum
description:
**Wall Tiles**  
The Seljuqs brought with them to Anatolia the art of tile production and decoration, which developed in relationship to architecture. Various techniques were used in the production of Turkish tile art, examples of which span many centuries. The main raw material of tiles, which was an important decorative element in mosques, *masjid*s, *madrasa*s, *türbe*s, and palaces, was clean and good-quality clay. Clay is cleaned of impurities and made into mud in pools; then it is transferred to a second pool and left to rest for a few days; later it is transported to a third pool. When the liquid-clay dough becomes thicker, it is shaped using moulds in the mould workshops and left to dry. Any rough parts are then cleaned using emery; then the tiles are baked in kilns. The hardened tiles are taken from the gradually cooling kiln and designs are drawn on them. They are then covered either with a transparent, coloured or colourless glaze and put back into the kiln.  
The tiles on display here in one of the southern cells are from the Edirne Şahmelek Mosque and date back to 1429. They form two rectangular panels, which are filled with turquoise-coloured unornamented tiles and on the border bands are floral motifs applied in the coloured glaze (*cuerda seca*) technique.  
  
**Gravestones**  
Displayed in the yard of the Archaeological Museum, is the headstone of Sitti Hatun, daughter of Süleyman, son of Zülfikar; she was married to Sultan Mehmed II and passed away in June 1486. Usually, there is one gravestone at the head and one at the foot of Anatolian graves. In the Seljuq and Emirates periods, both the headstones and the footstones were ornamented with inscriptions. Beginning in the 17th century, figures like cypresses, date palms and grapevines replaced the scriptures on the footstones. In the Ottoman period, the pinnacle of most female graves ended in a triangular pediment, the inside of which was filled with geometric and floral motifs or depictions of mosques and other buildings. This rectangular gravestone has a top section shaped like, and ornamented with, *palmette*s and *rumi*s. A carved niche resembling a *mihrab* is placed on the body of stone, and information about the deceased person is engraved in this niche; a single pinwheel and a rosette are carved in the corners of the niche; the niche is enclosed by a chain pattern.

es.name: Museo de Arte Turcoislámico y Museo Arqueológico
description:
**Azulejos**  
El arte de los azulejos, que se desarrolló en relación con la arquitectura, fue traído a Anatolia por los selyuquíes. En la producción turca de azulejos se emplearon diversas técnicas, y los ejemplos abarcan muchos siglos. La principal materia prima de los azulejos —importante elemento decorativo de mezquitas, *masyid*s, *madrasa*s, *turbe*s y palacios— era una arcilla muy pura y de buena calidad. Primero se limpiaba de impurezas y se reducía a barro en una pileta, luego se pasaba a una segunda pila y se dejaba reposar unos días antes de trasvasarla a una tercera. Cuando la pasta líquida se hacía más densa, se vertía en moldes y se dejaba secar. Una vez quitadas las asperezas con una lija de esmeril, las formas se cocían en hornos. Los azulejos se sacaban gradualmente del horno y se dibujaba en ellos la decoración. Finalmente, se cubrían de una capa transparente de vidriado, con color o no, y se volvían a meter en el horno.  
Los azulejos expuestos en una de las celdas de la parte sur pertenecieron a la mezquita de Şahmelek y se remontan a 1429. Forman dos paneles rectangulares de azulejos color turquesa sin adornos y con bandas de flores en *cuerda seca* en los bordes.  
  
**Lápida**  
En el jardín del Museo Arqueológico se puede ver la lápida de la cabecera de la tumba de Sitti Hatun, hija de Süleyman hijo de Zülfikar, casada con el sultán Mehmet II y muerta en junio de 1486. En las tumbas de Anatolia solían ponerse dos lápidas, una a los pies y otra en la cabecera. En el periodo selyuquí y durante los emiratos, ambas lápidas se adornaban con inscripciones. A partir del siglo XVII, en las lápidas de los pies las figuras de cipreses, palmeras y parras sustituyeron a las inscripciones. En el periodo otomano, las lápidas de las mujeres se remataban con una forma triangular cuyo interior se llenaba de motivos florales y geométricos, o representaciones de mezquitas y otros edificios. El remate de esta lápida rectangular tiene dicha forma y está adornado con palmetas y *rumi*s. En el cuerpo de la lápida vemos esculpido un nicho que recuerda un *mihrab* y en el que se han inscrito noticias de la difunta; en los ángulos del nicho aparecen girándulas y rosetas; alrededor del nicho se ha esculpido una cadena.

en.name: Pile carpet fragment
description: The dark green central square is surrounded by three light-coloured borders, which in their turn are framed by thin bands in various colours. The first border is decorated with polychrome zig-zags, the second with yellow dots placed on differently-coloured bands and the third has a perimetric *kufic* inscription, which bears the name of Allah, on an abrashed red ground. The pile is in relatively good condition, apart from the areas of dark brown which are noticeably worn, so that the surface of the carpet gives the impression of having concave sections. The original dimensions of the carpet were approximately 45 cm square, as indicated by the shape of the pattern, the inscription which runs around the central decorative feature, and the fact that in technique, design and dimensions it resembles Benaki fragments 16148 and 16193, as well as no.73.726 in the Textile Museum, Washington.

en.name: Alcove
description:
It was probably realised after 1704, surely before 1739, when it is mentioned in a biography dedicated to its author, the sculptor Giuseppe Mazza, here working together with the painter Ercole Graziani senior.  
Coming back from Venice, the artist was probably engaged by the Zaniboni family, owner of the palace, to create this superb nuptial bedroom lavishly decorated with stuccoes and sculptures (among them *Venus* and *Apollo,* allusive to abundance and fertility); every element contributes here to a very dynamic composition inspired by typically baroque concepts.
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Alcova
description:
Probabilmente realizzata dopo il 1704, sicuramente prima del 1739, quando è menzionata in una biografia dedicata al suo autore, lo scultore Giuseppe Mazza, che qui lavora insieme al pittore  Ercole Graziani senior.  
Al ritorno da Venezia lo scultore fu probabilmente ingaggiato dalla famiglia Zaniboni, proprietaria del palazzo, per creare questa superba camera nuziale riccamente decorata con stucchi e sculture (tra cui *Venere* e *Apollo*, allusive all'abbondanza e alla fertilità). Ogni elemento dà il suo contributo ad una composizione molto dinamica, ispirata a concetti tipicamente barocchi.

ar.name: قاعدة شمعدان.
description: قاعدة شمعدان من العهد المملوكي، مصنوعة من النحاس المصفَّح المطروق والمعشَّق بالنحاس الأصفر، ومطعَّمة بالفضة والذهب. وقد فُقدت صينية الشمع المتقطِّر التي يُفترض أن تكون متموضِّعة فوق الإطار العلوي للقاعدة. جسد القاعدة مزخرف بطوق عريض من الخط النسخي، منقسم إلى قسمين يفصل بينهما شكلان دائريان. أما النطاقات الرئيسية للزخرفة فتزينها أنساق من الورد الناعم المطعَّم بالفضة. والنقش، المطعَّم بالفضة، يعدِّد مزايا صاحب التقدِمة الذي تبرَّع بالشمعدان، لكنه لم يذكر اسمه! من الممكن أن يكون الكثير من هذه الشمعدانات قد أُهديت إلى المساجد والمقامات والمدارس الدينية في مصر من أجل استخدامها. وقد أصبح الحكام المماليك في مصر وسوريا رعاة كبار للفنون وفن العمارة. فالقاهرة كانت عاصمتهم التي حكموها من عام 647/ 1250 حتى عام 922 / 1517.

أعداد كبيرة من الشمعدانات الشبيهة بهذا، صُنِّعت خلال الحقبة المملوكية، لتقديمها هدايا إلى المساجد، و،المزارات والمدارس الدينية. والنقش المحفور بالخطّ العربي يقدِّم وصفاً لجملة ألقاب، وولاءات المحسن المملوكي، الذي أوعز بتنفيذ الشمعدان.

en.name: Candlestick base.
description: The base of a Mamluk candlestick made of beaten sheet copper that has been gilded with brass and inlaid with silver and gold. The drip-tray that would have sat on the top rim of the base is missing. The body is decorated with a wide band of *naskhi* script divided into two sections by two roundels. The main decorative fields are embellished with fine floral scrolls inlaid with silver. The inscription, which is inlayed with silver, describes the attributes of the patron who commissioned the candlestick but does not mention his name! Many such candlesticks would have been presented for use in mosques, shrines, and religious schools in Egypt. The Mamluk rulers of Egypt and Syria became great patrons of art and architecture. Cairo was their capital, which they ruled from AH 647 / AD 1250 to AH 922 / AD 1517.

Many metal candlesticks like this one were commissioned during the Mamluk period to be presented for use in mosques, shrines and religious schools. The Arabic calligraphic script describes the titles and allegiances of the Mamluk patron who commissioned the candlestick.
dates: Hegira, late 7th–early 8th century / AD late 13th–early 14th century.
keywords: Calligraphy; patronage; waqf
materials: Sheet copper, beaten and inlaid with gold and silver.
tags: Sheet copper, beaten and inlaid with gold and silver.

es.name: Base de candelero.
description:
Base de candelero del periodo mameluco realizada en una lámina de cobre batido y dorado con latón, a la que se añadieron incrustaciones en plata y oro. No ha llegado hasta nosotros la pieza superior que sujetaba la vela y recogía la cera. El cuerpo presenta un banda decorativa con una inscripción en cursiva *nasji*, dividida por dos medallones. La superficie está bellamente decorada con finas volutas florales de plata. La inscripción, incrustada en plata, describe las cualidades de quien encargó el candelero, pero no menciona su nombre.  
Estos candeleros se utilizaban en mezquitas, santuarios y escuelas religiosas de Egipto. Los gobernantes mamelucos de Egipto y Siria se convirtieron en grandes mecenas del arte y la arquitectura. El Cairo fue su capital y la gobernaron de 647 a 922 / 1250 a 1517.

En época mameluca se encargaron muchos candeleros metálicos como este para donarlos a mezquitas, santuarios y escuelas religiosas. La inscripción enumera los títulos y méritos del cliente mameluco que encomendó la pieza.
dates: Finales del siglo VII o principios del VIII de la Hégira / XIII-XIV d. C.
keywords: caligrafía; mecenazgo; waqf.
materials: Lámina de cobre batido, con incrustaciones de oro y plata.
tags: Lámina de cobre batido, con incrustaciones de oro y plata.

fr.name: Base de chandelier.
description: Base de chandelier mamelouk fabriqué à partir d'une feuille de cuivre battu dorée au laiton et incrustée d'or et d'argent. La bobèche qui devait reposer sur le bord supérieur manque. Le corps est orné d'un important bandeau d'écriture *naskhi* divisé en deux sections par deux rondeaux. Les principales zones décoratives sont ornées de fins rinceaux floraux incrustés d'argent. L'inscription incrustée d'argent décrit les attributs du client qui a commandé ce chandelier, mais ne mentionne pas son nom. En Égypte, de nombreux chandeliers de ce type étaient offerts à des mosquées, des mausolées et des écoles coraniques. Les souverains mamelouks d'Égypte et de Syrie furent d'importants mécènes des arts et de l'architecture. Le Caire était leur capitale, d'où ils régnèrent de 647 à 922 H / 1250-1517 J.-C.

De nombreux chandeliers en métal de ce type étaient commandités pour des mosquées, des mausolées et des écoles coraniques durant la période mamelouke. L’écriture en calligraphie arabe décrit les titres et les attributs du mécène mamelouk.
dates: Fin VIIe-début VIIIe siècle de l’Hégire (fin XIIIe-début XIVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: calligraphie ; mécénat ; waqf
materials: Feuille de cuivre battu à incrustations d’or et d’argent.
tags: Feuille de cuivre battu à incrustations d’or et d’argent.

en.name: Carpet
description:
Spanish carpet of the Crown style.  
Field: The field is formed of three full crowns of oak leaves along with a partial segment of a fourth in which a barely visible golden leaf litter stands out on the rounded bottom. The better distinguished blue flowers mark the quadrants of the wheels or crowns. Within the inner border, the field finishes off in a continuous line of the same colours.  
Border: The border is formed by candlestick motifs utilising the same colours as the field, which stand out against the dark blue background. On the larger sides they are arranged on a longitudinal axis, while on the smaller side, the same decorative motif is repeated horizontally.  
The colours of the wool used consists of molasses, gold and dark blue.  
The carpet is from the crown series which was largely produced throughout the 16th century and typical of the workshops of the Old Kingdom of Murcia.  
The laurels or crowns were a decorative element widely used in the Renaissance and can be found in numerous decorative designs. In exceptional cases they may also contain heraldic motifs or religious anagrams. However, the internal border that creates linked rhombuses is an outdated Mudejar stylistic element.  
This carpet is catalogued as belonging to the workshops of Alcaraz by several scholars, however certain stylistic elements such as its colour or composition may call into question this attribution. The range of colours (yellow, molasses and blue) as well as the arrangement of the crowns, free of any reference, would make it closer to the core of the Cuenca region, although today there are no parallels or documentary evidence.  
The carpet conforms to carpet number ten of the Weissberger collection visible in the collections acquisition catalogue, although the measures differ slightly.  
A similar carpet is found in: Ferrandis, J., 1933: Exhibition Catalog of Old Spanish Carpets. Madrid, nº 36, plate XXVIII, page 112. Another in the catalogue of the Textile Museum of Washington.
place: Old Kingdom of Murcia or Cuenca
keywords: Carpet; coronas

es.name: Alfombra
description:
Alfombra española de la serie de coronas.  
Campo: Formado por tres coronas de hojas de roble y un pequeño segmento de otra en la que apenas destaca la hojarasca dorada sobre el fondo melado. Se distinguen mejor unas flores azules que estarían marcando los cuadrantes de las ruedas o coronas. Como cenefa interior, el campo remata en una lacería continua de los mismos colores.  
Marco: Está formado por motivos a candelieri realizados en los mismos colores que el campo, que destaca sobre el fondo azul oscuro. En los lados mayores están dispuestos sobre un eje longitudinal, mientras que en los lados menores, este mismo motivo decorativo, se repite en sentido horizontal.  
Se utiliza lana en color melado, dorado y azul oscuro.  
Se trata de una alfombra de la serie de coronas, de numerosa producción durante todo el siglo XVI, propia de los talleres del Antiguo Reino de Murcia.  
Las láureas o coronas fueron un elemento decorativo muy utilizado en el Renacimiento y pueden encontrarse en numerosas aplicaciones decorativas. En casos excepcionales también pueden contener motivos heráldicos o anagramas religiosos. Sin embargo, la cenefa interna que crea rombos enlazados es un elemento retardatario de tipo mudéjar.  
Esta alfombra está catalogada como de Alcaraz por diferentes autores, sin embargo hay en ella elementos como el colorido o la composición que pueden poner en cuestión esta atribución. La gama de colores (amarillo, melado y azul) y la disposición de las coronas, libres de toda referencia, la harían más próxima al núcleo de Cuenca, aunque hoy por hoy, no existan paralelos ni evidencias documentales  
Con bastante seguridad es la alfombra número diez del catálogo de adquisición de la colección Weisberger, aunque las medidas difieran un poco.  
Un alfombra similar se encuentra en: Ferrandis, J., 1933: Catálogo Exposición de Alfombras Antiguas Españolas. Madrid, nº 36, lámina XXVIII, página 112. Otra en el catálogo del Textile Museum of Washington.
keywords: Alfombra; coronas

en.name: Nossa Senhora da Assunção (Paris Church)
names: Nossa Senhora da Assunção (Caminha Parish Church)
description:
Work began on the Parish Church in 1488; led by Tomé de Tolosa from Biscay and continued by Pêro Galego, who worked on a number of buildings in Alto Minho. Francisco Fial was yet another Spaniard who worked on the church.  
The portals were not concluded until the 1540s, the entrance arch to the Mariners’ Chapel is from a similar time period, probably 1551, though it is dated 1151, no doubt a slip on the part of the stonemason. The bell tower probably also served as a watchtower, for its position in relation to the sea certainly suggests this possibility.  
The interior with three aisles has a fine, maple Mudéjar ceiling, carved, dated and signed by Fernão Muñoz from Tuy, in 1565. The profile of the longitudinal arcades is of good quality, as are the ribbed vaults of the apse chapels.  
On the left, the Chapel of the Brotherhood of Navigators has a depressed rib vault, probably dating from 1530-1540, one of the most elegant examples of the Late Gothic ceiling in Alto Minho, and similar to others in Galicia.  
Outside, take note of the very elegant brattishing at the east end, clearly inspired by Braga Cathedral.

en.name: Colle Ameno Hamlet
description: The hamlet was conceived to be a self-sufficient and rational structural space. It included the Ghisilieri Villa with its own courtyard separated from the hamlet where the patron spent most of his time. The workshops and houses for the craftsmen formed the heart of the hamlet and were intended to function as a small town. The hamlet had its own hospital (1738-1768) built for all the nearby peasants living in poor conditions without any social assistance. It was totally financed by Filippo Ghisilieri who supplied doctors, nurses and medicines. There was also a small church, consecrated in 1747. In addition, the china factory (1758-1768) was producing characteristic blue monochrome ceramics which are well known in the area. China manufacturing had great success in the eighteenth-century and many china factories developed in Bologna and its surroundings.

The so called Colle Ameno Hamlet was built after the will of the nobleman Filippo Ghisilieri and it is an interesting example of local aristocracy philanthropic spirit, a typical feature of the age of enlightenment  
This complex included many different buildings, besides the patron villa: an oratory, a hospital, and the village with workshops for craftsmen and china manufacturers. The name Colle Ameno, meaning “pleasant hill”, was chosen by the patron himself who was particularly fond of this residence and used to spend here most of his time.
history:
Filippo Carlo Ghisilieri began building this hamlet from a small building with a chapel and a farmer-house on one of his family properties in the countryside a few kilometres from Bologna.  
The philanthropic purpose of the nobleman was to encourage commercial and artistic activities in his properties. At the same time the goal was to provide religious and sanitary assistance to people working there.  
Examples of small industrial organisations combining work and social assistance were quite common during the age of enlightenment, in part because of the presence of a still powerful land aristocracy. During the same time period, the Bourbons in Naples celebrated the creation of a silk factory next to a modern village in order to house the craftsmen.
keywords: Age of enlightenment; Commerce; Rural architecture; Villa
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Villaggio di Colle Ameno
description: Il villaggio fu concepito come una struttura autosufficiente e razionale. Si compone della Villa Ghisilieri, con la sua corte separata dal villaggio, dove il proprietario passava la maggior parte del suo tempo; le botteghe e le case degli artigiani che formano il cuore del villaggio, inteso come una piccola città con le sue strade; l'ospedale (1738-1768) costruito per i contadini dei dintorni che vivevano in povretà, senza assistenza sociale; fu interamente finanziato da Filippo Ghisilieri che metteva a disposizione dottori, infermiere e medicinali; la piccola chiesa, consacrata nel 1747; la fabbrica di porcellana (1758-1768) che produceva la caratteristica ceramica blu ben nota nella zona. La produzione di ceramica ebbe un grande successo nel XVIII secolo e molte fabbriche di ceramiche si svilupparono a Bologna e nei suoi dintorni.

Il cosiddetto villaggio di Colle Ameno fu costruito per volontà dell'aristocratico Filippo Ghisilieri ed è un interessante esempio dello spirito filantropico dell'aristocrazia locale, un aspetto tipico dell'Illuminismo.  
Il complesso è composto da vari edifici, oltre alla villa padronale: un oratorio, un ospedale e il villaggio con le botteghe degli artigiani e dei ceramisti. Il nome Colle Ameno fu scelto dal proprietario stesso che amava molto questa residenza e vi passava la maggior parte del proprio tempo.
history:
Filippo Carlo Ghisilieri iniziò a costruire il villaggio partendo da un piccolo edificio con una cappella e una fattoria che si trovava in una delle proprietà di campagna della sua famiglia, a pochi chilometri da Bologna.  
Lo scopo filantropico dell'aristocratico era quello di incoraggiare le attività commerciali, l'artigianato e le arti nelle sue proprietà e allo stesso tempo di assicurare assistenza religiosa e sanitaria alle persone che vi lavoravano.  
Esempi simili di piccole organizzazione industriali, che combinavano il lavoro e l'assistenza sociale, erano comuni nell'epoca illuminista, grazie alla presenza di un'aristocrazia terriera ancora molto potente. I Borboni crearono a Napoli nello stesso periodo una celebre fabbrica di seta con accanto un villaggio, per ospitare gli artigiani.
keywords: Illuminismo; Commercio; architettura rurale; Villa;

en.name: Kurdish carpet, so-called *Şarkışlar*
description: An Anatolian Kurdish carpet, most likely stemming from the middle of the 19th century and preserved in almost full size. Not much more is missing from the top and bottom of the carpet than the narrow border retained on the sides. Up to the 1990s, pile carpets formed part of the traditional tent decoration of Kurdish nomads in Anatolia. In their black goat-hair tents, the openings of which were located on the longer side, the pile carpet was accorded a central place. Only a very few examples of this type of carpet still exist. They are ascribed to the region around Şarkışla, southwest of Sivas. Characteristic here are the totem-like symbols in large, variously coloured rhomboid shapes, which, in alteration with small squares, form the carpet's tiled pattern. However, the central motif, which appears quite zoomorphic, can probably be traced back to plant shapes. The Dresden piece displays typical East Anatolian colouring and a straightforward, differentiated overall design. Despite some damage and later reworkings, this carpet makes a powerful and confident impression.
holder: Museum für Völkerkunde Dresden (Ethnological Museum Dresden), Dresden State Art Collections
keywords: Tribal
partner: Dresden State Art Collections, Museum für Völkerkunde Dresden (Ethnological Museum)

ar.name: إسطرلاب.
description:
إسطرلاب دائري من النحاس الأصفر، ذو إطار دائري وحلية من الأرابيسك في الأعلى كانت متصلة بحلقة ليتم تعليقه منها عند استعماله. لقد تم استعمال الإسطرلاب منذ القرن الثاني/ الثامن على الأقل، وهو أداة متعددة الاستعمالات تستخدم بطرق كثيرة سواء لمعرفة الوقت خلال النهار والليل أو لمراقبة بُعد الأشياء وارتفاعها وتحديده أو لقياس الارتفاع وقراءة الأبراج. ولاستعمال الإسطرلاب، كان يتم اختيار القرص المناسب، وإدخاله ضمن الإطار، وتحديد التاريخ والوقت حسب الموقع الجغرافي للمستخدم، وتساعد الصفيحة التي تحمل شعارات الأبراج على الدائرة الداخلية، ومجموعات النجوم على الدائرة الخارجية على إعطاء قراءة فلكية صحيحة.  
يظهر على الجزء الخلفي من الإسطرلاب اسم الحرفي عبد الكريم، مصحوباً بأسماء الملك والمعز وشهاب الدين، ولما لم يكن هناك أي حاكم يحمل هذا اللقب قبل عام 638/ 1241، فعلى الأغلب تمثل هذه الأسماء ثلاثة أشخاص مختلفين قد يكونون الملك الأشرف موسى الأول، أحد أقوى الحكام الأيوبيين في أوائل القرن السابع/ الثالث عشر، والمعز، وهو الأخ الأصغر للملك الأشرف، أما الاسم الثالث فهو لأخ أصغر آخر للملك الأشرف: الملك المظفر شهاب الدين الغازي الذي حكم مدينة ميافارقين في الفترة 17- 645 / 1220-47. ومن المحتمل أن يكون الأخوة الأيوبيون الثلاثة قد استخدموا هذا الحرفي، ولكن الأخ الذي أمر بصنع الإسطرلاب هو شهاب الدين.

لاستخدام هذه البوصلة، تمَّ إدخال قرص الرصد الرئيسي، من خلال إطار، وُضعت دائرة البروج على الإطار الخارجي، والكواكب على الإطار الداخلي، والتي يتمُّ تحريكها بشكل دائري، للحصول على قراءة فلكية. تمَّت الاستفادة من القراءات الناتجة، لتحديد أوقات الصلاة، وقراءة الأبراج.
keywords: علم الفلك.
materials: نحاس أصفر محفور ومطعم بالفضة والنحاس الأحمر.

en.name: Astrolabe.
description:
A round, brass astrolabe with a circular frame and an arabesque cartouche at the top from which a ring (the throne) would have been attached and the instrument suspended when in use. The astrolabe is an instrument used from at least the AH 2nd / AD 8th century. It is a multi-functional device that is employed in several ways: timekeeping by day and night; surveying and determining the distance and height of objects; measuring latitude and reading horoscopes. To use the astrolabe the appropriate disc is selected and inserted into the frame (mater) and set to a specific date and time according to the geographic location of the user. A plate (rete) with open-work zodiac signs in the inner circle, and other constellations in the outer circle, revolves over this giving an accurate astronomical reading.  
In the inscription on the back of the astrolabe is the name of the craftsman Abd al-Karim, accompanied by the names al-Malik, al-Mu’izz and Shihab al-Din. As there is no single ruler bearing this title before the year AH 638 / AD 1241, this is probably a list of three different individuals. It has been suggested that these names can be identified as: al-Malik al-Ashraf Musa I, one of the most powerful Ayyubid rulers of the early AH 7th / AD 13th century, and al-Mu’izz, a younger brother of al-Malik. The third name may be another younger brother of al-Malik al-Ashraf: al-Malik al-Muzaffar Shihab al-Din Ghazi who ruled the city of Mayyafariqin from AH 617–45 / AD 1220/1–47. These three Ayyubid brothers probably employed the craftsman, while the patron of this astrolabe is identified as Shihab al-Din.

To use this astrolabe, the appropriate disc is inserted into the circular frame. Zodiac signs on the outer circle and constellations on the inner circle are revolved to give an astronomical reading. The readings have many uses, from telling the time of day for prayer times to reading horoscopes.
type: Scientific instrument, metalwork, brass, copper, silver
keywords: Astronomy; science; timekeeping; zodiac; constellation; astrology
materials: Engraved brass with silver and copper inlay.
tags: Engraved brass with silver and copper inlay.

es.name: Astrolabio
description:
Astrolabio circular de latón con trono (remate superior) de arabescos al que está enlazada la anilla para tenerlo suspendido durante su uso.  
El astrolabio se utiliza al menos desde el siglo II / VIII y tenía muchas utilidades: medir el tiempo de noche y de día, calcular la distancia y altura de objetos, medir la latitud y leer el horóscopo. En su empleo, se selecciona el disco apropiado y se inserta en la madre (la placa), ajustando luego la fecha y la hora según la localización geográfica de quien lo está utilizando. El círculo interno con los signos del zodiaco calados, a los que se añaden las constelaciones del círculo externo, gira para proporcionar una lectura astronómica precisa.  
En la inscripción de la parte posterior del astrolabio figura el nombre del artesano, Abd al-Karim, junto con los nombres al-Malik, al-Muizz y Shihab al-Din. No se conoce ningún gobernante con estos títulos antes del año 638 / 1241, así que probablemente se trata de una lista de tres personas diferentes. Se ha dicho que estos nombres corresponderían a al-Malik al-Ashraf Musa I, uno de los gobernantes ayyubíes más poderosos de principios del siglo VII / XIII, y al-Muizz, hermano menor de al-Malik. El tercer nombre correspondería a otro hermano menor de al-Malik al-Ashraf, al-Malik al-Muzaffar Shihab al-Din Gazi, quien gobernó la ciudad de Mayyafariqin enlos años 617-645 / 1220-1247. Probablemente fueron estos tres hermanos quienes contrataron al artesano, aunque el destinatario del astrolabio era Shihab al-Din.

Este astrolabio se utiliza insertando el disco adecuado en la placa circular. Los signos del zodiaco y las constelaciones de los círculos giran para ofrecer la lectura astronómica. Son muchas sus utilidades, desde fijar las horas de los rezos a leer el horóscopo.
dates: Año 638 de la Hégira / 1240-41 d. C.
keywords: astronomía
materials: Latón labrado con incrustaciones de plata y cobre.
tags: Latón labrado con incrustaciones de plata y cobre.

fr.name: Astrolabe.
description:
Astrolabe circulaire en cuivre jaune à cadre circulaire et cartouche d'arabesques en partie supérieure auquel un anneau (le trône) était attaché pour suspendre l'instrument lors de son utilisation. L'astrolabe est utilisé depuis au moins le IIe siècle H (VIIIe siècle J.-C.). Instrument multifonctionnel, il servait aussi bien à donner le temps de jour comme de nuit, qu'à l'étude et à la détermination de la distance et de la hauteur d'objets, à la mesure de la latitude et à la lecture des horoscopes. Un disque gravé approprié était inséré dans le cadre (la mère) et positionné sur une date et une heure spécifiques en fonction de la localisation géographique de l'utilisateur. Un plateau (l'araignée) à signes du zodiaque ajourés dans le cercle intérieur, et d'autres constellations dans le cercle extérieur, tournait tout autour pour permettre une lecture astronomique précise.  
Dans l'inscription au verso de l'instrument figure le nom de son artisan, Abd al-Karim, accompagné de celui de al-Malik, al-Mouiz et Chihab al-Din. Comme aucun souverain ne porte ce titre avant l'an 638 H / 1241 J.-C., il s'agit probablement d'une liste de trois individus différents. On a pu suggérer que ces noms étaient ceux de al-Malik al-Achraf Moussa Ier, l'un des plus puissants souverains ayyoubides du début du VIIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.), et al-Mouiz, frère cadet du premier. Le troisième nom serait celui d'un autre frère cadet, al-Malik al-Mudaffar Chihab al-Din Ghazi qui gouverna la ville de Mayyafariqin de 617 à 645/1221-1247. Ces trois frères ayyoubides employèrent probablement cet artisan, tandis que le commanditaire de l'astrolabe serait Chihab al-Din.

Pour utiliser cet astrolabe, le disque approprié doit être inséré dans le cadre circulaire. On fait tourner les signes du zodiaque du cercle extérieur et les constellations du cercle intérieur pour permettre une lecture astronomique précise. Les usages sont multiples, de l'établissement des heures de prière à la lecture des horoscopes.
keywords: Astronomie
materials: Cuivre jaune gravé à incrustations d’argent et de cuivre.
tags: Cuivre jaune gravé à incrustations d’argent et de cuivre.

en.name: *The Religious Pilgrimage of the Mohammadans - Makkah (Arabia) - General View of the City, the Precinct and Enclosure of the Al-Haram Mosque and the Holy Kaaba*
names: *Le Peregrinacion Religiosa de Los Mahometanos-La Meca (Arabia) - Vista General de la ciudad, del Patio y Claustro de la Mezquita 'El-Haram' y de la 'Santa Káaba'*
short_description: This print was originally published in 'La Ilustracion Espanola y Americana', a newspaper published in Madrid on the 15th of April, 1882. Entitled 'La Peregrinacion religiosa de los mahometanos: Vista general de la Meca, del patio y claustro de la mesquita El-Haram y de la Santa Kaaba', it was copied from the first known photograph (at the time) depicting the Makkah precinct, taken - according to the newspaper - by the English traveller Mr [John Fryer Thomas] Keane.  Keane (1854-1937) was a clergyman, who converted to Islam and visited Makkah in 1877. In 1881, he published two books about his experiences in the Hijaz, 'Six Months in Meccah' and 'My Journey to Medinah'. The image shows the courtyard of the Makkah mosque with hundreds of pilgrims clustering around the Ka'bah at the centre. Beyond, the hills of Makkah with their traditional houses, many of them multistoreyed, can be seen.
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation /Sharjah Museums Authority

en.name: Incantation bowl
description:
A copper dish with a small, inverted dish at the canter, known as an incantation bowl. The entire surface, inside and out, is ornamented with religious inscriptions and talismanic numbers.  
  
The exterior rim is inscribed with Qur’anic verses: “In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful”; “Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The parable of His Light is as a niche and within it a lamp”; “Allah the Sufficient, Allah the Healer”; “In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful”; “In the Name of Allah, Who with His Name nothing can cause harm in the earth nor in the heavens, But Allah is the Best to guard and He is”; “In the name of Allah...the healer…”. The inner rim is ornamented with a band enclosed between two frames, each inscribed with repeated numbers (81 / 12).  
  
The band is inscribed with Qur’anic verse in Thuluth script: “Allah, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting by Whom all subsist, there is no god but Him. Neither slumber seizes Him, nor sleep; to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. Who is there who might intercede with Him save with His leave? He knows what lies before them and what is hidden from them, whereas they cannot attain to anything of His knowledge save what He wills them to attain. His Dominion overspreads the heavens and the earth, and their upholding wearies Him not. He is All-High, All-Glorious”.  
  
The inner base is surrounded by fifteen lobed medallions arranged in horizontal registers containing invocations reading: ”Allah the Sufficient / Allah the Healer / In the name of Allah,” repeated. At the very centre is a small, inverted dish. Its decoration begins with a band inscribed in Thuluth script repeating ”O Allah, grant us well-being”. Above it runs a row of pointed arches containing horizontally written numbers (II/II). The central surface of the dish is adorned with a star-shape formed of interlaced script reading ”O the most Compassionate, O the most Generous”.  
  
The exterior body is decorated with ornamental bands consisting of inscriptions and motifs. The outer rim begins with a band of Qur’anic verse: “Allah, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting by Whom all subsist, there is no god but Him. Neither slumber seizes Him, nor sleep; to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. Who is there who might intercede with Him save with His leave? He knows what lies before them and what is hidden from them, whereas they cannot attain to anything of His knowledge save what He wills them to attain. His Dominion overspreads the heavens and the earth, and their upholding wearies Him not. He is All-High, All-Glorious”. This is followed by a frame of repeated numbers (II/II).  
Around the outer rim of the bowl are fifteen lobed medallions arranged in horizontal registers, each inscribed with repeated invocations: ”Allah the Protector / Allah the Healer / In the name of Allah / Allah the Comforter”.  
Next comes a frame whose decoration is effaced, but traces of the number (81/12) remain visible.  
The recessed base begins with a band in thuluth script containing invocations: ”O Allah, grant us health / O Allah, be pleased with us”. This is followed by a row of pointed arches inscribed with numbers (81/12 and II/II). At the very center, a hexagram encloses the numbers (81/12).
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum FBQ Museum
keywords: Water; incantation; religion; bowl; copper
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

en.name: *Mount Tabor*
short_description: This depiction of Mount Tabor by the American artist John Douglas Woodward carries the caption 'Mount Tabor. Bearing among the Arabs, like so many other mountains, only the general name 'Jebel et Tur'. The scene suggests a rugged, primeval landscape untouched by modern humanity, the mystically lit, driven clouds that half veil the mounting evoking a spiritual and at the same time awe-inspiring atmosphere well suited to an important biblical site. In popular Christian tradition: Mount Tabor was associated with the Transfiguration of Christ. At the same time the mountain was to prove of historical importance, too.  In 1799, during the time of Napoleon Bonaparte's expedition in the area, the valley between Mount Tabor and the Moreh Hill saw a decisive battle in which a French force of about 3,000 soldiers under the command of Napoleon and General Jean Baptiste Kléber faced a Mamluk force of about 20,000 soldiers.

keywords: Jebel el-Tur; Mamluk

de.name: Deckelkrug
description: Dieses Tongefäß dürfte aus Terra Lemnia hergestellt worden sein. Schon die antiken Mediziner wie Dioskurides und Galenus  haben dieser Erde antitoxische Wirkung zugeschrieben. Durch die arabische Übersetzung der antiken Medizinschriften gelangte dieses Wissen in die islamische Welt, wo man wegen der genannten Eigenschaften Gefäße aus dieser Erde anfertigte. Ein solches Trinkgefäß sollte den Benutzer wohl vor einem Giftangriff in seinem Getränk bewahren.  Kaiser Rudolf II, der große Angst vor Vergiftung hatte, lies Gefäße dieser Art durch den Arzt der österreichischen Botschaft an der Hohen Pforte, Reinholf Lubenau, erwerben.

en.name: Lidded ewer
description: This terracotta vessel is probably made of a special clay called terra lemnia. This clay had been credited with antitoxic powers by ancient physicians such as Dioscorides and Galen. Arab translations of classical texts on medicine introduced this to the Islamic world, leading to the production of vessels made of this material. Such drinking vessels were probably also believed to protect drinkers from being poisoned. Afraid of dying from poison, Emperor Rudolf II charged Reinholf Lubenau, the physician at the Austrian embassy to the Ottoman court, with obtaining such vessels for him.
keywords: Furnishing; terra lemnia; medicine; science; scientific manuscript; Emperor Rudolf II; Habsburg; Ottoman-Austrian relations; court life; De Materia Medica

en.name: Balkan immigrants village at Sivrihisar
short_description: The civilian population living in the Balkans was forced to migrate to Anatolia due to the Balkan Wars at the end of the 18th century: the 1821 Mora rebellion, the 1856 Crimean war, the 1864 Russian-Caucasian war, the 1877-1878 Ottoman-Russian War, the 1896-97 Crete Rebellion, the 1912-13 Balkan Wars, World War I from 1914 to 1918 and the 1919-22 Greek-Turkish War. These wars resulted in mass migrations. The Ottoman Empire lost almost all its European territories west of the River Maritsa, drawing present day Turkey's western border. A large influx of Turks started to flee into the Ottoman heartland as a result of the lost lands. By 1914, the remaining core region of the Ottoman Empire had experienced a population increase of around 2.5 million because of the flood of immigration from the Balkans.

en.name: Jar with enamel decoration
short_description: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century and as a training school for specializing artisans. The idea was part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history passed down from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic traditions in the Middle Ages. In the 19th century there was also a rebirth of the Murano glass for different reasons. The jar with enamelled decorations, white flowers and green leaves was made in Murano and dates from the beginning of the 20th century. It shows evolution of forms and techniques through the new ideas coming from Art Nouveau and the diffusion of polychrome enamels.

en.name: ‘Animal combat’ carpet
description:
Indian carpets began to arrive in Portugal from the second half of the 16th century onwards. Despite apparently not having been introduced in significant quantities, Indian carpets constituted an alternative to the decoration present in their Turkish and Persian counterparts.  
This carpet is a beautiful example of North Indian production, with its palette dominated by tones of red, as well as by *ton sur ton* colouring. It features a rectangular field with a red background, filled by a vertically organised scene in which various felines are chasing herbivorous animals. Dense branches interspersed with floral motifs, bunches of grapes, cutout leaves and palmettes frame the scene.  
The wide border also has a red background. This is decorated with cutouts and a repeated, interlocking series of three coloured and poly-lobed cartouches, themselves filled with polychrome rosettes, which alternate with palmettes, Timurid-inspired sinuous cloudbands and floral and leaf arrangements.
keywords: Carpet; North India; wool; animals; palmettes; cartouches; flowers

ar.name: قناطر قيمربورغاز.
description:
مع تزايد عدد سكان استنبول خلال القرن 10 / 16 تفاقمت مشكلة نقص المياه. ويرُوى أن السلطان سليمان كان ذات مرة في رحلة صيد فلاحظ وجود منابع مائية من الممكن استثمارها، وعندئذ أمر بإجراء البحوث عليها. في ذلك الحين، كان المعمار سنان كبير معماري القصر، فأجرى مسحاً للمنطقة وأوصى بإنشاء نظام لجر المياه ونقلها إلى المدينة. وعلى ضوء ذلك، أمر سليمان بالشروع في بناء نظام لتزويد المياه في عام 961 / 1554. وقد أُنجز المشروع في عام 970 / 1563، ولكن سرعان ما هدمت الفيضانات جزءاً منه، فكان لابد من إعادة بنائه عام 971 / 1564. وقد كلَّف هذا النظام حوالي 50 مليون آقة، وهي الوحدة النقدية المتداولة في الإمبراطورية العثمانية.  
  
كان لنظام تزويد المياه هذا، بفرعيه الشرقي والغربي، أن يجمع المياه من ينابيع عدة تقع على بعد حوالي 25 كم شمال غرب استنبول، ويحاذي قرية قيمربورغاز من جهة الجنوب ثم يستمر بخط واحد وصولاً إلى مدينة استنبول. يتألف النظام من نطاق مغطى (بطول إجمالي قدره 55 كم ومقطع بقياس 55x175 سم)، و 33 قنطرة ومراكز تجميع وتوزيع؛ ويغذي بالمياه أجزاء المدينة التي تقع على ارتفاع لا يزيد عن 34 م. في مرحلة لاحقة، بين عامي 1029 / 1620 و 1234 / 1818، تمَّ بناء عدد من الخزانات والقناطر الإضافية. وهناك جزء ضئيل من نظام تزويد المياه هذا يعود إلى ما قبل عهد السلطان سليمان، مثل الجزء الواصل بين إغريقابي وجيبسقوي الذي يعود تاريخه إلى عهد محمد الثاني. هناك أجزاء أخرى من هذا النظام، كقناة قووق قيمر، تمَّ بناؤها على أنقاض بيزنطية.  
  
من بين القناطر الـ 33 التي تشكل نظام قيمربورغاز لتزويد المياه، ثمة خمس قناطر ضخمة تتكون من طبقتين أو ثلاث من العقود التي تمتد لمسافات طويلة. فقناطر باشا قيمري أو باليقزادة يبلغ طولها 102 م وارتفاعها 16.4 م، وهي من طبقتين. قناطر أوزونقيمر طولها 711 م وارتفاعها 25 م، وهي من طبقتين أيضاً؛ كما يبلغ قياس نطاقها العلوي المجصَّص 60x 175 سم، وتغطيه ألواح من الحجر. قناطر قووق قيمر أو قيريق قيمر طولها 258 م وارتفاعها 35 م، وتنعطف بزاوية 90 درجة؛ ويتألف مقطعها الأول من طبقة واحدة بينما مقطعها الثاني من ثلاث طبقات. قناطر ماغلوا أو موالاق، التي تعتبر الجزء الأضخم في النظام، يبلغ طولها 258 م وارتفاعها 36 م؛ وهي من طبقتين، أحداها تشتمل على ثمانية عقود كبيرة والأخرى تشتمل على ثمانية عقود صغيرة. قناطر غيزلجي قيمر أو غوزلوج قيمر يبلغ طولها 165 م وارتفاعها 34.5 م، وتتكون من طبقتين أيضاً. وهناك قناطر هامة ذات طبقة واحدة، وهي قناطر آيواد (185 م) وكورت (305 م) وقاراقيمر (62.6 م) وباليقلي قيمر (125 م) ووليد قيمر (38.8 م).  
  
هذا النظام يزود بالماء أكثر من 300 خزان في المدينة أصلاً، 135 منها تمَّ بناؤه كمؤسسات دينية تابعة للسلطان سليمان القانوني. أما الإضافات اللاحقة فرفعت العدد إلى 580 خزاناً. أجزاء النظام الواقعة خارج أسوار مدينة استنبول ما تزال مستخدمة منذ ما يزيد عن 400 عام.

en.name: Kırkçeşme water-supply system.
description:
As the population of Istanbul increased during the AH 10th / AD 16th century, so did its problems with water shortages. Tradition holds that once, while Sultan Süleyman was out hunting, he noticed possible water sources and ordered their investigation. The head architect of the palace at that time, Mimar Sinan, surveyed the area and recommended the construction of a water system to convey water to the city. Süleyman consequently ordered in AH 961 / AD 1554 that construction of the water system was initiated. The project was completed in AH 970 / AD 1563, but parts of it were soon damaged by floods and had to be rebuilt in AH 971 / AD 1564. The system cost about 50,000,000 *akche*s, the main currency unit during the Ottoman Empire.  
The system collects water from various springs located about 25 km northwest of Istanbul, in two branches, namely east and west, which join south of Kemerburgaz village and continue as a single line to the city of Istanbul. The system is composed of covered galleries (measuring 55 cm x 175 cm in section and extending about 55 km in total), 33 aqueducts as well as collection and distribution centres, and provided water to the areas of the town below 34 m in altitude. A number of reservoirs were built at a later stage, between AH 1029 / AD 1620 and AH 1234 / AD 1818, and so were further aqueducts. A small section of the water-supply system dates to before Süleyman, such as that extending between Eğrikapı and Cebeciköy, which dates to the reign of Mehmed II. Other parts of the system, such as that of the Kovuk Kemer, were built partially on Byzantine remains.  
Of the 33 aqueducts that make up the Kırkçeşme water-supply system, five are monumental, with two or three tiers of arches and of considerable length. Paşa Kemeri or Balıkzade is 102 m long, 16.4 m high and has two tiers. Uzunkemer is 711 m long, 25 m high and is also two tiered.The plastered gallery on top of it is 60 cm x 175 cm and covered with stone slabs. Kovukkemer or Kırıkkemer is 408 m long and 35 m high and makes a turn of 90 degrees. Its first section is single tiered while the second is triple-tiered. Mağlova or Muallak Aqueduct, the greatest part of the entire system, is 258 m long and 36 m high. It is two-tiered with eight large and eight small arches. Güzelcekemer or Gözlücekemer aqueduct is 165 m long, 34.5 m high and is also two-tiered. Other important but single-tiered aqueducts are Ayvad (195 m), Kurt (305 m), Karakemer (62.6 m), Balıklıkemer (125 m) and Valide Kemeri (38.8 m).  
The entire system is built of stone masonry and uses bossed stones.  
The system originally provided water to over 300 fountains in the city, 135 of which were built as pious foundations of Süleyman the Magnificent. Later additions raised the number to about 580 fountains. Parts of the system located outside Istanbul's city walls have been functioning for over 400 years.

Kırkçeşme water-supply system was built by the great Ottoman architect Sinan on the order of the Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent in order to solve Istanbul's growing problems with water shortage. The system comprises 33 aqueducts and numerous collection and distribution centres. It supplied more than 300 fountains in the beginning but this number later rose to 580. Parts of the system located outside the city walls are still functioning and serving the megapolis of Istanbul.
artist: Architects: Mimar Sinan assisted by Kiriz Nikola.
keywords: Water; aqueduct; Süleyman the Magnificent; Sinan; civil architecture; water architecture

es.name: Acueductos de Kemerburgaz.
names: Sistema de suministro de agua de Kırkçeşme.
description:
La población de Estambul aumentó durante el siglo X / XVI y, con ella, los problemas de escasez de agua de la ciudad. Según la tradición, cierta vez que el sultán Süleyman había salido de caza, encontró una zona con posibles recursos acuíferos y ordenó que los evaluaran. El maestro arquitecto de palacio en aquella época, Mimar Sinan, examinó entonces la zona y recomendó la construcción de un sistema que transportara el agua hasta la ciudad y, en 961 / 1554, Süleyman ordenó que se iniciara su construcción. El proyecto se culminó en 970 / 1563, pero ciertas partes se deterioraron pronto a causa de las inundaciones, por lo que los acueductos se reconstruyeron en 971 / 1564. El sistema costó alrededor de 50 millones de *akches*, unidad monetaria del imperio otomano.  
El sistema recoge el agua de diversos manantiales localizados unos 25 kilómetros al noroeste de Estambul, en dos conducciones –este y oeste– que se juntan al sur de la ciudad de Kemerbugaz y continúan unidas hasta Estambul. Este sistema, compuesto por galerías cubiertas (de 55 × 175 m de sección y con una extensión de unos 55 km en total), 33 acueductos y una serie de puntos de distribución, suministraba agua a las zonas de la ciudad situadas por debajo de los 34 m de altitud. En una etapa posterior, entre 1029 / 1620 y 1234 / 1818, se construyeron nuevos aljibes y acueductos. Una pequeña parte del sistema de suministro, la que se extiende entre Eğrikapı y Cebeciköy, es anterior a la época de Süleyman, ya que data del sultanato de Mehmed II. Otras partes, como la de Kovuk Kemer, se construyeron parcialmente sobre ruinas bizantinas.  
De los 33 acueductos que componen el sistema de suministro de agua de Kırkçeşme, hay cinco monumentales que poseen dos o tres niveles de arcos y una longitud considerable: el Paşa Kemeri o Balıkzade, de 102 m de largo y 16,4 m de alto; el Uzunkemer, de 711 m de longitud y 25 m de alto, con una galería enyesada y recubierta de losas de piedra de 60 × 175 cm; el Kovukkemer o Kırıkkemer, que mide 408 m de largo, tiene una altura de 35 m y describe un ángulo de 90 grados, con un primer tramo de un solo nivel y un segundo con tres alturas; el Mağlova o Muallak, el mayor de todo el sistema, con 258 m de largo y 36 m de alto, posee dos niveles y cuenta con ocho arcos grandes y otros ocho pequeños; el Güzelcekemer o Gözlücekemer, de 165 m de largo y 34,5 m de alto. Cabe mencionar otros acueductos igualmente importantes, pero de una sola hilera de arcadas, como el Ayvad (195 m), el Kart (305 m), el Karakemer (62,6 m), el Balıklıkemer (125 m) y el Valide Kemeri (38,8 m). Todo el sistema está construido con mampostería y sillares almohadillados.  
Originalmente, suministraba agua a unas 300 fuentes de la ciudad, 135 de las cuales se construyeron como fundaciones benéficas de Süleyman el Magnífico. El sistema se fue ampliando y llegó a poseer 580 fuentes. Algunas partes del sistema que están en el exterior de las murallas de la ciudad de Estambul se han utilizado durante más de 400 años.

El sistema de suministro de agua de Kırkçeşme, obra del gran arquitecto otomano Sinan, se construyó por orden del sultán Süleyman el Magnífico, que pretendía resolver los problemas de escasez de agua de Estambul. Comprende 33 acueductos y numerosos centros de recogida y distribución de agua. Empezó suministrando agua a más de 300 fuentes, que llegaron a ser 580. Hay partes del sistema situadas extramuros que aún llevan agua a la gran ciudad de Estambul.
artist: Mimar Sinan, asistido por Kiriz Nikola.
keywords: Agua; acueducto; Süleyman el Magnífico; Sinan; arquitectura civil; arquitectura para el agua.

fr.name: Système d’approvisionnement en eau de Kırkçeşme.
description:
Les problèmes d'alimentation en eau d'Istanbul se multiplièrent avec l'accroissement de la population au cours du Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.). La tradition veut que, au cours d'une partie de chasse, le sultan Soliman remarqua des sources et demanda qu'elles soient évaluées. L'architecte de la cour de l'époque, Mimar Sinan, étudia la zone et recommanda la création d'un système d'adduction pour alimenter la ville, dont Soliman ordonna le début des travaux en 961 H / 1554 J.-C. Le projet fut achevé en 970 H / 1563 J.-C. mais plusieurs parties furent rapidement endommagées par des inondations et durent être reconstruites en 971 H / 1564 J.-C. L'ensemble coûta environ 50 000 000 d'akches, l'unité de compte principale utilisé sous l'empire ottoman.  
Le système fait appel à diverses sources situées à 25 km environ au nord-ouest d'Istanbul qui alimentent deux branches – est et ouest – se rejoignant au sud du village de Kemerburgaz avant de poursuivre jusqu'à la capitale. Il se compose de galeries couvertes (de 175 x 55 cm de section et de 55 km de long au total), de 33 aqueducs ainsi que de points de captages et de distribution. Il alimente les quartiers de la ville situés à moins de 34 m d'altitude. Un certain nombre de réservoirs et d'aqueducs ont été construits ultérieurement de 1029 à 1234 H / 1620-1818 J.-C. Une petite section date même d'avant Soliman, dont celle d'Eğrikapi à Cebeciköy qui date de Mehmed II. D'autres parties, comme celle de Kovuk Kemer, ont même été édifiées sur des vestiges byzantins. Sur les 33 aqueducs qui constituent le système de Kirkçeşme, cinq à deux ou trois étages superposés sur une longueur considérable sont monumentaux. Paşa Kemeri ou Balikzade mesure 102 m de long, 16,4 m de haut et s'élève sur deux étages. Unzunkemer, également à deux étages, mesure 711 m de long et 25 de haut. Sa galerie supérieure couverte et plâtrée de 175 x 60 cm de section est recouverte de dalles de pierre. Kovukkemer, ou Kirikkemer, mesure 408 m de long et 35 m de haut et décrit un virage à 90°. Sa première section est à un seul étage, la seconde à trois étages. L'aqueduc de Mağlova ou Muallak, le plus important, mesure 258 m de long pour 36 m de haut. Il est à deux étages soutenus par huit grands et huit petits arcs. Celui de Güzelcekemer ou Gözlücekemer, de 165 m de long pour 34,5 m de haut, est également à deux étages. Les autres ouvrages d'art notables sont les aqueducs à un étage de Ayvad (195 m de long), Kurt (305 m), Karakemer (62,6 m), Baliklikemer (125 m) et Valide Kemeri (38,8 m).  
Le système dans son entier est en maçonnerie de pierre et pierres à bossage.  
Le système alimentait à l'origine plus de 300 fontaines urbaines, dont 135 étaient des fondations pieuses de Soliman. Plus tard, le nombre de points d'eau s'élèvera à 580 environ. Des parties de ce réseau situées hors les murs d'Istanbul fonctionnent depuis plus de quatre siècles.

Le système d’approvisionnement en eau de Kırkçeşme fut construit par le grand architecte ottoman Sinan sur ordre du sultan Soliman le Magnifique afin de résoudre les problèmes grandissants de pénurie d’eau rencontrés par Istanbul. Le système comprend 33 aqueducs et de nombreux points de captage et de distribution. Il alimentait plus de 300 fontaines à l’origine ; plus tard, le nombre de points d’eau s’élèvera à 580. Certaines parties de ce réseau situées hors les murs de la ville fonctionnent encore aujourd’hui et alimentent la mégapole d’Istanbul.
artist: Sultan Soliman le Magnifique (r. 926-974 H / 1520-1566 J.-C.).
Architecte : Mimar Sinan, assisté de Kiriz Nicola.
keywords: aqueducs ; Soliman le Magnifique ; Sinan ; architecture civile ; ouvrages d’art ; architecture hydraulique

tr.name: Kırkçeşme Suları.
description:
H. 10. / M. 16. yüzyılda İstanbul'un nüfusu arttıkça su sıkıntısı çekilmeye başlandı. öykülere göre bir gün Kanuni Sultan Süleyman avlanırken gördüğü pınarların araştırılmasını ister. Hassa Başmimarı Sinan, araziyi inceleyerek kente su getirecek bir sukemeri sistemi inşasını önerir. H. 961 / M. 1554 yılında Kanuni'nin emriyle başlayan inşaat 970 / 1563 yılında tamamlanır fakat kısa süre sonra gerçekleşen sel felaketleri nedeniyle kısmen zarar görür. Derhal onarılarak 971 / 1564 yılında tekrar hizmete girer. İnşaatın tamamı yaklaşık 50 milyon akçeye mal olmuştur.  
  
Kırkçeşme Su Tesisleri İstanbul'un yaklaşık 25 km kuzeybatısındaki çeşitli derelerden su toplar. Doğu ve Batı kolları, Kemerburgaz köyünün güneyinde birleşerek ana isale hattını oluşturur. 55x175 cm kesitli kapalı galerilerle kente su taşıyan sistem, 33 sukemeri, çok sayıda toplama ve dağıtım merkezine sahiptir. Toplam uzunluğu 54 kilometreye ulaşan isale hattı, kentin 34 metreden daha düşük kottaki semtlerine su sağlamıştır. 1029 – 1234 / 1620 – 1818 arasında inşa edilen çeşitli bentler ve isale hatları da sisteme bağlanmıştır. Sistemin küçük bir bölümü Kanuni'den önceki bir döneme, özellikle Eğrikapı ile Cebeciköy arasındaki kısım Fatih dönemine aittir. Kovuk Kemer gibi bazı bölümler kısmen Bizans kalıntılarının üzerine inşa edilmiştir.  
  
Sukemerleri: 33 sukemerinden beş tanesi iki ya da üç katlı kemerleri ve uzunluklarıyla anıtsaldır. İki katlı Paşa Kemeri (Balıkzade) 102 metre uzunluğunda, 16.4 metre yüksekliğindedir. 711 metre uzunluğundaki Uzunkemer 25 metre yüksekliğinde ve iki katlıdır. üstteki sıvalı galerisi 60x175 cm olup taş levhalarla örtülüdür. Kovuk (Kırık) Kemer 408 metre uzunluğa ve 35 metre yüksekliğe sahip olup, 90 derecelik açıyla kıvrılır. Birinci kısım tek katlı iken ikinci kısım üç katlıdır. Tüm sistemin en muazzam eseri olan Mağlova (Muallak) Kemeri ise 258 metre uzunluğa, 36 metre yüksekliğe sahiptir. Sekiz büyük ve sekiz küçük kemer gözüyle iki katlıdır. Yine iki katlı Güzelcekemer (Gözlücekemer) ise 165 m uzunlukta ve 34.5 metre yüksekliktedir. Diğer önemli sukemerleri arasında tek katlı olan Ayvad (195 m), Kurt (305 m), Karakemer (62.6 m), Balıklıkemer (125 m) ve Valide Kemeri (38.8 m) sayılabilir.  
  
Tamamı taş işçiliğiyle inşa edilen sistemde bosajlı taş kullanımı dikkat çeker.  
  
Başlangıçta sistem, 135'i Kanuni tarafından vakıf olarak inşa ettirilen 300'den fazla çeşmeye su sağlıyordu. Daha sonraki eklemelerle bu sayı 580'e ulaştı. Sistemin, İstanbul kent surları dışında kalan kısmı 400 seneyi aşkın bir süredir halen kullanılmaktadır.

Mimar Sinan'ın Kanuni Sultan Süleyman'ın emriyle İstanbul'un su sorununu çözmek amacıyla inşa ettiği Kırkçeşme tesisleri, 33 su kemeri ile çok sayıda toplama ve dağıtım merkezinden oluşmaktadır. Başlangıçta 300'den fazla, daha sonra 580 çeşmeye su sağlayan sistemin İstanbul kent surları dışında kalan kısmı günümüzde halen kullanılmaktadır.
keywords: Su; sukemeri; Kanuni Sultan Süleyman; Mimar Sinan; sivil mimari; su mimarisi.

en.name: Church of Our Lady in Szentgotthárd
description:
The sanctuary of the one-nave church closes in an arch. The church also houses a wide triumphal arch and a narrow entrance hall. The concave western façade, crowned by a tower with a clock and richly articulated with wall columns, mouldings and a tympanon, is decorated with statues of saints.  
Today's church is a simplified version of Pilgram's third design, which was altered due to financial difficulties. In his original plans, Pilgram also articulated the monastery with corner pavilions.  
The interior decoration of the church, especially the paintings, focus on the triumph of the Christian faith, and include paintings of Christian armies defeating the Turks at Szentgotthárd (i.e. the ceiling fresco in the nave by István Dorffmeister Senior and Junior from 1784) and the *Triumph of the Cross* (the work of Matthias Gusner, a Cistercian lay-brother from Heiligenkreuz). There are also illustrations of pious Christian life and “Happy Death” (*Buona mors*); the *Assumption of the Virgin Mary*; the *Resurrection of the Body* (on the vault above the sanctuary by István Dorffmaister) and the *Heavenly Altar of God's Lamb* (also by Dorffmeister).  
On the main altar is the *Assumption of the Virgin Mary* by Matthias Gusner, whose works are seen on the side altars also. (1) Either side of the Altar of St. Bernard of Clairvaux are angels bearing aloft the Instruments of the Passion (*arma Christi*). The oval painting in the middle is the *Pietà*, while St. Peter and Mary Magdalene are shown in high relief. (2) On the Altarpiece of St. Gotthard is the painting, the *Miracle of St. Gotthard*; either side are statues of St. Barbara and St. Catherine of Alexandria. The oval painting illustrates St. Sebastian and St. Roch, while the Saints Margit and Dorothy are in high relief. (3) The Altar of the Hungarian Saint King shows St. Stephen, St. Ladislaus, St. Imre (Emeric) and an angel holding a sword in defence of Hungary. Either side are statues of St. Agnes and St. Apollonia, and the oval painting depicts the Roman martyrs, St. John and St. Paul. St. Adalbert and St. Jadwiga are in high relief. (4) On the Altar of St. Joseph is the painting, the *Death of St. Joseph*. Angels stand on either side of the altar; the oval painting shows a Guardian Angel; St. Franca (abbottess) and St. Wendelin are in high relief.  
There are exquisite pieces of furniture: the engraved pulpit, choir, pews, and in the vestry, dressing cabinets. All the furniture was carved by Gáspár Schretzenmayer, a lay brother from Heiligenkreuz. The statues were carved by Joseph Schnitzer, a Cistercian master carver from Heiligenkreuz. The organ of the church was created by Ferdinand Schwartz in Graz in 1764. Today the Baroque organ case contains an organ from the 20th century.

The Cistercian Church and Monastery of Szentgotthárd are outstanding examples of 18th-century Hungarian religious architecture. Designed by Franz Anton Pilgram, construction began in 1740 and continued to 1769. The one-nave church with a frontal tower was consecrated in the honour of Our Lady. It is richly decorated with paintings, sculptures and carved furniture; the fresco was painted by Stefan Dorffmeister and his son, and the main altarpiece is the work of Matthias Gusner. The opulently carved and gilded furniture, the pews, pulpit and the organ in the church, are the work of the Cistercian monk Gáspár Schretzenmayer.
artist: György Széchenyi, Archbishop of Kalocsa; Abbot Robert Leeb (1728–1755); Abbot Fritz Alberik

Architectural design: Franz Anton Pilgram (1699–1761); fresco painters: Stephan Dorfmeister Sr (1725–1797), István Dorfmeister Jr (1770–1807); altarpiece paintings: Matthias Gusner (1694–1772); sculptor: Joseph Schnitzer (1707–1769); carving and gilding: Gáspár Schretzenmayer (1693–1782); organ maker Ferdinand Schwartz
history:
The Cistercian Monastery of Szentgotthárd was founded by King Béla III of the Árpád dynasty in 1183. French monks led by the abbot, arrived at the monastery from Trois Fontaines and commenced construction of the abbey in 1184. The church was consecrated to Our Lady. The abbey, which began to flourish soon after it was built, was donated by King Sigismund of Luxemburg to Palatine Miklós Széchy and his son. In the early 16th century, exercising their noble rights, the Széchy family relocated the monks from the monastery and converted the building into a family castle that served as a stronghold to protect them against the Turks. In 1556 the monks wanted to return, but Margit Széchy drove them away. Not long after this incident, the city commander, Wolfgang Tieffenbach a general of Emperor Rudolf, blew up the monastery.  
In 1675 Bishop György Széchenyi obtained the right of possession over the abbey from Emperor Leopold, and began construction of a new church between  
1676 and 1677, using the remains of the medieval church. The one-nave church with three altars was converted into a granary under King Joseph II in 1787. In 1988 it became a theatre and in 2007 it was transformed into a tourist centre.  
It was Emperor Charles VI who donated Szentgotthárd Abbey to the Cistercian Abbey of Heiligenkreuz in 1734. Robert Leeb, Abbot of Heiligenkreuz, decided to rebuild the church and entrusted Franz Anton Pilgram with drawing up plans for both the church and monastery. Pilgram's initial plans transformed the existing buildings but – probably at the request of Leeb – at first he altered these plans and then drew up another design for a completely new building. Construction of the monastery commenced in 1740 and by 1746 the monks were able to move into the half-complete building.  
The foundation stone of the church was laid in 1748, and in 1764, the new abbot, Fritz Alberik, blessed the almost complete building. However, it was not until 1779 that János Szily, first bishop of Szombathely, consecrated the building.  
The layout designed by Pilgram, follows South German traditions in its use of the so called lyre-shaped church layout. With sail vaults separated by cross-bracings that rest on pillars, the church has no side chapels; instead fairly shallow chapels have been inserted into the niches between the pillars. Due to these shallow chapels, the nave and the western façade are narrow and there is one tower in the middle of the western façade instead of two.  
During construction, the Abbey of Heiligenkreuz faced financial difficulties, and this is why Pilgram's plans were not fully implemented: his third set of designs foresaw the monastery with two additional wings that would have embraced the church from both sides. In the end, only the south wing was built. Of the north wing, only the foundation was completed, and this was another reason for the continued use of the old, so-called, granary-church.
keywords: Cistercian order, *Ordo Cisterciensis, OCist,* church, monastery, altar, Turks, King Béla III, György Széchenyi, Franz Anton Pilgram, Stephan Dorffmeister Sr., István Dorffmeister Jr, Matthias Gusner, Joseph Schnitzer, Gáspár Schretzenmayer, Ferdinand Schwartz, Robert Leeb, Fritz Alberik, János Szily, Szentgotthárd
partner: Eszterháza Centre for Culture, Research and Festivals

en.name: İshak Pasha Complex
description:
İshak Pasha was an important statesman in the time of Sultans Murad II (1421-1451) and Mehmed II (1451-1481). In the conquest of Istanbul he was an army commander, and later he acted as a governor and Grand *Vizier*.When he died in 1485 at Thessalonica, his body was brought to İnegöl and buried in the conventional cemetery to the south of the mosque he had built in his own name; in 1937 his grave was removed to the *türbe* to the southwest of the mosque. During his years in office he had many buildings constructed in several cities, such as Istanbul, Edirne, Kütahya, Bursa and, the income from several *hammams, shops, mills, and land rental was dedicated to the waqfs for the maintenance of these buildings and to pay the salaries of the staff. The complex built by İshak Pasha in İnegöl consists of a mosque, a madrasa, and a türbe; although the waqf charter mentions a han there is no han present today.  
  
**İshak Pasha Mosque**  
This mosque built with alternating rows of stone and brick like the madrasa and the türbe, has some brickwork decoration and that on the spandrels of the portico is especially noteworthy.The plain portico –closed off with glass panes– has five domed bays separated with brick and stone piers.The single brick minaret rising on the northwest corner of the building is entered from the western end of the portico.The inscription on the plain portal tells of the repairs carried out in 1877 by Sultan Abdülhamid II. One enters an inner court flanked on the east and west with what were once the tabhanes but which are now joined together by removing the walls in between.The rectangular areas that are topped with a vault to the north of these lateral sections, seems to have once been the way leading into the tabhanes. The plain prayer hall is to the south. All the domes inside rise above beautiful Turkish triangles. Although there is no inscription, it is believed that the mosque was probably constructed in 1476, based upon the inscription of the madrasa and the date of the waqf charter established by İshak Pasha.  
  
**Madrasa**  
The madrasa is “U”-shaped opening towards the mosque; this layout reminds us of the Süleyman Pasha Madrasa in İznik.The dershane rising higher than the rest of the structure is covered by a dome and also protrudes out on the north. A total of 12 domed student cells flank the dershane on both sides; each cell is furnished with a fireplace and a niche for daily use. In front of the student cells is a portico with vaulted bays resting on piers surrounding the open courtyard. According to the construction inscription of the madrasa, it was built in 1483, that is, a little later than the mosque. Today (2000) the madrasa is used as a Koran school.  
  
**Türbe**  
The türbe to the southwest of the mosque is known to have been built by İshak Pasha for his wife Tacü’n-nisa (Taj al-nisa) Sultan. This hexagonal structure is covered by a dome and has a very plain portal on the north. Inside are three graves, one of which belongs to İshak Pasha; since there are no gravestones, it is not known for certain to whom the other two graves belong. However, taking into account historical documents, it is reasonable to assume that one grave belongs to Tacü’n-nisa. It is said that the third grave belongs to the Pasha’s daughter, but this cannot be ascertained.*

es.name: Complejo de İshak Paşa
description:
İshak Paşa fue un importante hombre de Estado en la época de Murad II (r. 1421-1451) y Mehmet II (r. 1451-1481). En la toma de Estambul era comandante del ejército y, más tarde, llegó a ser gobernador y Gran Visir. Murió en Salónica en 1485 y su cuerpo fue llevado a İnegöl y enterrado en el cementerio que hay al sur de la mezquita que él mismo había hecho construir con su nombre. En 1937 se trasladó su tumba al mausoleo del suroeste. En sus años de servicio había hecho construir muchos edificios en Estambul, Edirne, Kütahya y Bursa, y las rentas que proporcionaban varios *hammam*s, comercios, molinos y tierras iban destinadas a los *waqf*s que se encargaban del mantenimiento de los edificios y de pagar los salarios del personal. El complejo construido por İshak Paşa en İnegöl consta de una mezquita, una *madrasa* y un *turbe*; aunque en el acta fundacional del *waqf* se menciona un *han*, no hay ninguno en nuestros días.  
  
**Mezquita**  
Esta mezquita, construida con filas alternas de piedra y ladrillo, igual que la *madrasa* y el *turbe*, tiene decoración de albañilería, entre la que destaca la del trasdós de los arcos del pórtico. Este sobrio pórtico —cerrado con cristaleras— tiene cinco crujías con cúpula separadas por pilares de ladrillo y piedra. Al alminar único que se alza en la esquina noroeste del edificio se entra por el extremo occidental del pórtico. La inscripción del sencillo portal informa de una reforma en 1877, ordenada por el sultán Abdülhamid II. Al atravesarlo, se entra en el patio interior, flanqueado a este y oeste por lo que debieron ser *tabhane*s y ahora forman un solo espacio al haber sido quitados los tabiques de separación; los espacios rectangulares abovedados que se encuentran al norte de estas secciones laterales parecen ser los pasillos que antes llevaban a los *tabhane*s. La sala de oración está en la parte sur. Todas las cúpulas interiores se alzan sobre preciosos *triángulos turcos*. Aunque no hay ninguna inscripción con datos sobre su construcción, se cree, basándose en la inscripción de la *madrasa* y la fecha del acta fundacional del *waqf* promulgada por İshak Paşa, que esta mezquita fue erigida en 1476.  
  
**Madrasa**  
La *madrasa* tiene forma de U con el lado abierto orientado a la mezquita; esta planta recuerda la de la *madrasa* de Süleyman Paşa de İznik. El *dershane*, más alto que el resto del edificio, está cubierto por una cúpula y sobresale al exterior en la parte norte. A sus dos lados se distribuyen 12 celdas de estudiantes, todas con hogar y hornacinas para el uso diario. Delante de ellas, rodeando el patio abierto, se extiende un pórtico de crujías con bóvedas que descansan sobre pilares. Según la inscripción, esta madrasa —que hoy es una escuela coránica— se construyó en 1483, es decir, un poco más tarde que la mezquita.  
  
**Turbe**  
De este *turbe*, situado al suroeste de la mezquita, se sabe que lo mandó construir İshak Paşa para su mujer Tacü’n-nisa (Tay al-Nisa) Sultan. Se trata de un edificio hexagonal coronado por una cúpula y con un sobrio portal en la fachada norte. En el interior hay tres tumbas, una de ellas la de İshak Paşa. Al no tener lápidas, se desconoce de quiénes son las otras dos. Si damos crédito a los documentos históricos, una de las dos tumbas tiene que pertenecer a Tacü’n-nisa. Se dice que la tercera es la de la hija de Paşa, pero no se tienen noticias ciertas.

ar.name: نقش الهكاري.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن لوحة مستطيلة من الرخام الأبيض تحتوي على نقش كتابي، وتتكون من ثلاث قطع تم ترميمها في فترة لاحقة. كتب النص في سبعة أسطر بخط الثلث الأيوبي البارز، وهو معجّم بشكل جزئي وغير مشكول، ولا يوجد مسافات فاصلة بين كلمات النص. حدِّدت حواف اللوحة الرخامية من جميع الجوانب بنحت الرخام بشكل قائم وحاد يعرَف بالزملة. كذلك استخدم أسلوب الزملة للفصل بين الأسطر داخل اللوحة.  
والنص الذي تحمله اللوحة هو نص تأبيني لشروة الهكاري الذي توفي في الرملة في فلسطين، ثم نقل جثمانه إلى مدينة القدس ليدفن في مقبرة باب الساهرة القديمة. وعائلة الهكاري هي عائلة كردية جاءت من العراق، وشارك عدد كبير من أفرادها في الحروب الصليبية تحت قيادة صلاح الدين الأيوبي. ونص النقش كما يلي:  
"بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم هذا قبر  
شروة بن داود بن ابراهيم الهكاري  
رحمه الله المستشهد في ارض الرملة  
بشهر ذي القعدة من سنة سبع  
وثمانين وخمس ماية هجرية رحمه  
الله ورحم من ترحم عليه امين  
يا رب العالمين امين."

نقش محفور على رخام، كُتب بخط الثلث الأيوبي البارز، وتخلو كلمات النقش من الحركات. والنص المحفور عبارة عن نص تأبيني (شاهد قبر) لـ "شروة الهكاري"، الذي مات بالرملة، ونقل جثمانه إلى القدس، ليُدفن في مقبرة عائلية، ويبدو أنه كان من المقاتلين الذي قضوا حياتهم في محاربة الفرنجة.
