en.name: Qur’anic manuscript No. 7.
description:
A *mashaf* bound with an embossed decorative cover that dates to the Ottoman period. Both sides of the binding are decorated with medallions that are connected at the top and bottom by a hanging ornament. The front of the *mashaf* is composed of scroll 3b–4a. These two pages contain identical illuminated panels, some parts of which have been lost as a result of age and usage over a long period of time. Restoration of the *mashaf* took place in AH 1117 / AD 1705, directed by the Ottoman governor in Jerusalem, Qura Mustafa Pasha, who ruled for just one year. Scroll 4b–5a consists of a two-page spread embellished with the Opening Chapter (Surat al-Fatiha) and the beginning of “Surat al-Baqara” (“Chapter of the Cow”,). The decorative bands specific to these two pages are lost and all that remains of their ornamentation is half a border, which lies above “Surat al-Baqara”. The chapter number, the verse number and the surrounding area are all placed within a rectangular frame with a blue background. Similar information with regard to the other chapters appears in the same form but unframed.  
The beautiful Mamluk *thuluth* script is written in black ink. A Farsi (Persian) translation of the Arabic text is written underneath each verse. The vowel marks of the *mashaf* are written in blue and the diacritical marks in red. The pause markers assume the shape of golden flowers. The symbols for the division of every five parts in the text assume the form of a pyramid-shaped blossom, whose place is indicated in the margin by a suspended ornament, and in the middle of which is a blue circle. Written in the centre of it is the word “one fifth” in illuminated *kufic* script against a red background. The markers of every one-tenth of the text take the form of a blue flower with four leaves. Its place is indicated in the margin by a circular-shaped ornament with the word “one tenth” written in it, in illuminated *kufic* script.

This is a Qur’anic manuscript written in Mamluk *thuluth* script and translated into Farsi. The Farsi text appears below each line. Its opens with beautiful decorative panels that reflect the elements of Mamluk decorative art. Chapter names are illuminated against a dark blue background and the letters are written in blue. Diacritical markers are in red.
holder: Islamic Museum, al-Aqsa Mosque / al-Haram al-Sharif.
dates: Hegira 7th century / AD 13th century; restored AH 1117 / AD 1705.
dynasty: Mamluk; restored in the Ottoman period
keywords: Leather; embossed leather; thuluth; Qur'an; mashaf; paper; religious manuscript
materials: Ink on paper; leather binding with embossed decoration.

es.name: Manuscrito coránico n.º 7
description:
*Mashaf* (o manuscrito del Corán) encuadernado con unas tapas decorativas de cuero repujado que datan del periodo otomano. Las dos caras de la encuadernación están decoradas con una composición de medallones unidos por arriba y por abajo con elementos colgantes. La primera parte del *mashaf* incluye los rollos 3b-4a. Estas dos páginas presentan paneles iluminados idénticos, con algunas partes deterioradas por el uso y el paso del tiempo. La restauración se llevó a cabo en 1117 / 1705 por orden del gobernador otomano de Jerusalén Qura Mustafa, que gobernó solamente un año. El rollo 4b-5a constituye un pliego de dos páginas adornado con el capítulo de introducción (la *Surat al-Fatiha*) y el principio de la sura “La vaca” (“Al-Baqara”). No se conservan las cenefas decorativas de estas páginas; únicamente se conserva medio borde superior de la sura “Al-Baqara”. El número del capítulo y la aleya, y la zona de alrededor están inscritos en un marco rectangular con el fondo azul. En el resto de las páginas también se recoge la misma información, pero sin enmarcar.  
El texto está escrito con tinta negra en una hermosa escritura *zuluz* mameluca y cada versículo tiene debajo su traducción correspondiente al farsi (persa). Las marcas de las vocales están escritas en azul y los puntos diacríticos en rojo. Las marcas de las pausas están señaladas con flores doradas. Las cinco partes del texto están delimitadas con flores piramidales con un círculo azul en el centro, señaladas en los márgenes con motivos colgantes. En el centro de la flor se lee “un quinto” en letra cúfica iluminada sobre un fondo rojo. Las décimas partes del texto están señaladas con una flor azul de cuatro pétalos, indicada a su vez en el margen con un adorno circular en el que se lee “un décimo” en letra cúfica iluminada.

Manuscrito coránico escrito en letra *zuluz* mameluca y traducido al farsi. La traducción es el texto escrito debajo de cada línea. Los bellos paneles decorativos con los que se inicia el manuscrito son un buen ejemplo del arte decorativo mameluco. Los nombres de cada capítulo están iluminados sobre un fondo azul oscuro, y las letras son en azul claro. Los puntos diacríticos destacan en rojo.
dates: Siglo VII de la Hégira / XIII d. C. Restaurado en 1117/  1705.
dynasty: Mamelucos; restaurado en el periodo otomano
keywords: Cuero; cuero repujado; escritura zuluz; Corán; mashaf; papel.
materials: Tinta sobre papel; encuadernación de cuero con decoración repujada.
tags: encuadernación de cuero con decoración repujada.
partner: Museo islámico en la mezquita de Al-Aqsa

fr.name: Manuscrit coranique n° 7.
description:
*Machaf* relié avec une couverture décorative en cuir estampé datant de la période ottomane. Les deux faces de sa reliure sont ornées de médaillons réunis au haut et au bas du document par un ornement. La première partie se compose des rouleaux 3b-4a. Ces deux pages contiennent des cartouches enluminés identiques dont certaines parties ont disparu avec le temps ou les dégradations d'usage. La restauration de ce manuscrit a été entreprise en 1117 H / 1705 J.-C. à la demande du gouverneur de Jérusalem, Qora Moustafa Pacha, qui n'exerça cette fonction qu'une année. Les rouleaux 4b-5 a consistent en une double page qui contient la sourate d'ouverture, “al-Fatiha”, et le début de la sourate “al-Baqara” (La vache). Les bandeaux décoratifs spécifiques à ces deux pages ont disparu et il ne reste de l'ornementation qu'une demi-bordure au-dessus de la sourate de la Vache. Le numéro de sourate, le numéro du verset et la zone environnante sont disposés dans un cartouche rectangulaire à fond bleu. Le procédé est identique pour les autres sourates, mais sans cadre cette fois.  
La superbe écriture mamelouke de style *thoulouth* est exécutée à l'encre noire. Une traduction en farsi (perse) du texte arabe figure sous chaque verset. Les marques des voyelles sont en bleu et les signes diacritiques en rouge. Les indications de pause sont en forme de fleurs dorées. Les symboles de division présents toutes les cinq parties représentent une fleur pyramidale dont la place est rappelée en marge par un ornement au centre duquel figure un cercle bleu, dans lequel est écrit le mot “Un cinquième” en coufique enluminé sur fond rouge. Les marques placées toutes les dixièmes divisions du texte sont en forme de fleur bleue à quatre pétales. Leur emplacement est souligné en marge par un ornement circulaire contenant le mot “Un dixième” en coufique enluminé.

Manuscrit du coran rédigé en écriture mamelouke de style *thoulouth* dont la traduction en farsi figure sous chaque ligne. Il s’ouvre sur de magnifiques planches décoratives qui reflètent les spécificités de l’art décoratif mamelouk. Les titres de chapitre sont enluminés sur fond bleu foncé, les lettres étant en bleu et les signes diacritiques en rouge.
holder: Musée islamique, mosquée al-Aqsa / Haram al-Charif.
dates: VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe siècle J.-C.) ; restauré en 1117 H / 1705 J.-C.
dynasty: Période mamelouke. Restauré au cours de la période ottomane
keywords: Cuir ; cuirs estampés ; écriture thoulouth ; Coran ; machaf ; papiers
materials: Encre sur papier ; reliure en cuir à décoration estampée.
tags: reliure en cuir à décoration estampée.

en.name: Lion of St. Mark
description: The silver lion of St. Mark was a gift from Venice to the council and citizens of the city of Zurich in 1608. At that time, Venice was being besieged by Austria and Spain and sought contact with Protestant cantons; the Venetian ambassador Padavino, who wrote extensively about his trip, was sent to Zurich. His account of the banquet to celebrate the presentation of the lion he had donated contains the report that the lion was circulated in a round of toasts: the head can be removed and used as a tumbler.
keywords: Lion of St. Mark; Centrepiece; Diethelm Holzhalb; Zurich; Switzerland

en.name: Bowl
description: This bowl belongs to a large group of early Islamic vessels decorated by pinching or stamping the surface with tongs or stamps most often made of iron. This mould-blown deep sea-blue bowl presents a rounded shape with an inverted base and a stepped gilded rim. The decoration of this bowl consists of impressed and repeated geometric motifs. These simple roundels, each containing six circles, can be seen on the sides of the bowl. Additional circles are positioned in the interstices above and below, with a band with ovals just below the stepped rim. This kind of decoration was very popular during the early Islamic period and is found on several surviving examples attributed to Egypt.
keywords: Glass; Bowl; Free-blown; Fatimid

en.name: *Raft Conveying Winged Bull to Baghdad*
short_description: Layard describes the removal of the winged bulls from the site of the mound of Nimrud in Nineveh and its remains, 1849, from where they had lain for approximately the last 2,730 years. They were carefully loaded on to rafts, made in the traditional way of using hundreds of inflated goat and sheep-skins supporting a wooden superstructure. Layard (who had learnt Arabic and Persian) recruited the crew locally, as he had done with his workforce. In April 1847, he sent them floating with the current, off on a six hundred mile journey down the river Tigris to Basra, where ships of the British Navy were waiting to take them the next 12,000 miles to England. Although the artist Cooper was not present on this occasion, he subsequently witnessed similar events, and would have been able to reconstruct the scene.
keywords: Engineering

en.name: *Flight of the besieged and retreat of the Swiss who drown in great numbers in the Ticino*
description:
The famous series of seven Flemish tapestries depicting the Battle of Pavia, which are displayed in a large room in the Museum of Capodimonte, entered the public collections as part of the 1862 bequest of Alfonso d’Avalos, who donated his family’s collection to the National Museum of Naples.  
Produced to be given to Emperor Charles V by the Estates-General of Brussels, on the occasion of the latter’s meeting in Brussels in 1531, the decorative series of tapestries was designed to celebrate the victory of the imperial troops over those of the French, under the command of Francis I. This victory, which occurred on 24 February 1525, was fought in the environs of the Visconti Park, at the gates of Pavia.  
Woven in Brussels, the tapestries were produced using designs by Bernard van Orley (now in the Louvre in Paris) in the workshop of William Dermoyen (or Van der Moyen), identified thanks to the presence of a weaver’s mark on the border of two tapestries in the series. Furthermore, the presence of the mark has allowed the years in which the series was produced to be established: that is, after 1528, the year in which a decree required tapestry workers to “sign” their products, and by the start of 1531, given that the tapestries would be presented to the Emperor in the March of that year.  
Recently, an interpretation of the entire cycle has been proposed that aims to recreate sequentially the landscape depicted in the seven tapestries as a single, panoramic, overview (Paredes 2014). According to this perspective, the tapestry examined here should be viewed immediately after the tapestry with *The taking of Mirabello Castle*, and it precedes the last in the series, *Flight of the French army and retreat of the Duke of Alençon across the Ticino*. In particular, from the juxtaposition of the three tapestries, one can reconstruct on the left the French encampment, bordered in the foreground by the walls of the Visconti Park and by the defensive system composed of a series of gabions, which one can also distinguish in the distance. On the right, one can recreate the landscape south of Pavia, distinguished by the presence of the small island of Gravellone and by the course of the waters of the Ticino.  
Dominating the tapestry is the depiction of the city of Pavia, bordered by walls, with the Visconti Castle on the left and the Covered Bridge on the right. This is the final phase of the battle: troops commanded by Antonio de Leyva burst out of the city besieged by the imperial troops and attack the French army from behind. In the centre, soldiers and civilians come out of their shelters, trying to flee, while several men, pushed towards the Ticino by the imperial cavalry, drown in the river. In the centre of the tapestry, one of the cavaliers of François de Laval, Count of Montfort, can be identified thanks to the writing embroidered on his horse’s harness.
artist: William Dermoyen atelier on a cartoon designed by Bernard van Orley
materials: Wool, silk and cotton; gold and silver thread
partner: MIC | Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte

it.name: *Sortita degli assediati e rotta degli Svizzeri che annegano in gran numero nel Ticino*
description:
La celebre serie dei sette arazzi fiamminghi della Battaglia di Pavia, esposti in una grande sala del museo di Capodimonte, entra nelle raccolte pubbliche con il legato testamentario del 1862 di Alfonso d’Avalos che dona al Museo Nazionale di Napoli la collezione di famiglia.  
Realizzata per essere donata dagli stati Generali di Bruxelles all’imperatore Carlo V, in occasione della riunione degli stessi a Bruxelles nel 1531, la serie decorativa intendeva celebrare la vittoria delle truppe imperiali su quelle francesi, comandate da Francesco I, avvenuta il 24 febbraio del 1525, e combattuta nella zona del Parco Visconteo, alle porte di Pavia.  
Tessuti a Bruxelles, gli arazzi sono stati realizzati su disegni di Bernart van Orley (oggi a Parigi, Musée du Louvre), nell'atelier di Willem Dermoyen ( o Van der Moyen), identificato grazie alla presenza del marchio del tessitore sulla bordure di due arazzi della serie. Inoltre, proprio la presenza del marchio ha permesso di stabilire gli anni di realizzazione del ciclo: cioè dopo il 1528, anno in cui un editto imponeva agli arazzieri di firmare i loro prodotti, e l'inizio del 1531, dato che verrà donato nel mese di marzo all'imperatore.  
Recentemente è stata proposta una lettura d’insieme del ciclo, tesa a ricostruire in sequenza il paesaggio rappresentato nei sette arazzi in un’unica, e panoramica, visione d’insieme (Paredes 2014). Secondo questa prospettiva, l'arazzo in esame va letto subito dopo il panno con la *Presa del Castello di Mirabello*, e precede l'ultimo della serie, *Fuga dell'esercito francese e ritirata del duca d'A'Alençon oltre il Ticino*. In particolare, dall'accostamento dei tre arazzi, si ricompone a sinistra l'accampamento francese, delimitato in primo piano dalle mura del Parco Visconteo e dal sistema difensivo costituito da una serie di gabbioni, che si intravedono anche in lontananza. Sulla destra, si ridisegna il paesaggio a sud di Pavia, caratterizzato dalla presenza dell'isolotto del Gravellone e dal corso delle acque del Ticino.  
Domina l’arazzo la rappresentazione della città di Pavia, cinta di mura, con il Castello Visconteo, sulla sinistra, e il Ponte Coperto, sulla destra. È la fase finale della battaglia: dalla città assediata dagli imperiali, irrompono le truppe comandate da Antonio de Leyva che attaccano, alle spalle, l’esercito francese. Al centro, soldati e civili escono dai ricoveri tentando la fuga, mentre parecchi uomini, spinti verso il Ticino dalla cavalleria imperiale, annegano nel fiume. Al centro dell'arazzo, è possibile identificare uno dei cavalieri con François del Laval, conte di Montfort , grazie alla scritta ricamata sui finimenti del cavallo.
holder: Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte
artist: Atelier di William Dermoyen su disegni di Bernard van Orley
materials: Lana, seta, cotone colorato con fili d'oro e d'argento
tags: Lana, seta, cotone colorato con fili d'oro e d'argento

en.name: Merinid Madrasa
description:
This educational institute, which specialised in the teaching of theology, philosophy and linguistics, was founded around 733/1333 by Abu al-Hassan, the famous “Black Sultan” whose tomb can be found in the *necropolis* of Chellah. The *madrasa* remained active for nearly six centuries due mainly to *habus* endowments left behind by its founder. Placed facing the Great Mosque which dates from the Almohad period, it highlights the differences between the two dynasties: powerful Almohad sobriety versus delicate Merinid finesse. In fact, inscriptions engraved in stone bear witness to this wish for studied refinement: *“The wonders of this madrasa perturbs the faculty of reason and captivates both ascetics and the pious alike”*, affirms one inscription, whilst another states: *“I am constructed like a tiered palace and sparkle like the rows of pearls on the neck of one that is engaged to be married”*.  
The elegant entrance gate is distinct for its pointed horseshoe arch which fits into a rectangular frame, displaying, within its upper half, a text written in *kufic* script, and surmounted by a very beautiful sculpted cedar canopy protected by varnished green tiles. One then enters the *madrasa* via an elaborately decorated hallway, which leads onto a rectangular courtyard, bordered by galleries supported by columns surfaced in *zellij* and decorated with stucco in the shape of honeycomb. The decor, which is specifically Merinid in style, leaves nothing untouched, time and time again making use of *zellij* ornamentation (black and green), chiselled plaster and carved wood. The prayer hall, small in scale like the rest of the building, possesses a finely decorated *mihrab* niche.  
Via the staircase in the hallway, one can reach the student accomodation and then the terrace, from where one can enjoy a gripping view of Salé, Rabat and the Bu Regreg estuary.

es.name: Medersa Meriní
description:
Este centro de enseñanza, especializado en teología, filosofía y lingüística, fue fundado hacia el año 733/1333 por Abu al-Hassan, el famoso “Sultán Negro” cuya tumba se encuentra en la necrópolis del Chellah. La *medersa* continuó su actividad durante casi seis siglos gracias, en especial, a los hábices legados por su fundador. Situada frente a la Mezquita Mayor, que data de la época almohade, en ella destaca el contraste de estilos entre ambas dinastías: la poderosa sobriedad almohade frente a la delicadeza y finura meriní. También las inscripciones grabadas en la piedra testimonian la voluntad de refinamiento estético: “Las maravillas de esta *medersa* turban la razón y cautivan a los ascetas y a los piadosos”, afirma una de ellas, en tanto que otra dice: “Mi construcción es la de un palacio escalonado y resplandeciente como las sartas de perlas del collar de una novia”.  
La elegante puerta de entrada se distingue por el arco de herradura apuntado, inscrito en un arrabá rectangular que lleva en su mitad superior un texto en escritura cúfica y está coronado por un bello tejadillo de cedro tallado, cubierto con tejas verdes barnizadas. Se accede a un vestíbulo, ricamente decorado, que desemboca en un patio rectangular, rodeado de galerías sostenidas por columnas revestidas de *zelish* y decoradas con labores de estuco en forma de paneles de miel. La ornamentación, específicamente meriní, cubre totalmente el conjunto, utilizando alternativamente *zelish* (negro y verde), estuco y madera tallada. En la sala de oración, de pequeñas dimensiones como el resto del edificio, hay un nicho o *mihrab* con una exquisita decoración.  
Por la escalera del vestíbulo se llega a las habitaciones de los estudiantes y a la terraza, desde donde se puede disfrutar de una vista sorprendente de Salé, Rabat y el estuario del Bu Regreg.

fr.name: Médersa mérinide
description:
Cet institut d’enseignement, qui s’était spécialisé dans la théologie, la philosophie et la linguistique a été fondé vers 733/1333 par Abou al-Hassan, le fameux “Sultan Noir” dont le tombeau se trouve dans la nécropole du Chellah. La médersa est restée en activité près de six siècles grâce en particulier aux biens *habous* légués par son fondateur. Située face à la Grande Mosquée datant de l’époque almohade, elle fait ressortir le contraste des styles des deux dynasties: puissante sobriété almohade, délicate finesse mérinide. D’ailleurs, les inscriptions gravées dans la pierre témoignent de cette volonté de recherche esthétique: “*Les merveilles de cette médersa troublent la raison et captivent les ascètes et les pieux*” affirme l’une, tandis que l’autre souligne: “*Ma construction est celle d’un palais étagé et étincelle comme les rangées de perles du collier d’une fiancée*”.  
L’élégante porte d’entrée se distingue par son arc brisé outrepassé qui s’inscrit dans un encadrement rectangulaire, portant dans sa moitié supérieure un texte en écriture coufique et surmonté d’un très bel auvent de cèdre sculpté, protégé de tuiles vertes vernissées. L’accès se fait par un vestibule richement décoré et débouchant sur une cour rectangulaire bordée de galeries, soutenues par des colonnes revêtues de *zellige* et décorées de stucs en forme de rayons de miel. Le décor, spécifiquement mérinide, est entièrement couvrant et utilise tour à tour le *zellige* (noir et vert), le plâtre ciselé et le bois sculpté. La salle de prière, de petite dimension, comme l’ensemble de l’édifice, possède une niche, *mihrab*, finement décorée.  
Par l’escalier du vestibule, on peut accéder aux chambres d’étudiants puis à la terrasse d’où l’on peut jouir d’une vue saisissante sur Salé, Rabat et l’estuaire du Bou Regreg.

ar.name: حامل مصحف نحاسي مُطعم بالفضة
description: يُعد هذا الحامل نموذجًا للأعمال الداعية للدين خلال عصر المماليك، وقد ابتكر خلال فترة اشتهرت بتشجيع إعادة التقييم الوطني للتراث المحلي. ويشبه حامل مصحف شهير ينتمي لعصر المماليك موجود في متحف الفن العربي بالقاهرة، منقوش عليه اسم سلطان المماليك الناصر محمد بن قلاوون (حكم في الفترة ما بين 1294 و1340) صُنع على يد محمد بن سنقر البغدادي.
dates: أواخر القرن الثالث عشر الهجري/ أواخر القرن التاسع عشر الميلادي

en.name: Silver-inlaid brass Qur’an stand
description: This stand is an example of Mamluk revivalist work, made during an age that encouraged the nationalistic reappraisal of indigenous heritage. It copies a famous Mamluk Qur’an stand in the Museum of Arab Art in Cairo, inscribed with the name of the Mamluk Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (r. AD 1294-1340) and made by Muhammad ibn Sunqur al-Baghdadi.
dates: Hegira late 13th century / AD late 19th century
keywords: Qur'an stand; Neo Mamluk; Mamluk Revival; silver; metalwork; inlay; furnishing; revivalism

en.name: Convent of Nossa Senhora de Espinheiro
names: Convent of Nossa Senhora do Espinheiro
description:
This Monastery, probably founded by Bishop D.Vasco Perdigão in 1458, was an important religious centre in the second half of the 15th century, and throughout the 16th century.  
Work was undertaken on the building in Manueline times and the living area, organised around a vaulted cloister, is of particular interest with its marked regional characteristics, similar to those of the *Convento de São Bento de Cástris* and the *Convento dos Lóios*.The building is smaller, but contains some interesting decorative elements, most notably the bosses on the vaulting ribs.  
The utilitarian parts of the building are also vaulted, with brick and *arris vaulting*, a characteristic feature of the Alentejo. This is the case with the large *adega*, or wine cellar, c.1525.The cistern was built a little later, with more traditional roofing on strong pillars supporting simple ribs.  
Set apart from the Monastery buildings is the Funerary Chapel of Garcia de Resende, one of the leading figures in Portuguese Humanism, who lived and died here.The contract to build the funerary chapel was signed in 1521, so that work on the small church with an open atrium, single vaulted nave and vernacular portal, must have been carried out immediately afterwards.  
The floor is covered with *cuerda seca Mudejar*  
tiles made in Seville and also a 16th-century Renaissance memorial stone that was certainly sculpted by Nicolas Chanterène.

en.name: Djama‘a al-Kebir (Great Mosque)
description:
The Great Mosque (Djamaa al-Kabir) rises over the sea, towering 12 metres above the shore. Its site appears to have been that of an ancient Christian basilica in Icosium on which a first mosque, dating from 408 / 1018, would have stood before being enlarged and renovated in 491 / 1097.  
The date carved on the *minbar*, or pulpit, 490 (AD 1097), permits attribution of the building’s construction to the reign of Almoravidus Yusuf ibn Tachfin. It is therefore the oldest building in the city.  
Like the other Almoravid mosques, it is wider than deep: 46 metres by 22 metres, a reversal of the typical proportions of the Almoravids’ religious monuments.  
The building is organised around a rectangular courtyard, enclosed by galleries, that provides access to the prayer room. This room consists of eleven naves and five bays. The naves are perpendicular to the *mihrab*, another plan variation in mosques typical of Almoravid architects, which followed the general orientation plan of the Great Mosque of Córdoba, as opposed to that of Damascus, whose naves are parallel to the *mihrab*.  
The Great Mosque of Algiers is built on rectangular pillars alternating with T-shaped or cruciform pillars. These pillars are simply whitewashed, without decoration, except for the elegant serpent motif that create a transition between the top of the rectangular pillar and the curved line of the arch. There are eighty of these in total.  
Most of the arches are broken, but the Almoravids introduced to the Maghreb the lobed arch that the Andalusians widely used in the Great Mosque of Córdoba, and which they favoured in their Maghreb mosques. In Algiers, variants with seven, nine, eleven, thirteen and up to twenty-five lobed arches introduce a veritable chain of arches that alternate with the pointed arches of the naves, giving a visitor an impression of balance and harmony.  
Above the arches, and representing a distinctly Maghreb feature, eleven naves are covered on the exterior by roofs of roman tiles that on the inside form triangular frames known as *fermettes* (little farmhouses). These frames attest to the Almoravids’ preference for wood, which was used also in religious furniture, including pulpits. We have a magnificent example – the oldest and most finely crafted of the country – that came from this mosque, according to the inscription on the arch of its entrance door that dates the entire building. This is the *minbar* of the Great Mosque of Algiers exhibited at the National Museum of Antiquities.  
Unfortunately, the mosque has not preserved the setting of its *mihrab*, except for two spiral columns of the 12th / 18th century that flank it on both sides, and a few plaster reliefs that decorate its pointed arch. The original *mihrab* was destroyed during the bombing of 1092 / 1682.  
We have no record of any minaret built at the time of Youssef ibn Tachfin or his successors. The one which rises at the northwest corner was built later; it was added, according to an inscription on its base, in 732 / 1234. Did the Almoravids consider a minaret to be a *bid’a* (heresy) with reference to the Mosque of the Prophet in Medina, which did not include one?  
The north facade of the mosque is preceded by a columned portico and multi-lobed arches from the Al-Sayyida Mosque (Mosque of the Lady), destroyed at the beginning of the colonial period due to a new street plan. Towards the sea, the east facade is unchanged, unspoiled – at once simple and detailed.

fr.name: Djamaa al-Kabir (Grande Mosquée)
description:
La Grande Mosquée (Djamaa al-Kabir) s’élève au-dessus de la mer, surplombant le rivage de 12 mètres. Son site semble avoir été celui d’une ancienne basilique chrétienne d’Icosium sur lequel une première mosquée datant de 408/1018 aurait préexisté avant d’être agrandie et remaniée en 491/1097.  
La date sculptée sur le *minbar*, 490 (1097 ap. J.-C.), permet d’attribuer la construction de l’édifice au règne de l’Almoravide Youssef ibn Tachfin. Elle est donc la plus ancienne de la ville.  
Comme les autres mosquées almoravides, elle est plus large que profonde : 46 mètres sur 22, une inversion des proportions propre aux monuments religieux des Almoravides.  
L’édifice s’organise autour d’une cour rectangulaire entourée de galeries sur les côtés et qui livre accès à la salle de prières. Celle-ci est formée de 11 nefs et 5 travées. Les nefs sont perpendiculaires au *mihrab*, autre changement dans l’axe de la mosquée caractéristique des architectes almoravides, qui reprenaient le plan général d’orientation de la Grande Mosquée de Cordoue par opposition à celle de Damas, dont les nefs sont parallèles au *mihrab*.  
La Grande Mosquée d’Alger est construite sur piliers rectangulaires alternant avec des piliers en T ou cruciformes. Ces piliers sont simplement chaulés, ne présentant aucun décor, si ce n’est l’élégant motif serpentiforme qui assure la transition entre le sommet du pilier rectangulaire et la ligne courbe de l’arc. On en compte quatre-vingts au total.  
La plupart des arcs sont brisés, mais les Almoravides ont introduit au Maghreb l’arc lobé que les Andalous ont largement utilisé à la Grande Mosquée de Cordoue et auquel ils font une place de choix dans leurs mosquées maghrébines. À Alger, des variantes à sept, neuf, onze, treize et jusqu’à vingt-cinq lobes introduisent dans leurs édifices une véritable hiérarchie des arcs, qui, alternant avec les arcs brisés des nefs, donnent au visiteur un effet d’équilibre et d’harmonie.  
Au-dessus des arcs et représentant une spécificité maghrébine, les onze nefs sont surplombées à l’extérieur par des toits en tuiles “romaines” qui, à l’intérieur, forment des charpentes triangulaires, à double pente, dites en “fermettes”. Ces charpentes en bois attestent la prédilection des Almoravides pour ce matériau également utilisé dans le mobilier religieux, *minbar*s ou chaires à prêcher. Nous en avons un magnifique exemplaire, le plus ancien et le plus finement ciselé du pays, provenant de cette mosquée et qui, par l’inscription qui se déroule sur l’arceau de sa porte d’entrée date tout l’édifice. Il s’agit du *minbar* de la Grande Mosquée d’Alger exposé au Musée national des antiquités.  
La mosquée n’a malheureusement pas conservé le décor de son *mihrab*, à part les deux colonnettes en spirale du XIIe/XVIIIe siècle qui le flanquent de part et d’autre, et les quelques stucs en relief qui soulignent son arc en ogive. Le *mihrab* d’origine a été détruit lors du bombardement de 1092/1682.  
Nous n’avons trace d’aucun minaret construit à l’époque de Youssef ibn Tachfin ou de ses successeurs. Celui qui s’élève à l’angle nord-ouest est de construction plus tardive ; il a été ajouté, selon une inscription à sa base, en 732/1234. Les Almoravides considéraient-ils la présence d’un minaret comme étant une *bid’a* (hérésie) en référence à la mosquée du Prophète à Médine, qui n’en comportait pas ?  
La façade nord de la mosquée est précédée d’un portique à colonnes et à arcs polylobés provenant de la mosquée al-Sayyida (mosquée de la Dame), détruite au début de la période coloniale en raison d’un nouvel alignement des rues. Vers la mer, la façade orientale est inchangée, intouchée, à la fois simple et précise.

en.name: *Boy with a Basket of Fruit*
description:
The canvas is one of the first works Merisi undertook in Rome, having joined the workshops of Giuseppe Cesari, known as the Cavalièr d'Arpino, shortly after his arrival in the city in 1592. He stayed there for several months, exercising his abilities as a painter of still-life. In this painting, the artist represents different qualities of fruit, some of which are very ripe, with extreme realism. The extraordinary realism of the boy showing us the basket, illuminated by a source of light behind his back, can be attributed to the young painter's Lombard influence, his sensitivity so similar to that of the Flemish school.  
The Borghese painting should be compared to the famous *Basket* from the same period in the Pinacoteca Ambrosiana in Milan, belonging to Cardinal Federico Borromeo and executed in Rome on recovered canvas in the mid-1590s. At the time, Caravaggio, unknown and in financial straits, used second-hand canvases to save money.  
This work was one of the pieces that Scipione Borghese had confiscated from the Cavalièr d'Arpino in 1607. The famous painter personally owned a valuable collection of paintings, which ended up in the hands of the greedy cardinal. They became the core of the splendid Borghese Collection.  
The technical ability that Caravaggio shows in the work exemplifies the artist's idea that the same method is required to paint people and objects.  
The subject has been interpreted in different ways. Fruit is used as an allegory for abundance, but on account of its natural tendency to perish, is also a metaphor for the transience of life.

This painting dates from the first Caravaggio period in Rome. The canvas is painted with a strong realism that gives the still-life the same importance as the figure. The Lombard, Venetian, and Flemish influences do not prevent the painting from representing a new artistic expression.
keywords: Realism; Flemish influence; Venetian influence; Lombard influence; allegory; still life

it.name: Giovane con canestra di frutta
description:
La tela è fra le prime opere eseguite a Roma da Merisi, entrato nella bottega di Giuseppe Cesari, detto il Cavalier d'Arpino, poco dopo il suo arrivo in città (1592). Qui egli  rimase per qualche mese, esercitando le sue qualità di pittore di 'nature morte'. Nel dipinto, con estremo realismo, l'artista raffigura infatti diverse qualità di frutta, alcune delle quali già molto mature. Lo straordinario naturalismo del fanciullo in atto di mostrare la canestra, rischiarato da una fonte di luce proveniente dalle spalle, è da ricercare nella componente lombarda del giovane pittore dalla forte sensibilità molto vicina a quella dei fiamminghi.  
Il dipinto Borghese va posto a confronto con la famosa *Canestra* della Pinacoteca Ambrosiana di Milano, appartenente al cardinale Federico Borromeo ed eseguita a Roma su tela di recupero alla metà degli anni '90, periodo al quale va riferita anche l'opera in esame. All'epoca Caravaggio, non ancora conosciuto e in ristrettezza economiche, si serviva infatti di tele già utilizzate, per risparmiare sul supporto.  
L'opera fa parte dei quadri che Scipione Borghese fece sequestrare nel 1607 al Cavalier d'Arpino. Il celebre pittore possedeva infatti una preziosa raccolta di dipinti, che finirono così nelle mani del rapace cardinale, andando a costituire il nucleo iniziale della splendida collezione Borghese. L'abilità tecnica che Caravaggio dimostra nell'opera esprime perfettamente il pensiero dell'artista circa l'analogo impegno necessario nel dipingere figure e oggetti.  
Diverse sono state le interpretazioni del soggetto, legato per la raffigurazione della frutta all'allegoria dell'abbondanza, ma anche, per la sua naturale deperibilità, alla metafora della caducità della vita.

Il dipinto è databile al primo periodo di Caravaggio a Roma. La tela è dipinta con un forte realismo che rende alla natura morta la stessa importanza attribuita alle figure. Le influenze lombarde, veneziane e fiamminghe non impediscono al dipinto di rappresentare una nuova espressione artistica.
keywords: Realismo; influenza fiamminga; influenza veneziana; influenza lombarda; allegoria; natura morta

ar.name: تاج عمود.
description:
يعتبر هذا التاج أحد النماذج المختلفة التي ابتكرها فنانو الدولة المرينية. وخلافاً للطراز الكلاسيكي، من ناحية المقاييس والزخرفة، حيث يكون الفارق جد بارز بين قاعدة التاج - الجزء السفلي الأسطواني - وبين الطبلية - الجزء العلوي المتوازي السطوح للتاج-، فإن تجاوز طبلية هذا التاج عن قاعدته لم يكن ظاهراً كثيراً والزخرفة ليست متقطعة.  
يستند التاج على كعب أسطواني على شكل حزام. وحفرت قاعدته على شكل زخرفة متعرجة لأقنتة ملساء معقوفة في القمة، وتم حشو الشقوق العمودية الوسطى والمسافات المتواجدة بين الزخرفة المتعرجة بتركيب حرشفي ذو تدرجات. تعلو هذه الزخرفة المتعرجة زخرفةٌ نباتيةٌ يفيض تنفيذها رهافة آسرة، تؤمِّن الربط بين كتلتي التاج، إذ يبرز، من بين سعفتي نخيل ثنائيتين تنتهيان بزوائد متصبعة من الأقنتيات البارزة في قمة الفواصل، فصان يلتفان بشكل حلزوني، ليعاودا الالتقاء في مركز التاج، ويشكلا ما يشبه قوقعتي حلزون متلاصقتين. ويتواجد في الأعلى إفريز مسطح منحوت بشكل بارز، يحمل نقيشة كتابية دينية بأحرف نسخية، تستنسخ جزءا من الآية القرآنية الكريمة "64" من سورة يوسف "12": "فالله خير حفظا وهو أرحم الراحمين". ومن كل جهة من جهات الافريز، تشغل زاوية الطبلية سعيفتان نخيليتان متناظرتان لهما زوائد متصبعة من الأقنتيات محيطة كليا بحلية على شكل حبة صنوبر مقوسة. ويزين المحور العلوي للتاج مسند مستطيل بارز ومزين بزخرفة نباتية.  
تميز هذه الزخرفة الزاخرة بالتدرجات وبالحيوية تيجان عواميد المساجد والمدارس خلال الفترة المرينية.

إنه أحد أنواع التيجان ذات الزخرفة النباتية الوافرة، والتنفيذ الدقيق الكبير الذي أبدعه الفنانون المرينيون من أجل المساجد والمدارس. يحمل هذا التاج على جزئه العلوي شريطا مسطحا نُقشت فوقه نقشاً بارزاً نقيشةٌ كتابيةٌ دينية بأحرف نسخية.
keywords: مبنى ديني؛ زخرفة نباتية؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ زخرفة كتابية؛ خط نسخي؛ زاوية؛ موقع شالة؛ تاج؛ رخام أبيض منحوت.

en.name: Capital.
description:
This marble capital is one of the different models created by artists from the Marinid dynasty. Unlike the classical type, where there is a marked difference between the bell (lower cylindrical part) and the abacus (upper parallelepipedic part) both in terms of proportions and ornamentation, here the abacus does not overhang the bell too noticeably, and the ornamentation is continuous.  
Placed above an astragal with a cable-moulded torus, the bell is represented by a smooth curved acanthus meander on the top. Overlapping scales rising above a step motif fill the central vertical slots and the gaps in the meander. The space above the meander is filled with very finely executed plant decoration that links the two volumes of the capital: two double palms with acanthus leaves tumbling from above the gaps bear coiled lobes that join at the centre of the capital to form two adjacent snail shells. Above this there is a flat strip bearing a pious inscription, sculpted in relief, in cursive characters taken from the end of verse 64 of Sura 12 of the Qur'an, 'Joseph': 'Allah is the best protector and is the most Merciful of the Merciful'. On either side of the band, two symmetrical palms with acanthus leaves fill the corners of the abacus and surround a curved pinecone. A projecting rectangular bracket decorated with a floral motif stands at the top of the capital.  
This subtle and vigorous decoration characterises the capitals of Marinid mosques and *madrasas*.

This is one of the types of finely executed capital with abundant plant decoration created by Marinid artists for mosques and *madrasas*. It has a flat band on the upper part with a pious cursive inscription sculpted in relief.
keywords: religious building; vegetal decoration; geometric decoration; epigraphic decoration

es.name: Capitel.
description:
Este capitel de mármol pertenece a uno de los diversos modelos creados por los artistas meriníes. El derrame del ábaco sobre el tambor no es muy pronunciado y la decoración es uniforme, contrariamente al patrón clásico, de acusada diferencia, en tamaño y decoración, entre el tambor (parte inferior cilíndrica) y el ábaco (parte superior prismática).  
El tambor, decorado con un meandro de acanto curvado en el vértice, descansa sobre un astrágalo decorado con un cordón. Las imbricaciones de escamas, dispuestas sobre un motivo escalonado, rellenan las ranuras verticales medianas y los intervalos del meandro.  
En lo alto del meandro, una profusa decoración vegetal de exquisita ejecución enlaza los dos componentes del capitel: dos lóbulos enroscados en espiral hasta el centro del capitel, a modo de caracolas unidas (o roleos), surgen de las dos palmas dobles con hojas digitadas de acanto que brotan del vértice de los intervalos.  
Por encima, un friso plano contiene una inscripción piadosa, con caracteres cursivos esculpidos en relieve, extraída del final de la aleya 64 de la sura XII, “Jusef”: “Allah es el mejor Protector y el más Misericordioso entre los Misericordiosos.” Dos palmas asimétricas con hojas digitadas de acanto flanquean el friso, invaden los ángulos del ábaco y contienen, en su interior, una piña de pino arqueada. Decorada con un motivo floral, una moldura rectangular en relieve adorna el eje superior del capitel.  
Esta decoración, repleta de matices y de vitalidad, caracteriza los capiteles de las mezquitas y madrasas meriníes.

Modelos de capitel con profusa decoración vegetal y primorosa ejecución, obra de artistas meriníes para las mezquitas y madrasas. Su parte superior luce una cenefa sobre la que está esculpida en relieve una inscripción piadosa en caracteres cursivos.

fr.name: Chapiteau.
description:
Ce chapiteau en marbre est un des différents modèles créés par les artistes de la dynastie mérinide. Contrairement au type classique où, tant dans les proportions que dans l'ornementation, la différence est très accusée entre la corbeille (partie inférieure cylindrique) et le tailloir (partie supérieure parallélépipédique), ici le débordement du tailloir sur la corbeille n'est pas trop sensible, et l'ornementation n'est pas discontinue.  
  
Posée au-dessus d'un astragale à tore strié en cordelière, la corbeille est représentée par un méandre d'acanthe lisse incurvé au sommet. Des imbrications d'écailles s'élevant au-dessus d'un motif à gradins remplissent les fentes verticales médianes et les intervalles du méandre. Au-dessus du méandre règne un décor végétal foisonnant d'une grande finesse d'exécution qui assure la liaison entre les deux volumes du chapiteau : de deux doubles palmes à digitations d'acanthes jaillissant du sommet des intervalles se détachent deux lobes qui s'enroulent en spirale pour se rejoindre au centre du chapiteau et former comme deux coquilles d'escargot accolées. Au-dessus, un bandeau plat porte, sculptée en relief, une inscription pieuse en caractères cursifs tirée de la fin du verset coranique 64 de la sourate XII, “Josef” : “Allah est le meilleur protecteur et il est le plus Miséricordieux des Miséricordieux.”De chaque côté du bandeau, deux palmes asymétriques à digitations d'acanthes occupent les angles du tailloir tout en cernant une pomme de pin arquée. Un tasseau rectangulaire en saillie décoré d'un motif floral meuble l'axe supérieur du chapiteau.  
  
Ce décor plein de nuances et de vigueur caractérise les chapiteaux de mosquées et de *madrasa* mérinides.

C'est un des modèles de chapiteaux au décor végétal foisonnant et d'une grande finesse d'exécution que les artistes mérinides créèrent pour les mosquées et les *madrasa*. Il porte sur sa partie supérieure un bandeau plat sur lequel est sculpté en relief une inscription pieuse en caractères cursifs.
keywords: édifice religieux ; décoration végétale ; décoration géométrique ; décoration épigraphique

en.name: Bab al-Bhar
description:
Up until the 13th/19th century, the waters of the lake of Tunis reached the town’s street level: hence the name given to this gate, Bab al-Bhar or Gate of the Sea, known of since the Hafsid era. In 1263/1848, following his voyage to Paris, Ahmed Bey ordered the demolition of the Hafsid gate and the construction of today’s gate in its place. The latter was built on a different site to that occupied by the former, in order to be positioned on the axis of “avenue de la Marine”, which today is known as “avenue de France”. The defensive purpose of the gates seems to feature less in the second construction. Perhaps this was due to changes in the art and technology of war and to the consecration of the era of artillery! Ahmed Bey used this gate to symbolise his capital’s entry into the modern age.  
When the Protectorat became established, the Bab al-Bhar was rebaptised Gate of France. Today, it has changed back to its old name, but, no longer attached to the city wall that branched off from its right and left sides, it looks like a piece of decoration which, despite everything, has conserved its wooden double door portal which is plated with iron.

es.name: Bab el-Bhar
description:
Hasta el siglo XIII/XIX, las aguas del lago de Túnez, el lago el-Bahira, llegaban hasta esta parte de la ciudad, de donde viene el nombre de Bab el-Bhar o Puerta del Mar, dado a esta puerta, conocida ya desde época hafsí. En 1263/1848, Ahmed Bey, después de un viaje a París, ordenó la demolición de la puerta hafsí y la construcción de la actual. Esta fue desplazada respecto a la que la precedía, para ser situada en el eje de la avenida de la Marina, actual avenida de Francia. El papel defensivo de las puertas parece haber sido relegado a un segundo plano, a causa, quizá, de los cambios en las técnicas de guerra con la llegada de la era de la artillería. Ahmed Bey entendía esta puerta como un símbolo de modernidad para su capital.  
Con la instauración del Protectorado, la Bab el-Bhar fue bautizada con el nombre de Puerta de Francia, aunque hoy en día ha vuelto a recobrar su antiguo nombre. Actualmente está separada de la muralla que la prolongaba a derecha e izquierda, de forma que se presenta como un elemento decorativo que, a pesar de todo, ha conservado su portal con dos hojas de madera reforzadas con herrería.

fr.name: Bab el-Bhar
description:
Jusqu’au XIIIe/XIXe siècle, les eaux du lac de Tunis, *el-Behira*, arrivaient à ce niveau de la ville, d’où le nom de Bab el-Bhar ou Porte de la Mer donné à cette porte, qui est connue depuis l’époque hafside. En 1263/1848, Ahmed Bey, après un voyage à Paris, ordonna la démolition de la porte hafside et la construction de la porte actuelle. Celle-ci fut décalée par rapport à celle qui la précédait, pour être placée dans l’axe de l’avenue de la Marine, actuelle avenue de France. Le rôle défensif des portes semble avoir été relégué au second plan. Peut-être était-ce à cause du changement des techniques de la guerre et de la consécration de l’ère de l’artillerie ! Ahmed Bey fit de cette porte le symbole de la modernité de sa capitale.  
A l’instauration du Protectorat, le Bab el- Bhar fut baptisé porte de France. Aujourd’hui, elle a retrouvé son ancien nom, mais, dissociée de la muraille qui la prolongeait à droite et à gauche, elle se présente comme un élément de décor qui a gardé, malgré tout, son portail à deux battants en bois, bardé de fer.

en.name: *Angel with Trumpet*
description:
Joseph Leonard Weber was a burgher of Buda from 1757. Probably born in Silesia into the Weber dynasty of sculptors in Svidnica, members of his family moved to Brno and Nagyszombat (Trnava). The Weber name can be found in the register of births in Buda from 1753 since all seven of the Weber children were baptised there.  
Weber's sculptural activity is documented from 1757 and includes the stone sculptures of *Faith*, *Hope* and *Charity* above the portal of St. Anne's church, dating from 1765, and the statue *St. Florian* on the facade of St. Florian Chapel, as well as the figures that decorate the organ and those on the high and side altars of the chapel (1761–1766).  
Almost the entire interior decoration of St. Florian Chapel, Buda is by Weber, made between the 1760s and 1770s. On 20 June 1761, Weber was paid 86 forints for the sculptural decoration of the chapel's organ.  
In the 1920s the chapel was rebuilt twice and the interior furnishing was dispersed. The sculptural ensemble of the organ, the white painted figures of King David playing the harp, two angels with trumpets, one with drums and several *putti*, came to the Municipal Museum of Budapest (today Budapest History Museum).  
The angel has an adolescent body and curly hair. He is playing a trumpet and has a puffed-out face; he stands *contrapposto*, with exact anatomy. His clothing consists of a light drapery fixed with a ribbon at his left shoulder. The abstract decorative shaping of the drapery was a Rococo stylistic feature of southern German origin. By around 1760, this feature was already a widespread motif used by the sculptors of Pest and Buda, and carried over to Hungary via the art of Károly Bebo, Lipót Antal Conti, Antal Eberhard and József Hebenstreit. It is still evident even during the Neo-Classical era.

Weber’s ascendants were sculptors in Silesia, who moved from Svidnica to Brno and Nagyszombat (Trnava). It was while a citizen of Buda in 1761 that Weber worked on the sculptural decoration of the St. Florian Chapel. The Rococo music-making angels once decorated the organ.
keywords: Neo-Classicism; Joseph Leonard Weber; Károly Bebo; Lipót Antal Conti; Antal Eberhard; József Hebenstreit; St. Florian; St. Anne; King David; Buda; Pest; wood carving; gilding; music; religious object
materials: Limewood, carved, painted, gilded and silvered
tags: Limewood, carved, painted, gilded and silvered

en.name: Panel
description:
Casper Lehmann is the earliest glass engraver about who anything is known. Born in the 1560s, he was trained in Munich, where there was a tradition of engraving hardstones, and glass was being engraved by the 1580s. By 1588 he was associated with the court of Emperor Rudolph II in Prague and in 1608 was styled 'Imperial Gem Engraver and Glass Engraver'. Lehmann's work is usually found on flat panels such as this one, and often contains symbolic allusions to contemporary political events.  
  
This panel's imagery remains obscure. The date - 1619 - is surmounted by the electoral hat of Saxony, and the intertwined numbers '3' an '8' reference the third and eighth letters of the alphabet 'C' and 'H' for Christian II of Saxony and Princess Hedwig of Denmark.

en.name: Passengers and onlookers waiting for the métropolitain at the Place de Bastille
names: Taken from *Vie et Métiers à Paris*
short_description: Eugène Atget (1857–1927) began developing an interest in photography in 1888. He created his photos in series, and sold them to institutions. It was thus, that around 1898, he came to photograph the old neighbourhoods of Paris destined to demolition, and sold these photographs to the new Commission du Vieux Paris. As he photographed roads dug up by the urban excavations, he also captured onlookers fascinated by this new mode of transport. The Bastille station is pictured here, one of the overground sections of the ligne 1, which explains how these people were able to comfortably observe. The Colonne de Juillet of the Place de Bastille is visible in the background.
keywords: Cities; métropolitain; Paris

fr.name: Voyageurs et curieux attendant le métropolitain place de la Bastille
names: Partie de Vie et métiers à Paris
short_description: Eugène Atget (1857-1927) s’intéresse à la photographie à partir de 1888. Il conçoit ses clichés par séries qu’il vend à des institutions. Ainsi vers 1898, il photographie les quartiers anciens de Paris voués à la démolition et vend ses clichés à la toute nouvelle Commission du Vieux Paris. En photographiant les rues éventrées par le percement du métropolitain, il a également pris quelques clichés des populations fascinées par cette construction puis ce nouveau mode de locomotion. Ici, il s’agit de la station Bastille, une des parties aériennes de la ligne 1, ce qui explique que les badauds puissent commodément observer. À l’arrière-plan, on aperçoit la Colonne de Juillet, place de la Bastille.
keywords: Villes; métropolitain; Paris

en.name: *Council of the Gods*
description:
The fresco was commissioned from Lanfranco by Cardinal Scipione Borghese to decorate the vault of a large room on the first floor of Casino Pinciano, designed at the time as a loggia opening on to the residence's park. The painter came up with the idea of a trabeated system (a construction using lintels rather than arches) painted in perspective along the perimeter of the walls, supported by pairs of telamons (supports or columns sculpted in the form of a man) alternated with lunettes (crescent-shaped spaces). The lunettes are open to the horizon and contain exemplifications of the rivers of the world. The central panel is a *trompe-l'œil* of heaven, where the gods are gathered in council among the clouds. Among others, we can see Jupiter in a central position between the female figures of Juno and Venus, and moving right: Mars, recognisable by his helmet; Apollo, his head framed with light; Mercury in flight; Bacchus holding a bunch of grapes; a faun seated in the foreground, looking down towards the viewer. In the centre, beneath the father of the gods, we can see Pluto and Proserpine with the dog Cerberus; on the left: Neptune and Ceres; Time with his scythe; Pan, with the features of a satyr and, on the edge, Minerva with an olive branch. The simulation of an open space and the extraordinary imagination with which the figures, freed in space, are arranged, are clearly inspired by the works of his fellow 16th-century countryman Antonio Allegri, known as Correggio, who painted the frescos in the cupolas of Parma. The amplifications of form and the capacity to express freedom of imagination clearly show the strength of his creative innovation, which in the Villa Borghese loggia fresco, is the precise starting point of the era of great Baroque decoration.  
At the end of the 18th century, during the renovation of the residence, it was decided to close the loggia. Lanfranco's fresco was restored, beginning in 1779 and completed in 1782, by the Viterbo painter Domenico Corvi (1721–1803).

The painter Lanfranco carried out one of the first examples of Baroque painting in Rome for Cardinal Scipione, *The Council of the Gods* in the loggia of Villa Borghese. Originally an open loggia, the large room was decorated by Lanfranco employing the illusionist device of the “*quadro riportato*” from the Roman tradition. The Loggia was closed in 1779 before being restored by Domenico Corvi, a Rome-based Neo-Classical painter.
holder: Borghese Gallery, vault of the Loggia
keywords: Fresco; mythology; telamons; palatial architecture; trompe-l'oeil; quadro riportato

it.name: *Concilio degli dei*
description:
L'affresco fu commissionato a Lanfranco dal cardinale Scipione Borghese come decorazione della volta del grande ambiente collocato al primo piano del Casino Pinciano, all'epoca concepito come loggia aperta sul parco della villa. Il pittore ideò la suggestione di un sistema di trabeazione dipinta in prospettiva lungo il perimetro delle pareti, sorretto da coppie di telamoni alternate a lunette. All'interno di queste ultime, aperte verso l'orizzonte, campeggiano le personificazioni dei fiumi del globo.  Il riquadro centrale è realizzato come uno “sfondato” verso l'empireo, dove gli dei appaiono radunati in concilio fra le nubi.  Vi si possono scorgere, tra gli altri, Giove, in posizione centrale tra le figure femminili di Giunone e Venere;  proseguendo verso destra: Marte, riconoscibile dall'elmo; Apollo con il capo incorniciato di luce; Mercurio in volo; Bacco con i mano il grappolo d'uva; un fauno che, seduto in primo piano, guarda in basso verso gli spettatori. Al centro, sotto il padre dei dei, si riconoscono Plutone e Proserpina con il cane Cerbero; a sinistra: Nettuno e Cerere; il Tempo con la falce; Pan, con le fattezze di satiro e, all'estremità, Minerva con il ramo di ulivo. La simulazione di uno spazio aperto e la straordinaria fantasia nella disposizione delle figure librate nello spazio appaiono chiaramente ispirate alle opere del conterraneo artista cinquecentesco Antonio Allegri, detto il Correggio, autore degli affreschi delle cupole parmensi. Tuttavia appare in modo evidente, nell'amplificazione delle forme e nella capacità di esprimere il libero fluire dell'immaginazione, la forza della sua innovativa creatività che, proprio nell'affresco della Loggia di Villa Borghese, dà il via alla stagione della grande decorazione barocca.  
Alla fine del sec. XVIII, durante la ristrutturazione della palazzina, venne decisa la chiusura della Loggia. L'affresco di Lanfranco fu restaurato e integrato tra il 1779 e il 1782 dal pittore viterbese Domenico Corvi (1721-1803).

Il pittore Giovanni Lanfranco realizzò per il cardinale Scipione uno dei primi esempi di pittura barocca a Roma: *Il concilio degli dei* nella loggia di Villa Borghese. Originariamente una loggia aperta, il grande salone è stato decorato da Lanfranco utilizzando l'artificio illusionistico del “quadro riportato”, di tradizione romana. La loggia fu chiusa nel 1779 e fu restaurata da Domenico Corvi, pittore rappresentativo a Roma dello stile neoclassico.
keywords: Affresco; mitologia; telamoni; architettura palatina; trompe-l'oeil; quadro riportato

en.name: Marseille: inauguration of M. Sanant's (Tunisia) exhibit - a picturesque corner of the West African pavilion
short_description: In the latter half of the 19th century, many European countries held exhibitions about their colonies, both during world fairs and smaller events. France used world fairs to "showcase" their colonies, both in the great Paris world fairs as well as smaller, colonial fairs organised in Marseille (1906, 1922) and Paris (1931). These expositions glorified colonial expansion, particularly by offering visitors an "object lesson". Tunisia took the spotlight in 1906 due to the central role it played in the ongoing dispute with Italy. The "indigenous villages", such as the one pictured in this photograph, were above all representations of the way Europeans imagined their colonies. They were later described as "human zoos" by historians of the late 20th century, due to the horrific practice of putting people for display as if they were animals.
keywords: Expositions; colonise

fr.name: *Marseille: inauguration de l'exposition par M. Sanant (Tunisie): un coin pittoresque du pavillon de l'Afrique Occidentale*
short_description: Dans la seconde moitié du XIX e siècle, des expositions sont dédiées aux colonies soit lors des expositions universelles, soit de manière spécifique, par les pays européens. La France "expose" ses colonies lors des expositions universelles organisées à Paris et lors d'expositions coloniales organisées à Marseille (1906, 1922) et à Paris (1931). L'expansion coloniale y est glorifiée et le visiteur est invité à une "leçon de choses". La Tunisie est particulièrement mise à l'honneur en 1906 en raison du conflit entre Italiens et Français à son sujet. Les villages "indigènes" , tels que celui que l'on peut voir sur cette photographie, répondent avant tout à l'imaginaire européen sur les colonies. Les historiens de la fin du XXe siècle les qualifieront de "zoos humains", les gens y étant exposés aux regards tels des animaux.
keywords: Expositions; colonies

en.name: Captured arms (with accessories) from the occupation-campaign in Bosnia-Herzegovina 1878
short_description: The 1878 Treaty of Berlin put the two Ottoman provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina under the administration of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Between the 20th of July and the 29th of October 1878, the Austro-Hungarian Empire led a military campaign in those two provinces in order to establish its administration. During this armed conflict, several objects were taken, like a 16mm flintlock pistol with an Oriental-style snaphaunce lock (miquelet lock) entirely wrought from iron and richly decorated, showing as high a quality of craftsmanship as the accompanying gunpowder pourers, ramrods and bullet pouches.
holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
keywords: Pistols; Bosnia; arms; armours; metalwork; military objects; accessories; Ottoman Balkans; Ottoman amy; war; warfare
partner: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History

en.name: Bab Boujloud
short_description: This impressive 12th-century Gate, restored in 1912, is adorned with blue and green ceramic tiling bearing the name of the location. Beyond the aperture of the gate and around it, the landscape stretches over a vast, nearly flat, and irregular area. This area, surrounded by high adobe walls pierced with several doors, holds the prestigious Mulay Idris High School. Place Boujloud is in a strategic position of great cultural importance and very much animated by its popular character. The portal, admired for its fine interlacing ornamentation of blue and green, consists of a central arch and two smaller side arches that are in very good condition.
history: Bab Boujloud was built in the 12th century and has been restored and refurbished several times since. In 1913, during the reign of Sultan Mulay al-Hafiz, the gate was redecorated in glazed ceramic, blue on the side facing the Old *Medina* and green on the other side. The gate provides a monumental entrance to the square of the same name, west of the Old *Medina* of Fez.

It originally formed part of a manuscript executed possibly in Iraq or Syria during the AH 4th century / AD 10th century. The fragment gives verse 14 from chapter 49 *Al-Hujurat* ("The Dwellings") of the Holy Qur’an.

de.name: Stuckdecke
description: Die vermutlich auch von Gigl stammende Stuckdecke setzt sich aus etwas anderen Motiven und Ornamentformen wie die Fassade zusammen. Die Randzone wird aus vielfach verschlungenen Bändern mit Akanthusblättern gebildet, in der Mitte, eingefasst von Band- und Rankenwerk, ein aus Bändern, Blättern und Muscheln zusammengesetzter Stern. Über dem Erkereingang das Wappen der Familie Fischer.

en.name: Stucco ceiling

The border area is composed of intricately intertwined bands with acanthus leaves; in the centre, framed by strap and vine scroll decoration, is a star composed of bands, leaves and shells. Above the entrance to the bay window the coat of arms of the Fischer family.

en.name: Wood panels (walls and ceiling) of Syrian Room
description: In the late 1970s, Doris Duke acquired a variety of components that were said to have come from a house owned by the Quwatlis, a prominent merchant family of Damascus. Combining historic elements with new pieces made in Hawai‘i by local craftsmen, Duke and her staff created an interior that conveys the spatial layout and multi-media, multi-sensory experience of the Syrian *qa‘a* (Arabic: hall), a reception room found in affluent courtyard homes of the late Ottoman period (in Syria: 1516–1918).

ar.name: رسم جداري من قُصَيْر عمرا.
description:
تقف امرأة بلباس قليل وعليها حليْ وجواهر كثيرة منتصبة أمام ركن. كما تتزين بأساور وتضع سلسلة حول عنقها تتدلى منها حلية معلقة دائرية. كذلك تضع على خصرها شريط زينة.  
شعر المرأة أسود ويتدلى حتى كتفيها وتضع فيه عدة سلاسل من لؤلؤ أبيض. ويمثل المشهد ركناً بين عمودين يرتكزان على قاعدة. ويظهر الركن مغطىً بقماش أزرق خلف المرأة وإلى جانبها. أما تفاصيل القسم الأسفل على الأخص فهي غير واضحة بسبب التخريب الذي أصاب الرسم.  
يعود هذا الرسم إلى الصالة الرئيسية في قُصَير عمرا. وهذا الرسم واحد من عدة رسوم جدارية في قصير عمرا تمثل صوراً مختلفة لنساء، وكانت هذه الرسوم النسائية موضوعاً مرغوباً به على الرسوم الجدارية الأموية، حيث كانت هذه الأشكال تعكس حياة الأغنياء في قصورهم ومقدار الحرية التي كانوا يتمتعون بها. وتحمل كل النساء في هذه الرسوم حُلىً وجواهر غالية الثمن، فبعضهن عاريات، والبعض الآخر يرتدي ثياباً طويلة. وكان من بين الاحتفالات التي تقام في الأوساط الملكية آنذاك مآدب يشرب فيها الخمر وتعزف الموسيقى ويقدم المهرجون والمطربات ذوات الصوت الجميل عروضاً لإمتاع الحاضرين. وقد ورد وصف لهذه الاحتفالات منذ زمن تشييد هذا القصر.

تبين قطعة اللوحة الجدارية المأخوذة من قُصيّر عمرة في الأردن، امرأة خفيفة الملبس، مُزَّينة بمجوهرات جميلة، في محراب. إنها إحدى لوحات النساء الجصية في غرفة عرس القصر وحمَّاماته التي تمثِّل ذوق العصر وحياة البلاط فيه.

de.name: Wandmalerei aus Qusayr Amra.
description: Vor einer Nische steht aufrecht eine nur leicht bekleidete, aber reich mit Juwelen geschmückte Frau. Sie trägt schmückende Armbänder und um den Hals eine Kette mit kreisförmigem Anhänger. Auch die Taille ist mit einem Schmuckband versehen. Die Frau hat eine Frisur aus dunklem Haar bis zu den Schultern. Im Haar trägt sie mehrere Ketten aus weißen Perlen. Das Ensemble scheint eine Nische darzustellen, die von zwei Säulen auf Postamenten flankiert ist. Die Nische scheint hinter und seitlich von der Frau mit einem blauen Stoff behängt zu sein. Die Details besonders der unteren Partie sind durch Graffitizerstörungen schwer zu erkennen Die Malerei stammt aus dem Hauptraum des Palastes von Qusayr Amra. Diese Frauendarstellung ist eine von mehreren Frauendarstellungen auf den Wandmalereien von Qusayr Amra. In der omaijadischen Wandmalerei waren solche Darstellungen gern gewählte Themen und gehörten zu dem Figurenrepertoire, das das reiche Leben in den Schlössern mit seinen vielen Freiheiten in dieser Zeit wiedergab. Alle dargestellten Frauen tragen kostbaren Schmuck mit Juwelen. Einige der Frauen sind unbekleidet, andere tragen lange Gewänder. Zu den Festen, die in dieser Zeit in höfischen Kreisen stattfanden, gehörten Gelage, bei den Wein getrunken, Musikvorführungen veranstaltet wurden, Gaukler auftraten und Sängerinnen mit schönen Stimmen erfreuten. Schon in den Quellen der Entstehungszeit des Schlosses wurden solche Feste beschrieben.

Dieses Teil einer Wandmalerei aus dem Umayyadenpalast von Qusayr Amra in Jordanien zeigt eine leicht bekleidete, mit einer Halskette geschmückte Frau in einer Nische. Dieses Fresko – eines von mehreren Frauenbildern, die sich im Thronzimmer und den Bädern des Palastes befinden – repräsentiert den Geschmack und das Leben bei Hofe in dieser Zeit.
dates: Regierungszeit von al-Walid I. 86-96 H. / 705-715, wahrscheinlich nach 92 H./ 711 n. Chr.
keywords: Umaijaden; Palast und Bad; Freskomalerei
materials: Freskomalerei auf Wandputz; stark zerstört und abgerieben.
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Fresco from Qusayr Amra.
description:
A woman stands upright in front of a niche, lightly clothed but richly adorned with jewels. She is wearing jewelled armbands and a necklace around her neck with a circular pendant. There is a jewelled belt around her waist. Her dark hair, decorated with strings of white pearls, falls to her shoulders. The representation seems to consist of a niche that is flanked by two pillars on pedestals. Behind and to the side of the woman the niche appears to be hung with a blue cloth. The details are hard to make out, particularly along the lower part as it has been spoiled by graffiti.  
The painting comes from the main room of the Qusayr Amra Palace. This depiction is one of several pictures of women on the frescoes in the Qusayr Amra. Such depictions represented popular themes in Umayyad wall frescoes, and formed part of the figurative repertoire representing courtly life, which was lived with great expense and freedom during that period. Each of the painted women is portrayed wearing expensive jewellery and jewels. Some of the women are unclothed; others wear long robes. During this period courtly celebrations included feasts at which wine was drunk, concerts were presented, acrobats performed and singers entertained. Such festivities already featured in the sources dating from when the castle was first founded.

This fragment of wall painting from the Umayyad palace of Qusayr Amra in Jordan shows a lightly clad woman adorned with beautiful jewellery within a niche. One of several frescoes of women in the throne room and baths of the palace, she represents the taste and courtly life of the time.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
dates: Reign of Caliph al-Walid I Hegira 86–96 / AD 705–715, probably after AH 92 / AD 711.
keywords: Umayyad; palace; bath; fresco; painting.
materials: Fresco painting on wall plaster; very damaged and peeled away.
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

es.name: Fresco de Qusayr Amra.
description:
Fresco de una mujer con vestiduras ligeras y muy enjoyada, representada delante de un nicho. Lleva brazaletes en los brazos y un collar con un colgante circular alrededor del cuello. Su cabello, de color oscuro y que le cae sobre los hombros, está adornado con hilos de perlas blancas. Detrás de la figura femenina se distingue un nicho flanqueado por dos pilares sobre pedestales y del que cuelga una tela azul, aunque resulta difícil apreciar los detalles, sobre todo en la parte inferior, tapada por grafitos.  
Esta pintura procede de la habitación principal del palacio de Qusayr Amra, y es uno de los varios frescos con representaciones femeninas. Se trata de un tema frecuente en los frescos omeyas y formaba parte del repertorio figurativo que retrataba la vida en la corte, de gran dispendio y libertad en este periodo. Las mujeres se representaban desnudas o con largos vestidos, pero siempre llevaban ricas joyas. Las celebraciones cortesanas incluían banquetes en los que se bebía vino, conciertos y actuaciones de acróbatas y cantantes. Las fuentes contemporáneas a la construcción de este palacio mencionan estas fiestas.

Fragmento de pintura mural procedente del palacio omeya de Qusayr Amra (Jordania). Representa una figura femenina vestida ligeramente y adornada con ricas joyas, dentro de un nicho. Es uno de los varios frescos con figuras femeninas de la sala del trono o los baños de palacio y representa el gusto y la vida de la corte en la época.
holder: Museo de Arte Islámico del Museo Pergamon
dates: Califato de al-Walid I, entre los años 86 y 96 de la Hégira / 705–715 d. C.; probablemente después del año 92 / 711.
keywords: omeya; palacio y baños; pintura; fresco
materials: Pintura mural al fresco sobre yeso, muy deteriorada y desprendida.
tags: Pintura mural al fresco sobre yeso, muy deteriorada y desprendida.
partner: Museo de Arte Islámico en el Museo de Pérgamo, Museos Estatales

fr.name: Peinture murale de Qousayr Amra.
description:
Une femme, légèrement vêtue mais parée de bijoux, se tient debout face à une niche, elle porte des bracelets, autour du cou un collier orné d'un pendentif circulaire, sa taille aussi est soulignée d'une riche ceinture. Ses cheveux bruns, ornés de rangs de perles blanches, lui tombent sur les épaules. On distingue une niche flanquée de deux colonnes sur piédestal, fermée d'un rideau bleu derrière la figure. Les détails, en particulier ceux de la partie inférieure, sont difficilement discernables à cause des détériorations provoquées par de nombreux graffitis.  
Cette fresque provient de la salle principale du palais de Qousayr Amra, et fait partie des nombreuses figures féminines représentées sur les murs du palais. Les fresques omeyyades privilégient souvent ce genre d'images évoquant la richesse et la liberté de la vie de cour. Toutes les figures féminines sont parées de joyaux, certaines sont nues, d'autres portent de longues robes. Au cours des fêtes données à l'époque dans les milieux de cour, on banquetait, on buvait du vin, on donnait des concerts et des spectacles d'acrobates ou de chanteuses. Les sources contemporaines de la construction du château citent déjà des festivités de ce genre.

Ce fragment de mur peint en provenance du palais omeyyade de Qousayr Amra en Jordanie montre une femme légèrement vêtue mais parée de magnifiques bijoux à l'intérieur d'une niche. Parmi les différentes fresques de femme ornant la salle du trône et les bains du palais, celle-ci représente le goût et la vie de cour de l'époque.
dates: règne de al-Walid Ier (86-96 de l’Hégire / 705-715 J.-C.), probablement postérieur à 92 711.
keywords: Omeyyade ; palais ; bains ; fresque
materials: Peinture à la fresque sur enduit préparé, fortement endommagée.
tags: Peinture à la fresque sur enduit préparé, fortement endommagée.
partner: Musée d’art islamique du Pergamon Museum (Museum für Islamische Kunst)

en.name: Hotel Kadri
description: Both the interior and exterior of the hotel are excellent examples Zahle's traditional stone architecture. It is one of the largest and most luxurious hotels in the city, and is frequently used by officials and dignitaries.
history: The Kadri Hotel was built in 1906, and has borne witness to much of the violence and turmoil in modern Lebanon. The hotel was taken over by the Ottoman army in 1914, who used it is a headquarters and hospital during World War I. It was later occupied by Syrian troops and sustained enormous damage. It was restored to its former glory following an extensive restoration project in the mid 90s. The hotel was briefly closed between February 2011 and 2013.
keywords: Kadri; Hotel; Zahle; Lebanon; Tourists; Tourism

en.name: Amen' glass
description: ‘Amen’ wine glass comprised of a trumpet-shaped bowl and plain drawn stem enclosing a tear, with a folded, circular foot. The bowl is engraved with a crown surmounting a mirrored monogram ‘JR’, intertwined with the number ‘8’, alluding to James VIII, together with two verses of the Jacobite anthem ending with the word AMEN. The verses of the anthem are as follows: God Save the King I pray / God Bless the King I pray / God Save The King / Send Him Victorious Happy and Glorious / Soon to Reign Over Us / God Save The King / God Bless The Prince of Wales / The True Born Prince of Wales / Sent to Us by Thee / Grant us one Favour more / The King for to Restore / As Thou hath done before / The Familie. On the foot, engraved in diamond point are the words: A Bumper To The Prosperity of The Family of Lochiell. The engraving on the glass informs that the object is associated with James Francis Edward Stuart. James was born in 1688 to the Catholic monarch James VII of Scotland and II of England, and his wife Mary of Modena. His birth was viewed as a threat to the established Protestant Parliaments and Churches of both Scotland and England and as a result, his family were forced into exile. The followers of the exiled Stuarts became known as the Jacobites, the Latin for James. Although James was never crowned king, to his supporters he was King James VIII and III. Cameron of Lochiel and his family were staunch Jacobite supporters throughout the Jacobite period.
place: Glass - probably England; Engraving - probably Scotland
keywords: Glass; Amen; Jacobites; Lochiell

en.name: Weaving shuttle
description: A tool designed to neatly and compactly store weft yarn while weaving. To weave the weft, shuttles are passed back and forth through the 'shed', the threads of the warp.

en.name: House
short_description: The architecture of the Reka Area does not show many similar characteristics with neighbouring regions but shares common features with houses in some regions in Bulgaria, Albania, and elsewhere. This is a “tower” type of house. The entire three-storey house was built of stone. Thick and massive stone walls and very small windows on the ground floor were constructed for the purpose of safety in turbulent times, as well as for keeping heat inside during cold winters. The walls on the upper storey with slightly bigger windows were plated with wooden laths. The spatial organization of tower-houses in the Reka area share common features with Albanian tower houses regarding the commodity and defence security. The type of tower-house that used to be built in the Reka Area was the creation of the construction *tajfa* of Maksim Krstich.
dates: End of 19th – beginning of the 20th century
history: The architectural concept of the 19th century "tower" house in Metochia and Montenegro influenced the development of spatial features of this type of house in Macedonia.
keywords: tower house

en.name: Chair
description: This chair, known as *jamuga* in the Spanish tradition, is most certainly a Moresque European piece designed from a combination of pattern books. The chair consists of a great widely decorated back and a curved seat with two arms. The four legs are delicately ornamented. The inscriptions probably have been taken from a design book or other visual model too, rather than being designed by an Arab master calligrapher. The decorated panels, aesthetically pleasing, are imprecise in terms of execution and calligraphic style.
keywords: Production of applied arts in Europe in the Islamic mode; Orientalism

en.name: Traditional blue ceramic plate from Fez
description: This ceramic dish is a remarkable example of craftsmanship in Fez, a Moroccan city renowned for its pottery production since the Middle Ages. The decoration is dominated by a circular rosette in the shape of a six-petaled flower, an emblematic motif of Islamic art combining geometry and symbolism. The centre is decorated with an interlaced six-pointed star (Star of David), symbol of infinity and universal harmony. The petals, finely filled with small blue dots on an off-white background, add texture and depth. Secondary floral motifs occupy the spaces between the petals, accentuating the decorative richness of the piece. The design is framed by a thick cobalt blue border, lending the work an elegance and striking visual contrast. This technique, which combines meticulous painting under a protective glaze, testifies to the mastery of its artisans. After being painted, the dish was baked at a high temperature to fix the colours and obtain the glossy finish characteristic of Fez ceramics.
dates: Hegira mid of 13th century / beginning of the 14th century – AD end of 19th century

en.name: *Cairo, the Nile Dam*
names: Taken from Marcel Jusserand, *Souvenirs d'Egypte* (Memories of Egypt)
short_description: The reign of Muhammad 'Ali Pasha was marked by a series of great changes, including attempts to take control of irrigation. The governor appointed French specialists, amongst whom was Linant de Bellefonds, and tasked them with the construction of a dam near Cairo. Linant de Bellefonds faced a great many difficulties during the construction, such as saving the pyramids, which the Pasha had wanted to destroy in order to supply the new dam with stone. The works were taken over by the engineer Eugène Mougel who added fortifications, as can be seen from this photograph, taken by a tourist at the beginning of the 20th century. The dam was completed c. 1835.
keywords: Irrigation; dams; Egypt

fr.name: *Le Caire, barrage du Nil*
short_description: Le règne de Méhémet-Ali est marqué par de grands changements dont la volonté de maîtriser l’irrigation. Il s’adjoint l’aide de spécialistes français dont Linant de Bellefonds qui se voit, entre autres, confier la responsabilité de la construction d’un barrage près du Caire. Linant de Bellefonds est confronté à de multiples difficultés sur le chantier, comme le sauvetage des pyramides que le Pacha souhaitait démonter afin de fournir le barrage en pierres. La construction du barrage est reprise par l’ingénieur Eugène Mougel qui y ajoute des fortifications, visibles sur cette photographie prise au début du XXe siècle par un voyageur. Le barrage est achevé vers 1835.
keywords: Irrigation; barrages; Egypte
