en.name: Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti
description:
After the palace's destruction in 1508 the façade remained unfinished. In 1680 a monumental staircase was built inside the hall, based on a project by the architect Gian Giacomo Monti.  
Some of the ceilings of the rooms on the first floor are decorated with important frescos, like the *Apotheosis of the Marescotti family,* painted between 1686 and 1687 by Giuseppe and Antonio Rolli. On ceiling of the “fireplace room” is the depiction of *Felsina between Peace and War,* painted between 1682 and 1683 by Marco Antonio Franceschini helped by the “quadrature” painter Enrico Haffner. In the same year Domenico Maria Canuti painted a fresco in Dionysus's room depicting Jupiter, Bacchus and Mercury.  
The Aldrovandi's apartment was built in 1680 to celebrate the wedding between Filippo Maria Aldrovandi and Elena Pepoli: on the ceilings are frescos showing mythological love stories by the Rolli's brothers and Marco Antonio Franceschini.

In 1508 the palace was partially destroyed by supporters of Bentivoglio family, one of the most powerful families in Bologna. The façade still preserves a few elements of the original arcades. Inside it’s still possible to see the monumental staircase by Gian Giacomo Monti and the rooms decorated with frescoes by Giuseppe and Antonio Rolli, Marco Antonio Antonio Franceschini and Enrico Haffner.
artist: Gian Giacomo Monti; Giuseppe Rolli; Antonio Rolli; Antonio Franceschini; Enrico Haffner; Giovanni Battista Caccioli
history:
Built at the end of the 15th century in place of previous medieval houses, the building was commissioned by the Marescotti family as a self-celebration of their political and economical power. From 1466 the family became a member of the Bolognese Senate, clashing with the most important Bolognese family, the Bentivoglio. In 1508 the supporters of the Bentivoglio destroyed the residence of the Marescotti's and in 1574 the Comune of Bologna offered a considerable sum of money in order to rebuild it.  
In 1680 count Raniero Marescotti asked Gian Giacomo Monti, probably the most famous and appreciated architect of that time, to build a monumental staircase for the palace's hall.  
In 1726 James III Stuart (possible heir to the throne of Scotland) arrived in Bologna. The Marescottis who claimed to be descended from the Scottish royal family, welcomed James III as a new king.  
Since 1997, the palace has belonged to The University of Bologna and houses the Department of Music and Performing Arts.
keywords: residential architecture; aristocracy self celebration; fresco; staircase; quadratura
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti
description:
Dopo la distruzione del palazzo, nel 1508, la facciata rimase incompiuta; nel 1680 venne costruito, su progetto dell'architetto Gian Giacomo Monti, lo scalone monumentale nell'ingresso.  
I soffitti delle stanze al piano nobile presentano importanti affreschi, come l'*Apoteosi della famiglia Marescotti* dipinto tra il 1686 e il 1687 da Giuseppe e Antonio Rolli; sul soffitto della Stanza del camino è rappresentata *Felsina tra la Guerra e la Pace*, dipinta tra il 1682 e il 1683 da Marco Antonio Franceschini, con “quadrature” di Enrico Haffner. Nello stesso anno Domenico Maria Canuti dipinse un affresco nella Stanza di Dioniso raffigurante Giove, Bacco e Mercurio.  
L'appartamento Aldrovandi fu costruito nel 1680 per celebrare le nozze tra Filippo Maria Aldrovandi e Elena Pepoli: sui soffitti ci sono affreschi con scene amorose dipinte dai fratelli Rolli e da Marco Antonio Franceschini.

Nel 1508 il palazzo fu parzialmente distrutto dai sostenitori della famiglia Bentivoglio, una delle più potenti della città. All'esterno rimangono ancora alcuni elementi del portico dell'antica facciata, mentre all'interno è ancora possibile visitare lo scalone monumentale di Gian Giacomo Monti e le stanze decorate con affreschi di Giuseppe e Antonio Rolli, Marco Antonio Franceschini e Enrico Haffner.
artist: Gian Giacomo Monti; Giuseppe Rolli; Antonio Rolli; Antonio Franceschini; Enrico Haffner; Giovanni Battista Caccioli
history:
Costruito alla fine del XV secolo al posto di case medievali preesistenti, il palazzo fu commissionato dalla famiglia Marescotti come architettura residenziale auto celebrativa. Dal 1466 la famiglia divenne membro del Senato bolognese, entrando in contrasto con la famiglia più importante di Bologna, i Bentivoglio. Nel 1508, i Bentivoglio distrussero palazzo Marescotti e nel 1574 il Comune di Bologna concesse una considerevole somma di denaro per ricostruire il palazzo.  
Nel 1680 il conte Raniero Marescotti chiese a Gian Giacomo Monti, forse l'architetto più celebre e apprezzato del momento, di costruire uno scalone monumentale per l'ingresso del palazzo.  
L'ultimo evento storico significativo avvenne nel palazzo nel 1726, quando Giacomo III Stuart (pretendente al trono di Scozia) giunse a Bologna. La famiglia Marescotti che riteneva di discendere dalla famiglia reale scozzese, accolse Giacomo III come il nuovo re.  
Dal 1997, il palazzo appartiene all'Università di Bologna ed è oggi sede del DAMS (Dipartimento Arti, Musica e Spettacolo).
keywords: Architettura residenziale; autocelebrazione dell'aristocrazia; Affresco; Scalone

en.name: Sanctuary of La Peregrina
description:
This Franciscan Convent known as the Sanctuary of La Peregrina (the Pilgrim), named after a statue of the Virgin Mary that is in safekeeping there, was founded in 1257, roughly at the same time as the church. The latter has a single nave with a polygonal chancel, while on its walls there are a wide variety of blind arcades of different types including multifoil and lancet arches. Although some of the motifs used here more usually appear in the Mudéjar architecture in Toledo, this church is earlier than Santa Fe in Toledo, which means that it might be considered the first example of the Gothic type. On the other hand, the ornamental motifs of the arches are found a century later in San Pablo de Peñafiel in Valladolid.  
Perhaps the most unusual aspect of the Sanctuary is the burial chapel of don Diego Gómez de Sandoval located on the Epistle side of the church. This square chapel’s interior is decorated with polychrome plasterwork that surrounds a substantial tomb and covers the walls completely with friezes of geometric latticework. Below, on the lower parts, strapwork and Gothic plant motifs alternate on a background of small-scale ataurique. An inscription in semi-uncial Latin letters runs around the wall: *Domine: Jhs: Xpe: Fili de(i) … (p)ecatori: Q(ui): Moribu*. The Sandoval family coat of arms – with one diagonal band – is arranged in different parts of the plasterwork, supporting documentation tells us that the first Conde de Castro, don Diego Gómez Sandoval, who died in 1455, is buried here. The will of his second son, whose name was the same, reads: “*Furthermore I leave to the monastery of San Francisco de Sahagún, where my Ancestors are buried, because they are charged with praying to God for their souls and my own, and for certain things which have to be done in the tombs of my parents and my brothers … 3200 maravedíes …*”.  
The plasterwork itself is evidence of a Mudéjar School of plasterers working in this area between 1430 and 1450 and who must have specialised in decorating memorial chapels. They have left important work in Sahagún and in Mayorga de Campos in Valladolid.

es.name: Santuario de la Peregrina
description:
El convento de franciscanos conocido como el santuario de la Peregrina, por albergar en sus muros una imagen de la Virgen bajo esta advocación, se fundó en 1257 y más o menos por la misma fecha se debió edificar el templo. Este tiene una sola nave con cabecera poligonal y en sus muros un amplio repertorio de arcos ciegos de diferentes tipos, entre los que destacan los lobulados y los de ojiva túmida. Aunque en él luzcan motivos usuales en el mudéjar toledano, el templo es anterior al de Santa Fe en Toledo, que podría considerarse el primer ejemplo de tipo gótico. Por otro lado, los motivos ornamentales de los arcos se repetirán un siglo después en San Pablo de Peñafiel (Valladolid).  
Quizás la obra más singular del santuario sea la capilla funeraria de don Diego Gómez de Sandoval, situada del lado de la epístola. De planta cuadrangular, se decora interiormente con yeserías polícromas que cobijan un amplio lucillo y cubren totalmente los muros con frisos de celosías geométricas y alternan en las partes bajas lacería y temas vegetales góticos sobre un fondo de *ataurique* menudo. Una inscripción en letras semiunciales latinas corre por el muro: “DOMINE:JHS: XPE:FILI DE(I)... (P)ECATORI: Q(UI): MORIBU”. El escudo de los Sandoval — con una banda— aparece en diferentes partes de la yesería y fundamenta la documentación que nos dice que allí se encuentra enterrado el primer conde de Castro, don Diego Gómez Sandoval, muerto en 1455, ya que en el testamento de su hijo segundo, del mismo nombre, se dice: “Otrosí mando más al monesterio de San Francisco de Sahagún, donde están sepultados mis Antepasados, porque tengan cargo de rogar a Dios por sus ánimas e la mía y por ciertas cosas que se han de faser en los enterramientos de mis Padres y Hermanos... 3200 maravedíes...”.  
Las yeserías, por su parte, hablan de una escuela de yeseros mudéjares que entre 1430 y 1450 trabajaba en esta zona y se dedicaba a decorar capillas funerarias, y ha dejado obras importantes en Sahagún y en Mayorga de Campos (Valladolid).

ar.name: غطاء قبر نبي الله إبراهيم.
description:
جرت العادة، سواءً في العصر المملوكي أو العصر العثماني، على أن يهتم السلاطين وكبار رجالات الدولة وأهل الخير والإحسان بقبور الأنبياء والصالحين، لا سيّما بتقديم الكسوة (غطاء القبر أو المقام) وتجديدها سنوياً أو كلما دعت الحاجة لذلك. وكانت تكسية القبور والمزارات تتم عبر احتفالات شعبية تجري في مواسم محددة كل عام. وغالباً ما حظيت هذه الخطوة على رضى واستحسان زوّار القبر أو المزار، وزادت من شعبية واهب الكسوة لدى العامة. وقد حظيت فلسطين خلال العصر العثماني باهتمام كبير لم يسبق له مثيل بالقبور والمزارات والأماكن المقدسة العديدة المنتشرة في أرجاء البلاد، وذلك في إطار الاهتمام الرسمي بالطرق الصوفية وشيوخها وأماكن ممارسة طقوسها. ونذكر هنا على سبيل المثال: قبر النبي موسى، وقبر النبي صموئيل، وقبر النبي داوود، وقبور الأنبياء وزوجاتهم في الحرم الإبراهيمي في الخليل.  
  
والقطعة المعروضة هنا عبارة عن غطاء قبر صنع من نسيج حريري أخضر اللون، وحيك على شكل قميص يغطي القبر بأكمله ماعدا الشاهد الذي كتب عليه اسم صاحب القبر "نبي الله إبراهيم". وطرِّزت طغراء (شارة) السلطان العثماني سليم الثالث على القطعة. وكتب على القطعة كتابات نصها "هذا غار" و "شريف"، بالإضافة إلى كتابات أخرى تتضمن أدعية دينية وآياتقرآنية.  
  
استمر التقليد الرسمي لإرسال الكسوة إلى المقامات والمزارات في فلسطين حتى نهاية العصر العثماني عام 1916. وتوقف بعد ذلك هذا التقليد بصفته الرسمية، ولكنه استمر قائماً بصفة شعبية حيث اهتم السكان المحيطون بمواقع القبور والمزارات بإعداد الكسوة، لكنها لم تعد بالفخامة ودقة الصنع التي كانت عليها زمن السلاطين العثمانيين.

جرت العادة على تجديد أغطية قبور الأنبياء، كل عام، ضمن احتفالات شعبية. ازدادت هذه التقاليد أهمية خلال الفترة العثمانية. وهذه الغطاء من الحرير الأخضر، حيك على شكل قميص للقبر، ليغطيه من كافة الجهات، بحيث يظهر فوق الشاهد اسم صاحب القبر المُغطَّى، كما تمَّ تطريز طغراء السلطان سليم الثالث عليها.
place: من المرجّح أن تكون القطعة قد صنعت في سورية أو اسطنبول، وصنعت خصيصاً للحرم الإبراهيمي في الخليل.
keywords: غطاء قبر؛ غطاء قبر إبراهيم؛ قبر؛ قماش؛ كسوة؛ نسيج؛ نسيج حريري؛ الجنائزية
materials: نسيج من الحرير مطرّز بخيوط حريرية فضية.
tags: نسيج من الحرير مطرّز بخيوط حريرية فضية.

en.name: *Kiswa* (tomb cover) for the Prophet of God, Ibrahim (Abraham).
description:
There was a tradition in both the Mamluk and the Ottoman periods, for sultans, noble personages of state, as well as the benevolent, to interest themselves in the tombs of the prophets and the devout by offering a *kiswa* (covering for a grave or tomb), and then to renew it each year or whenever necessary. The ritual draping of tombs and shrines were popular celebrations that took place in certain seasons every year. For the most part, this occurred in order to procure the good-will and approval of visitors to the tomb or shrine, and to enhance the popularity of the *kiswa*'s donor among the general public. It was during the Ottoman period in Palestine that there was a huge unparalleled interest in the tombs, shrines and holy places that were scattered throughout the region. This was within the context of the official interest in the Sufi orders, their sheikhs, and the venues where the rituals were practiced. An example of this veneration can be seen in the context of the tombs of the Prophets Moses, Samuel and David, and their wives, in al-Haram al-Ibrahimi (the Ibrahimi Mosque) in Hebron (al-Khalil).  
The *kiswa* exhibited here is made from woven green silk. The *kiswa* was produced in order to envelope the tomb completely, leaving only the tombstone visible, upon which was written the name of the deceased: “The Prophet of God, Ibrahim \[Abraham\]”. The *tughra* of the Ottoman sultan, Selim III (r. AH 1203-22/AD 1789-1807) is embroidered on the *Kiswa*, together with inscriptions that read, “This is a protector” and “revered”, in addition to other inscriptions that include religious supplications and Qur'anic verses.  
The official tradition as noted above, to send *kiswa*s to the tombs and shrines of venerated holy men and women, continued in Palestine until the end of the Ottoman period in 1916, when the tradition was officially stopped. At the popular level, however, locals who lived in the environs of these tomb sites and shrines continued preparing *kiswas* but they were no longer splendid, finely made textiles as had been the case during the period of the Ottoman sultans.

The coverings of the prophets’ tombs were renewed every year in popular celebrations. The importance of these traditions increased during the Ottoman period. This covering woven of green silk envelops the tomb leaving only the tombstone on which is written the name of the deceased. The *tughra* of Ottoman Sultan Selim III is embroidered on it.
holder: Islamic Museum, al-Aqsa Mosque / al-Haram al-Sharif.
place: Probably produced in either Syria or Istanbul, but made specifically for the Haram al-Ibrahimi (the Ibrahimi Mosque) in Hebron (al-Khalil).
keywords: Kiswa; tomb; cloth; fabric; silk; funerary object
materials: Silk embroidered with silver silk threads.
tags: Silk embroidered with silver silk threads.

es.name: Cobertura *(kiswa)* de la tumba de Abraham.
description:
Durante los periodos mameluco y otomano, los sultanes, la nobleza y otros benefactores seguían la tradición de interesarse por las tumbas de los profetas y mostrar su devoción regalando una *kiswa* y renovándola una vez al año o cuando fuera necesario. El ritual de envolver las tumbas y los santuarios se celebraba en determinadas épocas del año. En general, con el ritual se pretendía obtener los buenos deseos y la aprobación de los visitantes de la tumba o santuario, y aumentar la popularidad pública del donante de la *kiswa*. En la Palestina otomana se vivió una época de enorme interés por las tumbas, los santuarios y los lugares sagrados de toda la zona, dentro del contexto del interés oficial por las órdenes sufíes, sus *shaijs* y los lugares en los que practicaban sus rituales. Se veneraron, entre otras, las tumbas de los profetas Moisés, Samuel y David, y de sus esposas, que se hallan en al-Haram al-Ibrahim (mezquita de Ibrahim) de Hebrón (al-Jalil).  
Esta *kiswa* es de seda verde tejida. La pieza se fabricó para envolver totalmente la tumba y dejar a la vista la lápida con el nombre: “El profeta de Dios, Ibrahim \[Abraham\]”. Los bordados que decoran el manto presentan la *tugra* del sultán otomano Selim III (r. 1203-1222 / 1789-1807), inscripciones que dicen “Esto es una protección” o “Venerado”, aparte de otras que recogen súplicas y aleyas del Corán.  
La tradición oficial de enviar una *kiswa* a las tumbas y santuarios de los hombres y mujeres venerados pervivió en Palestina hasta 1916, al final del periodo otomano, cuando la costumbre se interrumpió oficialmente. Sin embargo, el pueblo decidió continuar con la tradición y las personas que vivían cerca de los santuarios y las tumbas siguieron haciendo mantos que, a diferencia de los de la época de los sultanes otomanos, ya no eran tejidos delicados y espléndidos.

Todos los años, en medio de celebraciones, se renovaban los mantos que cubrían las tumbas de los profetas, tradición que cobró mayor fuerza durante el periodo otomano. Este tejido de seda verde envolvería toda la tumba, dejando libre únicamente la lápida donde está escrito el nombre del difunto. Tiene bordada la *tugra* del sultán otomano Selim III.
place: Probablemente se fabricase en Siria o Estambul específicamente para el Haram al-Ibrahimi de Hebrón.
keywords: Kiswa; tumba; paño; tela; seda; objeto funerário
materials: Seda bordada con hilos de seda plateados.
tags: Seda bordada con hilos de seda plateados.
partner: Museo islámico en la mezquita de Al-Aqsa

fr.name: Kiswa, voile du tombeau d’Abraham.
description:
Au cours des périodes mamelouke et ottomane, les sultans, les hauts dignitaires et divers bienfaiteurs offraient des *kiswa* (couvertures, voiles) pour les tombeaux des prophètes et les renouvelaient chaque année – ou à la demande en cas de nécessité. Le drapage rituel des tombes et des mausolées donnait lieu chaque année à des célébrations populaires. L'important était de s'attirer les bonnes grâces des visiteurs des tombeaux et d'accroître la popularité du donateur auprès du peuple. Cette attention portée aux tombeaux, aux mausolées et aux lieux saints connut une recrudescence importante au cours de la période ottomane en Palestine dans le contexte de l'intérêt officiel pour les ordres soufis, leurs *cheikh* et leurs cérémonies. Cette vénération toucha, entre autres, les tombeaux de Moïse, de Salomon, de David et de leurs épouses à la mosquée d'Abraham à Hébron.  
La *kiswa* présentée ici est tissée en soie verte. Elle enveloppe complètement la tombe, ne laissant visible que la pierre tombale sur laquelle est gravé le nom du défunt : “Le prophète de Dieu, Ibrahim”. Le *tughra* du sultan Sélim III (r. 1203-1222 H / 1789-1807 J.-C.) est brodé dans le tissu, ainsi qu'une inscription disant : “Ceci est une protection” et “révéré” – mais il y a aussi d'autres inscriptions, qui reprennent des supplications religieuses et des versets coraniques. Cette tradition d'envoi de la *kiswa* s'est poursuivie jusqu'à la fin de la période ottomane en 1916, date à laquelle elle fut officiellement abandonnée. Au niveau populaire, cependant, les habitants des environs des tombes continuèrent à préparer des *kiswa*, mais qui n'étaient plus ces splendides tissus offerts par les sultans ottomans.

Les *kiswa* (voiles) des tombeaux des prophètes étaient renouvelés chaque année lors de célébrations populaires. L’importance de ces traditions s’accrut durant la période ottomane. Cette couverture tissée en soie verte enveloppe la tombe, ne laissant visible que la pierre tombale sur laquelle est gravé le nom du défunt. Le *tughra* du sultan ottoman Sélim III est brodé sur le tissu.
holder: Musée islamique, mosquée al-Aqsa / Haram al-Charif.
place: Probablement Syrie ou Istanbul, mais spécialement fabriqué pour la mosquée d’Abraham à Hébron.
keywords: Kiswa ; tombes ; tissus ; étoffes ; soie; objet funéraire
materials: Soie brodée de fils de soie argentés.
tags: Soie brodée de fils de soie argentés.

en.name: Portrait of Claudius Rich
short_description: Rich was the East India Company’s first Resident in Baghdad. He was a talented linguist. In his spare time he explored ancient sites, producing the first proper plans of Babylon and Nineveh. He hosted important travellers to Iraq, searching for sites of Biblical relevance. In 1821 he died during a cholera outbreak in Shiraz. His collection formed the nucleus of the British Museum’s collection.
keywords: Bible; travelling; archaeology; archaeological excavation; exploration; collecting; collector; museums

ar.name: قنديل مسجد.
description: قنديل مسجد له حجم وشكل القناديل المملوكية التقليدية، وعنق متجه نحو الخارج، وجسم عريض، وقاعدة مرتفعة، ومزوَّد بحلقات من الزجاج لربط حبال التعليق. تم تزيين القنديل بواسطة التطعيم بالمينا ولاسيما الأزرق والأحمر مع بعض الإبراز في استخدام الأخضر والأبيض والذهبي. أغلب الزخارف كتابية، ويذكر نقش بارز منها " مما عمل برسم الجناب العالي المولوي الأميري الكبير السيفي سيف الدين أقبغا عبد الواحد الملكي الناصري"، وقد تم ملء المساحات حول الكتابات بالنماذج الزهرية والأرابيسك. يظهر رنك سيف الدين أقبغا، وهو على شكل معين، على أرضية مستطيلة، في حليات دائرية على العنق. لقد بنى أقبغا مدرسة هامة في جامع الأزهر بالقاهرة (المدرسة الأقبغاوية) عام 740/ 1340، وتم تعليق هذا القنديل على الأغلب من سقف هذا المبنى، على الأرجح بواسطة الحبال التي ما تزال معلقة به حتى الآن.

مصباح من مسجد مُصمَّم على الطراز المملوكي، مُزخرف بالزجاج المطلي والمينا، ليشكل كتابات وزخارف نباتية. المالك هو سيف الدين أكبوغا؛ الذي قام بتأسيس مدرسة دينية، في مسجد الأزهر الشريف، في القاهرة عام 740 هـ/ 1340 م, وعلى الأغلب فإن هذا المصباح كان قد استُخدم في المدرسة.
keywords: قطعة ذات استعمال ديني.

en.name: Mosque lamp.
description: A mosque lamp of typical size and shape for Mamluk lamps, with flaring neck, wide body and high foot. Thick glass loops are attached for the suspension cords. It is decorated with enamelling, mostly in blue and red, with some highlights added in green, white and gold. The majority of the decoration is calligraphic. A prominent inscription states that 'This is one of the objects made for His High Excellency, our lord the great Amir, Sayf al-Din Aqbugha 'Abd al-Wahid \[officer of\] al-Malik al-Nasir'. The areas in and around the calligraphy are decorated with floral motifs and arabesques. Sayf al-Din Aqbugha's blazon, a diamond (napkin) on a rectangular field, appears in roundels on the neck. Aqbugha built an important *madrasa* at the Mosque of al-Azhar in Cairo (the Madrasa al-Aqbughawiyya) in AH 740 / AD 1340, and this lamp was probably suspended from the ceiling in that building, possibly with the very cords that are still attached to it.

A lamp of typical Mamluk shape, decorated with enamelled glass forming inscriptions, floral decoration, and blazons. The patron, Sayf al-Din Aqbugha, founded a *madrasa* (religious school) at the Azhar mosque complex in Cairo in AH 740 / AD 1340, and this lamp may originally have hung there.
keywords: religious object; Mosque interior decoration; enamel; calligraphy; floral decoration; arabesque; blazons; emblems; coat of arm

es.name: Lámpara de mezquita.
description:
Lámpara de mezquita de tamaño y forma típicamente mamelucos, con cuello abocinado, cuerpo ancho y pie alto. Las cuerdas para colgarla se atan a unas gruesas anillas de vidrio. Está decorada, en su mayor parte con motivos caligráficos en esmaltes azul y rojo, con algunos detalles en verde, blanco y dorado. Una inscripción resaltada dice: “Este es uno de los objetos hechos para Su Altísima Excelencia, nuestro señor el gran emir Sayf al-Din Aqbuga Abd al-Wahid \[oficial de\] al-Malik al-Nasir”. Los espacios en los huecos de las letras y alrededor del texto están rellenados con motivos florales y arabescos. En los medallones del cuello aparece el blasón de Sayf al-Din Aqbuga, una servilleta sobre campo rectangular.  
Probablemente, esta lámpara colgaba del techo de la madrasa al-Aqbugawiyya que el emir construyó en 740 / 1340 dentro del conjunto de la importante mezquita de al-Azhar (El Cairo).

Lámpara de forma típicamente mameluca con inscripciones, decoración floral y blasones en vidrio esmaltado, y que colgaría de la madrasa (escuela religiosa) que Sayf al-Din Aqbuga fundó en 740 / 1340 en el complejo de la mezquita Al-Azhar de El Cairo.
keywords: objetos religiosos

fr.name: Lampe de mosquée.
description: Lampe de mosquée à col évasé, large panse et haut pied, de dimensions et de forme typiques des lampes mameloukes. D'épaisses attaches de verre servent à fixer les cordes de suspension. Elle est décorée d'émail, essentiellement bleu et rouge, et de quelques rehauts en vert, blanc et or. Le décor est surtout calligraphique. Une inscription très importante précise : “Voici l'un des objets faits pour Sa Haute Excellence, notre seigneur le grand Émir, Sayf al-Din Aqbugha Abd al-Wahid \[officier de\] al-Malik al-Nasir”. Les zones dans et autour de la calligraphie sont décorées de motifs floraux et d'arabesques. Le blason de Sayf al-Din Aqbugha – un diamant (serviette) sur un champ rectangulaire – apparaît dans des rosettes sur le col. Aqbugha avait construit une importante *madrasa* à la mosquée al-Azhar au Caire (la *madrasa* al-Aqbughawiyya) en 740 H / 1340 J.-C., et cette lampe était probablement suspendue au plafond de ce bâtiment, sans doute aux cordes mêmes qui lui sont encore attachées.

Lampe de forme typiquement mamelouke en verre à décor émaillé (inscriptions, décoration florale et blasons). Le commanditaire, Sayf al-Din Aqbugha, fonda une *madrasa* (école religieuse) dans le complexe de la mosquée al-Azhar au Caire en 740 H / 1340 J.-C., et c'est vraisemblablement là que cette lampe fut initialement suspendue.
keywords: Objets religieux

ar.name: رحل
description:
هذا الموقف القرآني يرفع الكتب المقدسة الكبيرة لمنع الاتصال المباشر بسطح الأرض غير النظيف. يتميز الهيكل الخشبي المصنوع من الهند بنقوش زهرية عميقة.  
  
تزين المنحوتات المغولية مع صفوف من الأزهار والكروم منصة القرآن بدقة هندسية. بينما لا تزال الأعمال الخشبية الإسلامية في الهند غير مدروسة على نطاق واسع ، فإن الأقواس المفصصة للأرجل تذكر بالعمارة المغولية. علاوة على ذلك ، نادرًا ما تحمل الأعمال الخشبية للإمبراطورية المغولية نقوشًا ، مما يعيق التأريخ الدقيق ودراسة مجموعات القطع.  
  
لا تزال هذه المواقف مهد المصاحف في المنازل الفخمة والمساجد والمدارس الإسلامية (المدارس) وفي المقابر لأغراض التلاوة والعرض.
holder: متحف الشيخ فيصل بن قاسم ال ثاني
partner: متحف الشيخ فيصل بن قاسم ال ثاني

en.name: Qur’an Stand
description:
This Qur’an stand would elevate larger holy books to prevent direct contact with the unclean surface of the ground. The pigmented wood structure from India features deep floral carvings.  
  
Mughal-style carvings with rows of florals and vines adorn the Qur’an stand in geometric precision. While Islamic woodwork in India remains widely understudied, the lobed arches of the legs remind of Mughal architecture. Furthermore, the woodwork of the Mughal Empire rarely bears inscriptions, hindering an accurate dating and study of clusters of pieces.  
  
These stands still cradle Qur’ans in affluent homes, mosques, Islamic schools (*madrasa*), and in tombs for recitation and display purposes.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: India; Mughal; post-Mughal; Quran Stand
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

en.name: Convent of Jesus
description:
"The Convento de Jesus was founded in 1489 by D. Justa Rodrigues, wet nurse to D. Manuel I, when the latter was still only the Duke of Beja, and Administrator of the Order of Christ. The first stone was laid on August 17th 1490, and two years later, during a visit by D. João II, the ceremony was symbolically repeated. It is known that the Master of Works, Boytac, worked there before 1490 and the initial project was certainly his, although only a small part of what remains today is his work.  
When D. Manuel I ascended the throne, the original plan was altered to make a larger church and more ample residential quarters. The walls of the church, the crypt below the chancel, and the upper and lower choirs, date from the early times of the construction, and possibly the plan for the cloister, completed in 1520, also dates from the 15th century.  
The church has three aisles rising to the same height, separated by twisted columns in polished stone from the Serra da Arrábida. The chancel, higher and better built, was begun in 1520 by master masons who had worked on the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos in Lisbon. It has rich, complex vaulting with curved ribs forming a quatrefoil. The stained glass windows were only completed in 1539.  
The main vessel of the church was not the work of the same designer and must have been the result of a decision by D. João III to complete the building as quickly and as cheaply as possible. It is lower than the apse and retains the buttresses of the initial work on the exterior, while the doorway is Late Gothic in design.  
There is an interesting series of *Mudejar* tiles from Seville with inscriptions evoking death in the funerary crypt. The entire church has highly complex decorative elements in the Late Gothic style that are excessively naturalist in taste, as is the case with the triangular shaped part of the vault in the chancel, the niche in the sanctuary, the altar-niche in the sacristy, and the blind window on the left-hand side of the apse.  
The large cloister has two storeys and arcades with pointed arches, only broken by openings to the garth. The covered *lavabo* (wash room), an addition to the quadrangular plan, is at the opposite end of the church and has beautifully designed corbels with heads in high relief."

en.name: Yoke (*nīr*)
description: This yoke was used for animals to raise water from a *zājrah* well. Donkeys and bullocks typically work side-by-side to pull together against the weight of the water.

en.name: Alba
description:
The Alba metallurgical plant in Albergaria-a-Velha was in the early 1950s a large industrial plant belonging to Comendador Martins Pereira. His son António Augusto Martins Pereira, a motorsport enthusiast, wanted a brand purely dedicated to racing. Hence the Alba car brand was born. The first Alba was designed and built in 1952, and as was normal at the time in Portugal, France and Italy, it was equipped with the highly reliable 1089cc Simca-Fiat engine. The Alba’s styling was quite remarkably ahead of its time, especially when put next to other cars of the time, such as the DM or the FAP. Both the DM and FAP had comparatively very archaic aesthetics.  
  
The Alba racing team achieved early success in the hands of Martins Pereira and Francisco Corte Real Pereira. The latter, who helped develop the car, won the 1100cc class Boavista Circuit race two years in a row in 1951 and 1952. With three racing cars built, the company focused its competitive efforts on national events. Corte Real was usually at the wheel for circuit events and Martins Pereira competed in regularity tests and rallies.  
  
In 1954, the ACP, Portugal’s motorsport governing body, imposed new regulatory changes which increased engine capacities from 1 litre to 1.5. Small Portuguese builders like Alba had to find new engines if they were to comply. Alba began to develop several engines initially by increasing the bore of its 1.1 litre unit to 1.3. The company also later did a similar job on a Peugeot block.  
  
But with the rapid ascendancy of the Porsche engine, which proved to be unbeatable in both the Denzel and 550 Spyder, Corte Real Pereira devised a daring plan to help Alba compete. Taking an old Alfa Romeo 6C 1.7-litre unit, the company then reduced the bore size to 1.5, thus developing a curious 1.5 litre six-cylinder engine. The newly equipped Alba raced in Boavista 1955 and 56, then in Vila Real 1958, without much success.  
  
Alba’s life in competition continued for some time without notable success until 1961, when Corte Real Pereira finished third in the Rally Nocturno de Salgueiros.

en.name: al-Ghuta ash-Sharqiyya
description: After being weighed, sorted and washed, then treated with sulphur, apricots are placed on a large cement platform sheltered from the sun. Exposing the apricots to sulphur vapour before pressing is a major innovation in the process. After some trial and error, sulphurisation is now a well-established part of the process; although the main argument in favour of it is commercial, the operation has the essential advantage of purifying or sterilising the fruit, therefore allowing better preservation of the *Qamr ad-Din*. A suction pump on the platform is used to load the press. A worker in boots enters the platform and pushes the apricots towards the mouth of the suction pump with a wooden shovel.

en.name: *Sketch of Algeria, featuring the Roman occupation, the railway lines, roads suitable for mule and horse drawn vehicles, ports* \[…\] drawn from an archaeological point of view and dedicated to ...
names: Taken from *Revue Africaine: Journal des Travaux de la Société Historique Algérienne 78*
short_description: Founded in 1856, the Société Historique Algérienne organised excavations, published a journal, and created maps and plans. This map helped facilitate research on the Roman occupation of Algeria, by indicating clearly the main sites, how to get there, and other elements which allow the reader to better understand the Roman presence (such as marble quarries and thermal baths).
keywords: archaeological excavations; Algeria

fr.name: *Croquis de l'Algérie, contenant l'occupation romaine, les chemins de fer, les routes carrossables et muletières, les ports... dressé en vue de l'archéologie et dédié à la*
names: *Revue africaine*, bulletin n° 78. Travaux de la Société historique algérienne
short_description: Fondée en 1856, la Société historique algérienne entreprend des fouilles, publie une revue, et dresse des plans. Cette carte est destinée à faciliter les recherches sur l'occupation romaine en indiquant les sites principaux, les moyens de s'y rendre, et les éléments permettant de mieux comprendre la présence romaine (carrières de marbre, sites thermaux, etc.).
keywords: Fouilles archéologiques; Algérie

en.name: Al Qanāt, Abu Dhabi
description:
The tranquil waterway of Al Qanāt in Abu Dhabi is a modern landscape feature where urban architecture meets a natural waterway. At sunset the gentle canal becomes a reflective corridor linking the city’s contemporary skyline with the silhouette of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, creating a dialogue between heritage and modernity. In the Gulf region, waterways such as Al Qanāt play a vital role in shaping urban life. They cool the environment, support marine activity, and provide communal spaces for recreation and movement.  
  
Water remains a central element in the identity of Abu Dhabi — a functional resource and symbol of serenity, continuity, and connection.

ar.name: لوحة شخصية لشخص أوربي وفق طباعة جاك دو جين ""تيرا""
description: تبين هذه اللوحة المنمنمة صورة جندي أوربي والتي رسمت من قبل فنان مغولي في القرن السابع عشر والصورة الأصلية تستند إلى صورة مطبوعة أوربية من قبل صانع المطابع الهولندي جاك دو جين (1565-1629) وهذه اللوحة المصنوعة بتقنية الغواش على الورق التي تظهر شخص أوربي أبيض البشرة وذو شعر أشقر في طراز أوربي من الملابس يمسك جسما طويلا ربما سلاح مثل حربة أو مسدس وفي هامش  اللوحة منقوش كلمة ""أول"" ربما تشير لنوعية اللوحة وفي الخلف طباعة لأختام مغولية. وكان الإعجاب بالطبعات الأوربية شائعا بين الطبقة الحاكمة المغولية. إن الأباطرة مثل أكبر وجانجير الذي أتى لاحقا كانا من بين جامعي الطبعات المصورة الأوربية.

en.name: A Portrait of a European, after Jacques de Gheyn's print 'Terra'
description: This miniature painting depicted an image of a European soldier made by Mughal artist around 17th century. The original image is based on a European print by Dutch printmaker Jacques de Gheyn (1565–1629). This painting which is made with gouache on paper technique showing a European with fair skin colour in European style of clothes holding a long object, probably a weapon such as a spear or gun. At the margin of the painting inscribed the word ‘awwal’, possibly indicating the grade of the painting and at the back with Mughal seals impressions. The fondness to European prints was common in Mughal court. Emperors such as Akbar and later Jahangir were among the collectors of European prints.

en.name: Iron coffee roasting spoon
short_description: Iron coffee roasting spoon used to turn coffee beans while roasting them. Coffee-drinking in a communal setting is an essential part of traditions in Bedouin communities to celebrate or mourn.
holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
keywords: coffee; coffee roasting; coffee beans; domestic furnishing; domestic vessels
partner: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery

de.name: Kapelle der schmerzhaften Mutter (Fiegerkapelle)
description: Erbaut in Erweiterung der Vorhalle als Stiftung von Johann Karl Graf Fieger. Neben dem prächtigen Säulenaltar sind hier vor allem die Deckenfresken Kaspar Waldmanns von Bedeutung, eine Verherrlichung Mariae mit den sieben Gründern des Servitenordens und Szenen aus dem Leben Mariae.

en.name: Chapel of the Sorrowful Mother (Fieger Chapel)
description: Built as an extension to the vestibule, it was donated Johann Karl Graf Fieger. Together with the magnificent column altar, the most significant feature is the ceiling frescos from Kaspar Waldmann, a glorification of Mary with the seven founders of the Servite Order and scenes from the life of Mary.
place: Northern vestibule, The Servite Monastery Church of St. Charles Borromeo

de.name: Auffindung des Kreuzes durch Kaiserin Helena und Kreuzesprobe
description: Vor einer Jerusalem meinenden Stadtkulisse versucht Kaiserin Helena, das wieder aufgefundene Kreuz Christi im Vertrauen auf dessen Wundertätigkeit von den beiden Schächerkreuzen zu scheiden. Biografisch bedeutend verewigte sich einschließlich Signatur der schon schwer erkrankte Maler als Siechender inmitten einer auf Heilung durch Kreuzreliquien hoffenden Personengruppe, die dem Kreuzeswunder gegenübergestellt ist.

en.name: Finding of the Cross by Empress Helena and Trial of the Cross
description: In front of the city scenery of Jerusalem, Empress Helena tries to separate the rediscovered Cross of Christ, relying on its miraculous work, from the two thieves’ crosses. Biographically significant, the already severely sick painter immortalised himself, signature included, as an ailing person amongst a group of people, adjacent to the miracle of the cross, hoping to be healed by the cross relics.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Air Orient Company. Planisphere. Weekly Air Service France-Syria-Indochina
description: This 1930s Air Orient poster highlights the French airline’s east–west routes across the Middle East. From Beirut and Damascus to Baghdad and Basra, the service carried passengers and mail between Paris and the Levant. Produced in a republican France that was also a vast colonial empire, the poster embodies both the allure of modern aviation and the projection of French influence through new networks of mobility.

en.name: Lunchbox
description: Tin-plated copper casket for transporting food on journeys and campaigns. The whole surface is decorated with intricated designs, inscriptions and medallion with geometric motifs.

en.name: Control Tower Airport Basrah
description: Postcard; printed; monochrome real photograph showing the airport control tower, Basra, flying the national flag
keywords: Airport; Photograph; Architecture

ar.name: لوحة خشبية
description: القطعة هي لوحة خشبية ذات تزيين نباتي بنفور عالي وتشكل زخرفة بشكل كأس زهرة التي تصدر عنها أوراق محلزنة. واللوحة ممثلة لمرحلة انتقالية مميزة بتقنية مشطوفة للمرحلة الثانية التي المثال المميز لها هو باب مقدم من قبل الخليفة الحاكم لمسجد الأزهر في عام 1010.

el.name: Ξυλόγλυπτο πλακίδιο
description: Η ξυλόγλυπτη πλάκα προέρχεται από θύρα και φέρει φυτικό διάκοσμο σε ψηλό ανάγλυφο που σχηματίζει καλυκόμορφο σχέδιο από το οποίο φύονται σπειροειδείς βλαστοί. Η πλάκα είναι αντιπροσωπευτική ενός μεταβατικού διακόσμου από τη λοξότμητη τεχνική στην επόμενη φάση, εξαιρετικό δείγμα της οποίας είναι η θύρα που παρουσίασε ο χαλίφης αλ-Χάκίμ στο τζαμί αλ-Άζχαρ το 1010.

en.name: Wooden panel
description: Wooden panel from a door with vegetal decoration, in high relief, forming a calyx-shaped ornament from which spring spiralling leaves. The panel is representative of the transitional stage characterised by the bevelled technique to the next phase of which a distinctive example is the door presented by Caliph al-Hakim to the mosque of Al-Azhar in 1010.
keywords: Panel; Wood

ar.name: القسطل.
description:
يحتوي هذا الموقع على عدة أبنية ومنشآت: القصر، والمسجد الذي لم يبقَ منه سوى المئذنة، والحمام بالإضافة إلى وحدات سكنية. يوجد إلى الشرق من القصر نظام متطور لجمع المياه يشتمل على سد منيع. يتخذ القصر شكلاً مربعاً طول ضلعه 68 م. أقيمت في زوايا القصر أبراج داعمة دائرية تحصر بينها في كل جانب ثلاث دعامات نصف دائرية، باستثناء الجانب الشرقي الذي فتح في منتصفه المدخل. يحتوي الجانب الشرقي على أربع دعامات نصف دائرية، تحيط اثنتان منها بالمدخل. بالقرب من المدخل يمكن مشاهدة الزخارف المحفورة على عضادتي بوابة المدخل وعتبتها العليا. يؤدي المدخل إلى ممر أقيمت في جانبيه مجموعة من الدرجات ترتقي إلى الأعلى. يطل المدخل عند طرفه البعيد على ساحة مكشوفة مربعة الشكل (أبعادها 40 x 40 م) تحيط بها سقائف وست وحدات سكنية وزعت على نظام "البيت". تتألف كل وحدة أو بيت من أربع غرف أقيمت حول ساحة مستطيلة: غرفتان في كل من الجانبين تتصلان مع الساحة المكشوفة وتطلان عليها بحيث يشكل كل بيت وحدة سكنية مستقلة. كانت معظم أرضيات غرف القصر وأرضيات السقائف مرصوفة في الأصل بقطع فسيفساء ملونة بقي منها أجزاء قليلة متفرقة.  
  
تقع إلى الغرب من القصر المقبرة التي عثر فيها على العديد من شواهد القبور المنقوشة بكتابات عربية يعود بعضها إلى العصر الأموي وبعضها إلى العصر العباسي المبكر، وهي محفوظة اليوم في متحف مدينة مادبا الأثري. إلى الشمال من القصر يقع المسجد والمئذنة التي تبرز عن الزاوية الشمالية الغربية لساحة المسجد، ويتخذ بدنها شكلاً أسطوانياً أقيم فوق قاعدة مستطيلة. تجدر الإشارة هنا إلى أن أهمية هذه المئذنة تنبع من كونها المئذنة الوحيدة الباقية في بلاد الشام من العصر الأموي.  
  
استخدم القصر في العصرين المملوكي والعثماني كمساكن واسطبلات.

هذه الآبدة الواقعة على مسافة نحو 25 كيلومتراً إلى الجنوب من عمَّان مُجمّّع يتألف من قصر، ومسجد، وحمَّام، وأجنحة سكنية. القصر مبنى مُربَّع الشكل بمساحة 68×68م، وقد حافظ على أرضيات فسيفسائية. ربما كان القصر للخليفة يزيد بن عبد الملك (الذي حكم فيما بين عامي 101 - 104 هـ/ 720 - 724م). أما المئذنة والمقبرة الملحقتان بالمسجد، فيُعتقد بأنهما من أقدم الأوابد الباقية في أيٍّ من الأمكنة. إلى الشرق من المُجمَّع الرئيسي ثمة شبكة تجميع مياه واسعة، مُصانة جزئياً، مع سدٍّ مُهمٍّ، وقنوات ذات شأن.
artist: يزيد بن عبد الملك (حكم في الفترة 101- 105 / 720 - 724).
keywords: بيت؛ حمام؛ فسيفساء؛ القصور الصحراوية؛ نظام جمع المياه.

en.name: Qastal.
description:
Al-Qastal is situated approximately 25 km to the south of Amman, along the desert highway. The complex comprises a palace, a mosque of which only the minaret survives, and a bathhouse and domestic quarters. A vast water-collection system with a substantial dam and aqueduct is partially preserved to the east of the site. The palace is a square building of about (68 m x 68 m), the best preserved part of which is its southern wall. A circular tower articulates each of the four corners of the palace and three semi-circular interval towers are located along all of its walls, except for the eastern wall, where the entrance to the building is located. The eastern wall has two corner towers and two semi-circular interval towers. The middle semi-circular tower was split to provide access to the gateway. The decorated doorjamb of the entrance is still visible.  
Beyond the entrance is a gatehouse with stairs at both sides. Six self-contained residential units (*bayt*s) are organised around a central courtyard (40 m x 40 m sq) surrounded by porticoes. Each *bayt* is composed of four rooms organised around a rectangular courtyard. Sections of the mosaic floors are preserved. A postern-gate on the northern side leads to the mosque. The minaret and the cemetery associated with the mosque are believed to be amongst the oldest surviving anywhere. Some of the Abbasid inscribed tombstones in Madaba Archaeological Museum originated from al-Qastal. During the Ayyubid/Mamluk period (AH 6th–10th / AD 12th–16th centuries) the complex was converted into domestic quarters.

Situated around 25 km to the south of Amman, the monument is a complex comprising a palace, a mosque, a bathhouse and domestic quarters. The palace is a square building of about 68 m x 68 m and has preserved sections of mosaic floors. It probably belonged to the Caliph Yazid ibn ‘Abd al-Malik (r. AH 101–5 / AD 720–4). The minaret and the cemetery associated with the mosque are believed to be among the oldest surviving anywhere. To the east of the main complex there is a vast, partially preserved, water-collection system with a substantial dam and aqueducts.
artist: Probably Caliph Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Malik (r. AH 101–5 / AD 720–4).
keywords: Bathhouse; bayt; desert castles; gatehouse; mosaics; water collection system
partner: Ministry of Tourism & Antiquities, Department of Antiquities

es.name: Al-Qastal
description:
Al-Qastal es un complejo constituido por un palacio, una mezquita (de la que sólo se conserva el alminar), unos baños y dependencias domésticas. En la parte oriental se conserva parcialmente un enorme sistema de recogida de agua, con una gran presa y un acueducto. Del palacio, un edificio cuadrado de unos 68 × 68 m, lo que mejor se conserva es el muro sur. El edificio posee una torre circular en cada esquina y tres torres semicirculares distribuidas a intervalos regulares en todos los muros a excepción del oriental. En este último quedan cuatro torres, dos de las cuales flanquean la puerta principal del palacio. La decoración de las jambas es aún visible.  
Pasada la entrada se halla una torre con escaleras a ambos lados. Hay seis residencias independientes (*bayt*) ubicadas alrededor de un patio central porticado de 40 m². Cada *bayt* consta de cuatro aposentos dispuestos en torno a un patio rectangular. Aún se conservan partes de los suelos de mosaico. En el extremo norte del palacio hay una poterna que conduce a la mezquita. Se cree que el alminar y el cementerio anexos a la mezquita son dos de los monumentos de este tipo más antiguos que existen. Algunas de las lápidas abbasíes con inscripciones que actualmente se conservan en el Museo Arqueológico de Madaba proceden de al-Qastal. Durante el periodo ayyubí/mameluco (siglos VI-X / XII-XVI), el complejo se transformó en complejo residencial.

El complejo de Al-Qastal, a 25 km al sur de Ammán, comprende un palacio, una mezquita, un hammam y dependencias residenciales. En el palacio, de planta cuadrada (68 × 68 m), aún quedan algunos suelos de mosaico. El complejo perteneció, probablemente, al califa Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik (r. 101-105 / 720-724). El alminar y el cementerio de la mezquita están considerados como dos de los monumentos de este tipo más antiguos que se conservan. Al este del complejo quedan partes de un ingente sistema de recolección de agua, con una gran presa y acueductos.
dates: Anterior al año 126 de la Hégira / 744 d. C.
artist: Probablemente el califa Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik (r. 101-105 / 720-724).
keywords: baños; bayt; castillos del desierto; torre de entrada; mosaicos; sistema de recogida de agua.

fr.name: Al-Qastal.
description:
Al-Qastal est situé à environ 25 km au sud d'Amman, en bordure de la route du désert. Le complexe comprend un palais, une mosquée dont seul le minaret subsiste, des bains et des quartiers d'habitation. Un vaste système de collecte des eaux – dont un important barrage et un aqueduc en partie préservé – s'étend à l'est du site. Le palais est un bâtiment carré de 68 x 68 m environ, dont la partie la mieux conservée est le mur méridional. Une tour circulaire se dresse à chacun des quatre angles et trois tours semi-circulaires se répartissent à intervalles réguliers le long de chacun des murs, à l'exception du mur oriental qui n'en compte que deux, la tour semi-circulaire du milieu ayant été scindée pour ménager la porte d'entrée centrale, dont subsiste un piédroit décoré.  
Le corps de garde derrière l'entrée a conservé ses escaliers des deux côtés. Six unités résidentielles indépendantes (bayt) sont disposées autour d'une cour centrale (40 x 40 m) entourée de portiques. Chaque bayt se compose de quatre pièces réparties autour d'une cour rectangulaire. Des parties de sols en mosaïque sont conservées. Côté nord, une poterne conduit à la mosquée dont le minaret et le cimetière sont parmi les plus anciens monuments islamiques de ce type parvenus jusqu'à nous. Certaines pierres tombales à inscriptions abbassides ont été transférées au Musée archéologique de Madaba. Au cours de la période ayyoubide/mamelouke (VIe-Xe siècle H / XIIe-XVIe siècle J.-C.), le complexe a été transformé en logements.

Situé à environ 25 km au sud d’Amman, ce monument est un complexe comprenant un palais, une mosquée, un établissement de bains et des quartiers domestiques. Le palais est un bâtiment carré d’environ 68 m de côté et comporte des parties préservées de sols en mosaïques. Il appartenait vraisemblablement au calife Yazid ibn Abd al Malik (r. 101-105 H / 720-724 J.-C.). Le minaret et le cimetière associé à la mosquée sont considérés comme étant parmi les plus anciens monuments islamiques de ce type qui nous soient parvenus. À l’est du complexe principal se trouve un vaste système de collecte des eaux, partiellement préservé, dont un important barrage et un aqueduc.
artist: Probablement le calife Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik (r. 101-105 H / 720-724 J.-C.).
keywords: bains ; bayt ; châteaux du désert ; corps de garde ; mosaïques ; système de collecte des eaux

en.name: Coffee pot
short_description: This copper dallah goes back to a type allegedly first used in 17th-century Baghdad, By the 19th century, we know of several production centres in the Arabian peninsula. Its design reflects its functional needs. The broad base ensures stability on the fire or on the sand, the large beak prevents too much coffee sediment to reach the cup. The lid is weighted to avoid it opening during the pouring process.The quality and quantity of the coffee served indicated the wealth of the host and status of the guest. Throughout the Near and Middle East coffee lay at the heart of social ritual and hospitality, while providing sustenance during chats, debate and political discourse in the many coffeehouses in the region. In continental Europe, the fashion for coffee was at its height in the 17th and 18th centuries, with coffeehouses the preferred meeting places for intellectuals and artists. In Britain, meanwhile, tea soon overtook coffee in popularity, even though certain religious organisations tried to promote coffee houses for the poor in order to steer them away from pubs and bars.
holder: Sharjah Heritage Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
keywords: dallah

ar.name: وعاء/ زبدية تشبه الفخار الصيني
description: هذه الزبدية الخزفية المزينة بشكل كبير بأزرق الكوبالت مقابل شريط أبيض يشبه البرشمان هو أحد الأمثلة الأولى التي تتضمن التخطيط كعنصر أساسي في التزيين. والكلمة العربية (غبطة) مكررة على سطرين في المركز وتشكل تشكيل متوازن عندما تجتمع مع أنصاف الدوائر التي تزين الإطار . وإن صانعي الفخار العراقيين في القرن التاسع حاولوا تقليد نوعية السطوع والجسم الصلب لأوعية الفخار الصينية باستخدام زجاج أبيض معتم بالقصدير.

en.name: Bowl emulating Chinese stoneware
description: This ceramic bowl, boldly decorated in cobalt blue against a parchment-like white slip, is one of the earliest examples to incorporate calligraphy as the main element of decoration. The Arabic word *ghibta* (happiness) is repeated on two lines in the centre and creates a balanced composition when combined with the half-circles decorating the rim. Iraqi potters of the ninth century attempted to emulate the luminous quality and hard body of Chinese whitewares by using a tin‑opacified white glaze.
dates: Hegira late second–late 3rd century / AD 9th century
keywords: Abbasid; Basra; Iraq; earthenware; blue-and-white; Arabic inscription; bowl; calligraphy; clay; earthenware dish; glazed; inscription; kufic

en.name: Bridal coat (*Klashenik*)
short_description: A *klashenik* is a kind of over-garment women used to wear in winter. It is split in the front and made of thick woollen broadcloth called *klashna*. This piece is long to the hips. It is adorned with red braids along the hems. It is also decorated with embroidery of geometric patterns on the sleeves and at the breasts. Every ethnic area in Macedonia had distinct style of traditional costume, yet all of them show undeniable influence of Oriental art.
keywords: klashenik; broad cloth; textile; embroidery; geometric patterns; geometric motifs; costume; wedding; marriage
materials: Thick woollen fabric, twill-weave, embroidery with *srma* and decoration with wool braids

ar.name: قطعة من قربة حاج.
description: قطعة من الجانب المسطح لقربة خزفية بدون طلاء، مع جزء من حفر غير عميق لرامي سهام يمتطي صهوة حصان صنع في قالب. يمكن الحصول على فكرة عن الشكل الأصلي من عدد من القراب التي بقيت سليمة حتى اليوم، وقد كان الإبريق الأصلي برميلي الشكل ذي مصب دائري في الأعلى. جوانب الإبريق مسطحة وله عروتان على الحافة الدائرية. ونظراً لشبه هذه الأواني مع تلك التي كان الحجاج الغربيون يجلبونها من الأراضي المقدسة، سميت "قراب الحجاج". استعمل الفخار غير المطلي في تخزين المياه لأن الفخار ذي المسام كان فعّالاً في تبريد المياه، وهذه خاصية هامة لاسيماً في الرحلات الطويلة.

كسرة من قارورة للحج، مصنوعة من الفخار المطلي بالمينا غير المصقول، يظهر عليها جزء من رسم لفارس يمتطي جواده. استخدمت القارورة لحفظ الماء، وتشبه القوارير التي كان يحملها الحُجّاج القادمون من الأراضي المقدسة، من الغرب.
dates: القرن السادس- السابع/ الثاني عشر- الثالث عشر.
keywords: حج؛ حصان؛ رامي سهام.

en.name: Pilgrim bottle fragment.
description: An unglazed fragment from the flat side of a pilgrim bottle, with part of the depiction of an archer on horseback moulded in low relief. An idea of the original shape can be obtained from a number of pilgrim bottles that survive intact. The bottle would have been shaped like a drum with a spout attached at the top, circular in shape with two flat sides and two handles on the rounded edge. Due to their similarity with vessels brought back from the Holy Land by Western pilgrims these vessels are usually termed 'pilgrim bottles'. Unglazed pottery was used for storing water as the porous clay was especially efficient at keeping water cool, particularly important on long journeys.

A fragment from an unglazed earthenware pilgrim bottle showing part of the depiction of an archer on horseback. These bottles, used for carrying water, were termed pilgrim bottles due to their similarity to vessels brought back from the Holy Land by Western pilgrims.
keywords: Horse; archer; pilgrimage; pilgrim's flasks

es.name: Fragmento de cantimplora de peregrino.
description: Fragmento de cerámica sin vidriar del lado plano de una cantimplora, con un bajorrelieve que representa a un arquero a caballo. Las cantimploras conservadas ayudan a hacerse una idea de la forma original del objeto: una especie de tambor, con un pitorro en la parte superior y dos asas en los lados redondeados. Este tipo de botellas se denominan usualmente "cantimploras de peregrino"  por su similitud con los recipientes traídos de Tierra Santa por peregrinos occidentales. La alfarería sin vidriar era muy utilizada para guardar agua debido a que la arcilla es un material muy poroso que mantiene el agua fresca, algo importante en viajes largos.

Fragmento de una cantimplora de cerámica sin vidriar con parte de la figura de un arquero a caballo. Estas botellas, que se utilizaban para llevar agua, han sido denominadas "cantimploras de peregrinos" por su similitud con recipientes que los peregrinos occidentales trajeron de Tierra Santa.
dates: Siglos VI-VII de la Hégira /  XII-XIII d. C.
keywords: caballo; arquero; peregrinaje

fr.name: Fragment de gourde de pèlerin.
description: Fragment non vernissé du côté plat d'une gourde de pèlerin, à décor moulé en bas-relief reproduisant partiellement un archer à cheval. Une idée de la forme d'origine nous est donnée par un certain nombre de gourdes de pèlerin conservées intactes. Ce petit récipient était en forme de tambour doté en partie haute d'un bec, d'un dessus et d'un fond plats et de deux poignées sur la partie cylindrique. Par rapprochement avec certains récipients rapportés de Terre sainte par des pèlerins occidentaux, ces récipients sont généralement appelés “gourdes de pèlerin”. La poterie non vernissée servait à la conservation de l'eau, la porosité de l'argile lui permettant de maintenir plus longtemps la fraîcheur du liquide, ce qui était apprécié pendant les longs voyages.

Fragment de gourde de pèlerin en terre cuite non vernissée avec représentation partielle d'archer à cheval. Ces bouteilles, qui servaient à transporter de l'eau, étaient appelées  “gourdes de pèlerin” étant donné leur ressemblance avec des récipients rapportés de Terre sainte par des pèlerins occidentaux.
dates: VIe-VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIe-XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: chevaux ; archers ; pèlerinage

ar.name: قارورة
description: هذه القارورة غير العادية – المشكلة بشكل بيضوي ذات جانبين مسطحين يبدو أنها  الوحيدة الباقية وربما كانت وعاء للاستخدام الذي أنتجه فنانو الزجاج لاحتياجاتهم اليومية . وإن حلقة قاعدتها المستديرة البيضوية مصنوعة بالطوي وهي غير منتظمة بشكل طفيف ولها علامة أنبوب النفخ في مركزها مشكلة بواسطة قضيب معدني حيث أضيف له الزجاج وفوق مقبضيها المضافين يوجد عنق متضيق يؤدي إلى فوهة قصيرة مدورة وإطار الذي ينطوي للداخل.
keywords: قارورة ، زجاج ، بني ، أصفر ، مختومة

en.name: Bottle
description: This unusual bottle—formed as an elongated oval with flat sides—seems to have survived without a counterpart. It may have been a utilitarian vessel which glass artisans produced for daily needs. Its rounded oval footring, made by folding, is slightly irregular and has a pontil mark in its centre created by a metal rod with glass added to it. Above its two applied handles, a constricted neck leads to a short, rounded mouth and a rim that folds inwards.
keywords: Bottle; glass; brown; yellow; stamped
materials: Glass of honey yellow colour, greyish white weathering; free blown, pattern-pressed and applied, tooled, worked on the pontil

ar.name: إبريق على حامل
description: القطعة عبارة عن إبريق (أ) ذو أطراف دائرية مسطحة وله عنق طويل مستدق النهاية ذو مفصل وغطاء بشكل قبة ونهاية كروية مزخرفة. والمقبض يتصل من أسفل الغطاء مقابل مسكبة صغيرة.و الجسم يستند إلى قاعدة منفتحة وعند مركز كل جانب يوجد قطعة ألماسية وردية الشكل محاطة بثلاث ورقات ضمن حدود دقيقة مطلية بالمينا للمستطيلات المؤطرة للتشكيلات المزهرة.  الصينية البيضوية المتصلة (ب) تتميز برشات مزهرة مطلية بمينا على أعلى أربعة أقدام منفتحة التي تنتهي برؤوس فيلة.

en.name: Ewer on a stand
description: An ewer with flattened circular sides has a tall tapering neck with a hinged, dome cover and ball finial. A handle is attached below the cover, opposite a small spout. The body rests on a spreading foot. At the center of each side is a rosediamond inset flowerhead surrounded by trefoils within a fine enamelled border of floral cartouches. The associated oval tray features enamelled floral sprays and cartouches on top of four spreading feet terminating in elephant heads.

en.name: Souvenir des Relations télegraphiques entre Damas, Hedjaz, Damas (Syrie). (Memorial Column of Telegraphic Connections between Damascus and Hijaz, Damascus, Syria)
description: The Amud al Telegraph (the Telegraph Column or Telegraph Monument), sometimes locally known as Amud al Marjeh, is situated at the centre of Marjeh Square in Damascus. The monument was designed in 1900 by Raimondo D’Aronco and erected in Marjeh Square in 1904. It was constructed to commemorate the completion of the telegraph line linking Istanbul, Damascus and Mecca. The monument's bronze shaft is decorated with stylized representations of telegraph wires, poles and related equipment. The small structure at the top of the column is a model of the Yıldız Hamidiye Mosque in Istanbul, located near Yıldız Palace. The column formed the centrepiece of the redesign of Marjeh Square, transforming an open riverside space along the Barada River into a civic focal point, a transportation hub and a symbolic administrative centre.
keywords: Syria; Monument; Photograph; transportation

ar.name: إبريق بتصميم حيوانات ونقوش
description: القطعة عبارة عن إبريق فخاري مطلي بطلاء براق بلون بني وأبيض ذو جسم أسطواني الذي ينتفخ بشكل طفيف عند الصعود باتجاه الكتف ، والكتف مدور ويمتد منه مقبض مسطح وعنق ومسكبة. ويمتد المقبض للأعلى من الكتف ويدور بزاوية 45 درجة ليتصل بالعنق تماما أسفل الإطار. والعنق بشكل قمع وذو إطار مقلوب للخارج وهناك طوق قليل العمق (ضحل) في قاعدة العنق تماما أعلى نقطة الاتصال مع الكتف. ويتألف التزيين من طلاء براق بلون أصفر- بني فوق خلفية مزججة بيضاء غير شفافة ومركزة في منطقتين من الإبريق: القسم السفلي من الجسم والقسم العلوي ويتضمن العنق ،الكتف ،المقبض والمسكبة. وهذا يترك قسم مركزي كبير لزجاج أبيض غير شفاف على الجسم الذي يوجد عليه سطر وحيد منقوش تم إضافته بطلاء براق أصفر- بني. والنقش عبارة عن شعر ذو أبيات رباعية باللغة الفارسية يقول ما يلي : لقد أوصلت حبك لمهجتي (أعماق روحي /نفسي) / وقد عايشت أدق تفاصيله / حتى تغلبت على كل العالم/من أجل أن أوصل حبك للعالم / وهذا منسوب للكاتب أبو زيد الذي كتب نصه الخاص في سنة ستمائة .وفي المنطقة السفلية يوجد نقش ثان مكتوب بشكل رديف بخط كوفي كبير الحروف على خلفية براقة بلون أصفر – بني  ذو لفات صغيرة ودقيقة وخطوط حلزونية. ويكرر هذا النقش بشكل أساسي كلمة (العز) مع مثال أو مثالين هما (الدولة / الحظ الطيب) و(السلامة). ويتضمن تزيين المنطقة العلوية ثلاثة أجزاء  حيث يحتوي الجزء الأخفض سلسلة من طيور السمان حيث أقدامها على الأرض وأجنحتها ترفرف في الوسط وهي مطلية بطلاء براق مقابل خلفية من الأوراق الملفوفة الفاتحة. والقسم المتوسط يحتوي مشهد صيد من اليمين لليسار فيه حيوان الفهد موضوع في أقصى يسار المقبض ويمثل سلسلة من الغزلان التي تملأ بقية القسم على كلا جانبي المسكبة. والفهد مصور وهو يضع طوقا ذو حلقة مما يشير إلى كونه فهدا مدربا وليس بريا. والحيوانات المرسومة في الهامش مقابل خلفية من الطلاء البراق ذو لفات دقيقة. والقسم العلوي من الكتف فيه نقش كوفي آخر ربما عبارة (العز الدائم) مكتوبة بشكل براق ومثبتة بقوة حول قاعدة العنق والعنق مطلي بنموذج سلسلة صغيرة القياس وخارج الإطار مطلي بطلاء براق ثخين بينما يحتوي داخله تخطيط قريب من الكوفي وأخيرا الجزء الخارجي المواجه لطرف كل من المقبض  والمسكبة يظهر بأنه قد رسم عليه صور سعيفات بشكل تصاعدي وهناك الكثير من الشقوق الشعرية / الرفيعة في كل الوعاء والمسكبة والمقبض والإطار وكلها تم ترميمها جزئيا. والعصابة المركزية بالخط الكوفي له منطقة ملحوظة من تزجيج غير واضح ومتقطع.
keywords: إبريق ،خزف ،طلاء براق،مزجج،أوعية خزفية،كاشان،إيران ،آسيا،أبو زيد ،فارسي

en.name: Ewer with Design of Animals and Inscriptions
description:
A stoneware, brown and white Luster-painted ewer with cylindrical body that swells slightly as it rises toward the shoulder; rounded shoulder from which extends a flat handle, neck, and spout. The handle extends upwards from the shoulder and turns at a 45 degree angle to connect to the neck just below the rim. The neck is funnel-shaped with and everted rim; there is a hollow collar at the base of the neck, just above where it joins to the shoulder.  
The decoration consists of a yellow-brown Luster painting over an opaque, white glazed background and is concentrated in two zones of the ewer: the bottom section of the body and the upper section, including the neck, shoulder, handle and spout. This leaves a large, central section of opaque white glaze on the body on which a single line of inscription has been added in the yellow-brown Luster. The inscription, a quatrain in Persian, reads as follows:  
*man mihr-i tu dar miyan-i jan awardam / ba u hama khurda dar miyan awardam / akhir zi hama jahan bar awardam sar / ta 'ishq-i tu bar sar-i jahan awardam  
li-katibihi katabahu Abu Zayd bi-khattihi dar sana sittami'a*  
I brought your love to the midst of my soul / I discussed the smallest matters with it / Until I overcame the entire world / In order to bring your love to the world.  
\[This belongs\] to its writer.  
Abu Zayd wrote it in his own script in the year six hundred.  
In the lower zone is a second inscription written in reserve in large, Kufic script on a background of the yellow-brown Luster with small, delicate scrolls and spirals. This inscription mainly repeats the word *al-'izz* ("glory") along with one or two instances each of *al-dawla* ("good fortune") and al-salama ("well-being").  
The upper zone of decoration is comprised of three registers. The lowest register contains a series of plump birds with their feet on the ground and their wings in mid-flap. They are painted in Luster against a background of light scrolls. The middle register contains a chase scene moving from right to left with a cheetah, placed to the immediate left of the handle, pursuing a series of gazelles that fill the remainder of the register on either side of the spout. The cheetah is represented wearing a collar with a ring, indicating that it is a trained cheetah rather than a wild one. The animals are painted in reserve against a background of Luster with fine scrolls. The upper register of the shoulder has another *Kufic* inscription, possibly the phrase *al-'izz al-da'im* ("perpetual glory"), written in Luster and fitted tightly around the base of the neck. The neck is painted with a small-scale chain pattern. The exterior of the rim is painted in solid Luster while its interior contains *Kufic*\-style pseudo-epigraphy. Finally, the outward facing side of both the handle and the spout appear to have been painted with ascending palmette motifs.  
There are numerous hairline cracks throughout the vessel, and the spout, handle, and rim have all been partially restored. The central *Kufic* band has a notable area of blurring and streaking of the glaze.
artist: Abu Zayd, Persian, active late 12th–early 13th century
keywords: Ewer; Ceramics; Luster; Glazed; Fritware; Kashan; Iran; Asia; Abu Zayd; Persian; Lustre

en.name: Arab Quarter
description: The Arab Quarter of Sambuca, developed around the castle on the upper part of the hill, is only partly inhabited today, but retains its original plan, still keeping intact its own road network and the collective system of single houses despite undergoing modifications and changes. Limited by Via Fantasma to the north, by Via Belvedere to the south, by Vicolo degli Emiri to the east and by Vicolo Graffeo to the west, it can be reached by passing under the archway in Piazza Navarro. The Quarter is circumscribable within a triangular perimeter, the vertices being identifiable in the Mother Church, in the Church of the Rosario and in the former Church of San Giorgio. It forms a very compact and recognisable building complex in the city centre, characterised by courtyards of different typologies (elbowed, forked, bayoneted, hooked, etc.) and by an irregular road network, consisting of narrow streets mostly covered, or more simply accessible through archways. The village of Sambuca owes its origin to the Amir Ibn Mankud, according to a tradition confirmed by al-Idrisi and by later Sicilian historians: Tommaso Fazzello, Rocco Pirri, and Gioacchino Di Marzo. The primitive structure of the castle (demolished in 1854) dates back to about 1050, built on the top of a hill, in defence of the centre. A walled perimeter surrounded the Quarter, provided with three towers, one of which was later included in the bell tower of the Mother Church, while only traces of the foundations at the base of the small temple of the belvedere remain. The settlement remained unchanged up to the 15th century when it became necessary to expand beyond the walls in a north-westerly direction due to an increase in the population.

es.name: Barrio árabe
description: El barrio árabe de Sambuca, crecido alrededor del castillo, en la parte alta del cerro, hoy sólo está habitado en parte, pero mantiene los rasgos del trazado original, conservando intacto el trazado viario y el sistema de aglutinamiento de las viviendas individuales, pese a las modificaciones y las transformaciones sufridas. Delimitado por Via Fantasma al norte, Via Belvedere al sur, Vicolo degli Emiri al este y Vicolo Graffeo al oeste, se entra en él atravesando el arco de Piazza Navarro. El barrio se inscribe en un perímetro triangular cuyos vértices son la Iglesia Matriz, la iglesia del Rosario y la antigua iglesia de San Jorge; se presenta como un conglomerado de viviendas muy compacto y diferenciado del resto del centro urbano, y se caracteriza por sus patios de variado tipo (en recodo, en horca, en bayoneta, en garfio, etc.) y por un tejido viario irregular, constituido por callejuelas en gran parte cubiertas o más sencillamente encuadradas por arcos de entrada. El pueblo de Sambuca debe su origen al emir Ibn Mankud, según una tradición confirmada por al-Idrisi y por historiadores sicilianos posteriores: Tommaso Fazzello, Rocco Pirri, Gioacchino Di Marzo. Para defender el centro, en lo alto de la colina se edificó un castillo (demolido en 1854) cuyas primitivas estructuras se remontarían a 1050 aproximadamente. Rodeaba el barrio un perímetro amurallado, provisto de tres torres, una de las cuales ha sido incorporada posteriormente al campanario de la Iglesia Matriz, mientras que de la torre de planta circular sólo quedan restos de los cimientos en la base del templete del mirador. El pueblo permaneció sin alteraciones hasta el siglo XV, cuando, con el aumento de habitantes, se hizo necesaria una expansión extramuros, hacia el noroeste.

en.name: Coffee pots (*dallah*)
description: With its slender waist, graceful handle and elegant spout, this coffee pot (or *dallah*) is an exquisite example of Nazwa silversmithing. The silver souq in Nazwa is famed for its superb wares; smiths tend to work alongside jewellers and khanjar-makers to produce particularly fine goods. This *dallah* features a combination of arabesque and geometric designs, while the inscription at the bottom reads, in Arabic, "K. R. 21/6/1974" – a reference to its maker, Khalfan bin Rashid al-Sabahi, and its date of completion.
type: Copper, silver and brass (some with tin wash)
holder: The National Museum – Sultanate of Oman
materials: Copper, silver and brass (some with tin wash)
tags: Copper, silver and brass (some with tin wash)

en.name: Table clock
description: An example of a richly decorated table clock decorated with alabaster columns, the popularity for which spread at the end of the 18th century in Pest, Buda and Óbuda. Richly decorated table clocks such as this one were common in the late 18th century and this type with a column decoration shows the stylistic change that took place at the end of the century, marking a transition towards Neo-Classicism. Architectural elements such as this were often used instead of ornate decoration once the Neo-Classical style took hold. From among similar clocks preserved in the collection at the Budapest History  Museum, this example is one of the most characteristic and richly decorated. It is signed by the clockmaker, Johann Kerbacher.

This richly decorated table clock is a rare example documenting the mastery of Johan Kerbacher, whose signed clocks made in his workshop in Óbuda (Old Buda) are known from the second half of the 18th century. The alabaster-column decoration was a frequently used motif in the period, which popularity spread at the end of the 18th century in Pest, Buda and Óbuda, and marked the transition to Neo-Classicism.
keywords: Applied art; timekeeping; Neo-Classicism; enamel; alabaster; gilding; silver; gold; metalwork; Johann Kerbacher; Óbuda; furnishing; workshop

ar.name: دينار ذهبي.
description:
دينار ذهبي ضرب في المهدية في تونس عام 380 / 990، أثناء خلافة الخليفة الفاطمي العزيز (حكم في الفترة 365 - 386 / 975- 996).  
يظهر على وجه هذه القطعة في الوسط داخل دائرتين متحدتي المركز كتابة بالخط الكوفي من سطرين:  
السطر الأول يقرأ: "لا اله إلا الله محمد رسول الله، علي خير صفوة الله."  
السطر الثاني يقرأ: "محمد رسول اللهأرسله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون."  
  
كتب على ظهر القطعة داخل دائرتين متحدتي المركز كتابة من سطرين:  
السطر الأول يقرأ: "عبدالله ووليه نزار الإمام العزيز بالله أمير المؤمنين"  
السطر الثاني يُظهر اسم مدينة الضرب "المهدية" وسنة الضرب "380" هجرية.

دينار ذهبي، من آيلا في العقبة. على الوجه الآخر اسم الخليفة الفاطمي الخامس العزيز (الذي حكم ما بين عامي 365 - 368 هـ/975 – 996م)، مكان الضرب الذي هو المهدية، في تونس، والتاريخ عام 380 هـ/990م. يرد ذكر عليّ إضافة إلى النبي مُحمَّد على الأوجه الأول. أما الشعار فمكتوب بالخطِّ الكوفي.
keywords: خط كوفي؛ ذهب؛ ذهب مطروق؛ قطعة نقد؛ المهدية؛ نقود.

en.name: Gold coin (*dinar*).
description:
A gold coin (*dinar*) of the fifth Fatimid Caliph al-Aziz (r. AH 365–86 / AD 975–96), struck at al-Mahdiyya in Tunisia in AH 380 / AD 990. The legend is in *kufic* script.  
  
Obverse:  
  
Centre: raised point within two concentric circles.  
  
First margin: ''.لا اله الا الله، محمد رسول الله، علي خير صفوة الل'  
  
'There is no God except God, Muhammad is the Messenger. Ali is the best God's prime.'  
  
Second margin: **محمد رسول الله أرسله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون.**  
  
'Muhammad is the Messenger of God. He sent him with guidance and the true religion to prevail over all other religions, even though the idolaters may object.'  
  
Reverse:  
  
Centre: raised point within two concentric circles.  
  
First margin: **عبد الله ووليه نزار الإمام العزيز بالله أمير المؤمنين.**  
  
'Abd Allah and his supporter the Imam Al-'Aziz Billah Commander of the Faithful.'  
  
Second margin: **بسم الله ضرب هذا الدينار بالمهدية سنة ثمانون وثلثماية.**  
  
'In the name of God, this *dinar* was struck at al-Mahdiyya in the year 380.' (AD 990).

A gold coin (*dinar*) from Ayla in Aqaba. On the reverse is the name of the fifth Fatimid Caliph al-Aziz (r. AH 365–86 / AD 975–96), the place of minting, al-Mahdiyya in Tunisia, and the date 380 / 990. Ali is mentioned in addition to the Prophet Muhammad on the obverse. The legend is in *kufic* script.

es.name: Moneda de oro (dinar)
description:
Dinar del quinto califa fatimí, al-Aziz (r. 365-386 / 975-996), acuñada en Mahdia (Túnez) en 380 / 990. Presenta una inscripción en letra cúfica.  
Anverso: centro: punto en relieve dentro de dos círculos concéntricos; primer círculo: “No hay más Dios que el único Dios y Muhammad es su mensajero. Ali es el mejor fruto de Dios”; segundo círculo: “Muhammad, el mensajero de Dios, ha sido enviado provisto de la dirección y de la verdadera religión para proclamarla sobre todas las religiones, a pesar de la objeción de los idólatras”.  
Reverso: centro: punto en relieve dentro de dos círculos concéntricos; primer círculo: “Abd Allah y aquel que lo apoya, el imam Al-Aziz Billah, comandante de los fieles”; segundo círculo: “En el nombre de Dios, este dinar se acuñó en Mahdia en el año 380 (990 d. C.)”.

Dinar de oro encontrado en Ayla (Aqaba). En el reverso aparecen el nombre del quinto califa fatimí al-Aziz (r. 365-386 / 975-996), el lugar de acuñación (Mahdia, Túnez) y la fecha (380 / 990). En el anverso se menciona al profeta Muhammad. La leyenda está escrita en letra cúfica.

en.name: *Egypt. Suez canal.*
names: Taken from the collection *Lithiographies Représentant L'isthme de Suez*
short_description: The inauguration of the Suez Canal saw spectacular celebrations, attended by many European royalties. This was a huge victory for Ferdinand de Lesseps, who had sincerely hoped it would be a memorable and historical event. On his request, the painter Édouard Riou (1833–1900) produced a series of watercolours which were later published in *L’Album de l’Impératrice : Voyage Pittoresque à travers l’Isthme de Suez*.
keywords: Suez canal; Egypt; Ferdinand de Lesseps

fr.name: *Egypte. Canal de Suez*
names: Partie de Recueil. Lithographies représentant l'isthme de Suez
short_description: L’inauguration du canal de Suez donne lieu à des cérémonies grandioses, en présence des têtes couronnées européennes. C’est un triomphe pour Ferdinand de Lesseps qui entend bien en fixer le souvenir. À sa demande, le peintre Édouard Riou (1833-1900) va exécuter des aquarelles qui seront rassemblées dans L’Album de l’Impératrice : Voyage pittoresque à travers l’isthme de Suez.
keywords: Canal de Suez; Egypte; Ferdinand de Lesseps

en.name: São João Baptista (Parish Church)
names: São João Baptista (Vilar Formoso Parish Church)
description: Like the Parish Church at Vilar Torpim, the Parish Church of Vilar Formoso is yet another typical example of this group of frontier churches built or re-built at the beginning of the 16th century. It has a single nave divided by long, low ribbed arches. The chancel has a polychrome *Mudejar* ceiling, as did the main vessel of the church before rebuilding was carried out.

en.name: Roemer
description:
A 'Roemer' is a glass for white wine used throughout Germany and the Netherlands in the 17th century. Roemers are perhaps the most well-known type of forest-glass, which was the dominant glass industry in the northern and central parts of Europe. Forest glass is characterised by a green-yellow colour and was produced overwhelmingly for domestic use from the early Medieval period, often to quite crude designs.  
  
Nevertheless this roemer displays ornate and sophisticated diamond-point engraving signed by Willem Mooleyser, one of the most accomplished engravers working in the Netherlands in the late 17th century.

en.name: *Die stadt Algier*
short_description: According to the historiographer Gabriel Esquer, this illustration was the most detailed view of Algiers available in the 17th century. The artist has accurately mapped out the streets and houses of the city.
keywords: Print; traditional city

fr.name: *Die Stadt Algier*
short_description: Selon l’historiographe Gabriel Esquer, cette planche est considérée comme la vue d’Alger la plus détaillée du XVIIe siècle comportant le tracé exact des rues et l’indication des terrasses qui couvrent les maisons.
keywords: Estampe; cité traditionnelle

en.name: The Italian Politeama Rossini theatre in Tunis, inaugurated in 1903
short_description:
The Politeama Rossini was built by the construction company of Giuseppe Di Vittorio (a Sicilian who had migrated to Tunisia in 1882); the architect was a Mr. Baron. It could house an audience of 2,500.  
The first Italian theatre in Tunis was the “Teatro Tapia” founded in 1826. Other Italian theatres (such as the “Teatro Italiano” and the “Teatro Paradiso”) and concert halls (“Gran Teatro”, “Teatro Cohen”, etc.) were created in Tunis the following decades.
tags: Comitato Della Camera Italiana Di Commercio Ed Arti

en.name: *Kitchen of the Algerian Coffee Shop, at the Trocadero* \[Paris Exhibition 1878\]
names: *La cucina del Caffè Algerino, al Trocadero*
short_description: Within the International Exhibition in Paris, 1878, commercial activities typical of the colony were performed in the park next to Trocadero Pavilion. The scene shows the practice of making unfiltered coffee inside a kitchen decorated with *majolicas*, part of the reconstruction of a hypothetical neighbourhood in Algeria.
